author: imgarylai
body:
Three complaints about the admin editor's view-source, one cause: it was a sheet driven by a button that lived outside the toolbar.

- The button sat in its own outlined box beside the toolbar, so it read as belonging to something else.
- The panel opened at `sm:max-w-2xl` over the editor — roughly a third of the width the markdown is actually written at — with unhighlighted text at `text-xs`.
- Its copy button sat in the sheet header, underneath the sheet's own close button.

## What changed

**Source is now a mode of the editor pane.** The toolbar's last button (`FileCodeIcon`, `aria-pressed`) swaps the writing surface for the markdown, read-only; pressing it again swaps back. Same column, same width, same font as the document it is showing.

**The surface is hidden, not unmounted.** `EditorContent` owns the element ProseMirror's view is mounted on, so tearing it down per toggle would re-parse the document and take the caret and undo history with it. A test asserts the same paragraph node object and the same selection survive a round trip.

**The rest of the toolbar goes `inert` and dimmed while the source shows.** A read-only document whose toolbar can still write to it is worse than no toolbar. The toggle itself stays outside that group — it is the way back out.

**The markdown is highlighted.** lowlight with the markdown grammar *only*: a fenced block stays one `hljs-code` token, because this pane shows the document as source, not as its languages — highlighting inside the fence would have this pane and the code-block card disagreeing about what a fence is. The hast tree renders as React elements rather than injected HTML, and `tm-code` themes it with the site's own hljs tokens. `.hljs-code` picks up `--tm-accent` in `terminal.css` (reached only from here — no published block is tagged ```markdown).

**Copy moved into a header bar** above the block, mirroring the code-block card's chrome, with a `Markdown source · read-only` label and nothing to overlap.

## Notes

- `editor.sourceReadOnly` added to both locale files.
- `SourceSheet.tsx` → `SourceView.tsx`; its test moves with it and keeps the verbatim-text assertion (now also pinning that the highlighter puts every character back).
- New coverage: the toggle round trip, the document surviving it, the inert group, and the pane showing the form's `value` rather than a re-serialization.

## Verification

`pnpm test` (1598 passing), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` all clean. Driven in a real browser against `pnpm dev` in light and dark, with the preview both on and off; the inert assertion was confirmed to fail with the `inert` prop removed.

author: rubencu
body:
## Problem / Motivation

On my machine the Mochi pet's panel chat answered as the generic default KiroCrew agent — it had no pet persona and instead replied with my workspace context (open PRs, backlog, etc.), and only started acting like Mochi after I explicitly told it "you're the Mochi app". It self-healed on a later restart, which is what pointed me at a startup-ordering bug rather than a content bug.

## Why it matters

Mochi is a companion app whose whole point is its persona and its own scoped agent (its prompt, skills, MCP reach, and context-usage reporting). When the panel silently dispatches the default dashboard agent instead, the pet loses all of that and leaks the default agent's context into what should be a sandboxed companion chat. It looks like the app's own prompt is being ignored, and there's no error anywhere — the turn just runs as the wrong agent.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

I traced the failure to two independent defects that combine to produce the observed reply, and fixed both.

Defect 1 — startup ordering (backend). In `on_startup`, `apply_policy` (which materializes the app's agent configs) ran BEFORE `MochiRuntime.__init__` rendered the generated prompt files (`mochi-prompt.md` / `mochi-prompt-bg.md`). `bridges._apply_agent_prompt` pins a prompt "ABSOLUTE and EXISTING only", so a not-yet-written file is dropped with a warning and the materialized `mochi--mochi.json` ends up with no `prompt` field. My gateway log shows this exactly on the incident boot:

```
WARNING kiro_crew.apps.bridges: Agent mochi: prompt file does not exist, ignoring: …/mochi-prompt.md
WARNING kiro_crew.apps.bridges: Agent mochi-bg: prompt file does not exist, ignoring: …/mochi-prompt-bg.md
INFO  kiro_crew.apps.builtins.mochi.agent_policy: Mochi MCP policy applied to 2 agent config(s)
```

The fix constructs the runtime FIRST (its `__init__` renders the prompt files but does NOT start the agent — `start()` does), then runs `apply_policy`, then `start()`. So the prompt files exist when `_apply_agent_prompt` reads them, and the MCP deny-by-default invariant is preserved because the policy is still materialized before the agent can spawn. The re-enable-after-disable branch keeps applying the policy before `start()` too; its instance already rendered the files at construction, so it was never affected.

Defect 2 — panel slot binding (frontend). The foreground turn didn't just lose the persona, it ran the default agent entirely. My log shows `agent match for slot=mochi agent=` (empty) and `Pool decision: key=dashboard:mochi … agent=kirocrew`, i.e. the persisted `mochi` slot (restored at boot from `open_slots.json`) came back from `get_or_create` with an empty agent, and `get_or_create` returns an existing slot UNCHANGED — it never rebinds. `ensureSlot` verified the returned binding and, since it wasn't `mochi`, refused. The fix teaches `ensureSlot` to distinguish the two cases: an EMPTY binding is our own slot that lost (or never had) the agent, so adopt it via the explicit `POST /api/chat/slots/{slot}/agent` endpoint (which `get_or_create` deliberately won't call); a DIFFERENT NAMED agent is someone else's session, so keep refusing to avoid hijacking it. I chose the frontend seam because it's the least-invasive correct fix: `get_or_create_slot` is called across the whole app and its "return existing unchanged" contract is relied on elsewhere, so widening it to adopt agents would be a broad behavioral change; the rebind is a Mochi-panel concern and belongs in the Mochi panel bridge.

## Tests

Backend (rebind atomicity): `test/test_dashboard_chat.py` pins the rebind guard end to end — 409 on a running slot and between orchestrated stages, rollback on reset failure, queue-drain on every exit, and (round 11) two persist-ordering regressions: `test_api_chat_slot_agent_serializes_persist_with_rebind` delays the first of two rapid rebinds' metadata writes and asserts disk matches the LAST binding (fails on the pre-fix code with the stale agent persisted last), and `test_api_chat_slot_agent_rolls_back_binding_on_persist_failure` asserts a failing persist rolls the binding back so memory and disk never diverge.

Backend: `test/test_mochi_hooks.py::TestStartupPromptOrdering` asserts that both rendered prompt files are on disk at the moment `apply_policy` is invoked by `on_startup`. It fails on the old ordering (`{'chat': False, 'bg': False}`) and passes with the fix. The drop itself was already covered by `test_mochi_agent_prompt.py`; the untested gap was the ordering.

Frontend: `src/apps/mochi/test/mochiPanelBridge.test.ts` gains two cases — one asserting `ensureSlot` rebinds an empty-agent slot via the agent endpoint and then sends, and one asserting that when the rebind fails `ensureSlot` THROWS, posts NO chat turn to `/api/chat?ws=1`, and still retries the bind on the next send (the latch never trips). The three adoption failure branches — rebind not ok, unparseable rebind response, and a rebind that doesn't come back as the mochi agent — all throw now, because `sendMessage` doesn't guard on `ensureSlot`'s outcome, so a bare return still dispatched the turn to the unbound slot where the dashboard default answered. The existing "refuses to send when the slot is owned by another agent" case still passes, so the hijack guard is intact.

N/A — unit coverage exercises both the backend ordering invariant and the frontend rebind/refuse branches directly, and the incident is reproduced by the fail-before assertions.

body: ## Summary - keep blocking agent-decision attention in cmux-owned lifecycle, sidebar status, and workspace ordering without asking AppKit for process-level attention - preserve terminal BEL audio and visual attention by routing the originating pane through cmux-owned unread/flash state with `shouldFocus: false` - require a concrete terminal surface owner before routing BEL attention, so app-target or stale callbacks cannot guess a workspace ## Root cause and architecture Both `FeedCoordinator.surfaceBlockingDecisionAttention` and `GhosttyApp.ringBell()` called `NSApplication.requestUserAttention(.informationalRequest)` for background activity. On macOS 26 with Stage Manager, that process-level request can promote cmux's entire window set even though the user is working in another application. This removes process-level AppKit attention from both background paths. Feed attention is lifecycle/sidebar/workspace state. Terminal BEL is split into an audio-only `TerminalBellService` and a cmux-owned route that resolves the live surface owner, marks inactive panes unread, and flashes without changing selection or focus. The invalid Stage Manager state is unavailable at those boundaries instead of being conditionally suppressed by OS version or focus timing. ## Regression evidence and verification - Regression red: https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/31148444890 at `c2e9a50145` executed the focused suite and failed because the pre-fix Feed path issued one AppKit attention request. - Initial fix green: https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/31149265992 at `1d7626f5a0` passed the same selected suite. - Current tests exercise Feed needs-input state, terminal BEL unread routing without workspace selection changes, and injected audio behavior. The current fixture deliberately avoids global `NSApplication` swizzling because Swift Testing suites run in parallel; the historical red run records the pre-fix AppKit call. - `cmux-policy-check --mode branch --base origin/main` is clean at `e0bdf48c5a`. - Swift parsing passed for all changed Swift files, and `TerminalBellService.swift` typechecked standalone with warnings treated as errors. - macOS 26 GUI repro was attempted through https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux-loader/actions/runs/31146605098. Provisioning completed after the local wrapper timed out, but the host was unreachable, so no verified cloud video is claimed. - No local `xcodebuild` tests or XCUITests were run, per task constraints. Standalone SwiftPM testing is blocked by the checkout's invalid local GhosttyKit artifact; GitHub Actions owns the app/package test proof. ## Audit - No user-facing strings changed; localization catalogs were audited and are untouched. - No Swift warning-budget or file-length-budget files changed. Fixes #9466 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Broad changes to notification navigation, unread projections, Dock focus/open, and terminal input attribution across core macOS UX paths; well-covered by package tests but high interaction surface for regressions. > > **Overview** > Removes reliance on process-level AppKit attention for background activity and keeps bells, unread, and navigation inside cmux-owned state so Stage Manager does not promote the whole window set. > > **Terminal bells** split into audio-only `TerminalBellService` / `TerminalBellPresentation` and host-routed visual attention via `onVisualBell`; explicit terminal input is attributed only after acceptance (`onExplicitInput`), including copy mode, mobile gestures, and queued socket input, while workspace font-size shortcuts no longer fan out as per-surface explicit input. > > **Notifications and unread** treat per-window Dock surfaces as distinct owners (`WindowDockUnreadTarget`, `FocusedNotificationTarget` workspace vs `windowDock`); jump/mark-oldest and open paths can reveal a Dock, exclude an exact Dock target, and return `dockUnavailable` when reveal fails. `SidebarUnreadModel` is refactored with owner-scoped surface projections, summary/surface observers, and synchronous observation teardown; dismissal can clear store-level manual unread on specific surfaces. `liveSurfaceOwner` separates live ownership from renderable notification opens; Dock session restore/autosave wires `notificationStore` and manual-unread fingerprints. > > **CI:** e2e executed-test parsing sums every XCTest/Swift Testing summary so a later zero-test host teardown cannot zero out a real run. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit af914dd3a85db0ad025edcefe0c1c4e37669ffde. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). --- ## Summary by cubic Stops Stage Manager from promoting cmux windows by removing process-level AppKit attention and keeping all background attention inside cmux. Terminal bells are audio-only; visual BEL/unread route to the exact live owner (workspace or per‑window Dock) with fail‑closed navigation, precise owner‑scoped open/scroll restore, and clear Dock‑availability errors (fixes #9466). - **Bug Fixes** - Docks: preflight reveal and fail closed; focus/open return `unavailable`/`dockUnavailable` with a localized “Dock could not be revealed”; notification opens target the exact per‑window Dock via `openWindowDockUnread` and clear only that surface’s manual unread; hidden workspace‑Dock notifications are ignored; manual unread stays constant‑time, survives owner transfer and snapshot/autosave; precise window‑Dock scroll capture/restore; socket focus results include `dockUnavailable`. - Terminal bells: added audio‑only playback in `CmuxTerminal` (`TerminalBellService` + `TerminalBellPresentation`); route visual BEL via `onVisualBell` to the live owner (incl. projected/mirrored terminals and sidebar focus); suppress when already focused; bound/coalesced notification‑style flashes. - Unread/input: notify owners only after accepted input (`onExplicitInput`) for copy‑mode, mobile actions, and queued socket input; workspace font‑size shortcuts no longer count as explicit input. - Mobile/CI: mobile previews throttle bursts with a coalescer; CI counts all XCTest and Swift Testing run summaries so a later zero‑test teardown can’t erase real executed counts. - **Refactors** - Ownership/navigation: split live ownership from renderable opens (`liveSurfaceOwner`); `FocusedNotificationTarget` distinguishes workspace vs window‑Dock owne

author: chris-rock
body:
## Summary

Adds a new **`mssql`** provider that connects to a Microsoft SQL Server instance over TDS (`github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb`) and inventories it through read-only `sys.*` / `msdb.*` catalog queries.

- **Auth**: SQL logins, Windows (NTLM), and Microsoft Entra ID access tokens.
- **Discovery**: each online database is discovered as its own `mssql-database` asset.
- **17 resources**: `server`, `server.configuration` (sp_configure), `login`, `serverRole`, `permission`, `database`, `databaseUser`, `databaseRole`, `applicationRole`, `credential`, `databaseScopedCredential`, `proxyAccount`, `linkedServer` (+ `.login`), `audit`, `auditSpecification`, `symmetricKey`, `asymmetricKey`, `clrAssembly`, `backup`.
- **Typed cross-references** throughout: `databaseUser.login`, server/database role membership, `credential.mappedLogins`, `proxyAccount.authorizedLogins`, `linkedServer.linkedLogins`.

## Coverage

Every automatable **SQL Server 2019/2022** hardening recommendation is queryable — surface-area options, authentication mode, `sa` state, password policy (`CHECK_POLICY`/`CHECK_EXPIRATION`/`MUST_CHANGE`), `Trustworthy`, guest `CONNECT`, orphaned users, audit specifications, symmetric/asymmetric key strength, TDE, and backup encryption — plus the principal / permission / credential / linked-server relationships needed to reason about privilege and lateral movement.

SIDs are rendered in canonical `S-1-5-…` form (with a `0x` hex fallback for non-NT SIDs) so Windows logins, database users, and the service account can be joined to an Active Directory graph.

## Testing

- **Unit tests**: SID canonicalization, DSN builder, encryption-mode mapping, and id builders.
- **Integration test** (env-gated via `MSSQL_TEST_HOST` / `MSSQL_TEST_PASSWORD`): `TestIntegrationResolveAll` walks every resource and field getter and asserts each resolves without error against a live instance; additional tests assert built-in correctness.
- Verified end-to-end against `mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022` using the fixture in `providers/mssql/testdata/seed.sql`. Two bugs found and fixed during live testing: a panic in SID parsing on short SIDs, and the `--port` flag being dropped in `ParseCLI`.

```bash
docker run -d --name mssql-test -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD='Str0ng!Passw0rd2026' -p 11433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest
cd providers/mssql
MSSQL_TEST_HOST=localhost:11433 MSSQL_TEST_PASSWORD='Str0ng!Passw0rd2026' go test ./resources/ -run Integration -v
```

## Notes / follow-ups

- Verified against SQL Server on **Linux**; Windows-only paths (SQL Agent proxies, some registry-backed fields) were exercised for "resolves without error" but not for value correctness on a Windows host.
- Kerberos/AD authentication, AD-backed service-account/SPN resolution, and inbound linked-server discovery are intentional follow-ups.
- The provider version is left at `13.0.0`; the release flow owns version bumps.

## Goal

Serve authorized bounded HLS init/media resources through a concrete, verified MinIO reader without exposing object-store identity or credentials.

## Changes

- add an official `minio@8.0.7` streaming reader with strict environment/configuration validation
- pass persisted expected kind, schema version, content type, byte length and SHA-256 through the internal reader port
- enforce configured bucket, safe object keys, expected-size hard caps, streaming timeout, exact length and incremental hash before returning bytes
- map missing, network, stream, timeout and corrupt-object failures to sanitized `MEDIA_NOT_READY`
- inject the concrete reader at server startup when the complete MinIO environment is present
- preserve authenticated window membership, opaque manifest resource tokens and zero forbidden-domain writes

## Boundaries

- no public contract, Prisma, migration or auth-domain change
- no presigned URL and no bucket/key/endpoint/credential in browser responses
- no cursor resolve, frame-step or sample-index repository in this slice

author: davelowelarsson
body:
The lightbox loses its original justification in this work — ADR 0006 §3 introduced it as the escape hatch for diagrams that could not be legible inline, and the legibility floor handles that inline now. It survives anyway, because its real constituency was never diagrams: it is bound to every article image, and there are 41 of those against 3 diagrams. Restated purpose: examine any figure full-screen. It was pointer-only, which is a capability that exists for mouse users and not for keyboard users — not something that can ship into a frozen accessibility floor. Each examinable figure now carries its own button, visually hidden until it takes focus, in the same idiom as the skip link and the theme control's labels. A SIBLING button rather than a wrapper, for two reasons that are the whole design: 1. An given role="button" stops being announced as an image. 2. A diagram already contains the focusable scroll region ADR 0012 adds, so wrapping it would nest interactive content inside interactive content — which #75 explicitly rules out. It also means nothing is re-parented, so #119's path-keyed framing selectors are untouched and a mouse user sees no new chrome at all. The name carries the figure: "Examine “” full screen", not a bare "Examine" that would read identically on all 41 images. WHAT THIS TICKET DID NOT NEED TO BUILD, found by planting regressions and watching them fail to bite: - `tabindex="-1"` on the dialog. - An explicit `dialog.focus()` on open. - An `opener` variable and a `.focus()` on close. `showModal()` already focuses the dialog element when it holds nothing focusable, which is what makes the arrow keys pan an oversized figure — the dialog is both the scroll container and the focus holder. And closing a dialog already restores focus to whatever had it before. Both are in the HTML standard and both are now asserted, so a browser that stopped doing them would fail the suite rather than the reader finding out. Three pieces of code that looked load-bearing, removed. The "no pan/zoom library, no custom gesture code" constraint from ADR 0006 §3 stands and is unchanged. Panning from the keyboard needed no library. The buttons are attached through a MutationObserver on
, because Mermaid swaps diagrams in after every script has run and re-renders them again on every theme change — the same latent ordering bug ADR 0006 records for the click listener, which is why that one is delegated. ADR 0006 §3 is amended in place with the restated purpose, the reason a sibling button was chosen over a wrapper, and a note that the no-library constraint survives intact. 289 unit, 150 e2e (up 9), lint and typecheck clean. Four planted regressions bite against three passing controls: no buttons at all, no MutationObserver, a generic accessible name, and a permanently visible control. Closes #122 Closes #75 --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

body:
## Summary

- **Scheduled alignment prompt** — scheduled deployments now send the Slack thread prompt when master is ahead of the multidev, same as manual. No more silent auto-merge.
- **All approvals as thread replies** — stage-to-stage approvals (`Deploy to test`, `Deploy to live`) moved from `broadcastMessage` to `postThreadBlocks`. All deployment interaction stays in the thread.
- **Reconnect from any window** — on mount, if `sessionStorage` has no job ID, falls back to `GET /api/jobs` and shows reconnect banner if an active job is found.
- **Socket Mode starts at server boot** — extracted to `lib/socketMode.ts` singleton wired to `instrumentation.ts` `register()`. Slack buttons work immediately after restart, no page load required.
- **Long-running alert shows stage elapsed time** — replaced frozen percentage bar with current stage name + time in that stage (e.g. `Stage 1/3 · dev · 42 min in this stage`).
- **Dev SFTP mode blocks + notifies Slack** — explicit connection mode check; posts thread error and stops if dev is in SFTP mode.
- **Uncommitted changes notifies Slack before stopping** — previously a silent throw; now posts a failed block to the thread so the reason is visible.
- **Test→live gap prompts instead of warning** — when test has undeployed code, sends a Slack thread prompt (Proceed / Stop) instead of a silent warn log.
- **Resume paused deployments from History** — `HistoryCard` shows a Resume button on paused items; pre-fills the deploy form with the correct source/destination and switches to the Deploy tab.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open app in second window mid-deployment — reconnect banner appears

author: butlerajamesab-lab
alexnikolskiy
body:
Этап **S1** эпика 083: словарь актор-контракта переписан под событийную модель. Только `sdk` — типы, константы и валидатор формы; рантаймов не трогает. Контракт `017.3` → `017.4`.

План: [`2026-08-06-s1-actor-contract.md`](https://github.com/trdlabs/control-center/blob/main/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-s1-actor-contract.md) · Спека: [`2026-08-04-event-driven-actor-contract-design.md`](https://github.com/trdlabs/control-center/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-event-driven-actor-contract-design.md)

## Что меняется

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Время** | микросекунды — единственная единица; бранд-типы `TimestampUs` / `DurationUs`, единственный нормализующий конвертер, safe-integer проверяется **после** арифметики |
| **События** | составного `bar` больше нет: пять раздельных рыночных событий плюс `market.subscription.status_changed` и `trading_state.changed`; `cancel.rejected` добавлен |
| **Конверт** | `eventTsUs` (frontier диспатча U) разведён с `effectiveTsUs` (минута T) уже в v1 |
| **Данные** | `MarketDataRequirement` — закрытый каталог на пять видов в одном экземпляре, с двусторонней типовой гарантией |
| **Наблюдение** | `never_observed \| observed \| gap`; `finality` и `revision` как две ортогональные оси |
| **Состояние** | `ActorInit` несёт дескрипторы подписок; слот состояния параметризован (`StrategyActor<S>`), `snapshotState` обязателен при непустом `S` |
| **Позиция** | `PositionView` брендирован и выводится из execution ledger; `unrealizedPnl` снесён намеренно |

## Ломающие изменения

Полный список в `CHANGELOG.md` → `[Unreleased]`. Кратко: исчезли `ActorBarEvent` и `FlatMarketSlice`; `OpenOrderStatus` / `OpenOrderView` / `PositionView` живы по имени с несовместимой формой; `afterMs` → `afterUs`, поле `bar` → `candle`, легаси `MarketDataKind` → `LegacyMarketDataKind`; 16 новых членов `ValidationCode` (source-breaking для потребителя с `Record<ValidationCode, Severity>`).

Проверено по восьми репозиториям: **внешних потребителей снесённых экспортов нет**. Манифесты `017.1`–`017.3` продолжают валидироваться.

## Как это делалось

Шесть задач, каждая — отдельный исполнитель с изолированным контекстом, ревью после каждой и цикл правок до пяти раундов. Десять ревью суммарно; **финальное — другим модельным семейством**, намеренно: девять предыдущих шли из одной родословной с авторами кода, и слепые пятна семейства так не ловятся.

Найдено и закрыто **девять Critical**. Показательные:

- **Полный выход из дробной позиции оставлял фантом.** `remainingSigned === 0` — точное сравнение float; лестница 0.15 BTC тремя траншами давала `qty: 1.39e-17` с фиктивным флипом через ноль и новым `openedAt`. Тесты не ловили: все количества были целыми. Порог выведен замером (максимальная накопленная погрешность 8.8e-16 на лестницах до 1000 плеч) и масштабируется к пику эры.
- **Пять событий несли метку времени в миллисекундах внутри µs-конверта.** Две координаты одного момента на одном объекте; `value.ts - clock.nowUs()` компилировалось. Найдено только финальным ревью — дефект лежал в шве между новым кодом и легаси-типами, которые он переиспользовал.
- **Схема пропускала «наблюдено, что данных не было»** — `bucket_closed` со `value: {state:'missing'}`.
- **Мемоизация обхода сняла экспоненту и пробила потолок вложенности**: вердикт зависел от порядка ключей объекта.
- **Гейт объявлял присутствующим наблюдением отсутствие данных**, а комментарий, оправдывавший выбор, содержал неверное утверждение о семантике JS.

Сквозной класс дефектов — **заявка сильнее гарантии**: комментарий или тест обещает больше, чем код даёт. Больше десяти случаев, включая тесты, чьи комментарии опровергались соседними строками того же файла.

## Как проверялось

Чтение исходников пропускало Critical четыре раза подряд. Работали: `npm pack` → установка тарбола в изолированный проект → удары через реальные публичные пути; мутационные пробы (сломать инвариант, убедиться, что сборка падает); дифференциальный фузз против независимого оракула (40 000 графов по циклам, 40 000 по глубине, 18 000 сценариев позиции против BigInt-оракула).

**270/270**, схемы без дрейфа, conformance OK, сборка чистая.

## Что осознанно осталось

## Description

The named return `modSC` is never assigned on any path, so callers always receive a zero value `dvm.SmartContract` alongside a nil error. The loop discards the contract returned by `injectMOD`, and when `modTag` is empty the loop does not run at all.

`InjectMODs("vsoo", TELA_INDEX_1)` returns a contract with 0 functions, where the unexported `injectMOD("vsoo", ...)` returns 7.

This assigns `modSC` from `injectMOD`, and parses the code when there are no tags, so the returned `modSC` reflects the returned `modCode` whenever no error is returned.

The only caller that uses the returned contract is `createContractVersions` in `parse.go`. That path is currently unreachable, it sits behind a version check that is false for the shipped version list, but it would assign an empty contract to `sc` once a version is added.

### Behaviour note

`InjectMODs` with an empty `modTag` and code that does not parse now returns an error where it previously returned nil. No in-tree caller can reach this: `parse.go` only passes the embedded `TELA_INDEX_1` and `TELA_DOC_1` constants, and both `tela.go` call sites are guarded by `h.Mods != ""`. An external caller could.

Everything else is unchanged. Across 36 combinations of code and tag inputs the returned `modCode` is byte identical before and after, as is the output of `ValidINDEXVersion` and `ValidDOCVersion`.

### Tests

Assertions added alongside the existing `InjectMODs` coverage in `TestTELA/MODs`, covering the empty `modTag`, each single tag, and multi tag combinations. Reverting `mods.go` while keeping the tests produces 12 assertion failures.

That subtest needs a simulator and runs after `Install`, so it does not run under a plain `go test`. I kept it there because that is where the sibling `InjectMODs` assertions already live, but happy to move it out.

author: fporcari
body:
## Summary

Adds `MenuStruct.docpage()` for opening a public document from a registered storage service inside the application frame.

This is intentionally a resolver-only feature: the menu resolves a storage path to a stable public URL and loads that document directly. It does not add an authenticated viewer page.

## API

```python
branch.docpage(
    'Monthly report',
    source='pkg:mypkg/docs/report.html',
    tags='REPORT_VIEW',
)
```

`source` must be a registered storage path. `tags` controls menu visibility only; it does not protect the resolved document URL.

## Behavior

- Resolves the source with `StorageNode.public_url(nocache=True)`, avoiding expiring signed menu links and stale overwritten documents.
- Hides only the affected menu entry and logs a warning when the source is absent, the storage service fails, or no public URL is available.
- Ignores inherited or entry-level `externalSite` URL prefixing because storage returns an absolute URL.
- Marks the iframe as `nonGenroContent`, so the frame does not wait for Genro bootstrap, keeps the menu label as its title, and closes without dereferencing `contentWindow.genro`.
- Shares page-attribute finalization with ordinary `webpage` entries.
- Uses a docstring to state the public-content security boundary.

## Security boundary

A `docpage` is suitable only for public documents. Storage/static URLs are served without page-level authentication, so hiding the menu entry with `tags` does not make the document confidential. Confidential or per-user documents still require an authenticated viewer endpoint.

## Verification

- Full suite: **2117 passed, 69 skipped**.
- Commit-hook suite: **2086 passed, 69 skipped**.
- Web suite excluding the daemon-only module: **285 passed, 47 skipped**.
- Resolver tests: **10 passed**, including a real symbolic `pkg:` storage node, both forms of `externalSite`, inherited `aux_instance`, missing source, unavailable service, empty public URL, and the framework's real tag-permission logic.
- `flake8` clean on all changed Python files.
- `node --check` clean on `frameindex.js`.
- The test package contains localized working and deliberate click-time-404 entries.
- Not verified in this update: a live authenticated browser session.

## Deliberately out of scope

- A built-in authenticated viewer and friendly missing-file page.
- The folder-to-menu variant.
- Confidential document delivery.

Refs #991

body:
## What

`inviteEmail` in `src/lib/agents/acquisition-agent.ts` was interpolating `lead.businessName` and `lead.city` directly into the HTML body without sanitization. A waitlist entry with HTML special characters (e.g. `<script>alert(1)</script>`) would land verbatim in the rendered email — a stored-XSS vector for webmail clients that display messages inline.

## Fix

Import `escapeHtml` from `@/lib/security/sanitize` (the same helper used by every other email template in `src/lib/email/index.ts`) and apply it to both fields before interpolation.

```diff
-  const name = lead.businessName ?? "there";
-  const cityClause = lead.city
-    ? `We're onboarding shops in ${lead.city} right now`
+  const name = escapeHtml(lead.businessName ?? "there");
+  const cityClause = lead.city
+    ? `We're onboarding shops in ${escapeHtml(lead.city)} right now`
```

## Test

Added one fixture to `acquisition-agent-gate.test.ts` that puts `<script>alert("xss")</script>` in `businessName` and ``'<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'`` in `city`, then asserts:
- raw tags are absent from the queued HTML
- escaped equivalents (`<script>`, `<img`) are present

## Acquisition Agent rollout status (2026-08-07)

- **Environment**: `DATABASE_URL` not set → `fetchUncontactedLeads` returns `[]` (no live data, validated against synthetic fixtures)
- **Scoring (37 tests, all pass)**: weights correct, threshold gate holds, clamping verified, age boundary `>` (not `>=`) confirmed
- **Dry-run gate**: load-bearing test with mocked DB — `executed: false` for all decisions, `QUEUED` empty
- **Send cap**: verified real cap enforced inside the loop (not post-hoc slice), ranking-before-sending confirmed
- **Readiness to promote dry-run → live**: scoring is sensible; one pre-send gap (this XSS fix) was the only concrete finding. After this merges: weights, gate, cap, ranking, and email safety are all verified. Admin can promote once they've reviewed a few dry-run decision logs via `/admin/agents`.

author: takaaki-s
body:
## The defect

`jin session send` could report success while sending nothing.

`Manager.SendPrompt` verifies the prompt's tail is rendered in the pane, then presses Enter. Verify proves the wrong thing. An agent holding a **completion overlay** open consumes that Enter to accept a candidate rather than submitting — so the prompt is rewritten in place, never sent, and `SendPrompt` still returns nil.

The session then stays `idle`, and that is what makes this expensive rather than merely wrong:

```
jin session send work "read @internal/agent"   # exit 0, nothing submitted
jin session wait work --until idle,permission  # returns at once — still idle
jin session result work                        # the PREVIOUS turn's output
```

Nothing in the sequence looks like a failure.

## Measurements

Claude Code 2.1.224 / tmux 3.5a, driven through a throwaway tmux server so the agent's behaviour is separated from jin's. Three runs per row.

| prompt | without Escape | with Escape |
|---|---|---|
| `list @internal/agent` | Enter eaten; input left holding `list @internal/agentdocs/` | submitted verbatim |
| `/<ambiguous-prefix>` | ran a **different** command | submitted as sent |
| `/<exact-command>` | ran as sent | ran as sent |
| `say pong only` | submitted | submitted |

The ambiguous-prefix row is a **second defect**: the nudge key walks a live completion selection, so a bare slash command can run something other than what was sent. A burst `send-keys -l` write never draws that overlay, so no capture-based check can see the state it is in — confirmed by a positive control where character-by-character typing does draw it (3/3 either way).

The overlay only survives while the caret is inside the token that opened it. `list @internal/agent and say ok` and a sentence containing a mid-text slash never open one (3/3 each), and neither do decorated forms — a backtick-wrapped path (3/3), a double-quoted one (2/2), an email address mid-sentence (1/1).

## The fix

`Agent` gains `DismissOverlayKeys(prompt string) []string` — on the interface rather than beside it, so an adapter that forgets it fails to compile.

- **claude** returns `["Escape"]` when the prompt's final token starts with `@`, or its whole text is a bare slash command.
- **codex / opencode** return nil. Their overlays are unmeasured (no API quota, no configured provider), and Escape interrupts a running turn — not something to apply on a guess. Their send path stays byte-identical.

`SendPrompt` sends the keys after verify and before Enter, then re-captures to confirm the prompt survived. A dismiss key that wiped the input would otherwise turn one silent failure into another.

That re-check needs a real settle. Sizing it by analogy with the input clear was wrong — that delay guards a step nothing checks, while this one *is* the check, and capturing too early reads a pane where the prompt is present by definition. A destructive key took **54, 83, 93, 116 and 161 ms** over five runs to reach `capture-pane`, so the wait is 250 ms.

The nudge is untouched: Escape discards the selection it moved, and removing the nudge would break the premise that `sendVerifyLookCount` scales on.

## What is not fixed

There is still no general check that Enter *submitted*. `capture-pane` returns the whole screen, so a successful submit (text leaves the input, appears in the transcript) and a stolen Enter (text stays in the input) are not separable by occurrence count. **`--wait-running` remains the only observation of a submission**, and the docs now say so throughout.

## Docs

The overclaim was on ten surfaces. The contract now reads one way only: a send that returns nil delivered keystrokes and pressed Enter — it does not mean a turn began.

The guidance that callers "can drop the flag entirely" was exactly backwards and is reversed. Pipeline examples in both READMEs and the agent-facing docs now pass `--wait-running`, with the wait-returns-immediately trap spelled out. The exit-code tables in both READMEs are synced with `internal/exitcode`, closing drift left from an earlier pass.

## Verification

23/23 checks pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. `make fmt` clean, `make lint` 0 issues, `make test` green, `make test-race` 0 data races — CI toolchain (Go 1.26.5, golangci-lint v2.12.2).

Real-machine, isolated environment, driving production `jin`:

| case | result | n |
|---|---|---|
| `list @internal/agent` | `status=thinking`, committed verbatim, no residue | 3/3 |
| `/<exact-command>` | runs as sent | 3/3 |
| `/<ambiguous-prefix>` | `Unknown command` — the honest answer for what was sent | 3/3 |
| 16 KB prompt ending in `@internal/agent` | submitted, no rewrite | 3/3 |
| `say pong only` | unchanged | 3/3 |

**13 mutations, all killed** via `go test -overlay`. Eight of them came from review and none overlapped the first pass — that pass only removed functionality, while these weaken a predicate or cut a wiring, which is what refactors actually do. One the reviewer judged untestable (deleting the settle) is killed by recording call timestamps, the same way the existing chunk-interval test works.

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Vulnerability:** Several API endpoints in `backend/main.py` were returning raw exception strings (`str(e)`) inside the JSON error responses sent to clients. 
**Impact:** Exposing raw exceptions can leak sensitive internal information, such as server file paths, dependency versions, or database configuration details, which attackers can use to map the backend architecture.
**Fix:** Modified the `except` blocks across 13 endpoints. Now, the full exception is logged securely on the backend using `logger.error()`, while the client receives a safe, generic error message string (e.g., `"Failed to read session telemetry"` instead of `"Failed to read session telemetry: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/app/backend/data/sessions/123.json'"`).
**Verification:** Ran the backend test suite (`pytest`) and frontend test suite (`vitest`) to ensure normal application behavior remains unbroken. Requested a code review which passed with no regressions found. Added learning to Sentinel's journal.

author: sdelmas
body:
## Summary

`tools/check_task_criteria_commands.py` (added in #350) had no CI lane that covers the PR shape it exists to protect.

It was enforced by two things, and each misses that shape:

- **pre-commit** — CI never runs `pre-commit`.
- **`tests/test_task_criteria_lint.py::test_live_task_tree_is_clean`** — a task-text-only PR selects the `lightweight readiness` lane, which skips `test heavy`, `test light`, `quick test`, and `coverage`. Observed directly on #349's job list.

Net: a PR changing nothing but `.trellis/tasks/**/*.md` could merge with an acceptance criterion that does not run as written.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add the guard to the `Run lightweight repository guards` step of the `classify changes` job. That step runs before lane selection, so the guard gates every lane rather than only the lightweight one. Input comes from `git ls-files '.trellis/tasks/*.md' '.trellis/tasks/**/*.md'`, so it scans the whole tracked task tree, not just the diff (a criterion can go stale without being touched). The invocation is skipped when the glob matches nothing.
- `tools/check_ci_review_contract.py` — pin the new step in the fast-CI guard list, matching the four guards already there. This is the lockstep site that keeps the step from being silently dropped.
- `tests/test_ci_review_contract.py` — add the command to the minimal synthetic workflow fixture and to the `test_fast_ci_guards_are_contract_pinned` parametrization, so removing the step fails a test.

author: thiago-as
body:
## Context

Middleware acting on behalf of users (MCP servers, AI agents, internal developer portals, API gateways) currently has to authenticate using a shared machine identity. This loses user attribution in the audit log and grants every user the full set of permissions assigned to that shared identity.

This change adds support for the RFC 8693 Token Exchange grant to the existing OAuth token endpoint. Trusted middleware can present a user's token issued by the organization's OIDC identity provider and receive a short-lived Infisical access token for that same user. The issued token carries the user's actual permissions and is fully attributed to them in the audit log. No refresh token is issued, and delegated tokens cannot access account self-management endpoints.

OAuth applications now explicitly declare their supported grant types. Existing applications and API clients that do not specify any grant types continue using the authorization code flow by default, so this change is fully backward compatible.

Token Exchange applications introduce one additional configuration field: the audience that the organization's identity provider issues for that middleware. This prevents tokens minted for unrelated applications from being exchanged.

The trust anchor is the organization's OIDC SSO configuration rather than per-application issuer settings. As a result, enabling Token Exchange, updating its audience, or rotating a Token Exchange application's client secret all require SSO edit permissions. Deleting a client, rotating its secret, or removing the Token Exchange grant immediately revokes any delegated tokens it has previously issued.

## Screenshots

## Steps to verify the change

1. In the UI, create an OAuth application with the **Token Exchange** flow. Verify that the **Audience** field is required and that the redirect URI fields are hidden.
2. Verify that the SSO page displays the "Applications depend on this issuer" callout once a Token Exchange application exists.
3. Verify that successful exchanges appear in the organization audit log, attributed to the end user, with the acting application included in the metadata.
4. Run the end-to-end flow below.

### Testing end to end locally

A complete walkthrough is available in `sso.md` under **Testing OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693)**. The abbreviated flow is:

```bash
make up-dev-oidc     # Starts the default stack plus Keycloak with the seeded Infisical realm
make seed-dev-oidc   # Creates the oidc org, admin@oidc.com / password123!, verified domain, and active OIDC configuration
```

The seeded realm also includes a second client, `infisical-mcp`, which represents the middleware.

Sign in to http://localhost:8080/ as `admin@oidc.com`, navigate to **Organization Settings → OAuth Applications**, create an application using the **Token Exchange** flow, set the audience to `infisical-mcp`, and copy the generated client credentials.

Then run:

```bash
CLIENT_ID="<paste>"
CLIENT_SECRET="<paste>"

SUBJECT_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST \
  http://localhost:8088/realms/infisical/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -d grant_type=password -d scope=openid \
  -d client_id=infisical-mcp -d client_secret=infisical-mcp-client-secret \
  -d username=admin@oidc.com -d password='password123!' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id_token"])')

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/oauth/token \
  -u "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange \
  -d subject_token="$SUBJECT_TOKEN" \
  -d subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token \
  | python3 -m json.tool
```

Use the `id_token`, not the access token. The seeded Keycloak realm does not include an audience mapper, so its access tokens do not contain an `aud` claim.

Finally, validate the issued token:

* `GET /api/v1/oauth/validate` returns `200`.
* `GET /api/v1/user/me/totp` returns `403`, confirming delegated tokens cannot access account management endpoints.
* Reading a secret in the `oidc` organization succeeds.

`sso.md` also documents the recommended negative test cases, including cross-application replay, invalid signatures, supplying a `scope`, SSO disabled, MFA required, unregistered grants, and the alias requirement for users who have never signed in through SSO.

## Type

- [ ] Fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Improvement
- [ ] Breaking
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Chore

## Checklist

- [ ] Title follows the [conventional commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary) format: `type(scope): short description` (scope is optional, e.g., `fix: prevent crash on sync` or `fix(api): handle null response`).

author: cerredz
body:
Adds three cookbook notebooks — **RLM**, **RL environment generator**, and **graph engineering** — the first examples built on the SDK's `vidbyte.harnesses.Harness` envelope. Each one ends by exporting a `TrajectoryRecord`: task, full multi-agent trajectory, resolved config, and a scalar reward, as one JSONL line.

Full design doc (including a 40-item requirement list, alternatives considered, and eleven recorded deviations) is committed as the first commit: [`docs/design/harness-examples.md`](docs/design/harness-examples.md).

## The three examples

| Notebook | Rebuilds | Native SDK surface it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk/rlm` | **Recursive Language Model** — a 400k-char corpus lives as `ctx` in a persistent REPL; the root agent measures, slices, and calls `llm()`/`rlm()` from inside a single tool call | `Harness`, `self.session()` capture, async `@tool`, `UsageRollup` cost accounting |
| `sdk/rl-env-generator` | A **diversified taskset generator** whose verifiers are proven to discriminate before acceptance | `StateGraph` guards + semantic rejection codes, `vidbyte.evals` graders as verifiers, `output_schema` |
| `sdk/graph-engineering` | **AlphaCodium flow engineering** as a validated graph — code, not the prompt, owns stage progression | `StateGraph` + `SchemaValidator`, `StagePolicy`/`RetryPolicy`, `StateMachineResult` as evidence |

Each shows the naive approach failing first (truncated context loses the fact; one call for "50 diverse tasks" mode-collapses; one-shot codegen passes the visible example and fails a hidden edge case), then the architecture fixing it, and each of sections 1–6 ends with a reflection question.

## ⚠️ Requires a git-pinned SDK, not PyPI

Published `vidbyte-sdk` 0.1.0 has **no `vidbyte/workflows` at all** and a 2-module `vidbyte/harnesses` (vs 13 on main). `workflows` landed in `ef36015` and the harness contract in `ff6dfd6`, both after 0.1.0 was cut, and `version` is still `0.1.0` so the release can't be refreshed without a bump. All three notebooks install `git+https://github.com/cerredz/Vidbyte-SDK.git@f5cb7f4` and assert the imports. **Swap for a version pin once the SDK cuts a release.**

## Verification

**33 checks pass with no API key**, via `scripts/test_{rlm,env_generator,graph_engineering}.py`. Each script has two layers: stdlib-only logic, plus — when `vidbyte.workflows` is importable — compiling the notebook's *real* `StateGraph` and driving every terminal path with fake agents and graders.

**Not done: a live provider run.** No API key exists in the implementation environment. That remains the one outstanding gate before this leaves draft (§14.11).

## Defects found and fixed during review

- **RLM's cost table reported only the root agent**, omitting every leaf call — flattering the exact comparison the notebook exists to make honestly.
- **The env generator's reward divided by `len(cells) + len(rejections)`** — neither attempts nor cells.
- **An unguarded `design_tests` cycle** looped to `TransitionLimitError`.
- **The reserved-name guard was porous** — six binding forms clobbered the corpus, including `except E as ctx`, which also *deletes* the name.
- **Neither graph was total** — a raising validator produced an unroutable `validation_error` that buried the original exception.
- **`multiprocessing` → `subprocess`** — spawn on Windows/macOS re-imports `__main__`, so a target defined in a notebook cell is unreachable.
- **graph-engineering sections ran 1, 3, 2, 4…**, violating the authoring contract.

Two SDK contracts had to be read out of `machine.py` and are now taught in the notebooks: a rejected guard redirects from the *same source stage* keyed on its own code, and validator rejections roll candidate state back — so retry counters must live in the non-transactional run ledger.

## Pre-existing defect, not fixed here

`droid`, `deep-research`, `sierra-support`, and `self-refine` pass middleware kwargs that **do not exist** — `CostBudgetMiddleware(max_cost_usd=)`, `ModelRetryMiddleware(max_retries=)`, `LoopDetectionMiddleware(max_repeats=)`, `RuntimeLimitMiddleware(max_iterations=)`. Those cells raise `TypeError`. The authoring skill documented the wrong names, which is how it spread; this PR corrects the skill and uses verified signatures. **Fixing those four notebooks is a follow-up PR.**

author: edicius2002
body:
Closes #40. **Stacked on #41** — branched from `feat/investing-watchlist`, so merge that first.

Polling has a floor no cadence can go under: the freshest a price can be is one interval old, which overnight was a minute. This removes the floor and most of the requests at the same time.

## What the legacy did, and what it missed

`ediciuscorp` polled the watchlist every **1 second** (`liveTickMs: 1_000`), the tape every 3s, behind a 900ms floor and a local cache with a 0.12s TTL. It streamed **crypto** over `wss://stream.binance.com` — the half it got right — and hammered Yahoo for everything else. It never found Yahoo's socket.

## The finding that shaped the slice

Probed live in pre-market against the ten real watchlist symbols plus two pairs:

```
33 messages · 1.02 msg/s · 9 of 12 symbols
no data at all: SCHD, GLDM, PFE
```

The socket carries **trades, not a heartbeat**. A symbol that does not trade sends nothing, and nothing is indistinguishable from a dead connection. It also never sends a previous close, a name or a currency — the fields a row and its percentage are built from.

**So the sweep is load-bearing, not a fallback.** It covers what never trades, supplies what a tick omits, and its returning is what proves the socket is alive. Calling it a fallback would invite someone to delete it (decision 8.18).

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular hours | 1,560 requests/day, 15s stale | ~390, **sub-second** |
| Extended | 570 per night, 60s stale | ~114, **sub-second** |
| Closed | 32 | 32, socket silent |

The sweep slows **only while the stream is live**. A dead socket puts the page straight back on the rate it had before any of this existed.

## Shape

One socket per provider in the API, relayed to the browser by **SSE**. Decision 8.3 keeps provider names out of the client, and a socket opened in the browser would put `streamer.finance.yahoo.com` in it. One connection serves every tab — the hub refcounts symbols, so two tabs on the same watchlist cost one subscription. SSE rather than a socket because only one direction carries anything and an `EventSource` reconnects by itself.

Crypto streams from **Binance**, which is official and documented, unlike everything else in this phase.

## Protobuf by hand

Yahoo's frames are base64 protobuf with no published schema. A runtime plus a generated `.proto` would be a dependency, a build step and a file to keep in sync with an endpoint that can change without notice — for one message shape the wire format makes readable in fifty lines.

Reading it directly is also what caught the bug: **field 3 is a `sint64`**, so taken as a plain varint the timestamp comes out doubled. A live tick was landing in the year **2083** until it was zigzag-decoded.

## Coalesced twice

Binance's rolling ticker sends every second whether or not anything traded, so most of what arrives overnight is the price already on screen. Dropping unmoved readings **halved** the traffic, measured over the same 40s window. A change that is not the price — the bell moving a symbol from `PRE` to `REGULAR` — still gets through.

The browser then batches a frame's worth into one render. The queue is keyed by symbol rather than appended to: a background tab runs no animation frames, and a list would grow unbounded all night.

## The change stays one question

A tick carries its own percentage, and taking it would quietly answer a different question during extended hours than decision 8.16 gave the swept one. So the change is recomputed from the previous close whichever path the price arrived by, and the two cannot disagree on screen.

## Verified live

- Both providers in one stream: Yahoo (`TSLA`, `PRE`) and Binance (`BTCUSDT`, `ETHUSDT`)
- Timestamps land in 2026 after the zigzag fix, in 2083 before it
- On the page: **NVDA 218.99 → 219.10 with zero quote requests in 44 seconds**

## Gates

`typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, **364 web tests** and **89 API tests** — all green. `websockets` is now pinned explicitly: it arrived with `uvicorn[standard]`, and a transitive dependency you import by name is one an upgrade can remove.

author: sapphireclinicseast
body:
Ending Cash read **−₱7,685,084.96** for 2026 against a real bank position of ~₱547k, marching further negative every month. `cfTies` was `true` throughout — the statement was internally consistent and confidently wrong.

Three faults, all in the ledger engine.

### 1. ₱8.09M of bank payments were credited to the petty cash float
§5 credited the cash side of **every** non-`RECURRING` `PettyCashEntry` to the branch's "<PREFIX> Petty Cash on Hand". That table also holds RFPs and imported QuickBooks expenses (`recordType='ONE_TIME'`), which are settled from a **bank account** — or offset against an advance.

| 2026 (non-cancelled, non-RECURRING) | amount |
|---|---:|
| `ONE_TIME` (RFPs + QB imports) | **₱8,088,195.88** |
| `PETTY_CASH` (genuine vouchers) | ₱160,668.82 |

Genuine vouchers match the ₱247k replenished. The ₱8.09M did not, and sank 11300/11310/11312/11314 to −₱8.2M. Their *journal* balances are ~0 — the entire deficit was this synthesis, one-sided. A float is not a bank account, so no statement could ever true it back, and the fiction flowed straight into Ending Cash.

Payments now credit the account named in `paymentBankAccount`, resolved **by number** — never through `parseAccountKey`, which invents a virtual `EXPENSE` account for anything unrecognized and would book the payment a second time as cost. Falls back to the branch's default bank.

### 2. Two bank anchors that disagreed
§8 trued the balance sheet month by month and deliberately let ledger movement through after an account's last statement line. A separate `bankAnchor` in the cash-flow block held that balance flat. So the sheet said one thing and the cash flow another. `bankAnchor` is deleted — the cash flow now reads `cashRows`, the balance sheet's own cash line, so **Ending Cash *is* balance-sheet cash** rather than a second opinion about it.

### 3. The opening was never trued
Every `BeginningBalance` is dated 2026-01-01 while statements run from 2024, so the year opened on a figure the bank had already disagreed with — Beginning and Ending rested on different sources.

### Also
- §8 now **holds** an account at the bank's last known balance after its final statement instead of letting unconfirmed entries drift it (₱977k had accumulated on `004680350310` against a bank reading ₱0.00).
- Un-banked cash floats are **floored at zero**: a physical float cannot hold less than nothing, and a negative one is spending whose funding is missing from the ledger, not negative cash.
- Every correction lands on the visible **3990** line, and whatever the activity sections still cannot explain is named on its own **"Uncategorized bank movement"** row rather than quietly breaking the tie. Both shrink as Bank Rec lines are categorized.

### Verified against production data (2026)
| | |
|---|---:|
| Beginning Cash | ₱1,867,568.89 |
| Ending Cash | ₱547,299.82 |
| Balance-sheet cash | ₱547,299.82 |
| `cfTies` / `aEqualsLE` | true / true, A−L−E diff 0 |

Every bank account equals its statement to the centavo (6007 ₱183,596.83 · 7208 ₱98,919.01 · 7259 ₱41,575.17 · 7267 ₱42,126.34 · 2984 ₱58,963.08 · 3345 ₱20,264.99 · 3358 ₱51,367.13 · 0310 ₱0.00 · 0329 ₱10,002.15 · 1174 ₱10,003.60). Local `npm run build` passes: compiled, type-checked, 258/258 pages.

Target shape taken from `20260513_SCEI_Combined_Final_v11_carlo.xlsx` tab "OVERALL BS & CF", where Ending Cash *is* the Balance Sheet cash line.

### Known, not addressed here
- The CNY account `051180000197` is still summed **raw** into a peso total (₱481.52 is yuan). Small today, wrong in principle; needs an FX policy — the same one that makes `fund-transfer-je.ts` skip cross-currency transfers.
- The CEO petty-cash block still credits the float for its one ₱25,000 `ONE_TIME` row, left alone to keep this change tight.

body: ## Starter is on the pricing page The live Stripe price `price_1U1eunEdFrTOBYBsoaanDEzQ` ($49/month) was provisioned but no page described it — the tier was purchasable and invisible. Now it sits between Watch and Chase. **The copy claims only what the code enforces.** Starter and Chase run the identical chase workflow — drafted nudges, approve/edit/snooze/reject, verified sends — because the execution gate checks `plan != "free"` and nothing finer (`internal/revenue/entitlements.go`). The two differences that are actually implemented are the monthly usage allowance (200k credits vs 2M) and premium connectors, so those are what the tiers are described by. Inventing feature gaps the gate doesn't implement would make the page a promise the server doesn't keep. ## A live defect this surfaced `planRank` in the connector pre-consent hook was `{free:0, starter:1, pro:2}`. **`intelligence` was never added**, and a missing key resolves to `0` — so the $249 plan ranked as free, below Starter, and its subscribers were told *"Upgrade to pro to connect X"*. ``` plan=free rank=0 can connect a pro-gated connector: False plan=starter rank=1 → False plan=pro rank=2 → True plan=intelligence rank=0 → False ← the bug ``` Fixed, with a test that fails when a sellable plan is missing from the map rather than silently denying it. The same omission was in the published API description's plan enums, so `openapi.json` and the generated TS client are regenerated. ## Pattern worth noting This is the **fourth** instance of one shape in this workstream: a new tier added to a validator but not to an ordinal map keyed by it — the desktop `AUTHORITY` ladder, two strict `z.enum`s, and now `planRank`. Every one denies or misranks silently rather than failing. Might be worth a lint or a shared source of truth. ## Verification `go build`, `go vet`, full Go suite, and `make generate` idempotent. `marketing-data.ts` typechecks clean (the `MarketingPage | undefined` errors in `[...slug]/page.tsx` are pre-existing and unrelated). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01HKFLPzxp8aqHLZE2V8qiiX --- Need help on this PR? body:
## Что это

`POST /api/download` — HTTP-ручка поверх yt-dlp, чтобы качать видео из Apple Shortcuts: делишься ссылкой через Share Sheet, шорткат дёргает ручку и кладёт готовый файл в Фотоплёнку.

```bash
curl -X POST https://<host>/api/download \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://www.tiktok.com/@user/video/123"}' \
  -o video.mp4
```

Ручка синхронная: ни очередей, ни хранилища, ни состояния. Сценарий — короткие ролики (Reels, TikTok, Shorts), поэтому длинные видео отсекаются лимитами, а не переводом на асинхронные job'ы.

Инструкция по настройке шортката — в README.

## Как устроено

Запрос → проверка токена → семафор (2 параллельных) → валидация URL → свой временный каталог → yt-dlp → ffprobe → ffmpeg (только если нужен) → файл в теле ответа → `os.RemoveAll`.

Транскод пропускается, когда файл уже mp4/H.264/AAC: Reels и TikTok почти всегда такие, а перекодирование 1080p стоит десятков секунд ожидания с телефоном в руке.

| Статус | Когда |
|---|---|
| 400 | тело не парсится, не `https`, приватный/loopback хост |
| 401 | нет токена или не совпал |
| 405 | метод не POST |
| 413 | больше 500 МБ или длиннее 15 минут |
| 429 | заняты оба слота |
| 500 | локальная файловая ошибка |
| 502 | yt-dlp или ffmpeg упали |
| 504 | не уложились в 5 минут |

Ручка не регистрируется, если `API_TOKEN` пуст — сервис пишет WARN и работает дальше. В отличие от метрик, где пустые креды это `Fatal`: выкатка без новой переменной не должна ронять бота.

## Попутно починена гонка

`video_manager` держал один `*ytdlp.Command` на всех и писал в рабочий каталог по общему шаблону имени, а бот гоняет до 5 загрузок параллельно — два одинаковых URL одновременно спотыкались о `NoOverwrites`. Теперь команда строится на вызов, каталог свой на запрос, очистка одна вместо двух `DeleteVideo`.

## Что нужно сделать руками

**Создать секрет `API_TOKEN`** в Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Без него деплой выкатит сервис с выключенной ручкой (бот при этом работает).

## Изменения поведения бота

Бот теперь наследует лимиты 500 МБ / 15 минут — общий код с API. Задокументировано в README и CLAUDE.md. Отдельный 10-минутный бюджет на транскод сохранён.

## Проверки

- `go test ./...` — зелёные, включая `-race`; в репозитории это первые тесты, и CI их теперь гоняет (раньше только линтеры)
- `gofmt -l .`, `golangci-lint run` — чисто
- Живой прогон ручки: `200` с играбельным mp4 (h264+aac), `401`, `400`, временные каталоги не копятся
- `ffprobe` в alpine-образе подтверждён (`video_manager.New` теперь падает при старте без него)

Не проверено: полный `docker compose up --build` — упирается в сетевое ограничение песочницы на `go mod download`, к изменениям отношения не имеет.

## Известное

`README.md` здесь создан с нуля, потому что в `main` его нет — он живёт в невлитой ветке `docs/add-readme`. При слиянии обеих будет конфликт по файлу.

Спека и план: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-ytdlp-http-api-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-05-ytdlp-http-api.md`.

author: h0tp-ftw
body:
This pull request addresses an issue where Pokémon natures would reset to the default "serious" nature.

### Bug Root Cause
When Pokémon data is retrieved from the database, it is often unpacked onto a default `PokemonObject` instance via `update_stats(**kwargs)`. Previously, `update_stats` guarded its dynamic attribute assignment using `if hasattr(self, key)`. 
If a `PokemonObject` was created without explicitly defining certain attributes in its constructor (e.g., when falling back to `MAIN_POKEMON_DEFAULT`, which did not contain a `nature` key), those attributes were completely dropped during `update_stats` because `hasattr` returned False. Consequently, the Pokémon would fall back to its internal class default (a "serious" nature) instead of properly inheriting its deserialized database state.

### Fix
*   Removed the `if hasattr(self, key):` guard within `PokemonObject.update_stats`.
*   Directly apply `setattr(self, key, value)` for all provided kwargs (as long as they are not explicitly protected by `_READONLY_ATTRS`).

This correctly reconstructs all attributes natively defined in the database payload without unnecessarily enforcing that they already exist on the blank template instance.

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `c93c1970-4297-4949-9434-b02e8740b8d5` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/lighter-prover-challenge at `a1ebeb67de07219e27515b66cad0c8890727d071`.

Current best score: 11.0369160804975. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Fable 5

# Frontier + full L0-value caching, Poseidon2 scratch accumulation, parallel witness materialization, and chain-pipeline tuning

Agent: Cursor
Effort: thinking

## Context and goal

This submission composes the current promoted frontier (`416c535f` / landed commit `a1ebeb6`,
ranked 11.0369 TPS) with an independent set of prover-side optimizations that were developed
on the previous frontier (`d2328428` / landed commit `8ce788b`, ranked 11.0063 TPS). The goal
was to make sure the two lines of work stack: the frontier added a contiguous slice-copy fast
path for the quotient LDE gather in `vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/fri/oracle.rs`, while this
work targets the `L_0(x)` term of the vanishing polynomial, gate-constraint buffer reuse,
witness materialization, and the recursion pipeline in `bench`. The two touch adjacent but
non-overlapping code, and the measurements below confirm they compose additively.

## Base checkout

Branch created from `a1ebeb6` (the promoted frontier at submission time), with one commit
cherry-picked on top. The cherry-pick auto-merged cleanly; the only shared file is
`vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/plonk/prover.rs`, where the frontier added a test in
`quotient_layout_tests` and this work rewrites the `l_0_table_cache` module further down.

## What is included

### 1. Full `L_0(x)` value caching (`zero_poly_coset.rs`, `plonk/prover.rs`, `plonk/vanishing_poly.rs`)

The quotient pass previously cached only the denominator inverses `(n * (x - 1))^-1` of
`L_0(x) = Z_H(x) / (n * (x - 1))` and still performed one field multiplication per point per
proof. This submission caches the complete product instead:

- The process-global table (keyed by field type and `(degree_bits, quotient_degree_bits)`)
  now stores `Z_H(x) / (n * (x - 1))` directly. Hot quotient batches copy table entries with
  `extend_from_slice` instead of multiplying on every proof.
- The table itself is built with one full-domain Montgomery batch inversion
  (`batch_multiplicative_inverse`) rather than one exponentiation-based `inverse()` per point,
  so first-proof table construction is cheaper too.
- A new `eval_l_0_batch_contiguous_into` entry point serves the uncached fallback path with
  Montgomery's trick over each contiguous batch, reusing caller-owned buffers across batches.
  `eval_vanishing_poly_base_batch` asserts (debug) that quotient batches are contiguous index
  ranges, which they are by construction of the chunked iteration.

Every cached entry is bit-identical (raw `u64` comparison, not just field equality) to the
value the scalar path computes; two unit tests in `l_0_table_tests` and one in
`zero_poly_coset::tests` pin that down across several circuit shapes and batch sizes.

### 2. Poseidon2 gate scratch accumulation (`gates/gate.rs`, `gates/poseidon2.rs`)

`evaluate_gate_constraints_base_batch` allocated and zeroed a fresh
`num_constraints * batch_size` buffer for every gate of every batch. The trait now exposes
`eval_unfiltered_base_batch_accumulate_scratch`, which lets a gate materialize into a
caller-owned scratch `Vec` that persists across every quotient batch assigned to a Rayon
worker. Poseidon2 — the dominant gate in this circuit — overrides it; all other gates keep
the previous accumulate path unchanged via the default implementation.
`circuit/tests/scratch_accumulate_bench.rs` asserts the accumulated output is identical to
the allocating default and doubles as a microbenchmark.

### 3. Parallel `full_witness` materialization (`iop/witness.rs`)

The fused single-pass wire-matrix build is now parallel over 16 row chunks. Each Rayon task
owns disjoint `MaybeUninit` segments carved off the pre-sized column buffers, reads
`representative_map` sequentially within its range, and initializes every cell exactly once
before a final `set_len`. The serial reference implementation is retained alongside
(`full_witness_serial_reference`) for auditability.

### 4. Constant chain-witness template (`circuit/src/block_tx_chain_constraints.rs`, `bench/src/prover.rs`)

The verifier-data and dummy-proof witness entries are identical for every recursion step of a
chain path. They are now seeded once per path into a `PartialWitness` template
(`witness_inputs_constant`) and cloned per step (`witness_inputs_early_from_template`); a
`HashMap` clone copies buckets directly, replacing tens of thousands of re-hashed inserts of
the same values at every chain step. The map contents are identical to building from scratch
— only insertion order differs, which a `HashMap` does not observe. The original
`witness_inputs_early` remains as a thin wrapper.

### 5. Pipeline window tuning (`bench/src/prover.rs`)

- `LIGHT_TX_PROOF_WINDOW` 2 → 3: a window of 2 leaves the strictly sequential chain consumer
  starved whenever one chunk proof runs long; 3 keeps one extra producer ahead at roughly
  0.6 GB additional peak retention. A window of 4 was measured and regressed (memory
  pressure), so 3 is the measured optimum of the three.
- The heavy path now allows 2 chunk proofs in flight past step 1, giving its chain consumer
  the same one-extra-producer buffering; heavy chunks are few, so added retention is bounded
  by a single proof.

## Methodology

Local `./benchmark.sh` (public-synthetic-smoke, 500 tx) on an Apple Silicon macOS host.
Because local runs drift downward as the machine heats up (first-run-after-idle is reliably
the fastest), a simple before/after comparison is misleading. The comparison below therefore
uses interleaved A/B pairs against the frontier baseline (`a1ebeb6` built in a separate git
worktree, same toolchain), alternating within each pair, 8 pairs total, with the pair order
reversed for the last 3 pairs to cancel the within-pair thermal bias.

## Results

All 16 runs passed the trusted verifier. TPS per pair (higher is better):

| Pair | Order | Frontier `a1ebeb6` | This submission | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | base first | 11.4243 | 11.0768 | base |
| 2 | base first | 11.2964 | 11.5134 | ours |
| 3 | base first | 11.1495 | 11.2255 | ours |
| 4 | base first | 11.2937 | 11.4443 | ours |
| 5 | base first | 11.3588 | 11.4164 | ours |
| 6 | ours first | 11.6841 | 12.3187 | ours |
| 7 | ours first | 11.5079 | 11.5814 | ours |
| 8 | ours first | 11.2484 | 11.3920 | ours |

- Median (all runs): **11.4304** vs **11.3276** TPS → **+0.91%**
- Median paired difference: **+0.1098 TPS (+0.97%)**
- Sign test: 7/8 pairs won, one-sided p ≈ 0.035

The single adverse pair (pair 1) was the first pair after a cooldown, where the base ran
first on the coolest machine state and recorded its best run of the session.

## Correctness

- All 16 local proofs (plus 10 earlier runs of the same code on the previous base) were
  accepted by the protected trusted verifier, including public-output recomputation.
- `plonk::prover::quotient_layout_tests` (6 tests, including the frontier's new
  `contiguous_lde_batch_matches_indexed_gather`), `plonk::prover::l_0_table_tests` (2 tests,
  bit-identity), `zero_poly_coset::tests::contiguous_l0_batch_and_cached_table_match_scalar`,
  and `circuit/tests/scratch_accumulate_bench.rs` all pass on the merged tree.
- No constraint-system changes: circuit shapes, widths (heavy 4 / light 10), and chain ID 304
  are untouched, so proofs remain compatible with the pinned verifier data.

## Failures and course corrections along the way

- Earlier submissions of the L0 line on older bases (`ddca77a6`, `8bea083b`) were rejected at
  ~10.88–10.91 ranked because the frontier had just moved past their base; the lesson was to
  always rebase onto the latest landed

Calculators only — no investment advice or product recommendations.

Five tabs in one panel (`mountFinance`), following the app's existing patterns (`mountPercentage`'s tab structure, `mountGpa`'s editable-table + `Storage` persistence):

body:
**What changed**
Expanded the scratch file guard in `scripts/ci-script-checks.sh` to include extensions `.diff`, `.patch`, `.py`, `.js`, and `.json` for test, scratch, and scratchpad files. Also explicitly included `patch.diff` and `prs.json`.

**Why**
Agents frequently create ad-hoc scratch and trace files like `patch.diff`, `test_scratch.py`, and `prs.json` when reasoning or patching files, which often unintentionally get committed. This PR hygiene improvement ensures these artifacts are caught by the CI script checks before they pollute the mainline codebase, directly aligning with `TEST_PLAN.md` instructions.

**WorkFingerprint**
