author: zeroliu
body:
Relates to Brevilabs/obsidian-copilot-private#219

## Why

Open Settings → Agent → Codex today and the model list is 33 rows: `GPT-5.6-Sol (low)`, `GPT-5.6-Sol (medium)`, `GPT-5.6-Sol (high)`, `GPT-5.6-Sol (xhigh)`, `GPT-5.6-Sol (max)`, `GPT-5.6-Sol (ultra)`, then the same spread for Terra, Luna, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-Mini and Codex-Spark. Each carries its own enable toggle, so a user can enable GPT-5.6-Sol at `high` and not at `max` — a distinction that means nothing. The chat model picker shows the same 33 rows and never offers an effort dropdown.

The cause is a wire format Copilot got wrong. codex-acp addresses a model as `<base>[<effort>]` — `gpt-5.6-sol[ultra]` — and says so itself when given anything else:

```
Unsupported format of modelId: gpt-5.4. Expected: modelId[effort].
```

Copilot decoded `<base>/<effort>` and gated the trailing segment against a hardcoded `minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh` set. Splitting `gpt-5.6-sol[ultra]` on `/` yields one segment, so that set was never consulted and every advertised id decoded as an effort-less base model. Widening the set to add `max` and `ultra` would have changed nothing.

Everything downstream already collapses correctly — it was being fed 33 distinct "models."

## What

Codex models collapse to one row per base model, in both the settings list and the chat picker, with effort chosen from a sibling dropdown.

> **Before:** Settings → Agent → Codex lists 33 rows; picking `GPT-5.6-Sol (max)` in chat is picking a different model from `GPT-5.6-Sol (low)`, and there is no effort control.
>
> **After:** the same list shows 7 rows — one per base model. Selecting `GPT-5.6-Sol` in chat offers `low · medium · high · xhigh · max · ultra`; selecting `GPT-5.5` offers `low · medium · high · xhigh`.

Effort levels now come only from what the installed CLI advertises, per model:

| Model | Effort levels offered |
| --- | --- |
| GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5.6-Terra | low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra |
| GPT-5.6-Luna | low, medium, high, xhigh, max |
| GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-Mini, GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark | low, medium, high, xhigh |

Copilot no longer keeps a list of effort names, so a codex-acp release that introduces another level collapses correctly with no plugin change.

On upgrade, a settings migration folds each user's per-effort rows into one row per base model. A base model stays enabled if any of its effort variants was, and a saved default of `gpt-5.6-sol[xhigh]` becomes `gpt-5.6-sol` at `xhigh`. No model disappears from the picker.

## Non goal

- Codex keeps switching models through `session/set_model` with the bracketed id. It also advertises a `category:"model"` config option and a `reasoning_effort` selector; routing through those would cost a round-trip per model per probe for information the bracketed catalog already carries in full.
- The blurb on a collapsed row still comes from its first effort variant, so `GPT-5.6-Sol` reads "…Fast responses with lighter reasoning" until the next PR in this stack.
- opencode's own hardcoded effort list is untouched here.
- `fast-mode` and `collaboration_mode`, which codex-acp also advertises, stay unread.

## Screenshot

Not captured — the affected surfaces are Obsidian panes (Settings → Agent → Codex and the chat model picker) and this environment cannot drive the Obsidian UI to load the branch build.

In place of a rendered capture, the live catalog from `codex-acp@1.1.10` was replayed through the branch's real `wire.decode` and `translateBackendState`, which produce exactly what those panes render:

```
reported wire ids: 33   →   collapsed rows: 7
gpt-5.6-sol         | GPT-5.6-Sol         | [low,medium,high,xhigh,max,ultra]
gpt-5.6-terra       | GPT-5.6-Terra       | [low,medium,high,xhigh,max,ultra]
gpt-5.6-luna        | GPT-5.6-Luna        | [low,medium,high,xhigh,max]
gpt-5.5             | GPT-5.5             | [low,medium,high,xhigh]
gpt-5.4             | GPT-5.4             | [low,medium,high,xhigh]
gpt-5.4-mini        | GPT-5.4-Mini        | [low,medium,high,xhigh]
gpt-5.3-codex-spark | GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark | [low,medium,high,xhigh]
current: { baseModelId: "gpt-5.6-sol", effort: "high" }
```

Verification step 2 reaches the real panes.

## Risk

**High**

| Criterion | Status | Reason |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| No behavior change, or a cosmetic/copy/docs/config change visible where it renders, or deterministic tests cover the changed behavior | ✅ | `codexModelId.test.ts` covers parse/format including unseen effort tokens and malformed brackets; `descriptor.test.ts` collapses a transcribed live catalog to 7 entries with per-model effort sets; `codexModelIdMigration.test.ts` covers the collapse, the enabled set, the sticky default and idempotency |
| A defect would fail CI or be obvious on first use | ✅ | A wrong split changes the settings row count on the first probe; the collapse tests run in CI |
| A revert fully restores prior state, including persisted data | ❌ | The migration rewrites `configuredModels[].info.id` in place and stamps `settingsVersion: 9`. Reverting the code leaves base-form rows that the old codec's next probe would prune, dropping the user's enabled set |
| No auth, permissions, secrets, or input-handling surface changes | ✅ | Model id parsing only |
| No public API, plugin API, message, or on-disk contract changes | ❌ | The persisted settings schema changes: codex `ConfiguredModel.info.id`, `backends.codex.enabledModels`, and `agentMode.backends.codex.defaultModel` are rewritten under `settingsVersion` 9 |
| No core-path concurrency, async-lifecycle, or state-machine changes | ✅ | The codec is pure and the migration is synchronous, running before agent discovery is wired |
| No hot-path behavior lacks deterministic coverage | ✅ | Both decode branches, both encode branches, and the effort-snap in `applySelection` are covered |
| No new dependency | ✅ | Dependency manifests are unchanged |
| Human-only behavior stays in one feature area and surfaces quickly | ✅ | Confined to Agent Mode's Codex backend; a wrong result appears on the first settings open or model switch |

Review: inspect `src/settings/migrations/codexModelIdMigration.ts` — `planCodexModelIdCollapse` and `stripEffortLabel` — line by line against a real pre-upgrade `data.json`, since it is the only irreversible write here; then `src/agentMode/backends/codex/codexModelId.ts` (`CODEX_WIRE_ID`, `parseCodexModelId`) and `src/agentMode/backends/codex/descriptor.ts` (`codexWire`, `applySelection`, `firstAdvertisedEffort`). Run Verification steps 1–4, including step 4's upgrade-from-backup path.

## Verification

Requires `codex-acp` installed and logged in, on a vault whose Codex models were already enrolled by a previous Copilot version.

1. Copy the vault's `.obsidian/plugins/copilot/data.json` somewhere safe, and note which Codex models are enabled and which are not.
2. Build and load this branch, then open Settings → Agent → Codex. The list shows one row per base model — 7 with a current codex-acp — rather than one row per model-and-effort. Every base model you had enabled is still enabled; every one you had disabled is still disabled.
3. Open a Codex chat and the model picker. Select `GPT-5.6-Sol`: the effort dropdown offers `low` through `ultra`. Select `GPT-5.5`: it offers `low` through `xhigh`, with no `max` or `ultra`. Choose `ultra` on Sol and send a message — the turn runs rather than erroring.
4. Quit Obsidian, restore the backup `data.json`, delete its `"settingsVersion"` line, and relaunch. The list again shows one row per base model with the same enabled set — confirming the migration replays from a genuine pre-upgrade state, not just from already-migrated settings.
5. Reopen the picker and confirm the effort you chose in step 3 is still selected.

## Note

The issue proposed adding `max` and `ultra` to `KNOWN_CODEX_EFFORTS`. That would not have worked: with the delimiter wrong, that set never matched any advertised id. It is deleted here rather than

body:
## What this adds

Chapter three of the Sveltos fleet brief: an environment rollout with a per-cluster matrix in the Kubara matrix style. Builds on #1298 (its commit is included here so the npm catalog and verify chain stay consistent; absorb that PR first and this one rebases clean).

**The example** (`examples/sveltos/env-rollout/`): three per-environment `ClusterProfile`s (pilot, staging, prod) built from one shared baseline values document so the only reviewed difference is the selector; a fleet design with one management cluster and four workload clusters (pilot, staging, prod-a, prod-b); and a machine-readable change candidate that raises `backgroundController.replicas` from 1 to 2 in Kyverno 3.8.1. Version bumps stay reserved for the CVE chapter.

**The matrix** (`data/sveltos-env-rollout/`): sixteen rows across four checkpoints (baseline plus one per wave), emitted as csv, markdown, and self-contained colored HTML. Expected revisions are content hashes computed from the reviewed files. Every observed cell is empty and every row carries `awaiting-live-run` with the blocker, because no live run has been recorded: the approval boundary is still broken by confighubai/confighub#4975. Nothing is claimed that a receipt does not back.

**The generator** (`scripts/generate-sveltos-env-rollout.mjs`): `--generate`, `--verify` (byte-compare, in the repository verify chain), and `--self-test` (deterministic double compile, eight tamper refusals covering baseline drift, wave order, prod group size, selector scope, chart pins, and values-path integrity, plus a self-contained-HTML contract).

## Wiring

- npm lanes `sveltos-env-rollout:generate|verify|self-test`; verify chain extended beside the other sveltos lanes.
- Chapter one's README links onward to chapter three, which pulls both new pages into the rendered site (903 doc pages, generated with the pinned timestamp).
- `data/README.md`, `data/csv-index.csv`, and the npm script catalog regenerated.

## What comes next

The live proof reuses the two-wave runner's discipline once #4975 is fixed: one approval bracket per environment revision, portable OCI digests, Sveltos convergence per environment group, a zero-drift audit, and the observed matrix columns filled from the receipt. Fleet proofs run serially against the organization.

## Verified

All sveltos lanes (`--verify` and `--self-test` for the example, the delivery proof, and the rollout), npm catalog, data index, site generate and UX contract, no-personal-names, knowledge layer, and chart-claim-integrity pass. The pre-existing doc-map, lane-test CSV, and doc-freshness failures on main reproduce on a clean tree and are untouched.

author: esbenwiberg
body:
## Why

## Task

Fix sandbox completion so final change statistics, no-change classification, validation entry, and
cleanup decisions are derived from the verified materialized checkpoint rather than cached pod
counters. A non-empty canonical delta must enter blocking validation, while only a strictly proven
empty delta may use the no-change completion path; unavailable proof must fail closed and retain
recoverable state.

## Why

On 2026-08-06, \`plastic-duck\`, \`racial-vulture\`, and \`semantic-gamefowl\` all committed real work,
produced non-empty pre-submit diffs, and successfully materialized verified sandbox checkpoints,
but immediately completed as \`No files changed\`. Their cached counters remained zero, daemon
validation never ran, and readiness became risky; the preserved worktrees could later create PRs
#46, #50, and #51, proving preservation but not safe validation or managed merge eligibility.

The root cause is the \`pod.executionTarget !== 'sandbox'\` guard around both auto-commit and diff
statistics in \`pod-manager.ts\`. Skipping sandbox auto-commit is intentional because the checkpoint
is authoritative; skipping final change classification is not. The following no-change predicate
then trusts the stale creation-time \`filesChanged === 0\` value.

The full diagnosis and incident evidence are in
\`investigations/sandbox-checkpoint-false-no-changes/bug.md\`.

## Touches

- \`packages/daemon/src/pods/pod-manager.ts\` — completion ordering, strict final change decision,
  stats persistence, validation/no-op choice, recovery parking, and bounded structured telemetry.
- \`packages/daemon/src/pods/pod-manager.test.ts\` — orchestration matrix, base/fork behavior,
  unavailable-proof behavior, telemetry, local regression, and affected PR recovery.
- \`packages/daemon/src/interfaces/worktree-manager.ts\` — only if a strict finalization-specific
  diff/stat contract is needed instead of a pod-manager-local classifier.
- \`packages/daemon/src/worktrees/local-worktree-manager.ts\` and its test — strict canonical
  changed/unchanged/unavailable behavior without changing legacy fail-soft callers.
- \`packages/daemon/src/worktrees/sandbox-workspace-checkpoint.test.ts\` — real-Git snapshot matrix
  for committed, uncommitted, mixed, empty, and net-zero states.
- \`packages/daemon/src/test-utils/mock-helpers.ts\` — shared mock support for any new injectable
  strict classifier method.

## Does not touch

- \`packages/shared/src/types/pod.ts\` — no new pod status or persisted profile/pod field is required.
- \`packages/daemon/src/pods/state-machine.ts\` — preserve existing lifecycle states and transitions.
- \`packages/daemon/src/db/migrations/\` — the minimal durable fix needs no schema migration.
- \`packages/desktop/\` and \`packages/mobile-web/\` — no UI redesign is part of this repair.

Do not automatically rewrite historical terminal rows or introduce a broad recovery workflow in
this task.

## Constraints

- The sandbox checkpoint remains source-delivery authority. Preserve capture, transfer,
  verification, lineage, promotion, and materialization before diff, validation, PR, delivery, or
  cleanup decisions. Never restore recursive \`/workspace\` mirroring for sandboxes.
- Keep sandbox auto-commit disabled. The checkpoint commit already captures committed and
  remaining working-tree bytes through its private index.
- Use the same canonical deliverable semantics and exclusions as diff/validation. Working-tree
  cleanliness, commit count, pre-submit review counts, or cached pod counters are not proof.
- Scope the pod's work from persisted \`startCommitSha\`; keep the configured base branch as the PR
  target. Preserve linked/fork behavior when inherited branch changes still require validation.
- The current \`getDiffStats\` catches Git/base failures and returns zeros. Do not use a fail-soft
  zero as no-change authority. Finalization needs a strict \`changed \| unchanged \| unavailable\`
  result or equivalent typed failure contract.
- Before classifying or cleaning up, prove that the host branch HEAD/tree used for the decision
  still matches the verified checkpoint commit/tree.
- On unavailable base, Git failure, or checkpoint/host mismatch, park or fail through existing
  recoverable behavior and retain the sandbox/worktree. Never complete as a no-op.
- Persist fresh files/line stats from the same strict canonical delta before validation or no-op
  completion.
- Emit one bounded structured finalization record with pod/attempt/checkpoint correlation,
  selected base and branch, checkpoint and host proof, strict outcome, available stats, predicate
  flags, chosen lifecycle decision, and cleanup/validation/PR eligibility. Exclude diff/source/task
  content, credentials, and unbounded Git stderr.
- Preserve local sync-back, local auto-commit, deletion guards, true no-op behavior, checkpoint
  lineage barriers, retry-PR deletion protection, and provider base targeting.
- No SQL migration is expected. If implementation unexpectedly requires persisted columns or a
  dedicated table, stop and rescope rather than creating a migration implicitly.
- Historical affected pods remain source-recoverable through existing retry PR when the retained
  worktree is uncompromised, but that path must not claim missing daemon validation passed.

## Skills to reference

No specialized repository skill applies: this task does not add a profile field or pod lifecycle
state. Follow \`AGENTS.md\`, especially the shared test-mock convention and full validation process.

## Test expectations

- Add a completion orchestration matrix covering committed-only, uncommitted-only, mixed,
  true-empty, empty-commit, and commit-then-revert/net-zero checkpoint outcomes with cached zero
  counters.
- Prove every non-empty case persists fresh nonzero stats and enters blocking validation.
- Prove only strictly empty canonical snapshots take the no-change completion path.
- Prove unresolved base, strict diff/stat failure, and checkpoint/host mismatch are unavailable,
  retain recovery state, and never become zero-file success.
- Prove \`startCommitSha\` remains work scope while the configured branch remains PR base, including
  linked/fork behavior.
- Use real Git in the checkpoint integration test to prove committed, uncommitted, mixed, empty,
  and net-zero bytes are materialized as expected.
- Prove local completion and canonical path exclusions remain unchanged.
- Prove structured telemetry is complete and bounded for changed, unchanged, and unavailable
  decisions.
- Prove retry PR still pushes an affected materialized branch without claiming blocking
  validation occurred.
- Run the contract-required fact commands, then the daemon package tests and repository validation
  pipeline from \`AGENTS.md\`.

## Risks / pitfalls

- Moving the current fail-soft stats call outside the sandbox guard is insufficient because Git
  errors still collapse to zero.
- \`git status\` misses committed-only changes; commit count misclassifies empty commits and net-zero
  histories; review metadata is optional and non-authoritative.
- Comparing every pod to the PR base can include inherited work and break fix/fork scoping.
- Committed and uncommitted changes must be folded into one net snapshot rather than double-counted.
- Excluded daemon artifacts, binary files, renames, and deletions must retain canonical semantics.
- Cleanup must not race strict proof or make an unavailable result unrecoverable.
- Do not broaden this fix into automatic historical state transitions, UI work, or schema changes.

## Wrap-up

Before finishing:
1. Follow the profile finish prompt, if one is configured.
2. Re-run build and tests; both must still pass.
3. Commit and push.

## What

Sandbox completion now derives its final changed/no-change decision from a strict canonical delta over the verified materialized checkpoint, rather than cached counters. Host HEAD/tree must match checkpoint proof; base, Git, or proof failu

## Summary

計画書の残件「gate の中身が主張どおりか未確認」を、**違反を注入して検出されるか**で確かめた結果、1 本が主張どおりでなかった。

`public-path-alias-hygiene` のテスト名は「`src/app/(public)` の `_shared` import は `@/public` alias を使う」と主張していたが、実装が禁じていたのは:

```js
/from\s+["']@\/app\/\(public\)\/_shared\//
```

という **別 alias 形の 1 通りだけ**。alias を外す最も自然な書き方（`../../_shared/...`）を一切見ていなかった。計画書 P8 の **#31「test 名が主張過大」** と同じクラスで、しかも実際に 4 行がその形で残っていた。

## 文字列一致ではなくパスを解決する

`(public)` の下には `_shared` という名前のディレクトリが **3 つ**ある:

| ディレクトリ | alias |
| --- | --- |
| `(public)/_shared` | `@/public/*` |
| `(public)/mypage/_shared` | 無し（route ローカル） |
| `(public)/_components/_shared` | 無し（component ローカル） |

`_shared/` という文字列で判定すると 20 件ヒットするが、**alias 対象へ解決するのは `spaces/[slug]/page.tsx` の 4 行だけ**。import 元ディレクトリからの相対解決を実際に計算し、着地点で判定する形へ変えた。

`_shared` の内側から兄弟を指す相対 import は正しい形なので対象外にした（最初これを入れ忘れて `_shared` 内 28 ファイルを誤検出した）。

該当 4 行は `@/public/...` へ変換した。

## 他の gate の検出力（実測）

同じ方法で probe した結果:

| gate | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `section-config-widening-cast` | 検出 |
| `type-safety-cast-and-cache-tag-drift` | 検出 |
| `no-animated-opacity-on-text` | 検出 |
| `cross-surface-import-gate` | 検出 |
| `public-path-alias-hygiene` | **未検出** → 本 PR |

## Test plan

- **非空振りの実測**: 修正前の import へ戻すと該当 4 specifier を名指しして落ち、戻すと通る
- fixture で判定の両側を固定（着地点が alias 対象 / 別 `_shared` / `_shared` 内部 / 正しい alias 形 / 旧 alias 形）
- `bun scripts/run-tests.ts __tests__/unit/architecture-boundaries.test.ts __tests__/unit/architecture` — **166 passed / 0 failed**

author: gemisis
body:
fix(shell): bound how much of a command's output is captured (#252)

`wait_with_output()` buffered a child's entire stdout and stderr in the daemon's
memory with nothing to stop it. A command that printed at local-pipe speed for
its full 60-second budget is gigabytes of `Vec<u8>` in a process that is also
holding every other agent in the world, so one agent running `find / -type f`
could take the daemon down.

Each stream now keeps at most 1 MB. Sized just above `MAX_SCRIPT_IO_BYTES`
(900 KB), which caps the same text where it reaches a Rhai tool script, so that
one stays the tighter of the two.

### Draining past the cap is the whole design

The obvious implementation stops reading at the cap. That leaves the child
blocked on a full pipe, so a command producing more than the cap stops making
progress and dies at the timeout - turning a truncated result into a failed one,
which is worse than what it replaced. Past the cap the bytes are counted and
dropped, and the read loop keeps going to EOF.

A read error now ends the capture instead of failing the call. It means no more
output is coming, which is what EOF means too, and the exit status still
describes what the command did. Reporting "failed to spawn shell" for a command
that ran to completion would be a lie.

### The agent is told

A truncated result ends with a `[truncated]` line naming which stream overran
and how many bytes the command actually wrote. Silently handing back the first
megabyte would let an agent read a partial listing as the whole listing and
draw a confident wrong conclusion from it.

### Scope

This is the memory half of #252 and not the disk half. The 14 GB files in that
report were written by PowerShell redirects inside a single shell call, so those
bytes never passed through this pipe and this cap would not have bounded them.
That half is still open; see the issue.

### Tests

Six. The one that matters asserts the drain: a reader that counts its reads is
given ten chunks with a cap of one, and all eleven reads (ten plus EOF) must
happen. A test asserting only `kept.len() == cap` passes against the
deadlocking version.

The rest: kept/total either side of the cap, a mid-stream read error keeping
what arrived before it, the note staying silent when nothing was lost and naming
stdout, stderr, or both when something was. Plus the real-process twin - a
command writing 3 MB comes back truncated and successful in 0.13s rather than
timing out.

`cargo xtask coverage` clean on leviath-tools, full suite green.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Closes #3045

The doc comment on `PreviewListenerExposureNotice` is written as a specification — *"What the notice must say…"* — and requires **both** halves: that a network bind is pointless for a remote browser, **and** that it makes previewed dev servers reachable by anything that learns a tab's hostname. The runtime string carried only the comforting half: *"a network bind gains nothing"*.

That is worse than no warning at all. The notice exists so an operator can make an informed choice, and one that understates the exposure converts an unexamined default into an **examined and approved** one.

## What a network peer can actually do

The mechanism was already written down in the tree — I just never put it in the notice. `editorOriginPortIsSafe` states it plainly:

> On this listener the host label is the ONLY credential for every peer, and `*.localhost` resolution is irrelevant to an attacker: a remote client can simply send `Host: <label>.localhost` to an exposed ip:port.

So `*.localhost` is a browser **convention**, not a restriction on the port. Anything that reaches the address can set the `Host` header itself, and there is no bearer token on this listener — the label *is* the credential. A network bind therefore turns every tab hostname into a network-reachable capability, and one that leaks through a log, a screenshot, or browser history stops being usable only from this machine.

One precision worth stating: a label is `HMAC(secret, "host"‖sessionID‖tabID)`, so a peer cannot *read* a session identity out of it. What it gets is a durable bearer credential for that exact tab — which is the part an operator needs to weigh.

The reassuring half is kept deliberately. A remote browser genuinely cannot use the bind, and dropping that would overstate the risk in the other direction. The notice also now says editor tabs are withheld entirely while the listener is network-bound — the one thing standing between this and a code-execution exposure, since an editor origin fronts a `code-server` running with auth disabled.

## Why it shipped: the test asserted the reassurance

Every existing assertion checked a *comforting* clause — never borrows the control-plane warning, says "never serves the daemon control API", names the address, is one line. All of them passed against a string with the exposure missing entirely. The test confirmed the code that was written rather than the claim the comment made.

It now asserts the exposure clauses too, and I **verified it fails against the original text** before keeping it — every new assertion, not just one:

```
does not contain "only credential"
does not contain "Host: <tab>.localhost"
does not contain "log" / "screenshot" / "browser history"
```

## The same claim had spread to three more places

Found by scanning for the claim rather than the file:

- `docs/web.md` — "gains nothing (a remote browser still resolves `*.localhost` to its own machine), and the daemon warns about it"
- `docs/configuration.md` — "a non-loopback value here gains nothing"
- the `PreviewListenAddr` key comment — "same-machine viewing only", no caveat

All three now carry the exposure. Fixing only the runtime string would have left three surfaces telling an operator the opposite.

## Rendered

```
preview_listen_addr "0.0.0.0:8444" is reachable from the network · it is the web-tab preview
origin, kept separate from listen_addr so it never serves the daemon control API · it serves
your previewed dev servers, each on its own hostname · a remote browser gains nothing from the
bind: per-tab origins are *.localhost names, which a browser resolves to its own machine, so
remote viewers keep the same-origin preview on listen_addr · but *.localhost is a browser
convention, not a restriction — anything that reaches this address can send Host: <tab>.localhost
itself, and a tab's hostname is the only credential this listener checks, so a hostname that leaks
through a log, a screenshot, or browser history becomes readable from the network instead of only
from this machine · editor tabs are withheld entirely while this is network-bound · set it to a
loopback address such as 127.0.0.1:8444, or "" to disable it
```

Sentence case, ` · ` between fragments, `—` setting off the clause, one line, no caps-shouting — per CLAUDE.md.

`gofmt`, `go build`, `golangci-lint --fast`, `scripts/lint-file-length.sh`, `go test ./config/` all green; `scripts/gen-docs.sh` produces no drift.

author: ofalvai
body:
### Why

The test harness doesn't detect app crashes, and it only results in a test failure because asserts have a 20-minute timeout. Tests are also run without Mocha's `--bail` flag, so the run doesn't stop at the test failure.

Worst case, tests run for ours because:
- app crashes during a test case -> test harness idles for 20 minutes
- test harness keeps running the remaining test cases and potentially idles for another 20 minute per failing test

### What

1. Set the `--bail` flag so CI stops at the first test failure and reports the failure immediately
2. Lower the assert timeout to 5 minutes
3. Add a crash report collector that looks at `Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` after each test case and if it finds one `.ips` file, uploads it as a CI artifact.

author: huamick
body:
Five nodes declared `proof.real` bindings under packages that no longer exist — `packages/store` (dissolved by ADR-0077) and `packages/core` (dissolved by ADR-0068). All five are re-pointed at the code's verified real homes, and `contract-binding-drift` is drained to zero.

Found incidentally while driving `capability-layer-coverage-arc` increment 1 (#1199), which explicitly forbids touching `proof.real.sourceFile`.

## What moved

| node | was (dead) | now (verified present) |
|---|---|---|
| `cloud-sql-admin-rest` | `packages/store/src/cloud-sql-admin.{ts,test.ts}` | `packages/library/src/store/cloud-sql-admin.{ts,test.ts}` |
| `change-store-pg` | `packages/store/src/pg-change-store.{ts,live.test.ts}` | `packages/orchestrator/src/store/pg-change-store.{ts,live.test.ts}` |
| `source-drift` | `packages/core/src/source-drift.{ts,test.ts}` | `packages/orchestrator/src/proof/source-drift.{ts,test.ts}` |
| `change-event-store` | `packages/core/src/{store.ts,change-event-store.test.ts}` | `packages/storage-protocol/src/{store.ts,change-event-store.test.ts}` |
| `boundhash-on-verdict` | `packages/core/src/{proof.ts,boundhash-verdict.test.ts}` | `packages/proof-protocol/src/{proof.ts,shapes.test.ts}` |

**Two destinations are not the obvious guess.** `pg-change-store` did NOT follow the library mirror-image path — that adapter landed in the **orchestrator**. And `boundhash-on-verdict`'s test was **deleted, not renamed** (see below).

## What a re-point does to the existing signed verdicts: nothing

Two of the five carry a signed verdict, and both are **unaffected**:

| unit | outcome | run | commit | signed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud-sql-admin-rest` | `pass` | `real-mqgjuule` | `a8960bb8` | 2026-06-16 |
| `change-store-pg` | `pass` | `real-mqgodc71` | `8f8ed54a` | 2026-06-16 |

- Neither verdict doc contains a file path. Fields are `at, runId, signer, unitId, outcome, evidence[], commitSha, proofMode`; evidence refs are unit-scoped (`observation:red` / `observation:green`).
- Neither carries an `anchor`/`signingRow` binding a source-span hash, so there is no path-bound hash to invalidate.
- Nothing under `packages/orchestrator/src/proof/` reads `real.sourceFile` at all.

Each verdict remains a truthful record of a red-to-green observed at a commit where the old paths genuinely existed. What the re-point changes is **future** builds: `sourceFile` feeds the phase machine's IMPLEMENT write scope (`resolve-prove-spec.ts:593`) and the ADR-0192 landlord rule — both were pointing at nothing.

## Why the whole proof block, not just testFile/sourceFile

`pnpm --filter @storytree/store test` (and `@storytree/core`) prints "No projects matched the filters" and **exits 0** — measured, pnpm 9.15. Re-pointing only `testFile`/`sourceFile` would have left a declared typecheck **wall** (ADR-0031 section 2) passing having checked nothing, which is worse than the loud absence. Proof command, scope globs, typecheck filter and `change-store-pg`'s custom `proofCommand` all move too; that `proofCommand`'s package-relative path gains a `store/` segment. All five new filters match real workspaces carrying both `test` and `typecheck` scripts.

## `boundhash-on-verdict` — an absorption, not a rename

Both its bound files were **deleted** (git status `D`) in `e5c9b1b2`, not moved, and no file named `boundhash-verdict.test.ts` exists anywhere in the repo. Rather than invent a binding, the assertion was traced: it lives verbatim in the shared shapes suite at `packages/proof-protocol/src/shapes.test.ts:92-108` — identical `base` fixture field-for-field (same `at` timestamp), same `hash = "fnv1a:deadbeef"`, same two assertions (present preserved; absent undefined).

**Consequence, now recorded in the node's Guidance rather than left to be rediscovered:** `real.testFile` names a SHARED suite, so a rebuild would author into a file holding many other shape tests — not the dedicated file the node originally assumed.

## The landlord edge

Moving `change-event-store`'s source into `packages/storage-protocol/` made `binding-staleness` claim a file hosted in another story's building, and `check:boundaries` refused it (ADR-0074 section 4 either-endpoint / ADR-0192). Re-homing was not available — `store.ts` genuinely IS where the `Store`/`ChangeStore` seam has lived since ADR-0068 step 5 — so the edge is declared, the rule's first remedy. Verified acyclic first, and annotated in `artifact_edges` because no code import backs it (a hosted seam), which is what stops it becoming permanent "declared but code-unbacked" drift-WARN wallpaper.

Worth recording: this story's frontmatter **already** documented that `@storytree/core` was dissolved and the `Verdict` now lives at `packages/proof-protocol/src/proof.ts`, ending "do not restore it". The bindings were stale against their own story's stated intent.

## No new check was added, deliberately

The totality check for proof bindings **already exists** — `contract-binding-drift` in `check:verification-decay`, whose own docstring names `packages/core` dissolved by ADR-0068 and `packages/store` by ADR-0077 as its exemplars. It reported all five units **by name on every gate run** since it was baselined 2026-07-27, eleven days before this PR.

This was a **drain gap, not a detection gap.** A second instrument reporting the same facts to the same unread place would fail ADR-0311's bar (sixteen rungs retired for want of evidence). `packages/orchestrator/src/proof/source-drift.ts` is also the wrong axis for this — it compares content hashes of `derives_from` upstream artifacts and never touches file paths.

So instead of a new rung, the ceiling took the drain: **5 to 0**, aperture unchanged (ADR-0269 clause 5) — a repair lowering the number, not a narrowing owing a drop nor a raise owing a decomposition. Total decay signals 46 to 41.

**At zero the instrument now blocks**, which is the point. Zero also removes the slack that absorbed its ONE stated false positive — a genuine net-new unit that will CREATE a workspace package legitimately binds paths outside every package existing today. That case is documented AT the number with the sanctioned response: name it there per ADR-0269 clause 4(f), never raise silently.

## Deliberately not changed

- `change-store-pg`'s `outcome:` field still names two dead packages (`packages/store`, `@storytree/core`). No check reads it; it is arguably a truthful historical record of what the unit achieved.
- Both `packages/store` nodes still read `status: proposed` despite carrying signed PASS verdicts. A real inconsistency, but a proof-state question rather than a binding one.
- `change-event-store`'s body describes a three-part structure whose third piece (`changeStoreParitySuite`) now lives in `store-parity.ts`, and still references `packages/store` for `PgLibraryStore`/`PgWorkStore`. Both are more than a path swap.

## Verification

`pnpm gate` — **9/9 PASS**, scope FULL:

```
[1/9] PASS  check:boundaries          [6/9] PASS  pnpm -r test
[2/9] PASS  check:mirror-conformance  [7/9] PASS  check:guidance
[3/9] PASS  check:web-grounding       [8/9] PASS  check:agents
[4/9] PASS  check:web-engine          [9/9] PASS  check:verification-decay
[5/9] PASS  pnpm -r typecheck
```

All `stories/**` edits were routed through `story-author`. Every replacement path was confirmed present on disk before editing; no binding was inferred from a mirror-image guess.

author: hunghoang-ai
body:
Build a concurrency-safe seat-booking system in this repository. This is a fresh repository — set up a Python project with `uv` (pyproject.toml, pytest + httpx as dev dependencies) exposing a FastAPI app via an `app.main:create_app()` factory (mirroring the create_app() pattern used elsewhere in this codebase's task history), backed by PostgreSQL as the durable store and Redis for atomic seat holds, availability caching, and rate limiting — you choose the specific ORM/driver, token format, and password-hashing library; nothing below pins those. Data model (minimum fields): User(id, email unique, hashed_password, created_at); Event(id, name, venue, datetime); Seat(id, event_id, label, status derived as available|held|booked — status must be computed from Postgres (booked) layered under Redis hold state (held), never a separate column that can drift out of sync with either); Booking(id, user_id, event_id, seat_ids, amount, status, created_at). Auth: POST /auth/register {email, password} -> 201 (never echoes the password/hash back), 409 on a duplicate email; POST /auth/login {email, password} -> 200 with an opaque bearer token backed by a Redis-stored session (not a stateless JWT, so logout can actually invalidate it), 401 on bad credentials; POST /auth/logout (Authorization: Bearer <token>) deletes that session so the token is rejected by every endpoint afterward. Reads are public: GET /events lists events with no auth required; GET /events/{event_id}/seats returns the seat map (id, label, status) with no auth required, served from a Redis cache with a short TTL (env var CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, default 5) rather than hitting Postgres on every request, and must reflect a booking/hold state change within at most one cache TTL window — never permanently stale. Booking flow (auth required beyond this point): POST /events/{event_id}/holds {seat_ids: [...]} places a temporary, all-or-nothing hold on those seats using a Redis atomic primitive (e.g. SET NX PX per seat, or a Lua script covering the whole batch) — if any requested seat is not currently available (already held or booked) the whole request fails with 409 and no partial holds are left behind; on success returns 201 {hold_id, seat_ids, expires_at}. The hold's TTL is env var HOLD_TTL_SECONDS (default 300 = 5 minutes, must be overridable per-process so tests can use e.g. 1 second) and expiry is automatic via Redis key expiry alone — no cron job, background sweep, or manual cleanup endpoint may be required for a held seat to become available again. POST /bookings/checkout {hold_id, payment_token} runs a mock/stub payment step: any payment_token except the literal sentinel string "FAIL" succeeds — on success it durably persists a Booking row and marks those seats booked in Postgres (this must survive independently of whatever happens to the Redis hold key afterward), releases the Redis hold, and returns 200 {booking_id, status: "confirmed", amount} where amount is a positive number derived from the number of seats (a fixed per-seat price constant is sufficient, a full pricing model is not required); payment_token == "FAIL" releases the hold, leaves the seats available, and returns 402 without creating a Booking. Checking out a hold_id that has expired or never existed returns 404 and creates nothing; checking out a hold_id created by a different user than the caller returns 403. GET /bookings/me (auth) returns only the caller's own bookings. Rate limiting: the hold and checkout endpoints must reject a client (identified by authenticated user id) exceeding RATE_LIMIT_MAX requests per RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (env vars, sane defaults, both overridable for tests) with 429, implemented via Redis (e.g. INCR+EXPIRE or a sliding window), so a mass-grab burst against a popular event cannot exhaust the backend. Frontend: serve a minimal page at GET / (plain HTML + vanilla JS is sufficient, no framework required) that fetches an event's seat map, lets a user select available seats, and calls the hold/checkout endpoints — this only needs a basic reachability smoke test at the HTTP layer, not full browser automation, since that isn't practical for this repository's automated Tier-1 gate. Testability constraint that must be satisfied end-to-end: `uv run pytest -q` must pass in a clean environment with no externally pre-started services (no human running `docker-compose up` first) — use an ephemeral-service fixture (e.g. testcontainers-python spinning up disposable Postgres and Redis containers scoped to the test session and torn down after) or clearly-justified in-process fakes (e.g. fakeredis) that still preserve real atomicity semantics under test; whichever you pick, the concurrency test below must exercise genuinely overlapping HTTP requests (e.g. a ThreadPoolExecutor firing simultaneous calls against a real running server or the test client), not a mocked-out serialized call path that can't actually race. Docker constraint that must be satisfied, distinct from and in addition to this repository's standing Dockerfile/README.md requirement: this is a long-running network service, so the mandatory container smoke test (`docker build -t <tag> .` followed by a bare `docker run --rm <tag>` — no compose, no flags, no linked services, and no timeout on that command) must still exit 0 on its own. Do NOT make the image's default CMD serve traffic forever (that would hang the smoke test indefinitely). Instead, the default CMD must run a bounded startup self-check — construct the FastAPI app, verify it initializes and its routes are registered, exercise DB/Redis connectivity against whatever DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL are provided (falling back to sensible container-local defaults, e.g. sqlite/fakeredis, if absent) — and then exit 0 on success or a non-zero code with a clear message on failure. Document the actual long-running invocation separately in README.md (e.g. `docker run -p 8000:8000 -e DATABASE_URL=... -e REDIS_URL=... <tag> uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0`, overriding CMD) alongside a docker-compose.yml that runs the app with real Postgres and Redis for local development.

## Acceptance criteria
- POST /auth/register with a new email and password returns 201 with a body containing id and email, and never includes the password or hashed_password
- POST /auth/register twice with the same email returns 409 on the second call
- POST /auth/login with correct credentials returns 200 with a bearer access_token; POST /auth/login with a wrong password returns 401
- POST /auth/logout invalidates the token: any subsequent authenticated request using that same token returns 401
- GET /events and GET /events/{event_id}/seats both succeed with no Authorization header at all -- browsing is public
- GET /events/{event_id}/seats for a nonexistent event_id returns 404
- POST /events/{event_id}/holds with no Authorization header returns 401 -- booking requires an authenticated session even though browsing does not
- As an authenticated user, POST /events/{event_id}/holds with seat_ids for currently-available seats returns 201 with hold_id, seat_ids, and expires_at, and an immediately following GET /events/{event_id}/seats shows those seats' status as held rather than available
- As a second authenticated user, POST /events/{event_id}/holds for a seat already held by the first user returns 409, and that seat's status does not change as a result
- Requesting a hold on a batch of seats where at least one is unavailable places no hold at all on any seat in that batch (all-or-nothing) -- the still-available seats in the batch remain available afterward
- Central concurrency guarantee: firing 20 genuinely concurrent POST /events/{event_id}/holds requests for the exact same single seat, each from a distinct authenticated user, results in exactly one 201 response and nineteen 409 responses -- repeat the burst multiple times across the test run and confirm exactly-one-winner holds every time, never zero and never more than one
- With HOLD_TTL

author: sachiniyer
body:
Closes #3044.

This is my own #3007 diverging from the transport it was built to reuse, which makes it the exact failure the abstraction existed to prevent: the argument for returning an ssh host was that **af owns transport one way**.

## The divergence

| Input | `backend=ssh` | hook provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `host: "10.0.0.7:2222"`, `port: 3333` | **2222** (embedded wins) | **3333** (field wins) |

Same record, different destination, and neither error explains why — a host that connects under one backend fails under the other.

## Shared, not matched

`resolveSSHHostPort` is now the single rule, and both entry points call it. That is deliberate rather than incidental: a *"mirrors the ssh backend"* comment is unenforced and false the moment either side is edited (#2097). One function cannot disagree with itself.

`sshProvisioner.hostPort` keeps its own **default** (22 when nothing is specified) — that is a default, not a different rule, and the test asserts the distinction.

## A conflict is refused, not ranked

Two different ports in one configuration means one of them is a mistake. Picking either silently sends the session somewhere nobody asked for, so both backends now refuse and the error names **both** values:

```
ssh address "10.0.0.7:2222" embeds port 2222 but the port field says 3333;
they must agree, so remove one — af will not guess which was meant
```

Agreement is fine: `10.0.0.7:2222` with `port: 2222` says one thing twice. This follows the issue's own preference for rejecting ambiguity over silently choosing, and the repo's precedent from #2862.

**Behaviour change worth naming:** a `backend=ssh` user whose config is *already* self-contradictory now gets an error instead of a silent 2222. Their config could never have expressed both, so this converts a latent surprise into a fixable message — but it is a change, not purely additive.

## Malformed ports are named as ports

Both old paths passed one through — ssh handed `"abc"` to the ssh binary, hook kept `"host:abc"` as the entire hostname — and each failed later complaining about the *address*. `10.0.0.7:ssh` and `10.0.0.7:99999` are now rejected naming the port.

## Verification

The regression test drives **both real entry points** with one input and requires agreement, rather than asserting each in isolation. Mutation-tested by restoring the original opposite precedence in the hook path:

```
--- FAIL: TestSSHAndHookResolveTheSameAddressIdentically/both,_agreeing
--- FAIL: TestConflictingPortsAreRefusedByBothBackends
        hook provisioning must refuse a conflicting address
```

Also covered: IPv6 (`[::1]:2222` splits, bare `::1` is not a host:port), agreement, and each field alone.

## Validation

`gofmt -l .` (no output) · `go build ./...` · `golangci-lint run --timeout=3m --fast` · `scripts/lint-file-length.sh` · `go test ./session/ ./config/` green. No containerized suites, no daemon/app tests on the host.

Closes #3044

author: tmattio
body:
Integrates @hennequin's gtree contribution (hennequin-lab/raven@3c4ed3c), cherry-picked as-is, with a rework on top. The design is adopted wholesale, payload-generic structures, a bridge functor into Ptree.S, checked unpacking, a deriver with a mirror mode for concrete records. The rework renames the surface and merges the derivers.

Ptree.Gtree → Ptree.Uniform (the module type of structures with a uniform payload), Ptree.Tensor_tree → Ptree.Make. Mirror mode generates module Uniform, to_uniform, of_uniform. The generated module is an instance of the identically-named signature.

[@@deriving gtree] is merged into [@@deriving ptree], which dispatches on the declaration:

- concrete type → rank-2 traversals (unchanged);
- one type parameter occurring outside tensor leaves, unannotated → uniform traversals (map, map2, iter, fold, fold2, names);
- [@@deriving ptree ~mirror] on a concrete type → additionally the uniform mirror.

Positions carrying a [@ptree.*] attribute keep their rank-2 meaning, so existing records like { tag : 'tag [@ptree.ignore]; ... } derive exactly as before; abstract signatures default to rank-2.

author: aviatesk
body:
Test.jl macro replacements left anonymous functions in top-level lowered code. For example:

    @test_broken any(items) do item
        first_check(item)
    end && any(items) do item
        second_check(item)
    end

The closure in the right-hand branch became a concrete definition requirement. Reaching it could concretely execute the first `any` call, causing side effects or top-level errors instead of inference reports.

This change outlines only thunk-safe tested expressions containing conditionally defined anonymous functions into zero-argument functions. Calls, expression-level control flow, literals, and type expressions are accepted by an explicit whitelist. Bindings, named definitions, control transfers, and unknown macros remain inline. The `skip=` path defines the thunk outside its generated branch and invokes it only when enabled.

A minimal reproducer now reports an undefined global in the first closure through inference instead of concrete top-level execution. The focused `@test macros` tests pass 96/96.

This is a Test-specific mitigation for a general virtual-process limitation. A future fix should distinguish compiler-generated closure materialization from runtime concretization during statement selection. It can avoid selecting enclosing control flow when closure setup has no runtime-value dependencies, while retaining current behavior otherwise.

Warm median timings were neutral versus disabling the wrapping: 4.44 seconds versus 4.57 seconds for Struct2JSONSchema, which had no eligible expressions, and 20.83 seconds versus 21.18 seconds for JET's test file, which had two.

author: vitalijssilins
body:
Fixes #283.

## What

`MCPORTER_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER` was parsed only inside the auth command's argv handling (`consumeBrowserSuppression`), so the serve/daemon path still launched the system browser on every 401 — a focus-stealing, context-free tab when a token expires under an MCP bridge, and a tab loop when auth keeps failing (details in the issue).

## How

- `redirectToAuthorization` now falls back to the env var when no explicit `suppressBrowserLaunch` option was passed: `this.options.suppressBrowserLaunch ?? suppressBrowserLaunchFromEnv()`. An explicit option always wins, and the accepted values (`1`/`true`/`yes`, case-insensitive) mirror the auth command's `TRUE_VALUES`.
- When suppression is active but no `onAuthorizationUrl` callback is registered (the headless serve/daemon case), the authorization URL is logged at warn level and the pending authorization is **rejected with a server-named `BrowserLaunchSuppressedError`** — callers fail fast with an actionable message (`run 'mcporter auth <name> --no-browser'`) instead of silently waiting out the authorization timeout (the "remaining risk" flagged in #283's review).
- The rejection path is deliberate: the SDK invokes `redirectToAuthorization` from unawaited send paths, where a throw becomes an unhandled rejection that kills the daemon (we hit exactly that in a real run while iterating).
- Existing callers that pass `suppressBrowserLaunch: true` with a callback (the auth command) are unaffected.

## Real behavior proof (daemon, real 401)

Isolated `$HOME` with an empty vault (guaranteed 401), one keep-alive OAuth server (Supabase's public MCP endpoint), foreground daemon built from this branch, real `callTool` through the daemon client:

```
$ HOME=$PROOF MCPORTER_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER=1 node dist/cli.js daemon start --foreground --log
[daemon] 2026-08-07T08:41:41.627Z Daemon host started.
[daemon] 2026-08-07T08:41:45.606Z callTool start server=supabase-room tool=list_tables
[mcporter] Authorization required for supabase-room; browser launch suppressed (MCPORTER_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER). Visit https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=cf4aec55-…&code_challenge=…&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A62199%2Fcallback&… to authorize.
[mcporter] OAuth authorization required for 'supabase-room'. Waiting for browser approval...
[mcporter] OAuth authorization failed while waiting for callback.
BrowserLaunchSuppressedError: Authorization required for 'supabase-room' but browser launch is suppressed (MCPORTER_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER); run 'mcporter auth supabase-room --no-browser' to authorize.
[daemon] 2026-08-07T08:41:47.396Z callTool error server=supabase-room tool=list_tables err=Authorization required for 'supabase-room' but browser launch is suppressed (…)
[daemon] 2026-08-07T08:41:47.399Z closeServer success server=supabase-room     ← daemon healthy, handles the error
[daemon] 2026-08-07T08:41:48.341Z Shutting down daemon host.                   ← clean shutdown at end of capture

$ time HOME=$PROOF node dist/cli.js call supabase-room list_tables
[mcporter] Authorization required for 'supabase-room' but browser launch is suppressed (MCPORTER_OAUTH_NO_BROWSER); run 'mcporter auth supabase-room --no-browser' to authorize.
call exit: 1
2.828 total    ← fails in ~3s with the actionable error, not the 300s authorization timeout
```

No browser launched at any point (no `open` spawn; nothing hit the OS). On current main the same run logs `Authorization required for supabase-room. Opening browser...` and launches the system browser from the daemon.

(The client_id in the transcript is a throwaway Dynamic Client Registration from the isolated home, since deleted.)

## Tests

- Env var set, no session options → `openExternal` not called, URL surfaced at warn level, late-attaching waiter rejects with `BrowserLaunchSuppressedError` (server-named).
- Falsy value (`0`) → browser opens as before.
- Explicit `suppressBrowserLaunch: true` + callback (auth command path) → unchanged, existing test still green.
- `pnpm check` and full `pnpm test` green (1283 passed).

author: assapir
body:
## Summary
Closes #44.

The JIT path (`quilon run`) built `argv` from `std::env::args()` **raw**, so a program's `^`'s `args :: []Text` saw the `quilon run <file>` CLI prefix. The native (AOT) binary gets a clean argv from the OS. The two paths disagreed on `args.size` and `args` contents.

## Fix (Option A — mirror AOT)
- `src/jit.rs::run_program` now takes an explicit `args: &[String]` instead of reading `std::env::args()` itself. `env` still comes from the process environment (unchanged), matching what the OS hands a native binary.
- `src/main.rs`'s `Run` subcommand captures trailing user args (`trailing_var_arg` + `allow_hyphen_values`, so `quilon run f.ql --flag x` forwards `--flag x` to the program instead of to quilon) and builds `argv = [<file>, <user args...>]` — the `quilon`/`run` prefix is stripped and the `.ql` path becomes `argv[0]`.

Result: `quilon run f.ql a b c` mirrors `./f a b c` — same `args.size` and same trailing arguments (`argv[0]` is the `.ql` path rather than the compiled binary's path).

### Before / after — `quilon run f.ql a b c`
| | `args` the program receives |
|---|---|
| **before** | `["quilon", "run", "f.ql", "a", "b", "c"]` (size 6) |
| **after** | `["f.ql", "a", "b", "c"]` (size 4) — matches native `./f a b c` |

## Tests
- `jit_uses_caller_supplied_argv` (tests/run_test.rs) — fast JIT-API anchor: `run_program(&p, &argv)` yields `args.size == argv.len()`.
- `jit_and_aot_argv_agree` (tests/args_native_test.rs) — drives **both** the real `quilon run` CLI and a native build for the empty, `a b c`, and `--flag x` cases, asserting both agree on `args.size` (skips gracefully without a C toolchain).
- Docs updated (LANGUAGE.md, README.md).

Full gate green locally: `cargo build`, `cargo test` (incl. native-AOT gate), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

author: groganz
body:
## What

S2 of the marketplace in-card install epic (#2371). The marketplace card's **Install now** no longer opens a popup: for the three install-access-target kinds (connector / artifact / workflow) it swaps the card's **body** in place to the shared install panel, keeping the header band — icon, name, byline — exactly as it was. No install dialog is mounted anywhere on the card path.

Built on current `main` with **zero dependence on #2406** (S1 is unmerged). Per the owner's serialize ruling, #2406 rebases onto this.

## What changed

- **`CardFaceSwitcher`** (`packages/extensions/src/screens/card-face-switcher.tsx`) — a client shell over TWO server-rendered faces that mounts **exactly one** at a time. A hidden second face would keep a stale open panel, duplicate every stable testid and leave a focusable picker behind the card; `{open ? install : idle}` is the whole guarantee. The card component stays pure, and the filter-only client grid still receives one opaque node per extension. Panel ids are `useId`-derived, so N cards hold N open panels without colliding.
- **`ExtensionInstallScopePanel`** (`extension-install-scope-panel.tsx`) — the panel body: the `Install for` eyebrow, the shared `AccessCombobox` over the SERVER-COMPUTED rows, and Cancel / Install now. It takes the **UNBOUND** scoped action plus `packageName` / `packageVersion` and the picker context — the same shape the scoped dialog path takes. Bound zero-argument actions stay where they were, on the direct agent/skill forms.
- **Filter lifecycle** (`extensions-marketplace-client.tsx`) — a non-matching item's node is now **unmounted**; the stable grid-item wrapper stays, so visible-cardinality assertions are unchanged. A filtered-away card cannot retain an open panel, and filtering it back mounts a fresh idle node. Focus stays on the filter control throughout.
- **Availability** (`install-panel-availability.ts`, pure) — one discriminated state resolved server-side in a fixed order: `no-active-organization` (own copy naming the real cause; no picker, no submit) → `ready` (default = the `Workspace: All` **audience** row; narrower audiences still selectable) → `no-installable-scope` (existing role-oriented empty state, copy unchanged). Marketplace-local: the shared `pickDefaultPickerValue` the agent registry uses is untouched and is consulted only as the fallback. Installer **authority** and installed-extension **audience** are named as the two separate dimensions they are; neither is weakened.
- **Errors → toast** — a failure keeps the panel exactly as the admin left it, selection retained, and mirrors the SAME classified copy into a visually hidden `role="alert"`. No inline alert. The classified no-raw-detail contract is unchanged.
- **Geometry** — both faces share the spec-pinned card block size as a floor and stretch together with `h-full`, so an `auto-rows-fr` track can neither shrink nor grow across open/close. The panel's flex chain is `min-h-0` and only its middle region scrolls; the picker's popover is portalled, so it is never clipped.
- **Focus** — open moves focus to the panel's first enabled control (or its heading when there is none); close remounts the idle face and returns focus to the Install CTA it came from.
- **Conformance** — new stable testids join the contract; the pinned card contracts (`extension-card-cta`, `data-cta-state`, `contents`, element types) are preserved verbatim. The artifact card's "Installing…" state now lives on the panel's submit, and its driver and geometry proof follow it there.

## Conformance ledger vs the issue plan

| Plan item | Status | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| `CardFaceSwitcher` over two SERVER-rendered faces; exactly ONE mounted | Met | jsdom: idle face is unmounted, not hidden; live: 1 install face + 29 idle cards |
| Idle CTA and panel ✕ signal the switcher via context; card stays pure | Met | `InstallPanelOpenButton` / `InstallPanelCloseButton` / `InstallPanelCancelButton` are the only stateful pieces |
| Shared panel takes the UNBOUND action + identifiers + picker context | Met | `installAction={installExtensionPackageFormAction}`; jsdom asserts the exact call shape |
| Grid keeps one opaque node per extension | Met | screen builds `node`; grid unchanged in shape |
| All panel ids `useId`-derived; N concurrent panels, unique ids | Met | jsdom + live: two panels, distinct `aria-labelledby` and picker ids |
| Filter: node UNMOUNTED, wrapper kept; filter-back returns to idle | Met | live: 75 hidden items with zero children, 6 mounted; away→back leaves 0 panels |
| Focus stays on the filter control throughout | Met | live: `document.activeElement === search` across both filter steps |
| Deterministic geometry; no runtime measurement; tracks never jump | Met | live at md/lg/xl + resize-while-open + sole-card case; new Playwright regression |
| Fixed header + footer, only the middle scrolls; popover outside the overflow | Met | live: popover resolves outside the card face |
| Focus enter on open, restore to the CTA on close | Met | jsdom + live for both ✕ and Cancel |
| `Workspace: All` preselected and rendered verbatim in the trigger | Met | live: trigger reads `Workspace: All`; the checkmark is on the `workspace` row |
| Availability order: no-active-organization → ready → no-installable-scope | Met | 7 pure unit tests + jsdom render of all three states |
| Shared default-picker helper untouched | Met | `pickDefaultPickerValue` unchanged; used only as `fallbackDefaultValue` |
| Authority-vs-audience comments clarified without weakening either | Met | screen + availability module |
| Inline Alert removed; toast + hidden `role="alert"`; selection retained | Met | live: same copy in both channels, same reference, panel and selection intact |
| New stable testids in the conformance contract; pinned card contracts verbatim | Met | contract check green |
| AC1 body swaps in place, ✕ returns to idle, no dialog on the card path | Met | live: 0 dialogs while the panel is open |
| AC5 failing install fires the toast AND the in-panel alert, no raw detail | Met | live, twice, with the diagnostic reference |

## Design-surface conformance

Pinned spec: `design@f4489c5`, `specs/app-extensions.html` — §I.1 "The in-card install panel". Checked bidirectionally against the drawing: header band carried over unchanged; the `Install for` mono eyebrow; the picker trigger reading `Workspace: All` with its chevron; Cancel / Install now right-aligned; the ✕ in the header's top-right; errors as a toast, never inline. Nothing renders that the spec does not draw. The ✕ is overlaid rather than passed through the banner's badge slot, because that slot reserves right padding on the name and would re-wrap a long title between the two faces — the header is byte-identical across the swap this way.

**Which pinned conformance entries this satisfies.** With the manifest temporarily re-pinned to `design@f4489c5` locally (reverted before commit — this PR does not move the pin), the functional-acceptance suite ran **28 passed / 1 failed**:

A driver, a harness mount and the testid contract for this surface all land here, so the entry goes green the moment the pin arrives.

body:
## Perché

`openfatture/ai/tools/payment_tools.py` non aveva **alcun** test. È così che `import_bank_transactions` ha potuto importare due moduli inesistenti e sollevare `ImportError` a ogni chiamata senza che nessuno se ne accorgesse (corretto in #21).

## Cosa

**Copertura del tool.** Test su database reale isolato (`runtime_db`) invece che con sessione mockata: il tool apre la propria sessione via `get_session()`, e la deduplica che implementa ha senso solo contro righe realmente persistite.

Casi coperti: import iniziale con creazione account, re-import dello stesso file (tutto skippato per FITID), stesso statement su due account distinti (le reference non sono condivise), file assente, estensione errata, file non parsabile.

Verificato che i test catturano davvero la rottura originale — reintroducendo l'import inesistente:

```
6 failed, 1 warning in 4.93s
```

**Scritture in batch.** L'import emetteva un `SAWarning` a ogni riga:

```
SAWarning: Object of type <BankTransaction> not in session,
add operation along 'BankAccount.transactions' will not proceed
```

`OFXImporter` costruisce ogni transazione con `account=account`, quindi finiscono tutte in `account.transactions` fin da subito; il flush riga-per-riga di `add()` prova poi a cascatare un append per oggetti ancora pendenti. Ora si raccolgono i sopravvissuti alla deduplica e si scrive con `add_batch`, rimuovendo i duplicati skippati dalla collection perché non vengano cascatati.

## Verifica

| gate | esito |
|---|---|
| `mypy openfatture/` | 0 errori |
| `black --check` / `ruff check` | puliti |
| suite | 1688 passed, 10 skipped |

author: dalquier
jnsereko
body:
Fixes **Issue 2** from UAT round 2 — *"Downloaded study doesn't appear as an attachment"* — and thereby unblocks **Issue 4**, which couldn't be tested while no attachment existed to open.

`eip_processed_orthanc_study` had **zero rows for the entire life of the deployment**. Not one study had ever been processed.

### Cause: authentication, in two places

OpenMRS has SSO enabled, so its filter answers `302 -> /openmrs/oauth2login` for any API request without an accepted token — basic auth is never honoured. Both config classes in the bridge built a Basic header regardless:

- **`OpenmrsConfig.authHeader()`** returned Basic unconditionally, despite already injecting `${oauth.enabled}` and a `TokenCache` — neither was ever read. Its header covers the native REST calls, including the `POST /ws/rest/v1/obs` behind `saveResult()` that records the study on the chart.
- **`OrthancConfig.authHeader()`** likewise. That can't work against an Orthanc running the authorization plugin with `AuthenticationEnabled=false`, where only a token is accepted. Measured against the running instance:

| credential | `GET /studies` |
|---|---|
| none | 403 |
| `Basic orthanc:orthanc` | 403 |
| `Bearer <orthanc-service>` | **200** |

The second is why the first couldn't just be switched on: `oauth.enabled` is a **single global flag**, so enabling it for OpenMRS also routed Orthanc through it — trading 400s on OpenMRS for 403s on `GET /studies`. One flag, two legs, mutually exclusive outcomes.

Both classes now prefer a bearer token from the existing `OrthancTokenProvider` and fall back to Basic when none is available, so a non-SSO deployment is unchanged.

### Plus the missing OpenMRS user

`oauth2login` maps a token onto an OpenMRS user via `preferred_username` (`openmrs.mapping.user.username`), so a *valid* token whose service account has no matching user is rejected exactly as Basic is. `service-account-eip` had one — which is why the **Odoo bridge worked all along** — and `service-account-orthanc-service` did not.

The Liquibase changeset adds it, mirroring the roles `service-account-eip` holds, with a random password hash and salt so it can only authenticate by token. Ids resolve by subquery rather than hardcoded (unlike the older user changesets above it) and `preConditions` make it a no-op where the user already exists.

### Verified on UAT, end to end

```
403s 0 · 302s 0 · 400s 0 · ERROR lines 0 · restarts 0
eip_processed_orthanc_study: 3 rows        (was 0, always)

saveResult: created Observation 6db24588-… for patient 7f401e9d-…
Saved attachment for patient 7f401e9d-… study 60b80ebe-…
```

And in the database: three `ATT IMAGE ATTACHMENT` complex obs alongside three `General patient note` obs carrying the Stone viewer link, across the two distinct patients the studies belong to.

### Notes for review

- **Requires `OAUTH_ENABLED=true`**, a matching change in LIME-EMR-Tooling (`d3f9f85a2`). With an older jar that flag reintroduces the Orthanc 403s — the two go together.
- The source change is an 87-line diff against `Virlein/eip-openmrs-orthanc` and **belongs upstream in that fork**; this commit ships only the built artifact, as `89f7a39` did. The patch file is available for Valentin to apply and review.
- **Not addressed:** order-to-worklist. Orthanc exposes no `/worklists` REST API, and authorizing writes to a Python-provided one has no clean option — the plugin's `Permissions` key *replaces* the 48 patterns `StandardConfigurations` installs rather than adding to them. Unchanged from `9ab9e88`.

author: mohsen1
body:
tsc's `getIndexType` resolves an `any`/`unknown`/`never` operand to its fixed key-space result (`string | number | symbol` / `never`) immediately at type-construction time, so the resulting type carries no `aliasSymbol` and the `keyof` operator never reaches `typeToString`. tsz built a deferred `KeyOf` node unconditionally in both places a `keyof` type-operator gets constructed (`crates/tsz-checker/src/types/type_node_advanced.rs`'s `get_type_from_type_operator`, and `crates/tsz-lowering/src/lower/advanced.rs`'s `lower_type_operator`), so `declare const v: keyof any;` computed the right semantic type but displayed `keyof any` verbatim.

Root cause was two independent gaps stacked on the same repro:

1. Both `keyof`-operator construction sites deferred unconditionally instead of eagerly evaluating for a degenerate `any`/`unknown`/`never` operand, matching tsc's `getIndexType`. Fixed by eagerly calling `evaluate_keyof` for exactly those three operands; every other operand (object, interface, generic) keeps the deferred `KeyOf` node so `keyof T` still displays.
2. Even after (1), the assignment-source diagnostic formatter's "declared annotation" fallback (`declared_type_annotation_text_for_symbol_type` / `declared_type_annotation_text_for_expression_with_options`) reproduces a variable's ANNOTATION SOURCE TEXT verbatim when a reverse type-to-symbol lookup finds one, regardless of whether that annotation is something tsc still preserves. For `keyof any` it isn't (per (1)) — this repainted the already-correctly-evaluated union with the literal `keyof any` text. Fixed with a new structural guard, `annotation_is_keyof_over_degenerate_operand`, declining the text fallback for exactly this annotation shape (mirrors the existing `annotation_names_type_query_alias` guard already used at every one of these call sites). A parallel `keyof_degenerate_operand_source_display` gate (same family as #16610's `longhand_primitive_union_source_display`) covers the case where the freshly-evaluated union coincidentally interns to the same `TypeId` as a genuinely-referenced `PropertyKey` elsewhere (e.g. inside the loaded lib), which would otherwise repaint it via the reverse type-to-def lookup.

While investigating, found that #16610's core repaint bug (rows 1-4) and its TS2344 sibling #16663 were BOTH already fixed on main by #16645 (`3b916ec`) — closed both issues with test-run evidence rather than re-deriving a fix that had already landed, and picked up the one genuinely open row from #16610's own matrix (row 5, `keyof any` display) as this PR.

Adjacent-case matrix (`union_display_alias_repaint_parity_tests.rs`, oracle-verified against pinned `typescript@7.0.2`):

| case | tsc | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyof any` (unreferenced alias in scope) | structural | `keyof any` | structural |
| `keyof never` (sibling degenerate operand) | structural | `keyof never` | structural |
| renamed unused alias in scope | structural | `keyof any` | structural |
| `keyof <named interface>` (negative control) | `keyof Name` | `keyof Name` | `keyof Name` (unchanged) |
| named alias whose body is `keyof any`, referenced by name | structural | `Foo` | `Foo` (pinned `#[ignore]`d tripwire — separate, deeper mechanism, out of this PR's scope) |

## Goal
Goal: hold

## Verification
- `cargo test -p tsz-checker --test union_display_alias_repaint_parity_tests --test ts2344_primitive_key_union_alias_constraint_display_tests` — 28 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored (5 new live rows, 1 new documented tripwire; re-verified after rebasing onto main tip `8ceb4ae`, which independently fixed the pre-existing alias-chain tripwire in the same test file).
- `cargo build -p tsz-checker -p tsz-lowering --lib` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p tsz-checker -p tsz-lowering --lib --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo fmt -p tsz-checker -p tsz-lowering -- --check` — clean.
- `python3 scripts/arch/arch_guard.py` — clean (split `keyof_degenerate_operand_source_display` into `keyof_source_display.rs` to keep `assignment_formatting.rs` under the 2000-line ceiling).
- Manual cross-check against pinned `typescript@7.0.2` for every row in the adjacent matrix above.
- Owed: full `cargo test -p tsz-checker --lib` (~10.4k tests) was still running in the background at push time (long-tail suite per the board's standing notes, and this cloud container is disk-constrained); will report the count in a follow-up comment if it turns up anything.

body:
## Summary

The `pnpm audit` CI job is failing on every branch, `release/v0.35.0` included, since GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj was published: a high-severity quadratic-CPU parse of `!!omap` in js-yaml, reached transitively through `electron-builder > app-builder-lib`.

One line in `pnpm.overrides` plus the lockfile it regenerates.

## Why a pin and not an ignore

The two entries already in `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` are there because nothing upstream fixes them. This one has a fix: 4.3.1 carries the patch. The tree only ever resolved a single js-yaml (4.3.0), and nothing in the repo imports it directly, so this is a patch bump on a dev-only transitive dependency, the same shape as every other entry in `pnpm.overrides`.

## Testing

- `pnpm audit --ignore-registry-errors`, the exact CI command, exits 0. The two remaining advisories are the pre-existing ignored pair.
- Lockfile regenerated with `pnpm install --lockfile-only`; the only resolution that moved is js-yaml 4.3.0 to 4.3.1.
- No direct `js-yaml` import anywhere in `src/`, `server/`, `scripts/`, `headless/`, or `electron/`.

Unblocks the audit job for every open PR, including #3035.

## T044 — Shopify controlled writeback (Epic E04)

**Deny-by-default, consent-gated** Shopify writeback (`packages/connectors/src/shopify/writeback.ts`) — the highest-risk connector action, every safety gate pure and explicit.

- **Allow-list (deny by default)** — only product fields `title/descriptionHtml/productType/vendor/tags` and variant fields `barcode/sku/price/compareAtPrice` may be written; anything else is rejected; gids validated; empty sets rejected.
- **Consent gate (never inferred)** — `assertWritebackAuthorized` requires `approved: true` + `approvalId` + an idempotency key (spec: *never infer repair consent*).
- **Conflict detection** — recompute the current remote product's T043 fingerprint vs the plan's baseline; a mismatch → **non-retryable `conflict`** (no clobbering concurrent merchant edits).
- **Gated mutation building** — `buildProductUpdateMutation` / `buildVariantUpdateMutation` only build GraphQL after re-asserting authorization + validation; `userErrorsToConnectorError` maps Shopify `userErrors`.

No dependency, env var, schema/migration, or boundary change. The worker apply loop + issuing the `approvalId` (RBAC/approval) are follow-ups.

**Evidence:** full CI gate locally — **264/264 tests**, `tsc -b` clean, ESLint 0 errors, repo-owned files Prettier-clean, both hooks passing. `tests/shopify-writeback.test.mjs` (7) covers allow-list, consent, conflict, mutation building, and userErrors.

body:
## Obiettivo

Impedire che heartbeat, reconnect o apertura di una lega attivino timer appartenenti a un’altra lega. Il timer viene reclamato solo per la combinazione esatta `user + league + auction` dopo una conferma esplicita della visualizzazione.

## Contenuto

- nuovo endpoint `POST /api/leagues/:leagueId/auctions/:auctionId/response-timer/viewed`
- controllo membership e ruolo admin
- claim SQL atomico con verifica di lega e asta attiva
- una sola attivazione e una sola notifica Socket sotto concorrenza
- test realistici con tre richieste simultanee
- report tecnico in `docs/PR/PR-multileague-timer-disconnects.md`

## Importante

Questo PR introduce il confine server-side e i test. Le chiamate legacy a `activateTimersForUser` nel polling e nel servizio stato devono essere rimosse nel follow-up frontend/server prima del merge finale, altrimenti il vecchio comportamento può ancora attivare timer durante il polling. Non considero quindi questa patch da sola la migrazione completa.

## Fuori scope

Non modifica budget, acquisizione giocatori o regole d’asta. Il fix dei `locked_credits` in chiusura definitiva deve essere una PR separata perché richiede rivedere l’ordine delle query in `processAuctionWinner` e testare più offerenti con auto-bid.

author: educlopez
body:
## What

Adds `pull_request` to the `CLI Windows` triggers, and adds `.goreleaser.yaml` to its path filter.

## Why

The suite only ran on push to main, a nightly, and manual dispatch — so it blocked nothing. When it went red, nobody was waiting on it. Five Windows-only bugs reached users that way, including one where rollback deleted the user's own files.

The stated reason for keeping it out of the PR matrix was cost: Windows runners are slow enough to tax every PR that has nothing to do with Windows, and a merge gate plus a nightly would catch breakage within a day. Measured, the job takes **about 90 seconds**. And "within a day" is not what happened — catching a failure requires someone to be looking at a workflow that does not block anything.

The path filter keeps it off PRs that do not touch the CLI, so the cost lands where the risk is. `main` is unprotected, so a skipped run cannot leave a PR hanging on a check that never reports.

`.goreleaser.yaml` joins the filter because the self-update tests read it to render the archive name they assert against. The archive-name mismatch was the original bug behind self-update, so a change to that template alone has to run this suite — it is where the zip-instead-of-tar.gz decision lives.

## Deliberately not split

There is a tempting alternative: a small "release blockers" subset gating PRs, with the full suite elsewhere. That shape exists to stop a backlog of known platform failures from holding up releases. This suite has no backlog — it is green in every package — so there is nothing to quarantine, and splitting it would only create somewhere for failures to hide.

## Testing

This PR touches `.github/workflows/cli-windows.yml`, which is in the filter it edits, so it triggers the gate it adds. `CLI Windows` appearing as a check on this PR *is* the verification.

author: kerrokapple
body:
## 问题

#216 合并后，main 的 `4f80135` **没有任何 workflow run**——不是红，是压根没跑。

原因链：该分支上跑过 `update-goldens`，机器人留下一条提交

```
test(golden): regenerate baselines on ubuntu runner [skip ci]
```

squash 合并时 GitHub 把各条 commit message 并进 squash commit 的 **body**，`[skip ci]` 随之进入 main 的提交信息，于是 `ci` / `smoke` / `secret-scan` 三个 workflow 全被静默跳过。

内容本身是验过的（#216 的 CI 对同一棵树跑绿），但 main 缺绿色记录。而且**这坑会复发**：任何跑过 `update-goldens` 的分支合并后都会中招——而那正是 UI 改动的必经流程。

## 修

**① `ci.yml` 加 `workflow_dispatch`**
原先只有 `push: [main]` 和 `pull_request` 两个触发，被 skip 之后无从补救。加上手动触发后可以对 main 补跑。

**② PLAYBOOK 记录**
- §2.3：写清传染路径（update-goldens 机器人提交 → squash body → main 被 skip）与补跑方式
- §1 第 7 步：合并后复核那句补一层——「**没有 run**」和「**红**」是两种不同的不绿，前者容易误读成"还没跑完"，要按 commit SHA 核对而不是看最新几行

## 这个 PR 自身就是补跑

本 PR 的 commit body 不含 `[skip ci]`，合并后 main 会正常触发一次完整 CI，把绿色记录补回来。
