author: fahd070
body:
## Summary
- Resolves audit finding F-6 (MEDIUM): Express `trust proxy` was never configured while the backend runs behind Render's reverse proxy, so `req.ip` / `express-rate-limit`'s client-IP detection defaulted to Express's `false` default.
- Verified topology before applying anything: `render.yaml` confirms a native Node "Web Service" (`runtime: node`), `docs/DEPLOY-RENDER.md`'s architecture diagram shows a direct Electron → Render Web Service path with no CDN/WAF in front, and the app is reached exclusively via Render's own default `onrender.com` domain (confirmed via every health check throughout this project's history) — no evidence of any additional proxy hop. Render's own docs confirm their load balancer terminates TLS and forwards over HTTP to the service (one hop), and express-rate-limit's official docs explicitly recommend `trust proxy: 1` for exactly this single-PaaS-proxy topology (naming Render/Heroku as examples).
- Added exactly one line: `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`, placed immediately after `express()` and before all other middleware (including `helmet()` and the rate limiters) so every downstream consumer of `req.ip`/`req.protocol` sees the corrected value.
- Deliberately **not** `true` — inspected `express-rate-limit`'s own source (`node_modules/express-rate-limit/dist/index.cjs`) and confirmed it explicitly rejects `trust proxy: true` as `ERR_ERL_PERMISSIVE_TRUST_PROXY` ("allows anyone to trivially bypass IP-based rate limiting"), which is exactly the failure mode `1` avoids.
- Also found, from the same source inspection, the actual current-state defect this PR fixes: with `trust proxy` unset (defaults to `false`), express-rate-limit's `keyGenerator` throws `ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR` on every request that carries an `X-Forwarded-For` header (i.e. every real Render request) — caught internally and only `console.error`-logged (not a hard failure), but it means **every single production request has been logging this warning**, and worse, `req.ip` was falling back to `req.socket.remoteAddress` (Render's own internal edge IP) for every request — collapsing every real user's rate-limit bucket into one shared bucket keyed by Render's proxy, not the actual client.

## Test plan
- [x] 8 new focused tests (`packages/backend/tests/trustProxy.test.ts`) against the real Express app + real rate limiters, verified via `x-ratelimit-remaining` bucket tracking: a single `X-Forwarded-For` entry resolves as the client's own bucket; a spoofed left-most entry prepended to a real right-most entry is ignored (only the right-most/trusted-hop entry is used); a long crafted multi-address chain still only trusts the one configured hop; two different simulated client IPs get independent buckets (not collapsed); the real, unchanged `authLimiter` (max=50) still returns 429 after exactly 50 requests; an uninvolved IP is unaffected by another IP's exhausted bucket; a direct/no-XFF request behaves safely; and `console.error` is confirmed to no longer log any `ERR_ERL_*` warning — all pass
- [x] Full backend regression suite — 102/102 tests pass across 15 files (94 previous + 8 new), no other test affected
- [x] Backend `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `packages/web` production build — clean (unaffected, no frontend files touched)
- [x] `packages/unified-app` build (electron-vite + electron-builder) — clean (unaffected)
- [x] `git diff --check` clean
- [x] No frontend source changed, no Prisma files changed, no auth logic changed, no rate-limit thresholds changed (both limiters' `windowMs`/`max` values are byte-identical to before), no production secrets/config changed

Out of scope, deliberately untouched: F-5 (Electron), F-7 (react-router), F-8 (dashboard duplicate deletion routes), F-9 (VITE_API_URL), localStorage JWT architecture, pre-existing TypeScript/test issues from earlier fixes.

author: iharbury
body: Prove that converting an ordinal Decimal finite increasing arithmetic progression yields a finite general progression. ### Approach - `tryGetElement_le_limit`: every returned element is ≤ the progression limit. - `le_of_tryGetElement_eq_some`: the Peano index is ≤ the element's `toPeano` (using that the common difference is positive). - `toProgression_finite`: at index `successor limit.toPeano`, a returned value would need to be both ≥ that index and ≤ `limit.toPeano`, which is impossible. Helpers mirror the existing Ordinal Peano `FiniteArithmeticIncreasing` proofs, adapted via `toPeano` / `add_toPeano`.

author: emabello
body:
## Il punto di partenza

Dopo la ripartizione introdotta nella #9 restava una domanda senza risposta: **dove finiscono i soldi del giroconto?** Finivano in `spese`, ma quella sezione era una pagina di sola lettura con scritto *"l'inserimento non è ancora attivo: per ora la scrittura passa dal database"*. Il denaro arrivava dove non si poteva guardare.

Qui il conto personale diventa una sezione vera, e l'audit dell'app tira fuori tre bug — tutti attorno al giroconto, tutti silenziosi.

---

## 1. Il conto personale

| Pagina | Cosa fa |
|---|---|
| `/spese` | dashboard: saldo del mese, ultimi movimenti, **quanto è arrivato dalla P.IVA** |
| `/spese/movimenti` | elenco con filtri per anno, mese, tipo, categoria e testo; ripartizione delle uscite per categoria |
| `/spese/movimenti/nuovo` · `/<id>` | inserimento e modifica |
| `/spese/risparmi` | periodi di stipendio, risparmio consigliato ed effettivo |

Più le API: `/spese/api/movimenti` (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE), `/spese/api/categorie`, `/spese/api/risparmi` (GET, PATCH).

**I giroconti si vedono**: la dashboard ha un blocco dedicato col totale dell'anno e il link a quei movimenti, la lista ha un KPI *"Dalla P.IVA"* e ogni riga il suo marchio.

**I risparmi seguono i periodi di stipendio**, non i mesi solari: è così che ragiona `v_periodi_stipendio`, e la pagina si limita a leggerlo invece di reinventare un calcolo parallelo.

**Le categorie sono a due livelli**: la sottocategoria si popola in base alla categoria e rispetta gli accoppiamenti ammessi da `cfg_categoria_sottocategoria`. Non è testo libero, e il form rifiuta le coppie non previste.

### Un solo posto che scrive

Tutta la scrittura passa da `spese/dati.py`, che è l'unico modulo a conoscere le regole di quella tabella:

- `mese` e `anno` sono NOT NULL senza default e vanno ricavati dalla data;
- l'id si assegna col primo libero, tramite `insert_spesa_first_free_id`;
- la categoria è un rimando a `cfg_categoria_sottocategoria`, non un testo;
- l'importo è sempre positivo: la direzione la dà `tipo`.

**Il giroconto della ripartizione ora usa quello stesso livello** invece della copia che si era portato dietro. Due copie delle stesse regole prima o poi divergono, e qui divergere significa scrivere movimenti che il budget personale non vede.

---

## 2. I bug trovati nell'audit

### Il KPI della launchpad ignorava i giroconti

`kpi_spese` sommava solo `entrata` e `uscita`. Il saldo del conto personale risultava più basso del vero di **tutto quello arrivato dalla P.IVA** — proprio i soldi che la ripartizione ci aveva appena messo.

### Una fattura già ripartita poteva uscire da "incassata"

Nessuna guardia impediva di riportarla a `trasmessa_sdi` o `annullata`. I due movimenti restavano sui conti senza più un incasso a giustificarli: conto P.IVA alleggerito, personale gonfiato, e niente che lo segnalasse. Ora l'endpoint risponde 409 e spiega che va prima annullata la ripartizione.

### Il movimento nato da un giroconto era cancellabile

Dalla sua pagina si poteva eliminare metà spostamento, lasciando l'altra riga sul conto P.IVA senza contropartita. Ora l'endpoint rifiuta con 409, il pulsante non compare, e la pagina dice dove annullare la ripartizione per intero.

---

## 3. Pulizia e documentazione

Eliminati: tre guide superate (`GUIDA_messa_online.md`, `STEP1_README.md`, `STEP2_README.md`), nove file di migrazione, due README secondari e la query di dump.

**Il `README.md` è ora l'unico documento**: architettura e mappa dei file, le tre aree con le rotte, modello dati completo (tabelle, viste, funzioni), logica fiscale con le formule, i quattro scenari di accantonamento, il ciclo di vita della fattura, **le trappole del database**, sicurezza, deploy e convenzioni di sviluppo.

Le migrazioni **non ancora applicate** e la query di ispezione dello schema sono dentro il README, con l'SQL per intero: eliminare i file non ha fatto perdere nulla.

---

## Verifiche

- **Tutte e 31 le rotte GET** rese con un database simulato: rispondono, nessuna eccezione.
- **Sezione spese**: sei pagine verificate sul contenuto reale; API testate su percorso felice, tipo non valido, importo a zero, eliminazione di un movimento da giroconto (409) e di uno normale (200), importo negativo normalizzato a positivo.
- **Guardia sul cambio stato**: cinque casi — con e senza ripartizione, avanti e indietro lungo il percorso.
- **Giroconto dopo il refactor**: verificato che passi dalla funzione del database con `mese`, `anno` e **categoria** valorizzati, e che il ripiego sull'insert diretto li valorizzi allo stesso modo. La categoria è il campo che, se nullo, farebbe sparire il movimento dal calcolo del risparmio.
- **SQL del README**: estratto dal file e rieseguito su PostgreSQL 16 con una replica dello schema, due volte, per verificare che sia valido e idempotente.

## Da eseguire su Supabase

Le tre migrazioni della [sezione 8 del README](README.md#8-migrazioni-da-eseguire), in ordine: categoria del giroconto, vista fiscale e RLS, dati dell'emittente.

La RLS su `spese` e `risparmi_periodo` resta commentata di proposito: se un altro client legge quelle tabelle con la chiave anon, attivarla lo taglierebbe fuori: e le `cfg_*` hanno già una policy di lettura che suggerisce che qualcosa lo faccia.

No need to use a third-party library when this functionality is available in the Java Platform.

Part of the effort to remove Commons Lang 2 from Jenkins core — jenkinsci/jenkins#16404,
jenkinsci/jenkins#26105. Commons Lang 2 is EOL and carries an unfixed advisory
(GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v).

## What's changed
- `StringUtils.isBlank` → `Util.fixEmptyAndTrim(x) == null`, across 8 files. Several arrived via

- `StringUtils.join(collection, sep)` → `String.join(sep, collection)`; `StringUtils.EMPTY` → `""`;
  `StringUtils.replace(a, b, c)` → `a.replace(b, c)`.
- Removed an import of `io.jenkins.cli.shaded.org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils` in
  `CodeScanBuildStepTest` — that is the copy of Commons Lang shaded inside the Jenkins CLI jar, almost

Spotless.

The `ban-commons-lang-2` enforcer rule was left disabled because it needs parent POM

author: anthonykewl20
body:
## Slice

Closes #86 · Closes #87 · Closes #89  ·  Slice id: `COMPILER-GENERALITY`  ·  Milestone: `Milestone 1 - Authentication Vertical Slice`

> ⚠️ **Do not merge until #88 reconciles `auth-domain-pack` (cross-slice).** See *"Cross-slice dependency"* below. This PR is `STATUS: blocked` on that one test by design.

## What & why

Three compiler-generality fixes that came out of the #27 M1-EXIT de-risk spike, done sequentially in one branch because all three edit `spec-generator.ts` / `compile-policy.ts`:

- **#89** — the reviewed `nonSemanticLocatorRationale` was a *blanket*: one rationale approved **any** CSS/XPath locator in the whole generated source. The gate now approves **only** the exact `page.locator('form')` form-scope shape (and only with a rationale); every other non-semantic locator (`page.locator('#x')`, `page.$`, `page.$$`, `xpath=`, bare CSS `locator(`) is blocked regardless of rationale, and `page.locator('form')` without a rationale is blocked too.
- **#87** — the goto route and `url:` assertion were derived from the workflow IR alone (state name → path; exact `toHaveURL`). The entry-state goto now resolves from the **runtime observation url** (first required transition's `from`) so single-page apps no longer need state-name tricks; `url:` now emits an anchored RegExp that is exact on origin+pathname but tolerant of query/fragment, so redirects like `/?message=Logged%20in` no longer fail while genuinely wrong routes still fail.
- **#86** — single-input submits (email-only form) stayed ambiguous when ≥2 forms share the label. The form-scope locator now also requires a semantic submit-button filter and emits `await expect(form).toHaveCount(1);` so residual ambiguity surfaces as a clear failure instead of a cryptic strict-mode violation.

## Semantics chosen (judgement calls — for the integrator)

- **#87 goto:** the runtime `EvidenceRef.url` is the actually-observed surface URL. The entry state = the `from` of the first *required* transition (the observed surface); that transition's goto reproduces the runtime url. Later transitions fall back to state-name-derived `statePath`, since the single runtime observation only covers the entry.
- **#87 `url:` match:** `^<escaped expectedUrl>(?:[?#].*)?$` — exact origin+pathname; `?query` and `#fragment` ignored. `url:/` matches `http://h/`, `http://h/?m=x`, `http://h/#y`; rejects `http://h/login`, `http://h/dashboard`, wrong origin.
- **#86 limitation (explicit):** the Workflow IR carries **no** submit-button accessible name, so two forms sharing both the input label *and* a matching submit button (e.g. Express Login + Forgot, both `Email` + a submit button matching the broad regex) **cannot** be disambiguated from the IR — the `toHaveCount(1)` guard surfaces this clearly rather than silently picking one. The submit-button filter narrows where it can (non-submit forms).

## Cross-slice dependency (read before merging)

**This PR does not touch `packages/auth-domain-pack` (owned by #88), but #87 invalidates a stale expectation there.** The vulnerable-auth-app login candidate now `verify`s where it was `contradicted`: the old `contradicted` was a false negative (the compiler hardcoded a `/login` goto the Express app does not serve). This makes `packages/auth-domain-pack/src/real-world.test.ts:74-77` fail in CI. Reconciling it (which of login/logout/password-change flip; needs a full pack re-run) is **#88's job**, not a one-line fix, so this PR's CI is red on that one test by design. **Merge order:** land #88's expectation update (rebased onto this compiler behaviour) before/with this PR. The reference-auth-app auth-domain-pack path is unaffected (no regression). See `docs/_slice-notes/COMPILER-GENERALITY.md` for the handoff block.

## Engineering checklist (charter §3–§6)

- [x] **Seams**: `generateSpec` (service) + `enforceCompilePolicy` (action/gate) + the frozen `WorkflowCompiler.compile` contract
- [x] **Sad paths RED-FIRST**, mapped to truth states: unrationed/second CSS locator → `blocked`; `page.locator('form')` w/o rationale → `blocked`; `page.$$` → `blocked`; two real forms sharing Email+submit → `blocked` (count guard); runtime entry URL ≠ state path → `observed`; query/fragment URL suffix → `observed`
- [x] **Real-world proof**: real Playwright 1.62.1 Chromium against the real vulnerable Express app — observes the two Email-labelled submit forms, exercises the residual-ambiguity `toHaveCount(1)` failure, and compiles the observed entry URL; both fixture apps stay compiler-discoverable (`real-world.test.ts` + `generality.real-world.test.ts`)
- [x] Happy path last
- [x] **Layering**: spec emission is the service mechanic; the policy decision (which locator shapes are permitted) stays in `compile-policy.ts`
- [x] No `skip`/`fixme`/`only`, no assertion weakening, no success-by-quarantine

## Gates

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` green (repo-wide)

author: octalide
body:
Closes #2570

Stacked on #2638 → #2631. Merge those first, in that order.

## The declaration surface

The issue left the channel open between the attribute and decorator channels and asked for one to be picked and documented. **The decorator channel**, since that is where codegen directives live now:

```mach
#[stage("vertex")]
fun vertex_main() { }

#[stage("compute")] #[workgroup(64, 1, 1)]
fun compute_main() { }
```

One directive with a closed, sema-checked value set (`"vertex"` / `"fragment"` / `"compute"`) rather than a decorator per stage. Execution models are the obvious axis this grows along, and adding tessellation, geometry, or a ray-tracing model is now **one constant, one row in the accepted table, one row in the model mapping** — no new decorator, no new plumbing. An unrecognized value is a compile error rather than a module that quietly forms no stage.

Documented in `doc/language/decorators.md`: both directives get a section, the grammar block, and the applicability table.

## A staged function's signature

It takes **no parameters and returns nothing**, checked in the backend and reported against the function that declared the stage. A pipeline stage has no caller — its inputs arrive through input interface variables and its results leave through output ones, so there is no argument list or return value to carry them. Leaving this to `spirv-val` would report it as a type mismatch on a generated id.

## The consequence that reaches furthest

**A module is now a shader module or a library module, never both.**

A library module (no stage anywhere) declares the `Linkage` capability and publishes each function as a `LinkageAttributes` export. That is right for compiled mach code a consumer links against, and it is what the backend has always emitted. **Vulkan forbids that capability outright:**

```
error: Capability Linkage is not allowed by Vulkan 1.3 specification
  OpCapability Linkage
```

So the presence of any entry point drops `Linkage` and every linkage export with it. Both kinds are valid SPIR-V; they answer to different consumers. Adding the first `#[stage(...)]` to a module therefore stops it exporting its functions — a real behavioural cliff, so it is called out in the decorator docs.

**Entry point names are the bare source name**, not the mangled linkage name. `OpEntryPoint Vertex %1 "vertex_main"`, not `"_M4case4mainN11vertex_main"`. It is a lookup key a pipeline-creation call passes, and a shader module has no linker symbols to mangle.

## Execution modes are emitted, not delegated

A fragment stage without a framebuffer origin and a compute stage without a workgroup size are not stages a consumer can use, so the backend emits both with the stage:

```
OpEntryPoint Vertex %1 "vs"
OpEntryPoint Fragment %2 "fs"
OpEntryPoint GLCompute %3 "cs"
OpExecutionMode %2 OriginUpperLeft
OpExecutionMode %3 LocalSize 64 1 1
```

`OriginUpperLeft` is the only origin Vulkan permits. `#[workgroup(...)]` is optional and defaults to the single-invocation `(1, 1, 1)`, but the mode is always emitted.

## Validation — this is where the issue's acceptance actually bites

`spirv-val` is available here. **The universal environment checks none of the rules above** — not the Linkage prohibition, not the mandatory origin, not the mandatory workgroup size. Validating a shader module universally would have passed while a real Vulkan consumer refused it, which is exactly this repo's recurring defect shape.

So the int harness grows a **`spirv-val-vulkan`** producer, and `int/surface/spirv-entrypoint` is validated against `--target-env vulkan1.3`. The existing three spirv cases stay on the universal environment, correctly: they are library modules and *cannot* satisfy Vulkan, by design.

The issue's second acceptance item — "entry-point interface rules (Input/Output variable lists on `OpEntryPoint`) are emitted correctly" — is met as far as it can be here: the interface list is **empty**, which is valid for a stage that reads and writes no interface variables. #2571 fills it in, and that is the coordination the issue anticipated.

## Files outside the SPIR-V backend

Flagging explicitly, since the track is otherwise backend-local. A declaration surface cannot live in the backend, so this touches three shared files, all additively:

- `src/lang/fe/sema.mach` — validate the two directives
- `src/lang/me/ir.mach` — `stage` / `wg_x` / `wg_y` / `wg_z` on `ir.Function`
- `src/lang/me/lower/decl.mach` — read them off the decorators

None is on the owned-elsewhere list for this session, but a reviewer should confirm no collision.

## Checks

- `mach test .` — 1198 passed, 0 failed
- `int/run.sh --target linux` — full suite green
- self-host fixpoint: stage b == stage c, byte-identical

body: ## What Implements **N7f.1**: after an accepted `move_unit`, the client gates further **local input** until the moved unit's real visual arrival — rapid clicking can no longer submit a second move mid-walk and skip the intended arrival moment. Independent of `cursor/n7f-uphill-foot-ik` (PR #5); branched from verified `origin/main`. ## How - **`game/presentation/world/world_units_view.gd`** — new `unit_arrived(unit_id)` signal, emitted **exactly once** per completed glide at the exact final-anchor pose (locomotion entry removed, Idle resumed). Never emitted for spawns, identical reapplies, ordinary idling, degenerate settlements, or units removed mid-glide. Presentation output only; locomotion/grounding untouched. - **`game/cloud/world_play/world_interaction_state.gd`** — arrival gate bound to the exact moved unit id + accepted revision. While active: every pick kind is inert, End Turn is disabled, destination rows are hidden and unsubmittable, snapshot-apply directives are `{summary: false, selection: false}` (no legality fetched), the moved-unit selection is preserved, and the status line reads "unit moving…". `try_release_arrival_gate` accepts only the gated unit; gated-unit removal, turn loss, and different-revision authoritative snapshots resolve the gate safely (reconnect/bootstrap can never keep or infer one). - **`game/cloud/world_play/cloud_world_play.gd`** — only an accepted `move_unit` with a usable snapshot enters the gate, **before** the snapshot applies; the authoritative snapshot and root anchor still apply immediately (gameplay never waits for animation). Degenerate/synchronous settlement releases the gate in the same submit call (no deadlock); accepted-without-snapshot fails visibly and never gates; a matching arrival triggers exactly one current-revision summary (+ still-valid selection) refetch, from which markers/End Turn return. Camera and F12 capture stay usable; `_request_busy` remains a separate transport concern. ## Review follow-up (commit `3ab8a16`) - **Pending-request race fixed:** while a move POST was in flight (`_request_busy`), `_on_terrain_picked` could still classify picks and change/clear the selection before the accepted response entered the gate (no second POST, but the gate then bound the moved unit while the UI held the wrong selection). Every terrain gameplay pick is now inert while `_request_busy` is active — guarded before any classification, selection mutation, or submission. End Turn was already guarded; camera/F12 never route through picks; transport-busy and the arrival gate remain separate states. - **Deferred-response regression:** the scripted session gains a genuinely asynchronous mode (POST suspends on a signal across a real process frame). The new test reproduces the race (fails without the guard) and proves: own-unit / empty / destination / miss / cliff picks plus End Turn during the pending POST change nothing, selection stays unit 1, served rows stay unchanged, exactly one POST exists; on resolution the snapshot applies, the gate binds to unit 1 + the accepted revision, unit 1 stays selected, and no legality is fetched before the visual arrival. - **Degenerate/no-glide regression:** an accepted `move_unit` whose applied snapshot starts no glide (unit stays at its anchor) releases the just-entered gate **synchronously** through the existing degenerate-settlement path — no false `unit_arrived` needed, no permanent lock, no duplicate release/refetch, exactly one summary + still-valid-selection refresh. No production change was required for this path. ## Authority boundary (permanent rule, recorded) The client arrival gate is **pacing/visibility only** — never gameplay authority and never the sole anti-skip enforcement. Mandatory future on-entry outcomes must be server-atomic with movement or server-owned pending interaction state (`docs/CLOUD_PLAY.md`, `docs/DECISION_LOG.md`). ## Tests (T2, all green) - New `game/presentation/tests/test_world_units_arrival_event.gd` — 19 checks (exactly-once semantics, exact-pose timing, retarget/removal/reapply/multi-unit cases). - `test_world_interaction_state.gd` — 88 checks (arrival-gate section added). - `test_cloud_world_play_interaction.gd` — 66 checks (scripted-session production wiring incl. the **rapid-click single-POST proof**, the **pending-POST inertness race regression**, the **degenerate/no-glide synchronous release**, no fetch during locomotion, wrong-unit arrival inert, rejection/transport/no-snapshot/non-move never gating). - Runner: new `slice n7f1`; arrival test added to `slice n7` and the full list. Full `slice n7` + `slice n7f` green. `full`/`cloud`/`presentation` profiles skipped per TESTING.md T2 policy for a focused slice. ## Docs `PHASE_PLAN.md` (N7f.1 row — **one-PC/manual gate PENDING**), `CLOUD_PLAY.md` (N7f.1 + permanent boundary rule), `UNITS.md`, `TESTING.md` (slice n7f1), `VALIDATION_CHECKLIST.md` (N7f.1 manual gate section), `DECISION_LOG.md` (boundary-rule decision). ## Manual gate **PENDING** — Niclas's one-PC verification (rapid clicking cannot double-move, controls hidden while walking, re-enable exactly at arrival) per the new checklist section.

author: wombat164
body:
What the scale cannot see: fat and fat-free mass, derived (#46, G36)

`schema.py` has stated the intent plainly for a long time - `kg` and
`body_fat_pct` are the OBSERVED atoms, fat mass and fat-free mass are DERIVED
from them and never stored - and nothing was built.

A weight goal is a proxy. What an athlete usually wants is less fat, and scale
weight is a lossy stand-in that also moves with water, glycogen and muscle.
Two cuts ending at the same weight can be opposite outcomes, and a weight-only
view says one went down and one went up and stops there. On the shipped record
the rollup now says: -3.1 kg overall, fat -2.8, everything else -0.3, and 91
per cent of the change was fat.

MOSTLY A REFUSAL, which is the half worth having. Both figures are arithmetic
on a bioimpedance estimate, and exact arithmetic on an input that cannot
support it, presented as a measurement, is the failure this project already
names as a 0 m elevation out of GPS noise.

THE BAND COMES FROM THE RECORD, NOT FROM THE LITERATURE, and this is the one
place I deviated from the issue's own framing. It cites a repeatability figure
of 2 to 3 percentage points; adopting that would be the engine asserting an
accuracy claim about hardware it has never seen, which is the per-source
accuracy claim it refuses everywhere else. The issue answers itself two
paragraphs later: `kg_lo`/`kg_hi` and `body_fat_lo`/`body_fat_hi` are the
band, and this is where they earn their place.

So a change is resolvable when the two readings' fat-mass INTERVALS DO NOT
OVERLAP. No constant appears anywhere in the module, and a test asserts that.

Three answers rather than two. Resolvable, where the intervals separate. Not
resolvable, where they overlap - reported as NOT RESOLVABLE with no share,
because a percentage of a difference nothing observed is a figure invented by
division. And unknown, where the reading declared no band at all: treating
that as "not resolvable" would blame the instrument for the record's silence.

FIVE FIELDS GOT THEIR FIRST WRITER AND THEIR FIRST READER IN ONE CHANGE.
`body_fat_pct`, `kg_lo`, `kg_hi`, `body_fat_lo` and `body_fat_hi` were all on
the field-population backlog, and `kg_lo`/`kg_hi` were the register's own
worked example of "the producer exists and works, and there is no consumer".
The demo gains two clinic scans rather than composition on every row, because
a home scale reporting mass only is the shape of most records - and a fixture
carrying the point estimates without the bands would exercise the arithmetic
and none of the refusal.

Six mutations run, each confirmed to land.

Closes #46.

author: yuens1002
body:
**Version:** 0.4.104 → 0.4.105

Closes #237.

## What was broken

`scripts/db-push.ts` has no migration-tracking table — it replays every `.sql` in filename order under `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`. That's a fine design, but it requires every migration to be re-runnable, and five weren't. The earliest sorts first:

```
create table public_profile (   -- ERROR: relation already exists
```

So `npm run db:push` died on **line 4 of file 1 of 16** against an existing database. Nothing after it ever ran. Every migration since has had to be applied by hand — which is how the #235 privacy guard nearly shipped without its SQL.

## The part the issue didn't anticipate: the duplicates already existed

Eight indexes were declared without a name. Unnamed `create index` **never errors on replay** — PostgreSQL just auto-generates a fresh name. So rather than failing loudly, a past re-run silently built byte-identical second copies:

| index | size |
|---|---|
| `thoughts_embedding_idx1` | **31 MB** — hnsw, re-maintained on every write |
| `thoughts_metadata_idx1` | 400 kB |
| `thoughts_created_at_idx1` | 136 kB |
| 5 × `…_idx1` on job-hunt tables | 16 kB each |

~32 MB of storage, but the real cost was write amplification: every insert or update to `thoughts` maintained **two** HNSW vector indexes.

Confirmed identical by normalising `indexdef` and grouping — not by trusting the naming convention to imply it.

## Fix

Per statement type:

- **tables** → `create table if not exists`
- **indexes** → named with the identifiers PostgreSQL *originally assigned*, then `if not exists`. This is the trap in the obvious fix: any other name leaves the original in place and builds a third copy.
- **policies / triggers** → `drop … if exists` before create. PostgreSQL has neither `create policy if not exists` nor `create trigger if not exists`.
- **seed row** → `on conflict (id) do nothing`

Plus `20260807000000_drop_duplicate_indexes.sql` to remove the existing duplicates, guarded with `if exists` so it's a no-op on a fresh project.

Editing historical migrations is safe here precisely because there's no tracking table — the files *are* the state, and they're replayed from scratch anyway.

## Test plan — verified against production

- [x] `npm run db:push` **twice consecutively**: both exit 0, second run reports **0 errors**
- [x] Indexes **27 → 19** — exactly the eight duplicates, nothing else
- [x] `public_profile` still **1 row** (the `on conflict` guard works)
- [x] `thoughts` still **4181 rows** — no data touched
- [x] Canonical indexes intact: `thoughts_embedding_idx`, `_metadata_idx`, `_created_at_idx`, `_content_hash_idx`, `_pkey`
- [x] Policies (1 on `thoughts`) and trigger `thoughts_updated_at` still present after drop-then-create
- [x] #235 privacy guard survives the replay — `match_thoughts` GUARDED, `match_thoughts_owner` UNGUARDED, `match_thoughts_public` GUARDED
- [x] `POST /query` and `GET /info` both 200 afterwards
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run test:unit` 548 tests, 0 failures

author: vjt
body:
Refs #579. Client-only; the server has accepted the full RFC 2812 §3.4.2
shape since #571.

## What

`lusers: (_verb, _rest) => ({ kind: "lusers" })` discarded `rest`, so a
user's arguments never reached the wire. The parsed type is now
`{ kind: "lusers"; mask: string | null; server: string | null }`, split
positionally like `/stats`' `query` + `target`, and both tokens thread
through `pushLusers` to the existing `lusers` verb.

Naming follows the server's `server` (not `target`), per the issue.

## `server` without `mask`

That is the shape `validate_lusers_args/2` rejects as `:invalid_line`. A
positional parse cannot BUILD it, so there is no reachable input for a
client-side rejection to refuse — the mirror is an unconstructible state
rather than a runtime guard, and the guard would be dead code.

An invariant test pins the property instead, and it is not vacuous:
`/whois`'s two-arg form is `<server> <nick>` (server FIRST), so copying
that order here would make the one-token form yield exactly the mask-less
shape the server refuses. Measured — the test fails against that mutation.

## What the args actually do on bahamut

Read `azzurra/bahamut` `src/s_serv.c` while writing this: `m_lusers` calls
`hunt_server` only when BOTH tokens are present, and the answering server
reports its own local counts — the two-token routed form is the one with a
visible effect. `send_lusers` never `match()`es the mask, so a mask alone
is accepted and ignored there; its forced cache-bypass wants oper AND a
fourth parameter, which grappa's 2-slot path cannot produce. We still send
the mask: an RFC-honouring ircd may filter on it, and dropping user input
is the bug. The third commit corrects the earlier comments accordingly.

## Wire

Additive: the `lusers` verb is unchanged and a null arg omits its key
(pushMotd/pushLinks' shape), so a bare `/lusers` sends byte-identical
params to a pre-#579 client. No `protocol_version` bump.

## Gates

- `bun run check` (biome + tsc) — exit 0.
- `bun run test` — 244 files / 4538 tests, exit 0.
- Mutation-measured: the payload tests fail against a `pushLusers` that
  ignores its new args; the parser invariant fails against the `/whois`
  argument order.

## Not verified

No e2e. Per the source above, the single-token form is NOT observable on
bahamut by construction. The two-token form would be — the e2e testnet is
a real mesh (hub + leaf-v4 + leaf-v6) and `/lusers * hub.azzurra.chat`
should return the hub's local counts rather than leaf4's — but I could not
run the e2e lane in this pass, and I am not shipping a spec I never
executed. Flagged for the orchestrator rather than guessed at.

author: nayeem-ahmad
body:
Two commits: the costing engine, then the reports built on it.

## 1. Weighted-average costing (`a60b3d2`)

A sale snapshotted `unit_cost_at_sale` from the newest `ProductPrice.cost` — a standard cost someone typed into the catalog, which drifted from real buying prices the moment a supplier changed a rate.

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Grain | **Per product, tenant-wide** (`ProductCost`). Transfers are pure quantity moves; every report agrees on what a unit cost. |
| Precision | `Decimal(12,4)` — rounding to paisa per receipt compounds over a few hundred movements. |
| Existing data | Replay history **and restate past sales**. |
| Basis | Per-tenant `costing_method` (`WEIGHTED_AVERAGE` default, `LATEST_COST` = old behaviour). |

All averaging rules live in one pure function (`applyToPool`), called from `applyInventoryMovement` — so all 36 stock-touching call sites go through one chokepoint, and the backfill replays through the *identical* function. Movement types are `REVALUE` / `REVERSE_RECEIPT` / **`QUANTITY_ONLY` by default**, so an unclassified type can move stock but never silently revalue the pool.

Fixed along the way: three callers passed a **selling price as a cost** (opening stock, shrinkage write-offs, both sale paths), and manufacturing disagreed with itself — jobs valued materials at standard cost while the stock came out of a real one, and finished goods entered at the *output product's catalog cost* rather than what the run cost.

## 2. Gross-profit reports (`ea719d7`)

Three arithmetic bugs first, since the new reports would inherit them:

- **Uncosted lines counted as free stock** — `cost*qty : 0` in four places gave a line with no basis zero COGS, so it read as 100% margin. The dashboard already did this correctly, so one tenant saw two different figures depending on the screen.
- **Returns reduced revenue but never reversed COGS** — every refund overstated profit by the full cost of the returned goods. New nullable `SalesReturnItem.unit_cost_at_return`, taken from the original sale line where there is one; goods go back at the cost they left at, so a refund books no profit of its own.
- **Invoice discounts never reached line-level margin** — `discountAmount` and loyalty reduce `total_amount` while `price_at_sale` stays at list. Fixed by a pro-rata ratio at report time: no schema change, and it self-corrects all history.

These now live in `gross-profit.utils.ts`, which reduces every revenue-bearing event — sale line or return line — to a **signed `MarginLine`**, so a return is a negative line and needs no special case downstream. An uncosted line is excluded from **both** sides of the margin, and a margin with no basis is **null, never zero** — "we cannot say" is not "we broke even". Every figure carries a `coverage` block so a thin basis is visible rather than inferred.

**Five reports** behind `VIEW_FINANCIAL_REPORTS` (cost is not price and shouldn't share a permission):

| Report | Answers |
|---|---|
| By product | Which products actually earn, ranked by profit not revenue |
| By salesperson / counter | Margin by who rang it up — commission on profit, not discounting |
| Margin exceptions | Every line under a floor, judged on the **discounted** price |
| Margin bridge | Volume / price / cost / mix, effects always summing to the total |
| Cost coverage | The list that makes the other four defensible |

`by-customer` and `by-category` gained COGS and margin — the customer one answers "which credit customer are we selling to at a loss", which nothing in the system could previously say. `getSalesSummary` keeps invoice totals for the top line and allocated lines for attribution, and now buckets days in **Dhaka time** rather than UTC, which had been putting evening takings on the previous day.

Five frontend pages under `sales/reports/gross-profit/`, en/bn/ms, `PageShell`/`PageHeader`, blue-600 only, null margins render as a dash.

## Migration

```bash
cd packages/database && npm run backfill:product-costs        # dry run
cd packages/database && npm run backfill:product-costs -- --apply
```

Rebuilds the pools, restates `unit_cost_at_sale`, and fills return costs from the restated lines. Safe because ERP71 is **periodic inventory** (`posting-contract.ts:140`) — no COGS voucher per sale, so nothing desyncs from the trial balance.

⚠️ **Until it runs, pools are empty and sales silently fall back to `ProductPrice.cost`** — the old behaviour, with nothing on screen saying so.

## Verification

- **68 new unit cases** (30 costing, 24 margin arithmetic, 14 service) covering blending, quantity-weighting, negative/zero stock, purchase-return round-trips netting to zero, no drift over 300 receipts, discount allocation reconciling to the invoice, uncosted exclusion from both sides, and bridge effects summing to the total.
- Backend **197/201 suites, 3280 tests**; frontend **207/207 suites, 2385 tests**; locale parity green; both typechecks at their known baselines (no new errors).
- **Against a real Postgres**: 10 assertions driving `applyInventoryMovement` end-to-end plus the backfill restating a sale from a standard cost of 120 to the real average of 90 (idempotent across runs); and 22 assertions driving the real reports service over a scenario carrying all three report bugs at once — a discounted sale, a partial return, and an uncosted product.

**Not verified:** the four `test/*.spec.ts` HTTP integration suites do not run in this sandbox — signup 500s on infrastructure the container lacks, at baseline as well as on this branch.

## Deferred

One item from the original list is deliberately not built: the **operational-vs-ledger tie-out**. Under periodic inventory the P&L and the sales reports legitimately differ — stock is expensed at purchase, so the P&L shows purchases where these reports show COGS of what actually sold. Reconciling them needs a decision about which basis the owner is meant to trust for tax, which is a call for you rather than a bug to fix. Filed in `TODO.md`.

新增「💰 现金流质量」标签页，数据覆盖 2001—2025 全部 25 份年报。

## 图表

| 图表 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| 经营活动现金流量净额 vs 净利润 | 利润是否有现金支撑 |
| 销售商品、提供劳务收到的现金 vs 营业收入 | 收入是否真实收到钱 |
| 收现比（销售收现 ÷ 营业收入） | 25 年每年均 >100% |
| 现金余额、资本开支、现金分红、有息负债 | 现金去向与负债水平 |

## 数据来源

新增 `extract_cashflow.py`，从 25 份年报 PDF 的「合并现金流量表」「合并资产负债表」
逐年提取，结果存入 `贵州茅台_现金流数据.json`。经营现金流序列已与报告原有
`OCF_ANNUAL` 交叉校验完全一致；2001—2006 净利润/营收已与次年年报「上期数」逐年勾稽。

## 跨年度格式差异的处理

25 年间年报格式变化较大，以下几点是提取时踩过的坑，已在脚本注释中记录：

- 董事会报告正文也会出现「销售商品、提供劳务」等科目名（2015/2016/2018 尤其明显），
  仅按关键词首次出现会抓到正文而非报表；改为先按文档位置排除前段，再取首个命中
- 2001/2002 资产负债表列序为「年初数 期末数」，与后续年份相反，需按表头判断
- 部分年份粗体标题被 pdfplumber 提取成重复字符（「合合合合并并并并」），需去重后匹配
- **2020 年起并表集团财务公司**，大量资金列示于「存放中央银行款项」而非「货币资金」，
  若沿用货币资金口径会出现失真的断崖（1220 亿 → 361 亿）。故现金余额统一采用
  现金流量表「期末现金及现金等价物余额」，口径说明已写入页面脚注

## 验证

已在本地起服务用浏览器逐张确认：4 张图均渲染正常，25 个数据点无缺失。

author: xjacka
body:
## What

Three additions in one PR (v3.1.0):

### 1. Post-onboarding structure verification (`scripts/verify-onboarding.sh`)

Wired into ONBOARDING Step 7: after the sentinel is written, the agent runs the script and repairs whatever it flags before reporting to the operator. Goal: every deployed instance ends up structurally identical, differing only in configuration values.

One-shot, fully offline, read-only structure check (same *detects, never acts* contract as `preflight.sh`; its only write is one structured log event). It verifies shape, never data:

- **Definition checkout at `$HOME`** — repo present, allowlist `.gitignore` (`/*` rule), clean `git status` (no work//secret leaks, no missing definition files), `origin` matches `definition_repo`, checkout on `definition_branch`, sentinel with a UTC timestamp, harness adapter hooks registered (Claude Code harness only).
- **`work/` state** — plain data directory (no inner `.git`); `CONFIG.md` required keys (`definition_repo`, `bot_login`, `review_marker`), owner/repo slug shapes, enum values (`slack_notifications`, `rereview_trigger`, `mention_replies`, `audit_report`, `log_level`, `stall_alert_threshold`), `artifact_skill`/`artifact_targets` formats, review-skills table shape; `MEMORY.md` template sections; `REVIEWS.md` header + row format per docs/review.md → Tracking format; `LESSONS.md`; `work/VERSION` = checked-out `VERSION`; `reviews/` + `logs/` naming; Slack coupling (roster parseable — table **or** bullet format, mirroring `preflight.sh` — and `escalation_owner` resolvable to a member with a valid `slack_id`).
- Unexpected top-level entries in `work/` are a **warn**, never a FAIL — runtime extras are surfaced, not punished.

Every `FAIL` line names the broken file and carries a `fix:` instruction (pointing to the ONBOARDING Steps 3b/4 templates or the relevant doc); the agent applies the fixes and re-runs until `PASS`. Exit 0 iff nothing failed.

### 2. Weekly audit: *Learned this week* report block

The memory consolidation (docs/audit.md task 29) already walks `MEMORY.md` at audit time; it now also collects what the agent newly learned that week — Feedback Log and Observed Insights bullets dated inside the stats window, plus rules the consolidation promoted — and the report template gets a *Learned this week* block (≤5 compressed lines, then "+N more in MEMORY.md"; explicit `nothing new` otherwise). Zero extra file reads or API calls.

### 3. `work/` confidentiality hard invariant

`work/` may hold sensitive, instance-private data (config, roster with Slack IDs, memory, review history, logs). New bullet in CLAUDE.md → **Hard invariants**: work/ data leaves the agent only as the `$GITHUB_REPO_WORK` backup or through the configured output surfaces (chat UI, target-repo reviews/comments/issues, Slack when enabled), each message carrying only what it needs; the documented definition-repo tracking issues carry error evidence at most, never config/roster/memory content. Protected from weakening in self-modification.md §10; one-sentence pointer in README → Persistence.

## Why

- Onboarded instances drifted in structure (differing roster formats, missing files, stale adopted versions) and nothing checked the result of onboarding itself. A deterministic verifier makes the expected layout explicit and gives the agent actionable repair instructions immediately, while the operator is still present.
- The audit reported memory-consolidation *counts* but not *content* — the operator had no view of what the agent actually learned from feedback each week.
- Nothing stated explicitly that work/ contents are confidential and where they may legitimately flow.

## Validation

- `bash -n` on the new script; `scripts/tests/test_verify_onboarding.sh` added (11 cases: green path, missing MEMORY section, malformed REVIEWS row, missing roster, owner outside roster, bullet-format roster, inner `work/.git`, version drift, invalid enum, extras warn-only); full `scripts/tests/run.sh` passes.
- Sanity-checked against a real deployed instance's work state (cloned read-only into a local sandbox): PASS with one legitimate warning about non-standard extras; the roster dual-format support was found this way. No instance data appears in this PR or in any commit.
- Cross-reference + size sweep done; `VERSION` 3.1.0 = newest CHANGELOG heading, bumped exactly once for the whole PR.

## Cost footprint

- Verification: one script invocation per onboarding (once per agent instance, operator-triggered) — zero heartbeat/per-run cost.
- *Learned this week*: reuses the consolidation's existing MEMORY.md pass — no extra reads or API calls; a few extra report lines per week.
- Confidentiality invariant: +1 always-loaded CLAUDE.md bullet.

body:
## Summary

1. **Current behavior:** every ffmpeg non-frame result collapses to `RTSP stream yielded no frame`.
2. **Root cause:** the byte-only helper discards ffmpeg's timeout, exit status, and stderr classification.
3. **Minimal fix:** add a typed, secret-safe frame-grab result and propagate stable failure kinds through `SnapshotAttempt`; retain the existing `bytes | None` helper contract.
4. **Risks:** classifier regressions could mislabel a failure; unknown output remains the generic `rtsp_error` category and raw stderr is never returned.
5. **Impacted components:** direct RTSP still capture and downstream snapshot diagnostics.
6. **Required tests:** success, timeout, authentication, decoder, empty-frame, fallback, URL-cache, and backward-compatibility tests.
7. **Regression estimate:** low; transport arguments and fallback order are unchanged.

Risk: medium (vendor transport diagnostics, no protocol mutation)

Tests:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_rtsp_snapshot_backend.py tests/test_snapshot_attempt_reporting.py` — 45 passed
- `ruff check src/pytvt/xml_api.py src/pytvt/device_sdk/manager.py tests/test_rtsp_snapshot_backend.py tests/test_snapshot_attempt_reporting.py`

## Autonomous checklist

- [x] Scope is limited to RTSP frame diagnostics.
- [x] Tests fail before / pass after the change.
- [x] No migrations or deployment changes.
- [x] No secrets are logged or returned; raw ffmpeg stderr is classified locally only.
- [x] No live vendor calls were made.
- [x] No force push or merge was performed.

## Summary

- eliminate modulo bias in shared dice and board randomness
- validate LAN controller/host messages and authorize controller actions against each player's private pending action
- restore remote roll and punishment-choice flows, and clear stale pause requests after automatic host transfer
- reject corrupt cached player settings and add accessible names to player-count controls
- remove the fixed Vite HMR port and cap Playwright workers to avoid resource-driven false timeouts
- enforce zero-warning lint, update vulnerable transitive dependencies, and prepare the v1.14.1 Pages/room-server release metadata

## Root causes

Several trust boundaries relied on TypeScript casts rather than runtime validation, controller actions were routed without matching the player's assigned action, random integers used modulo reduction, and the development/test configuration assumed fixed local resources. The room failover path also cleared skip votes but retained pause votes.

## Impact

Classic remains the default and Party/online flows remain opt-in. The changes improve fairness, LAN controller correctness, failover behavior, startup resilience, accessibility, local development, CI stability, and dependency security.

## Validation

- `npm test` — 28 files / 236 tests passed
- `npm run test:e2e` — 63 passed / 55 conditional skips / 0 failed
- `npm run lint:check`
- `npm run type-check`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run validate-config`
- frontend and room-server production builds
- room-server load test — 20 rooms / 160 connections, p95 0.5 ms, RSS 78.4 MiB
- production and full `npm audit` — 0 vulnerabilities
- dual Vite instances verified on ports 4173 and 4175

## Release boundary

This PR prepares v1.14.1. After merge, the immutable tag will trigger GitHub Pages deployment and the room-server image will be deployed separately. Real iOS/Android and 4/6/8-person field acceptance remains a separate manual evidence gate.

body:
Часть A задачи #296. Часть B (процессное правило про мутанта у контрольной
суммы) владельцу не выносится в этом PR ни в каком виде — критерий готовности
прямо требует, чтобы `DEVELOPMENT_PACE.md` остался нетронутым, и это проверено
ниже.

## До → Меняем → После

**До.** `docs/engineering/EVIDENCE_WORKFLOW.md` не содержал факта о том, что
именно накрывают `deterministicChecksum` и `viewInvariantChecksum` из
`verify.ps1`. Issue #281 записала критерий готовности «обе суммы совпадают с
X», и независимый review PR #292 показал по коду, что один из двух критериев
не мог быть нарушен ни одной мутацией партиции.

**Меняем.** В `EVIDENCE_WORKFLOW.md` добавлен раздел «Что покрывают
контрольные суммы `verify.ps1`»: `deterministicChecksum` — только
`SimulationWorld`, `viewInvariantChecksum` — состояние `PrototypeWorld`, не
отрисовка. Каждое утверждение — со ссылкой на код и командой, которой оно
снято, на актуальном `main` (не перенесено из PR #292). Добавлен живой пример
на Issue #281. Правило (часть B) не пишется нигде, в том числе как «пояснение
к правилу 32».

**После.** Следующий координатор, формулируя критерий готовности вида «сумма
совпадает», может свериться с записанным фактом вместо повторного чтения
`verify.ps1` и `Program.cs`/`Main.cs` с нуля.

## Что изменено

- `docs/engineering/EVIDENCE_WORKFLOW.md` — новый раздел «Что покрывают
  контрольные суммы `verify.ps1`» (после раздела про SHA-256 evidence bundle),
  дата в шапке обновлена на `2026-08-07`.
- `evidence/296-checksum-coverage.json` — сырые команды и их вывод, которыми
  подкреплён каждый факт, плюс перекрёстная сверка с `evidence/287-verify-result.json`.
- Один коммит: `3a9b3b9`.

## Покрытие сумм (адреса — на коммите `a44e14d`, актуальный `main`)

**`deterministicChecksum` — только `SimulationWorld`.**

```bash
rg -c -- '--prototype' scripts/verify.ps1 ; echo "exit:$?"
```
Вывод: пусто, `exit:1` — совпадений нет, флага `--prototype` в `verify.ps1`
нет вовсе.

Стадия `sim` (`scripts/verify.ps1:418`) вызывает `Invoke-Scenario`
(`scripts/verify.ps1:111`), которая запускает `tests/DungeonFortress.Scenarios`
без `--prototype`. `Program.cs` без этого флага идёт по ветке
`SimulationScenario.Run(config, options.TickCount, commands)`
(`tests/DungeonFortress.Scenarios/Program.cs:33`), и `checksum` в
`scenario_result` (`Program.cs:57`) — это `result.Checksum` именно этого
прогона. `PrototypeWorld` и `Main` сюда не входят.
`verify.ps1:1152` берёт итог как `$simResult.DeterministicChecksum`, которое
стадия `sim` ставит строкой `verify.ps1:440` как `$sameA.checksum`.

```bash
rg -n "DeterministicChecksum" scripts/verify.ps1
```
Вывод: `440:                DeterministicChecksum = $sameA.checksum` и
`1152:        $summary["deterministicChecksum"] = $simResult.DeterministicChecksum`.

**`viewInvariantChecksum` — состояние `PrototypeWorld`, не отрисовка.**

```bash
rg -n "viewInvariantChecksum" scripts/verify.ps1
```
Вывод: `1176:        $summary["viewInvariantChecksum"] = $godotStageResult.ViewChecksum`.

Стадия `godot` четыре раза прогоняет `godot_headless_smoke` с разными
camera/frame/UI-scale (`verify.ps1:640-669`) и требует совпадения `checksum`
во всех четырёх (`Assert-SameNonEmptyValue`, `verify.ps1:693-695`). Это число —
`_checksum` в `src/DungeonFortress.Game/Main.cs:675`, а присваивается оно один
раз:

```bash
rg -n "_checksum" src/DungeonFortress.Game/Main.Session.cs
```
Вывод: `312:        _checksum = PrototypeScenario.Capture(_world).Checksum;`

```bash
rg -n "PrototypeWorld\? _world" src/DungeonFortress.Game/Main.cs
```
Вывод: `44:    private PrototypeWorld? _world;`

Camera/frame/UI-scale в этот checksum не попадают по построению — в этом и
есть инвариант стадии `godot`. Значит сумма полностью слепа к отрисовке.

## Живой пример: Issue #281

Партиция #281 — `Main.cs` и `PrototypeWorld.cs`. Критерий готовности требовал
совпадения обеих сумм с зафиксированными значениями
(`e65273aa...`/`7e9fffa7...`).

`deterministicChecksum` в этом критерии был **структурно нулевым**: партиция
#281 не содержит ни одного файла на пути `SimulationScenario.Run` —
`SimulationWorld` в неё вообще не входит. Ни один мутант внутри `Main.cs` или
`PrototypeWorld.cs` не мог сдвинуть эту сумму; критерий выполнялся бы, даже
сломай разрез `PrototypeWorld` целиком.

`viewInvariantChecksum` для той же партиции — рабочая проверка наполовину: она
видит мутанта в `PrototypeWorld.cs` (через `_world`), но слепа к той части
`Main.cs`, которая не пишет в `_world`, то есть к собственно рендерингу.

Отдельное подтверждение стабильности этих значений: `evidence/287-verify-result.json`
(полный `verify.ps1`, снят 2026-08-07 для другой задачи, #287) несёт те же
`deterministicChecksum` и `viewInvariantChecksum`, что и в теле Issue #281 —
значит обе суммы действительно не сдвигались чем-то посторонним между PR #292
и текущим `main`, и вывод про #281 не является случайным совпадением момента
замера.

## Законный исход (часть A показывает, что правило не нужно?)

Я не заявляю, что записанного факта достаточно и правило не нужно. Факт
объясняет уже случившийся структурный ноль в #281 постфактум, но сам по себе
не мешает координатору *в следующий раз* написать столь же нулевой критерий
для другого файла — он помогает только если критерий сверяется с этим
разделом перед тем, как его записать. Другими словами: факт полезен для
диагностики задним числом, но не является механизмом предотвращения. Оставляю
это владельцу как есть — часть B туда и была вынесена, эта оценка её не
предрешает.

## Как проверено

- `git diff --stat origin/main -- docs/engineering/DEVELOPMENT_PACE.md` →
  пусто (файл не тронут).
- Полный `verify.ps1`:
  ```bash
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1
  ```
  → `{"event":"verification_result","status":"ok","scope":"full",...}`,
  9 из 9 стадий `ok` (`scripts` 220.4s, `build` 11.4s, `tests` 452.6s, `mcp`
  9.9s, `sim` 1.2s, `load` 0.7s, `godot` 102.1s, `ui` 10.1s, `screenshots`
  28.3s), `deterministicChecksum` = `e65273aa102f4db01d2cf64ecc48b1556700544f5da0fe7c19378d1d089b6f6f`,
  `viewInvariantChecksum` = `7e9fffa76dfa479623ceb5890c9585a63a77441d7b279d997d0919f7e538fead`
  — оба совпадают со значениями из #281 и `evidence/287-verify-result.json`,
  полный вывод сохранён локально в `.artifacts/verify-296.log` (не коммитится,
  `.artifacts/` в `.gitignore`).
- Все шесть команд из раздела «Покрытие сумм» выше прогнаны заново на этой
  ветке; вывод совпадает с процитированным. Сырые пары команда/вывод — в
  `evidence/296-checksum-coverage.json`.
- Относительные ссылки: в добавленный раздел новых markdown-ссылок не
  добавлено (только код-ссылки в backticks), так что битых ссылок раздел не
  вносит.

## Мутант

Мутанта нет, и это ожидаемо: правило 21 требует мутанта для симуляции,
детерминизма и контракта — эта задача не трогает ни одного из трёх (документ
+ evidence). Способ проверки — прогон команд и сверка вывода, что и сделано
выше.

## Риски и ограничения

- Раздел фиксирует факт на коммите `a44e14d`; если `verify.ps1`,
  `Program.cs` или `Main.Session.cs` снова порежут, номера строк устареют
  так же, как устарели адреса из PR #292 — раздел не самообновляющийся.
- Живой пример разбирает только `deterministicChecksum` для #281 как
  структурно нулевой. Про `viewInvariantChecksum` в разделе честно сказано,
  что он рабочий лишь наполовину партиции — это не «второй структурный ноль»,
  а другая, более узкая слепота.

## Документы и решения

- Обновлён: `docs/engineering/EVIDENCE_WORKFLOW.md` (раздел «Что покрывают
  контрольные суммы `verify.ps1`», дата в шапке).
- Не обновлён и не должен быть: `docs/engineering/DEVELOPMENT_PACE.md` —
  часть B туда не идёт в этой задаче.
- Новый: `evidence/296-checksum-coverage.json`.

## Расход токенов

Оценка из брифа: 120–220k вместе с review (основание — #215, тот же род
работы: проверить утверждение прогоном и записать проверенное).
Модель: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` (Sonnet 5, как назначено меткой
`tier:standard`, правило 34). Точного числа из goal u

author: chrischurchsc
body:
> the audience tag is still not being shown connected on grid

The same question as #269 and #271, asked by a **third** surface and answered differently. Those two fixed the *board*. This is the *grid*.

## What was wrong

`cardsForRow` feeds the grid's **Made from** column. It walks upstream from the row, its channel and the campaign, then looked each returned id up in `board.objects` and skipped whatever it did not find.

A placement's members carry **no wire of their own** — you wire the object, not the cards inside it — so `upstreamCardIds` stops *at* the placement and returns its id, which is not in `objects`. Every card inside a smart object was therefore invisible to the grid.

The comment sitting on that exact line claimed `upstreamCardIds` "already returns those separately". It does not. And there was **no placement anywhere in `cardsForRow.test.ts`**, which is why the claim was never checked.

## Measured before the fix

One board, an Audience card inside a smart object, the object wired to the campaign:

```
upstreamCardIds(campaign) = ["pl1"]                <- the placement, not its members
wiredRefsFor(campaign)    = [segment:s_1]          <- the writer DOES get the audience
cardsForRow               = []                     <- the grid sees nothing
```

So **Made from** showed no audience for an asset whose audience was reaching the copy writer through that very object. The board said connected, the grid said unset, and both were reading the same wire.

## The fix

A placement is expanded to its member cards, which is what its own comment always said it was ("a bag of cards"). `wiredRefsFor` has resolved a placement to the records inside it since forever (see `refsOf`); this is the same rule applied to the cards, so the two surfaces stop disagreeing.

Contained to `cardsForRow` deliberately — the grid's source — rather than changing `upstreamCardIds`, which the copy resolver also uses and which is already correct for its own purpose.

## Tests

`cardsForRow.test.ts` grows to 16, with the first placement coverage it has ever had. The negatives are pinned as hard as the positives:

- listed when the object is wired to the campaign, to the channel, or to the row
- carry their kind and record, so Made from can render a real, openable chip
- **not** listed when the object is wired to nothing
- still dropped when the channel is cut off from the brief
- a member wired in its own right is listed **once**, not twice
- a card wired *into* the object arrives alongside the ones inside it

583 tests pass across 59 files. `tsc -b --noEmit`, `npm run build` and `npm run changelog:check` all clean.

## One thing I did NOT change

`cardsByRow` returns nothing when the grid has no single campaign in scope (`SheetGrid.tsx:568`), so a grid spanning campaigns shows the audience only via the plain-string fallback from #268, never as a card. That looks deliberate — there is no one board to walk — so I left it. Say if it should behave otherwise.

⚠️ Changelog entry is **v1.56**.

body:
No need to depend on a third-party library here when the Java Platform provides this functionality natively.

Part of the effort to remove Commons Lang 2 from Jenkins core — jenkinsci/jenkins#16404,
jenkinsci/jenkins#26105. Commons Lang 2 is EOL and carries an unfixed advisory
(GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v).

- `StringUtils.isBlank` → `Util.fixEmptyAndTrim(x) == null`.
- `StringUtils.leftPad(Integer.toString(n + 1), 5, '0')` → `String.format("%05d", n + 1)`, which is the
  same zero-padded fixed width without the intermediate string.
- Enables the `ban-commons-lang-2` enforcer rule.

### Testing done

`mvn -B -ntp clean verify` passes locally on Java 21 / macOS.
The `ban-commons-lang-2` enforcer rule is enabled in this PR, so the build fails if an
`org.apache.commons.lang.*` import comes back.

body:
## User value

- Users add SSH hosts once in **Hosts & settings** and select them from the workspace drop-down on later runs.
- A command-level `host` automatically selects and locks the target, reducing accidental execution on the wrong machine.
- Local text transforms hide the SSH control because it has no effect on those commands.
- Command definitions can provide input labels and placeholders, reducing ambiguity such as the previous generic “Input 1”.
- The existing command drop-down, editing workspace, output pane, and history layout remain in place, so the routine workflow does not need to be relearned.

## Implementation

- Persist normalized saved hosts, default host, and the most recent user-selected host.
- Add host add/remove/default controls to Settings.
- Bind the workspace to a saved-host ComboBox.
- Preserve fixed-host behavior from `commands.yaml`.
- Extend the existing YAML contract with optional `input1_label`, `input1_placeholder`, `input2_label`, `input2_placeholder`, and `show_second_input` fields while retaining old entries.
- Validate duplicate command IDs, unsupported types, and invalid fixed hosts.
- Fix history restore and rerun lookup so a missing command does not fall through to the first entry.

## Validation

- Avalonia XAML files parse as XML.
- C# source passed delimiter and lexical balance checks in the available environment.
- Product-level compilation and tests run through the MyPowerTools integration PR CI.

author: hugocasa
body: ## Summary Resource values had no history: editing one destroyed the previous value, with no way to see what changed or roll back. Flows, apps and scripts all keep version history; resources did not. This adds append-only version history for every resource value, surfaced in the resource editor as a History drawer with a diff view and restore. The motivation is reusable AI agents, which are `ai_agent` resources: without version history you cannot attribute a behaviour change to a prompt edit, because the prompt it replaced is gone. Versioning is workspace-wide rather than agent-specific because the primitive is useful for every resource type. ## Changes - **`resource_version` table** mirroring `flow_version`'s shape, keyed `(workspace_id, path)` with a cascading FK so a rename carries history to the new path and a delete takes it along. RLS joins back to `resource`, so visibility follows the parent rather than restating its several policies. The migration seeds one version per existing resource so the first edit has something to diff against. - **Recording lives in a database trigger**, not the API handlers. Resource values are written well outside them: variable renames rewrite a linked resource, workspace forks clone resources wholesale, native integrations upsert them, and trashbin restores reinsert them. A handler-level hook missed all of those, and a rename that changes path and value in one statement left the newest version holding the pre-rename value while the UI labelled it "Current". - **`state` and `cache` are excluded** — both are rewritten by every job that calls `setState` or caches a result. Same exclusion workspace export already applies. - **An unchanged value records nothing**, so no-op saves, renames and description edits don't accumulate rows. (Deleting a resource cascades its history away, so a trashbin restore starts a fresh history at v1 rather than continuing the old one.) - **History is capped at 100 versions per path.** Unlike flows, resources are not only edited by humans: `setResource` from a scheduled script reaches the same write path. - **Three routes** — list history, fetch one version with its value, restore. Restore writes the old value forward as a new version rather than rewinding, so history stays append-only and the restore is itself attributable and reversible. - **Dangling references are surfaced, not blocked.** A version fetch reports `$var:`/`$res:` paths that no longer resolve so the UI can warn before restoring; refusing would make a version unrestorable for a reason outside the resource. - **`prune_versions` gains a `"resources"` arm** for cloud parity with scripts, flows and apps. ## Screenshots Version list, value view, and the dangling-reference warning: ![v2-history-value](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/agent-screenshots-internal/main/shots/ai-agents-evals/1786113645-v3-history-value.png) Diff against the current value: ![v2-history-diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/windmill-labs/agent-screenshots-internal/main/shots/ai-agents-evals/1786112590-v2-history-diff.png) Rows use the shared `VersionListItem` component, which `ScriptVersionHistory` was also converted to, so the two history drawers stay visually identical. The warning uses the standard `Alert` component. ## Test plan - [ ] Edit a resource twice, open History, confirm both versions listed with author and timestamp - [ ] Diff a version against current and confirm the changed fields are highlighted - [ ] Restore an older version: value reverts, a new version is appended (history does not shrink), and both drawers close so a stale editor cannot save over it - [ ] Re-save a resource without changing the value and confirm no version is added - [ ] Rename a resource and confirm its history moves with it and no version is added - [ ] Clear a resource's past versions and confirm only the current value remains and the resource itself is untouched - [ ] Rename a variable linked to a resource and confirm the newest version matches the live value - [ ] Confirm a `state` or `cache` resource accumulates no history - [ ] Restore a version referencing a deleted variable and confirm the warning appears and restore still succeeds ## Notes - Behaviour change worth flagging: `update_resource_value` on a nonexistent path previously returned 200 and silently did nothing; it now 404s. The handler is shared with restore, where a missing resource is a real error. - Version rows hold the same value the `resource` row already holds and inherit its permissions, so the audience is unchanged. Values written through the UI keep secrets in linked variables, but one pushed by `wmill` or written by `setResource` can hold an inline credential — so rotating such a credential would leave the old one readable in the history. **Clear past versions** (in the History drawer, owner-gated) is the remediation: it drops every version but the current value. - History captures the resource, not its transitive closure: two versions can be byte-identical while behaviour differs because a referenced variable changed. Documented in `docs/reusable-ai-agents.md`. - Non-secret **variables** are the natural follow-up and the drawer was built to be reused for them. Secret variables should never be versioned — retaining rotated credentials would make rotation stop being remediation. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds append-only version history for resource values with diff, restore, and an owner‑gated “Clear past versions” in the Resource Editor. Recording uses a DB trigger (covers direct writes), history is pruned by a periodic sweep, and the UI opens History unselected and diffs against the newest version for a consistent view. - New Features - Resource history API: list versions, get one with value and missing `$var:`/`$jsonvar:`/`$res:` references, restore, and clear past versions; OpenAPI updated. - Workspace pruning supports `resources`, and Cloud quotas show prunable resource versions. - Bug Fixes - Frontend: open History with no preselected version; discard stale loads when the path changes; reset the pane and disarm Clear confirmation when the selection moves; scope history to the selected workspace; treat the newest row as “Current”; never show a diff if the baseline can’t load and explain why; restore operates on the loaded version; diff baseline uses the newest version instead of the live row. - Backend: cap listings to 100 versions; trim history in the monitor; tighten RLS (SELECT-only) and write via a SECURITY DEFINER trigger; warn on high write rates (20/min) and harden in‑process counters; `update_value` now 404s on a missing resource. - CI: increase Node heap for `svelte-check` via `NODE_OPTIONS`. Written for commit 3b25b5c407eeb08cffa51b0aaaa9f79ddf014d57. Summary will update on new commits.

author: novanoticia
body:
Closes #1 — aunque no como pedía el issue. Al ir a hacerlo resultó que **en este repo no hay ningún servidor MCP**, y que la documentación existente describía uno inexistente.

## Lo que encontré

`packages/claude-code-mcp/` contenía el paquete **`@token-calc/cli`**: binario `token-calc`, un único fuente `src/cli.ts` de 242 líneas que hace `switch` sobre `process.argv`, **sin `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, sin JSON-RPC y sin transporte stdio**. Lo compilé: produce `dist/cli.js`.

El README, en cambio, mandaba compilar y registrar `packages/claude-code-mcp/dist/mcp-server.js` bajo `mcpServers`. Ese fichero no existe ni ha existido — **quien seguía las instrucciones se atascaba** en el paso *«You should see `mcp-server.js` in this directory»*. Tres instrucciones más estaban rotas:

- El paso de compilación usaba `yarn workspace @token-calculator/claude-code-mcp build`, un workspace que no existe: el paquete se llama `@token-calc/cli`.
- **`yarn build` en el root solo compilaba `@token-calc/core`**, así que el CLI no se compilaba nunca por esa vía — ni en local ni en CI.
- Faltaba el requisito que hoy rompe la instalación de entrada: los workspaces usan el protocolo `workspace:*` y el lockfile es Berry v8, así que con Yarn Classic `yarn install` **falla** con `Couldn't find package "@token-calc/core@workspace:*"`. Lo reproduje.

## Estado real de los cuatro puntos del issue

| Punto | Estado |
|---|---|
| 1. `.yarnrc.yml` con `nodeLinker: node-modules` | **Ya estaba hecho** |
| 2. `@types/node` en las devDependencies del root | **Ya estaba hecho** |
| 3. `typeRoots` en el tsconfig | **Ya estaba hecho** |
| 3. `lib: ["ES2020", "DOM"]` | **No aplicado, a propósito** — ver abajo |
| 4. Documentar la instalación | Reescrito, porque lo que había era falso |

**Por qué no añado `DOM`:** el paquete compila **sin un solo error** con `lib: ["ES2020"]`; lo verifiqué con `tsc` 5 y `@types/node` 20. Añadir `DOM` a un CLI de Node no arregla nada y mete tipos de navegador que dejarían pasar el typecheck a APIs inexistentes en runtime. Si aparece un error concreto que `DOM` resuelva, con verlo lo añado.

## Qué cambia

- **`packages/claude-code-mcp` → `packages/cli`.** El desajuste entre el directorio y el nombre del paquete era el origen de la confusión que generó el issue.
- **Scripts del root**: `build` encadena ahora `build:core` y `build:cli`, ambos disponibles por separado. Como el CI ejecuta `yarn build`, esto hace además que **los errores de compilación del CLI se detecten**, algo que hasta ahora no ocurría; el paso del workflow se renombra para que su nombre no siga mintiendo.
- **Sección «For Claude Code» del README, reescrita**: distingue las dos vías reales —instalar el plugin para las cuatro skills, o compilar el CLI y dejar que Claude lo llame por Bash— con los comandos verificados y sus flags, y una nota explicando por qué no hay `mcp-server.js`, con enlace a este issue para quien llegue desde una búsqueda.
- Referencias al directorio viejo corregidas en el README (árbol y tabla de documentación) y en `CONTRIBUTING.md`. La tabla apuntaba a `packages/claude-code-mcp/src/mcp-server.ts`, otro fichero inexistente.

## Comprobado

Compilando de verdad, no leyendo la configuración:

- [x] `build:core` y `build:cli` compilan **sin errores** con `tsc` 5 y `@types/node` 20, tras el renombrado
- [x] La salida es **`packages/cli/dist/cli.js`** — que es lo que demuestra que `mcp-server.js` nunca existió
- [x] Los tests de core pasan
- [x] **Los cuatro comandos que documenta el README se ejecutan correctamente**: `tokens` con sus cuatro flags, `convert`, `file --type/--size` y `help`
- [x] Reproducido el fallo de Yarn Classic que ahora queda documentado
- [x] Ningún enlace relativo roto en el README; la conformidad del plugin con Agent Plugins 1.0.0 sigue intacta
- [x] Los cuatro checks de CI en verde: `build (18.x)`, `build (20.x)`, `security` y `docs`

## Notas

**Corregí una instrucción mía antes de publicarla.** Había escrito `yarn workspace @token-calc/cli link` para poner `token-calc` en el `PATH`, y no vale: el `yarn link` de Berry enlaza un paquete *dentro de otro proyecto*, no en el `PATH`. La versión que queda usa `npm link`, con una alternativa por alias.

**El `yarn.lock` está vacío**: solo la cabecera `__metadata`, sin una sola entrada. Las instalaciones no son reproducibles hoy. No lo he tocado porque no puedo completar un `yarn install` real en este entorno y un lockfile a medias sería peor que ninguno, pero conviene generarlo y commitearlo.

**Si de verdad quieres un servidor MCP**, es una funcionalidad nueva: SDK de MCP, transporte stdio y *tools* envolviendo `@token-calc/core`. Dímelo y lo implemento en un PR aparte; este se limita a que la documentación deje de describir algo que no existe.

Rama rebasada sobre `main` tras el merge del PR #4, conservando solo este commit.

author: konih
body:
Closes audit finding **ARCH-03**. Implements **D-120**.

## Why

The `DecisionRecord`'s `pins.toolDigest` was `sha256(toolVersion)` while the frozen schema promised
a "content digest of the evaluating tool build". Two binaries built from different source at the same
version produced the **same** digest. It was a provenance claim that was false.

## What

`toolDigest` now hashes the binary's canonical Go build info — module path/version/sum, dependency
checksums, VCS revision and dirty flag — per D-120's published input list. The schema's `toolDigest`
**description** is republished verbatim from spec Appendix A.2 so the contract statement and the
implementation agree. `git diff -- schemas/` is exactly that one line; no validation keyword moved.

## The trap this avoids

The obvious implementation — fall back when `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` reports unavailable — **would not
fire** for a `go test -c` or `-buildvcs=false` binary: build info *is* available there, it just
carries no main-module identity. The digest would have silently become **one constant across every
source revision of the repo** — ARCH-03 reintroduced in a new shape. The predicate keys on
main-module content (`Main.Sum != "" || vcs.revision != ""`) instead, and anything else takes a
labelled, version-bound fallback that a consumer can recompute.

Verified across five build modes, including a real goreleaser snapshot: **the released artifact is
content-bearing on all five targets.**

## Verification

`task check` (coverage 90.1% → 90.2%), `task determinism`, `CI=true go test ./...`, schema-drift
guards green. Five mutants planted and killed, including the naive `if !ok` variant — empirically
proving the simpler predicate would have emitted a dep-only constant.

Independent review re-ran every mutant itself. Two are worth noting:
- **A correct-but-unwired function would have shipped green** — reverting only the call site turned
  nothing red until `TestRunRecordPinsToolDigest` was added to drive `runRun` end to end.
- **A post-merge landmine, caught before merge**: the new drift test anchored on the *old* schema
  description read from `origin/main`, which passes today and reds main the instant this lands. The
  anchor is now regex-derived and every substitution fails on a no-op. Defused, verified by
  simulating the post-merge baseline.

## Ownership expansion (ratified in review)

`internal/schemadrift` carries a second, branch-scoped frozen-schema guard that diffs against
`origin/main` — committing does not satisfy it, so without a fence this lane would be permanently red
in three packages. The new fence admits **only** `$defs.pins.properties.toolDigest.description`
(sentinel substitution + whole-document `DeepEqual`); a mutant that normalised every description was
caught. No weakening of the frozen-schema protection.

Follow-ups recorded: a D-120 addendum tightening the fallback-trigger wording, and a CHANGELOG note
that pre-D-120 records carry `sha256(toolVersion)` — **the latter must land before the release tag**
(AUD-S02 owns `CHANGELOG.md`).

Refs: ARCH-03, D-120, spec Appendix A.2 · REQ-AUD-S04-01/02 · SEMVER-VISIBLE

author: egavazzi
body:
AURORA expects every energy bin to be narrower than the smallest ionization threshold. This holds for the default grid (`make_energy_grid` saturates at ΔE ≈ 11.65 eV, below all default thresholds — O2 is the closest at 12.07 eV), but nothing enforced it. With this PR we add a warning at model initialization when a custom grid or custom species breaks that assumption, listing the offending species and thresholds.

## Why

`update_B!` applies the in-bin retention factor `max(0, 1 - E_loss/dE)` to all inelastic channels, including ionizing ones, while `compute_ionization_spectra!` independently renormalizes the cascading spectra so that one full primary (plus its secondaries) lands in strictly lower bins. These two paths are only consistent when every ionizing collision moves the primary out of its energy bin, i.e. when `dE < E_loss`. On a coarser grid both paths become active at once, and each ionizing collision then produces up to ~2 primaries and inflated secondaries, breaking particle and energy conservation.

- make `OwnerSessionStore` an auto-provided root service and make refreshes await fresh `httpResource` state

- add protected-API session-expiry handling that returns the Owner to sign-in with a visible message and preserved destination

Signed-out visitors do not invoke protected lazy loaders. Owners return to the exact requested Car view after magic-link or passkey authentication, receive a clear session-expiry path, and get consistent loading, retry, announcement, and heading-focus behavior during lazy navigation.
