author: ryo-wtnb11
body:
Closes #970.

## Why

`FusionRule` is what every provider implements, and it carried
`fusion_channels_in_table` and `coupled_sector_fold` — a partial-representability
vocabulary with a prose-only safety contract that U(1), Z2, fZ2, SU(2) and
Fibonacci have no use for.

The issue first argued these were dead. They are not: three `Infallible*`
adapters forward to them and test doubles exercise the guard. The stronger
reason is that the extension point they serve **cannot be occupied**. An
infallible provider's `fusion_channels` is total, so on an escaping pair it must
panic or return a truncated set, and only the guarded preflight paths would
notice — every other call in recoupling reaches the provider unguarded. A
provider with a finite table implements `CheckedGenericFusion`, which is what
that trait's own documentation prescribes and where the real guard lives.

After removal the rule is definitional rather than optional: infallible means
unbounded. The adapters forward representable channels to the complete channels
and inherit the checked default fold.

Worth recording for the next auditor: `SUNFusionRule::try_fusion_channels_in_table`
is currently an alias of `try_fusion_channels`, so the checked capability has no
real bounded implementor either. It is retained for the table tier (#539).

## Second commit — the fold type

`CoupledSectorFold` exposed `clean`, `tainted`, `out_of_table` and `poisoned` as
four independent public fields, but they are not independent: a lost
classification means no candidate may be reported clean, and a sector cannot be
both clean and tainted. Every producer re-established those conventions and
every consumer re-checked them, and the aggregate loop restated the demotion by
hand after building the fields.

Three variants — `Complete`, `Partial`, `Unknown` — plus
`CoupledSectorFoldBuilder`, whose `seal` applies the two cross-tuple rules once:
tainted-anywhere beats clean-somewhere, and an unknown split demotes every
candidate. `seal` is the old accumulation operation for operation, including
vector ordering, because `FusionOutsideTable` messages format those vectors.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` green; `cargo build --workspace --tests` warning-free.
- Three new unit tests pin the conventions in their new home; the unknown branch
  previously had no coverage on either side of this change.
- Reviewed independently before opening: whether dropping the block-dimension
  guard loses a rejection for any provider that can exist, whether
  `CheckedGenericSpy`'s restored counting override preserves what its
  failure-budget tests measure or merely restores a number, whether `seal` is
  operation-for-operation the old loop, the variant chosen at each construction
  site, and whether `is_fully_clean` as `matches!(Complete)` can reject a fold
  the old predicate accepted. Two findings are fixed in the third commit.

## Breaking

`FusionRule` loses two methods and `CoupledSectorFold` becomes an enum. A
downstream provider or consumer fails at compile time, never silently.

author: iansmith
body:
Refs #481. Fixes the enumeration under one of #479's two conditions.

## The defect

#479 specified **what** to compare and never **how to enumerate**, so the obvious implementation greps `func Test` / `def test`. A declaration is not a node-id — the runnable units live *inside* them as subtests, parametrized cases and table rows, and none has a declaration line of its own.

## Reproduced the near-miss

Built PLTF-2562's exact shape — an outer test whose contract lives in a `t.Run`, plus a 3-row table — then deleted **only** the guard subtest and one table row, leaving every `func Test` line untouched:

| | before | after | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| runner-enumerated | 6 | 4 | **SHRINK**, naming `…/no_undiscovered_setter-shaped_dependency_anywhere_in_the_graph` and `…/row3` |
| naive grep | 2 | 2 | **no shrink reported** ← what shipped |

pytest, losing one parametrize case *and* the class-nested test:

| | before | after | dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| runner | 3 | 1 | `TestGroup::test_inner`, `test_cases[beta]` |
| grep | 1 | 1 | **0** — the nested test is indented, so `^def test` never saw it at all |

**No-op where the coarse form was already right:** a flat suite enumerates identically both ways (`[TestA TestB]`).

**`could-not-enumerate`:** a suite that won't build returns exit 2 and the phrase, never an empty set. An unenumerable suite must not clear a check.

## The constraint everything bends around

Measured, not assumed: **Go cannot be enumerated statically.**

```
go test -list '.*'  ->  TestOuter, TestPlain      # subtests INVISIBLE
go test -v          ->  === RUN TestOuter/no_undiscovered_setter …
```

Subtests are created when the body executes. Documented with an explicit *"do not simplify this back to `-list`"* warning — it's faster, produces a plausible shorter list, and silently drops every subtest. Go normalizes subtest names (spaces → underscores), so the parsed form **is** the runnable form.

## No stage gains a suite run

The set comes from runs that already happen — `red-tests` Steps 3/6, `implement` Step 1.3, `mutation-check` Step B1. **B1 now reports the set it enumerated**, which is the half of the comparison only it can produce without a second execution.

## Both consumers fixed

- #479's freeze comparison.
- **Refactor mode's *"the same suite green after"***, which had the identical exposure and now means the same runnable node-id **set**, not the same count — equal counts with different members is a substitution and reads as clean to anything counting.

## Notes

New reference `skills/run/references/node-ids.md`, added to `manifest.txt`. This is the **first worker → run/references pointer** in the repo (`red-tests` and `mutation-check` both cite it); verified the installer's path rewrite handles it — the generated `slopstop-red-tests/SKILL.md` resolves to `.claude/skills/slopstop-run/references/node-ids.md`.

Only Go and pytest are claimed, because only those two were measured. The reference says so and tells the next person to establish others the same way rather than inferring from these.

Charter **C13**: no Python file added or removed. Repo stays at **4**, all `tools/fleet-sync/`.

## Quoi

`lastUpdatedLabel` combinait la date de DÉBUT du bloc (`date_montreal_tz`) avec l'heure de publication (fin + 1h, réforme #195), sans décaler la date quand le bloc traverse minuit (`23-03`) ou en légacy (`20-24`). Un bloc `23-03` daté du 6 août, publié à 4h, affichait « 6 août, 4h » au lieu de « 7 août, 4h » — signalé aujourd'hui par Adrien qui a cru le pipeline figé depuis 31h alors qu'il tournait normalement.

Nouvelle fonction `publicationDateFromInterval()` dans `lib/dates.ts`, branchée sur le seul appel concerné dans `headlineEvents.ts` (partagé par Une des Unes et Deux solitudes). L'autre appel de `lastUpdatedLabel` (tables journalières, sans heure de bloc) n'est pas touché.

Vérifié en local sur les vraies données de `main` (bloc `23-03` du 6 août) : le libellé passe de « jeudi 6 août 2026, 4h » à « vendredi 7 août 2026, 4h ».

## Note de journal

Correction d'un libellé de fraîcheur des données qui pouvait afficher un jour de retard pour certains blocs horaires.

author: semtex1987
body:
💡 **What**: Reduced the STFT frame overlap in `spectral_scan` from 75% (`hop_length=1024` with `n_fft=4096`) to 50% (`hop_length=n_fft//2`).
🎯 **Why**: The 75% overlap was unnecessarily computing overlapping frames for a macroscopic heuristic check (the 95th percentile over time). Since the algorithm merely looks for broad frequency characteristics and cliffs, this level of overlap provides no additional accuracy but doubles the computational cost. Reducing overlap all the way to 0% (`hop_length=n_fft`) failed curve parity tests, so 50% overlap was the safest optimization.
📊 **Impact**: ~2x speedup on the STFT extraction phase (from ~0.40s to ~0.20s in isolated 10x benchmarks).
🔬 **Measurement**: Benchmarked the function on 10 seconds of random noise. `spectral_scan` time dropped from ~0.40s to ~0.20s per 10 iterations. Full test suite still passes successfully, ensuring no regression.

author: ounospanas
body:
## Summary

Home Assistant entities without a device registry entry — SmartIR and template climate, manually configured Local Tuya devices, helpers — were dropped before the entity list ever reached the actuator or the planner, so devices visible on the user's own dashboard could not be controlled or automated. The second commit stops sending the model data no prompt uses: the resolver now receives entity ids, names, areas, states and colour attributes instead of the full dashboard payload, roughly halving the prompt on real setups.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Chore / dependency update

The first commit is a bug fix. The second is a behaviour change (logged under `### Changed`): the model sees a smaller payload, though nothing referenced by a prompt or by post-processing was removed.

## How to test

**1. The entity that used to be invisible.** On a setup with an entity that has no device registry entry — check Developer Tools → States for something absent from Settings → Devices & Services → Devices; a manually configured Tuya or SmartIR climate entity is the usual case — ask the assistant to control it (e.g. "turn on the air conditioner"). Before: "I couldn't identify a matching device for that request." After: the service call fires.

**2. Nothing else regressed.**
- "turn off the tv" / "lock the front door" still resolve to the right entity.
- "make the light blue" still works — this exercises `supported_color_modes`, which the compacted payload deliberately keeps.
- Every actuation still logs its `Guard: resolver returned N action(s), kept X, dropped Y` line. Post-processing reads the full payload, not the compacted one, so this should be unchanged.
- Ask for a device you do not own; it should still refuse rather than substitute a neighbour.

**3. Disabled entities.** Disable an entity in HA and ask for it. It should not be offered to the model at all — previously it was, and the resulting service call failed silently.

**4. The HA map view** (`home_assistant_map_agent` reads the same helper). Device-less entities now appear grouped under a pseudo-device card named after their area, e.g. "Office room (no device)", or "Entities without a device" when they have no area. Confirm this renders sanely — it is the one visible UI consequence.

**Measured prompt reduction** on two real Home Assistant instances:

| setup | before | after | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A (309 entities) | 24,304 tok | 10,251 tok | −58% |
| B (331 entities) | 26,264 tok | 12,120 tok | −54% |

The largest single field removed was `unique_id` (18 KB on setup A) — identifiers like `00:17:88:01:02:ab:cd:ef-0b`. `unique_id`, `platform` and `swid` are referenced zero times by any prompt in the codebase, as are icons, entity pictures and `supported_features` bitmasks. This matters most for small local models, where the noise both competes for attention and can overflow a short context window.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests pass (`make test`)
- [ ] Lint passes (`make lint` and `make lint-py`)
- [x] Added / updated tests for new behaviour
- [ ] Docs updated if public API changed
- [x] CHANGELOG.md entry added (under `[Unreleased]`)

Tests added: pseudo-device grouping and area inheritance, disabled entities skipped, and four cases for `compact_devices_for_prompt` (keeps what the prompt and colour repair need, drops what nothing references, survives missing/malformed fields, and is substantially smaller). The existing `test_fetch_devices_entities_with_location_without_states` asserted that a device-less `switch.orphan` was **absent** — that assertion was encoding the bug and now asserts the opposite.

No public API changed; `compact_devices_for_prompt` is a new internal helper in `ha_helper`.

## For reviewers

Merge once:

- [ ] CI is green (Python matrix + coverage, lint, frontend)
- [ ] Change is covered by tests, or the **How to test** steps were verified
- [ ] Scope matches the summary — no unrelated drive-by changes
- [ ] CHANGELOG + docs updated where the change is user-facing

Worth a closer look:

- The first commit is **not** a strict no-op for existing users: it adds entities that were previously dropped and removes disabled ones. Both are corrections, but the actuator sends the device payload uncapped, so a setup with many helper or template entities will see its prompt grow — partly offset by the second commit.
- The pseudo-device entries carry `device_id: "no-device:<area_id>"` and a null `manufacturer`/`model`. The output shape (a list of devices) is unchanged, so every consumer keeps working, but the map view now has an extra card.

## Related issues

Closes #

author: aarushgarg1110
body:
Closes #58.

## What was wrong

`MAX_CHUNK_CHARS = 4000` was enforced by **slicing** `chunk_text`, so anything past char 4000 never reached `session_chunks`. Three paths did it:

1. **A single message over the cap** — `chunker.py:114` said so outright: *"A single message larger than the cap becomes its own chunk (truncated)."* A 12k-char handoff report is one message → one 4k chunk.
2. **`_merge_undersized`** folded a sub-250-char chunk into its predecessor with no size check, then the result was sliced — undoing #41's pre-cut guard after the fact. This was the common case: 479 of 558 at-cap chunks in the live DB spanned multiple turns.
3. **`_chunk_fixed`** joined up to 20 messages and sliced.

## What changed

- `_split_oversized(text, max_chars)` — breaks at the last whitespace inside the window so words stay intact; hard-cuts only whitespace-free runs (minified JSON, base64). Only the single whitespace char at a cut point is consumed.
- `_materialize(messages, bounds, max_chars)` — now the **only** place `chunk_text` is produced. Both `_chunk_fixed` and `_chunk_by_topic` build `bounds` and delegate, so no path *can* truncate. Pieces of one span share `turn_start`/`turn_end` and take consecutive `chunk_index` values; nothing downstream keys on turn-bound uniqueness (`store.py:178` only selects them).
- `_merge_undersized` takes `max_chars` and declines a merge that would overflow — a slightly-small chunk beats a truncated one, and splitting it back apart would just recreate the tiny chunk.

Funnelling three sites into one materializer over patching each slice: it makes truncation structurally impossible instead of fixed in three places that can drift.

## What that actually cost

Not keyword findability. `sessions.all_user_text` stores the full conversation **uncapped** (`parser.py:37`: *"full conversation text (user + assistant), no cap"*) and `sessions_fts` indexes it, so a truncated passage still matched at session level. What it lost is everything only a chunk provides:

1. **Navigation** — a session-level hit carries no `chunk_index`, so `medulla_session_detail` can't open the passage. You learn *which session* mentions it, not *where*.
2. **Semantic search entirely** — `vec_chunks` embeds `chunk_text` only. Truncated text has no vector, so hybrid/vector search cannot reach it at all.
3. **Ranking** — BM25 over a 1,088,571-char session blob instead of a focused 4k chunk.

Verified on the live index: 40 verbatim 70-char slices of cut text, one per affected session, were findable in a chunk 1/40 before and 40/40 after. Example — session `ecc33884`, a 9,364-char conversation that had exactly 4,000 chars of chunks: the same query returns a bare excerpt before, and `→ medulla_session_detail(session_id="ecc33884", chunk_index=1)` after.

## Measured on 100 real local sessions

Committed chunker (via `git show HEAD:`) vs. this branch, same inputs:

| metric | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| chunks | 2,784 | 3,433 | +649 |
| indexed chars | 7,987,170 | 9,619,442 | **+1,632,272 (+20%)** |

52 of 100 sessions gain content; the worst goes 10 → 41 chunks (it was indexing ~25% of its own text). A per-session invariant check — concatenated `chunk_text` == input modulo cut whitespace — passed on all 100.

## Tests

- Flipped `test_very_long_single_message_truncated` → `..._splits_instead_of_truncating`; it had been *asserting* the bug.
- 14 new tests: `_split_oversized` (under cap, exact cap, exact multiple, whitespace cuts, whitespace-free hard cuts, no empty pieces), the merge cap guard both ways plus the first-chunk forward fold, an oversized turn mid-session with neighbours intact, the fixed-window path, and a cross-path no-content-loss invariant.
- `_split_oversized`'s loop is `while True` — the `while start < n` exit is unreachable (the remainder-fits break always fires) and showed as a permanent partial branch.

**647 passed; statement coverage 95.69%** (gate 95%), `chunker.py` at 100% statements.

## Migration

`medulla scan --force` after merge — re-chunks and re-embeds inline (`scanner.py:107`).

> Note: this PR is the second half of the story. The live index was also being built by a **frozen, non-editable `uv tool install` from Jun 9** whose chunker predated #41 — so #41's migration never actually took effect. Reinstalling with `--editable` and re-scanning recovered a further +2,236,770 chars (+43%) on its own. Details in `reflections/fix-chunker-split-not-truncate.md`.

author: rickfelix
body:
## Problem

**BETA-blocking 2 of 4.** §H10 mandates that verifier disagreement is *journaled and never silently resolved* — but the journal schema had no way to express one.

On run `s2026-alpha4-0807` two fresh-context verifiers disputed the runner's own summary. Both `EVENT_KINDS` and `FINDING_TYPES` are closed allowlists, so `kind: 'verifier_disagreement'` threw and `finding_type: 'VERIFIER_DISAGREEMENT'` threw. Both verdicts had to be demoted to `lifecycle`, where they are indistinguishable from ordinary run narration and invisible to any reader filtering by kind. BETA's §4 grading reads that record — **a disagreement not findable by kind never reaches the grader.**

The closed allowlists are good design; they stop typo'd kinds. §H10 was simply added without a matching kind.

## Fix

A first-class `verifier_disagreement` kind carrying **both verdicts plus the governing rule**. Recording that verifiers diverged without recording which verdict wins leaves the reader to guess — and guessing *is* the silent resolution §H10 forbids. `DISAGREEMENT_RULES` is `owner_recount` (the §H10 default), `verifier_majority`, or `unresolved`.

Two decisions worth review:

- **Validation matches `finding`'s discipline.** A disagreement missing either verdict, or carrying an unknown rule, is rejected *at write time* rather than persisted as an unreadable half-record.
- **The three fields are PERSISTED at top level, not merely validated.** I caught this while writing it: the row builder would have validated `claim`/`counter_claim`/`governing_rule` and then dropped them, since it only copies an allowlist of fields. That is precisely the failure this whole QF set exists to fix — the write looks correct and the record comes back empty. Top level rather than nested in `detail` so a reader can filter them the same way it filters by kind.

## Verification

- **7 tests**, including the QF's stated acceptance case: replay the real `s2026-alpha4-0807` disagreement and find it by kind, with both verdicts surviving the round-trip and the lifecycle-demotion path confirmed gone.
- **Mutation-proved:** making the row validate the fields and then drop them turns exactly the persistence test and the acceptance test red, and leaves the other five green — so those two are genuinely load-bearing rather than decoration.
- Assertions read **back from disk**, not from the return value, because the record is what the grader actually sees.
- No regression: 20 harness test files / 177 tests green, and the §H9 seeded-defect calibration still returns GO.

2026-08-07 に実際に踏みました。PR #95 の CI で `Install Linux dependencies`（apt-get）が **20 分以上返らない**実行が出ています。

author: zihangli-hndsm
body:
## Goal
PR B（`feat/unified-visualization-playground`）：把 Linear Regression / KNN 从两个独立 Playground 重构为运行在同一个 **Unified Visualization Playground Runtime** 上的两个模型 preset。不涉及 PR C（Agent 生成脚本）与项目 schema/Agent API 变更。

## Files changed
- 新增 `src/core/playground/`：`playgroundRuntime.js`（唯一 session reducer）、`model/`（modelRegistry + linearRegressionAdapter + knnAdapter）、`data/datasetAdapter.js`、`trace/`（traceTypes + traceBuilder）、`visualization/`（primitives、scriptSchema、scriptValidator、scriptRuntime、presetRegistry）、`presets/`（linearRegressionIntro、knnIntro）。
- `src/core/playgrounds/`：`linearRegression.js` / `knn.js` 降级为纯元数据描述符（新增 `adapterId`），`session.js` 改为统一 runtime 的兼容薄封装。
- 新增 `src/components/playground/`：UnifiedPlaygroundDialog、PlaygroundToolbar、PlaygroundStage、PlaygroundInspector、PlaygroundTimeline 与 11 个 primitive renderer；删除旧模型专用视图（KnnView / LinearRegressionView / viewRegistry / PlaygroundShell 等）。
- `scripts/check-core.mjs`、`docs/architecture/overview.md`、`docs/architecture/playgrounds.md`、`src/locales/ui.js`、`CHANGELOG.md`。

## Architecture decisions
- **单一 reducer**：UI、Canvas Agent 与 script runtime 都通过 `dispatchRuntimeAction()` 派发同一套 JSON action；旧描述符不再实现 `reduce/createInitialState/deriveScene`（check-core 断言其不存在）。
- **Model Adapter 契约**：`initialize / applyModelAction / deriveScene / buildPrimitives` + capabilities；LR 复用 `linearRegressionMath`，KNN 复用 `knnMath`（同一 `fitKnn`/split/seed=2026），KNN fit trace 保持 lazy-learning（split → normalization → 保存样本 → ready）。
- **语义 trace**：JSON-safe、确定性（id/step/timestamp 用会话内计数器）；LR 10 类事件、KNN 10 类事件。
- **Visualization Script DSL**：JSON preset（version 1），validator 拒绝未知模型/primitive/operation/binding/trace event、可执行字符串、超限复杂度；script runtime 把每个 step 翻译成同一套 playground action，seek/reset 通过重放实现。
- **边界**：adapter 不 import React（静态断言）；renderer 不 import 模型数学（静态断言）；Stage 只认识 primitives。

## Acceptance（PR B 1–10）
1. LR 与 KNN 都在同一 `playgroundRuntime` 上运行（共享 traces/script/primitives/visualState）✓
2. 不存在两个独立 session reducer（描述符无 `reduce`；唯一实现为 runtime）✓
3. 两个模型使用不同 Model Adapter（modelRegistry 断言）✓
4. UI renderer 不 import 模型数学（静态断言覆盖全部 `src/components/playground/**`）✓
5. 模型 adapter 不 import React（静态断言）✓
6. preset 是 JSON-safe declaration（structuredClone + validator 通过）✓
7. preset 可 serialize → deserialize → replay（同一 preset + seed + data 重放 trace 逐位一致）✓
8. Agent API open/inspect/play/pause/step/seek/reset/subscribe 保持可用（既有契约测试通过）✓
9. 同一 script + seed + data 得到相同 trace（LR/KNN preset 各重放两次 deepEqual）✓
10. PR A 全部 regression tests 保持通过（`npm run check` 全绿）✓

## Commands run
- `npm run check` ✓（41 组件/双框架/12 示例 + 新增 PR B 断言）
- `npm run check:compiler` ✓
- `npm run build` ✓（666 modules）
- `git diff --check` ✓

## Evidence
- LR preset 重放：7 步完成，最终 weight/bias 收敛到最小二乘最优（1.959 / 0.935），80 条 trace，两次重放 deepEqual。
- KNN preset 重放：11 步完成，showNeighborOrder/showDecisionRegions=true，38 条 trace 含 prediction.emitted，两次重放 deepEqual。
- Agent 端到端：LR 打开（script=linear-regression.intuition）→ runScenario('intro') completed；KNN 打开（script=knn.intro）→ completed，runtimeAccuracy=0.975。

## Browser checks
本会话无浏览器自动化工具，未做交互式浏览器实测；构建与 Node 级场景验证覆盖视图所需 primitives 契约，可启动本地实例人工复核。

## Known limitations / deviations
- Agent API 未新增 `loadPreset/validateScript/generateScript`（属 PR C 范围）。
- `linearRegressionIntro` 最后一步 `setBestFit` 会清空训练时间线（与旧 intro 行为一致），故 loss-curve primitive 在结束后不再显示。
- 交互式浏览器验收留待人工/后续轮次。

body:
## Problem

Every rollback ended with the same block, regardless of what happened:

```
⚠️  Application Startup Issue Detected
💡 Possible causes:
   Your application was unable to start within the expected timeframe
🔧 How to fix:
   1. Port Configuration: Ensure your application listens on port 8080
   ...
```

Including manual rollbacks of applications that started perfectly well.

## Cause

`print_deployment_error_hints` was the last step of `rollback.yaml`, running **after** `delete deployment`. The diagnosis it performs reads the failed deployment's pods:

```bash
kubectl get pods -n "$K8S_NAMESPACE" -l "deployment_id=${DEPLOYMENT_ID}"
```

Those pods were deleted two steps earlier, so the query always came back empty. With no `FAILURE_REASON`, `SUGGESTED_FIX` stayed empty, and the script's fallback for "nothing detected" printed the generic block:

```bash
if [[ -z "$SUGGESTED_FIX" ]]; then
    print_generic_hints
fi
```

The specific diagnosis — image pull errors, crash loops, OOM kills, failed health checks, each with a targeted suggested fix — could never run in a rollback.

## Change

Move the hints step ahead of the deletion. One step reordered, no script changes.

The failed deployment's pods are still present at that point under both strategies:

- **blue/green** — `scale_deployments` is a no-op; its entire body sits inside `if [ "$DEPLOY_STRATEGY" = "rolling" ]`.
- **rolling** — `build_context:115` floors green replicas at `MIN_REPLICAS` *after* the traffic-based calculation, with the comment "Apply minimum after the blue replica calculation so we do not remove pods with 0% traffic switch".

## Not addressed here

A manual rollback of a healthy deployment will still reach the generic block, because "nothing detected" and "nothing was wrong" are indistinguishable to the fallback. Separating them means changing the shared script's contract — `wait_deployment_active` sources it on deploy timeout, where the generic hints *are* the right output. That deserves its own change.

## Tests

`k8s` BATS suite green (38 tests). Workflow YAMLs have no unit tests in this repo; the file was validated by parsing it and asserting the resulting step order.

author: nightskyguy
body:
## Why

A user asked whether brokerage basis step-up at death was implemented, after running `?bk=2e5` and seeing Brokerage $113,423 / Basis $13,920 in 2049 where they expected the two to match.

It is not implemented. The README said nothing about it either way, so the Basis column falling straight through the first death reads as a bug rather than a known limitation.

## Validation, before writing anything

Three independent confirmations:

1. **Grep is exhaustive.** `balance.BrokerageBasis` is mutated in exactly three places, none death-related: proportional reduction on withdrawal (`optimizer_core.js:292`), surplus reinvestment (`:2018`), DRIP dividends (`:2282`). `computeIncome`'s death block (`:1088-1089`) moves the **IRA only**.
2. **Reproduced live.** At the page defaults (`birthyear1=1960`/`die1=88` → first death 2049; `birthyear2=1952`/`die2=98`), `status` flips `MFJ` → `SGL` in 2049 while `Basis` keeps falling monotonically through it: 2048 $148,013/$9,630, 2049 $128,542/$7,888, 2050 $106,082/$6,139.
3. **The repo already knew.** `task_plan.md` has P35 PR 3d and PR 4 both unchecked, and line 524 already lists "no basis step-up at death" among the 16 deferred README caveats.

The reporter's own figures are self-consistent with pro-rata reduction and no reset: $8,419/$13,920 = 0.6048 against $72,739/($113,423 × 1.06) = 0.6050.

## The part that was not already known

`afterTaxNetWorth` (`optimizer_core.js:3626-3627`) and `_afterTaxBuckets` (`:3001`) both value terminal brokerage as `basis + max(0, brokerage - basis) * (1 - capGainsRate)` — taxing heirs on gains IRC §1014 steps up in full.

This is the **larger** of the two distortions, because it feeds Break Even, the "Optimize for" ranking, and every cross-strategy comparison. And it is one-sided: Roth and Cash are unaffected, so the bias runs consistently **in favor of** Roth conversions. P35 PR 4's recorded spec covered only the first-death `resolveHousehold` hook, so this is now written into the phase as in-scope.

## What changed

Documentation only, by decision. No engine change; no shipped number moves.

- **`README.md`, "Limitations and Restrictions"** — one entry covering both deaths, each with its direction of error named (the section's existing style). Notes that the default state CA is a community-property state, where the full step-up the reporter expected is the *correct* answer rather than an approximation, and gives the raise-Basis-by-hand workaround for sizing the effect today.
- **`README.md`, brokerage FAQ** — cross-reference from the DRIP "Gotcha". That paragraph was the only place using the phrase "step up", and it meant the sense that *does* happen, so it is exactly where a reader chasing this question lands.
- **`.planning/retirement-optimizer/task_plan.md`** — absence validated against a live run with the numbers, so a later session does not re-derive it. The PR 4 README item is marked done ahead of the code, and its wording corrected: it said "the uncovered-tax-situations section", but no section by that name exists. Terminal-valuation gap added. `'auto'` and the 7-state `COMMUNITY_PROPERTY` list re-confirmed, with a note that no such constant exists in `taxengine.js` yet.

## Reviewer notes

- **No version bump, no `?v=` cache-token change, no changelog entry.** Nothing under an `.html` file's load path changes.
- **No browser check.** A README edit cannot move the in-page suite; there is no `.html`/`.js`/`.css` in this diff.
- node **214/32/22** green (pre-commit hook ran them). Zero em-dashes in `README.md`, per the repo's user-facing text convention.

author: tortoisewolfe
body:
**T022.** Without this the uploader is half a feature. A buyer can attach eight screenshots of the site they have and the look they want, and there was nowhere to look at any of them — `intake-uploads` is a **private** bucket (FR-016), so no URL exists to paste anywhere. The files were reachable by nobody.

There was no `/admin/orders` route at all. Admin had audit, email, messaging, payments and users; nothing rendered an order, its intake, or its attachments.

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**Reads on the admin's own session, not service-role.** Two policies already grant exactly this and no more: `Admin can view all orders` (`is_admin()`) on `public.orders`, and the `is_admin()` branch of the `intake-uploads` SELECT policy. A service-role client in the browser would bypass RLS entirely — a far larger grant than a read-only page needs.

**Signed URLs are minted per click, not per render.** An `<a href>` per attachment would sign a live one-hour credential for every file on the page whether or not anyone opened it — each one landing in browser history and any logging in between. It is a button; nothing is signed until the operator asks.

## Failure modes it distinguishes

A failed query and a genuinely empty result look identical if you only check array length, so the panel reports `permission denied` rather than rendering "No orders yet" over a broken query. A signing failure surfaces as an alert instead of opening a blank tab.

## Registration

Added to **both** places that list admin pages — `AdminGate`'s nav and the e2e nav spec. Adding a tab without adding it to that spec would leave the new page the one admin route nothing exercises. The name "Orders" was checked for substring collisions against the existing entries first (#378's shape, where a new accessible name shadowed an existing locator).

10 new tests · structure validator 134/134 · types and lint clean.

Refs #560

author: samcat116
body:
ADR 0001 stage 8. Closes STR-150.

Snapshots and checkpoints were the last durable *artifacts* driven by imperative
agent RPCs: seven messages that each blocked on a response with a hand-tuned
timeout, with three controllers hand-rolling the same background verdict
machinery around them. The worst of that was the ambiguous case — a reply is
delivered once, so a socket that dropped mid-flight left the control plane
unable to tell a failed checkpoint from a successful one whose reply it never
saw, and both paths answered by issuing a speculative delete and marking the row
`.error` for a checkpoint that half the time existed.

The header this converts opened by asserting a checkpoint "is an *action* rather
than a state". True of the verb, false of the result: **"checkpoint C exists for
VM V" is a durable artifact** with an identity, a footprint and a host.

`volume_snapshot`, `volume_snapshot_delete`, `vm_checkpoint`,
`vm_snapshot_delete`, `sandbox_snapshot_create`, `sandbox_snapshot_delete` and
`sandbox_snapshot_export` are deleted at wire v32. All three snapshot tables are
`ConvergingResource`s and `FinalizableResource`s now; every endpoint answers
`202` and clients poll `conditions`.

## Four decisions worth reviewing

**One kind-tagged list, three tables.** The families differ only in which backend
writes the bytes and what metadata comes back; identity, the generation guard,
the absent-then-confirm dance and the export placement fact are the same shape
three times. So the wire carries one list. They stay three *tables* — three quota
paths, three IAM node types, budgets an order of magnitude apart — sharing
behavior through `SnapshotArtifactResource`.

**A capture is a create strategy**, read only while the artifact is absent from
the host. Without it, a level-triggered entry carrying "pause this guest and copy
its RAM" would re-checkpoint a running VM on every replayed sync. Pinned by
`SnapshotReconciliationTests.presentArtifactIsNotRecaptured`.

**Export is a placement fact.** The upload route stamps `exported_at` on the PUT
that completes the set, which removed the export RPC's last reason to exist; the
agent's word still never stamps it.

**Retention is designed here** — the `Job.ttlSecondsAfterFinished` lesson the ADR
names as this stage's cost. Absolute `expires_at` per artifact plus a
cluster-singleton sweep attributed to `system`. Count-based retention is
deliberately deferred; the reasoning is in `docs/architecture/storage.md`.

## Departure from the issue text

The issue asks for both "retire the `VMSnapshotService`/`SandboxSnapshotService`
scaffolding" and "wire-version bump + dual-mode window", which cannot both hold:
a dual-mode window preserves every background verdict half this stage exists to
delete. This is a **hard cutover**, following stage 5's precedent (recorded in
the ADR).

Where the gate sits could not be copied from stage 5, though. A volume is
*placed* by the control plane, so v31 could refuse to schedule one onto an agent
that could not converge it; an artifact inherits its parent's host, so there is
no placement decision to gate. `supportsSnapshotSync` gates **capture admission**
instead — `POST .../snapshots` against a pre-v32 agent is refused with `409`,
which is what the pre-v22/v9 capability preflights already did, one floor higher.
Artifacts already on such an agent freeze until it is upgraded; deleting one
still works, because the delete path force-clears the agent-absence finalizer.

## Fell out along the way

- **`SnapshotRecordStore`** — the agent needed a durable inventory, for
  `VMManifestStore`'s reason: a Firecracker checkpoint's fork-layout version and
  CPU template are not recoverable from its files, and enumerating qcow2 internal
  snapshots costs a subprocess per VM per report.
- **A volume no longer passes through `snapshotting`** — that status existed only
  to represent something happening *to* the volume that had nowhere else to live.
- **A checkpoint no longer occupies the VM's one pending operation slot**, which
  could block start/stop/delete for half an hour behind a bare `409`.
- **Three `agent_id` indexes**, since sync assembly and observed-state
  application both scan by it, once per poll and once per report.

## Testing

`swift test` green on all three packages (209 / 931 / 2236), `swift format lint
--strict` clean, `bun run lint` and `bun run build` clean, `redocly lint` valid.
New: `SnapshotReconciliationTests` (shared, agent) and `SnapshotConvergenceTests`
(control plane), each pinning one direction of the nil-versus-empty contract —
read wrong, silence here destroys a point in time nothing can recreate.

author: ihid
body:
Completes the i18n half of the content split: every translated content type can now be published from here.

## What is already reviewed, and what is new

This branch **includes the commits of three earlier PRs**:

- **#4** (`ihid-i18n-publish`) — a mutable `current.json` pointer beside every artifact
- **#5** (`ihid-i18n-renderer`) — translated concept pages via `@jiki.io/content-renderer`
- **#7** (`ihid-i18n-publish-flow`) — publish from `main`, and only from `main`
- **#8** (`ihid-i18n-test-corpus`) — `maze-solve-basic`, the `maze` family catalog, one blog post

**New here** are the last two commits:

- `Publish posts and exercise instructions, and make "nothing partial ships" true`
- `Keep the source export out of an --out-dir tree`

### The `publish.mjs` conflict between #4 and #5

Both rewrote `emit()` and the `main()` docs. Resolved by taking **#5's structure** (async, `emit`/`emitBytes` split) and layering **#4's pointer emission inside `emitBytes`**, so rendered HTML gets a pointer on exactly the same terms as a catalog. The one true conflict was the `manifest.json` comment, where #4 corrects the premise (#5 still described the manifest as a hand-back the front-end needs); kept #4's framing plus #5's renderer-version rationale.

#8's narrow `blog-post` type is **removed**, as its own comment anticipated — superseded by the three `blog`/`articles`/`guides` types here.

## 1. Posts

Three new content types, one per layout, rendered with the renderer package's second pipeline (`renderPost`). Project episodes stay front-end published: a UUID directory that is not the slug, plus per-episode `config.json` metadata, do not fit this repo's `(type, locale, slug)` coordinates.

Images are **resolved, never copied**. The fingerprinted URL hashes bytes that live in the front-end's `content` package, and English references the same images, so the front-end publishes them and this repo only names them. A translation referencing an image English does not is a hard error rather than a dead link. The source-repo checkout is taken lazily, so a corpus whose posts reference no images publishes without one.

## 2. Exercise instructions

An artifact here for the first time. They could not be while the front-end cached instructions, stub and solution in one file, because stubs and solutions are code this repo does not hold. The front-end now splits them along their real keys, so this publishes the prose half plus the per-locale prose index that names it — and that index carries **no code hashes**.

Category concepts (`arrays-group`, ...) are skipped: an empty body is a heading in the concept tree, and the front-end renders no HTML for one.

## 3. Untranslated prose has THREE conventions, not two

All three are now refused, skipped and counted:

1. **The sentinel** (`U+FFFD`) — machine-readable, handled on the catalog path
2. **Copied English** — byte-identical body. Exact, and the most dangerous: it satisfies every structural check trivially, carries a valid staleness stamp, and would publish as a healthy artifact serving English from a translated URL
3. **A translation notice** — fully translated frontmatter over a one-line body saying the page is not translated yet. **Nothing in the file marks it**

The third is caught **corpus-wide** rather than per-file: group a locale's items by translated body, and any group with more than one member whose English bodies differ is untranslated, because two items whose English differs cannot share one correct translation.

That is **exact, not heuristic** — no thresholds, no phrase list, no knowledge of any language — so it works on the thirtieth locale as well as the first. Its one blind spot is a notice used exactly once in a locale.

Measured over the real hu corpus (185 file pairs): **17 copied-English and 17 notice items, zero false positives, zero misses**. The hu notice convention alone has three distinct phrasings, which is why a phrase list was rejected.

## 4. The partialness defect

`publish` measured completeness against the **mirror** in `locales/source/`, which is a subset by design. So a locale that had translated everything it imported looked complete — and the check passed most convincingly exactly when the mirror was smallest, which is when it mattered most. On `main` today that meant the curriculum copy catalog published from a 1-exercise corpus.

`sync-source` now records the **real per-type corpus size** in `.manifest.json` as `corpus`, on the same terms as the family map: a fact only the front-end holds, captured at sync time so `publish` still needs no front-end checkout. **A manifest without `corpus` counts as unknowable, not complete.**

Pre-existing defect, but it directly undermined the rule this PR implements.

## 5. `--allow-partial` and `--allow-incomplete` are gone

Both refusals are now properties of the script rather than of how it was invoked, which is the only place a rule like this survives — mirroring the English guard, which has never had an override.

They **skip loudly and continue** rather than abort, so one unfinished locale cannot block every finished one, and a merge-triggered publish does not turn `main` red on most merges. **A run with nothing shippable exits 0**: a green no-op, not a failure.

## 6. `--out-dir`

Writes the same tree into a front-end checkout, which is what its `pnpm dev` runs. Under `--out-dir` the tree is not wiped first (it is shared with the front-end's own generators), no `manifest.json`/`sync.sh`/upload is produced, the `dist/export/` source tree is skipped (it would be Markdown served to the internet), and the final guard re-walk is skipped — that tree is full of English this repo did not write, and every key this run emitted was guarded at `emit()` anyway.

## Verification

Against a scratch worktree pinned at `initial-catalog`, with the full corpus synced and hu imported so both sides render identical input:

| artifact class | byte-identical | differing |
|---|---|---|
| concepts | 43 | 0 |
| posts | 5 | 0 |
| exercise prose | 100 | 0 |
| exercise messages | 106 | 0 |
| **total** | **254** | **0** |

- `node scripts/test.mjs`: all assertions pass, including 8 new ones for the untranslated-prose rules
- `node scripts/validate.mjs all --no-stamp`: 10 items, 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `node scripts/sync-source.mjs --check`: mirror clean

## Companion

Pairs with **jiki-education/front-end#1038**, which owns the renderer and the exercise cache split.

author: jgw2210
body:
The round-8 map pass: the world becomes an interconnected web of coherent biome islands rather than a mottled expanse. Poll answers implemented: quadrant climates; the custom "archipelago joined by narrow shallows rivers, still warden-gated"; all four void-flare packs; monumental multi-hex landmarks.

## Worldgen

- **Quadrant climates** — stronger N/S temperature gradient with less noise, east mountain bias, and a radial "home" damping so the start vale is always meadow/forest. No more desert or glacier bleeding into the middle island (0 impure home tiles across the 40-seed suite).
- **Speckle purge (pass 3.2)** — lone off-biome tiles adopt the local majority, so biomes arrive as contiguous sweeps.
- **Archipelago erosion (pass 2.5)** — clumped fbm noise gnaws every coastline into bays and headlands; rifts widen 1.7 → 2.1. New pass 6.8 replants the start in region 0's largest fragment so the connectivity cull can never drown the world.
- **The water web** — causeways are now *Warded Shallows*: narrow star-water fords, gold-warded, mechanically unchanged (same gates, same sealing passes). Pass 6.9 carves river-joins from each channel mouth to the nearest waters so lake, river, and crossing read as one web.
- **Forgotten islets (pass 10.5)** — three hidden micro-worlds adrift in the rifts (hermit trader, wrecked sky-ship, sundered observatory), each revealed by detonating on a humming shore, with leak-proof folded footbridges, an `islefinder` feat, and save-v4 persistence.

## World view

- **Rift debris fields** — instanced hex plates, rocks, and slabs drifting in the void, with a scattering of visibly tumbling pieces.
- **Island undersides** — rocky root cones beneath each region and satellite, coastal stalactites, stardust falls bleeding off the edges.
- **Sky weather** — aurora ribbons over the tundra, ember plumes over the caldera, pooled shooting stars, drifting cloud shadows.
- **Monumental landmarks** — walled capital city-mounds with banners and kingdom-colored sky-beacons; towns with windmills and chimney smoke; biome-carved dungeon facades (colossus, hollow tree, ziggurat, obsidian fangs, ice vault, geode, barrow); towering gate arches with spinning keystones; shrine rune-rings; satboss thrones; a nebula swirl; hand-built islet models.

author: orvixcompute
body:
## Description

Four related fixes to things production was getting wrong in ways users could feel. **Authored in a separate session; this PR carries it through review and deploy.**

### `fix(api)` — tell "all providers busy" apart from "no provider serves this model"

Both answered the same refusal, so a caller could not tell a transient condition from a permanent one.

### `fix(auth)` — persist challenge nonces so a restart stops breaking sign-in

Nonces lived in a dict on `AuthService` and failed two ways:

- **A restart wiped every pending challenge.** One issued at 20:14:38 was rejected at 20:14:45, three seconds after the service came back at 20:14:42. With seven restarts in a day while deploying, anyone signing in at the wrong moment was turned away.
- **The dict was keyed by wallet and held one entry**, so a second `/challenge` call silently invalidated the first — a client that asked twice, or re-rendered, broke the signature the user had already approved in their wallet.

Both surfaced as the same opaque 401. Migration 017 stores challenges as rows keyed by nonce, which is what allows several outstanding per wallet; the wallet is still checked against the row so a nonce cannot be redeemed by anyone else. Expiry, single use and the 5-minute TTL are unchanged.

### `feat(api)` — say which models are actually being served

The catalog is static, so `/v1/models` listed three chat models while the single connected node ran one. Picking `mistral-7b` returned 503 — correct, but only discoverable by failing. Entries now carry an additive `available` flag from the live registry.

Also fixes a self-inflicted inconsistency in `/v1/network/stats`: only `nodes.online` was overlaid live on the cached snapshot, so a node reconnecting inside the 30s window produced an impossible response — `online=1` beside `ready=0` and `offline=1`.

### `feat(inference)` — wait briefly for a slot instead of dropping the request

A burst overshooting `max_concurrent_jobs` was refused the instant it arrived, though the jobs ahead finish in a second or two. In production four requests were turned away with `capacity_exhausted` while sitting between two batches the same node completed successfully. `acquire_node()` now polls for up to `CAPACITY_WAIT_SECONDS` and returns the moment a slot opens. It does **not** wait when nothing serves the model — that answer cannot change by waiting — and re-checks mid-wait, so a node dropping out turns the wait into an immediate refusal.

## Related Issue
Requires migration 017 (already applied — see below).

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor (no functional change)
- [ ] Chore (build, dependencies, CI)

## Component
- [x] Orchestrator
- [ ] Node
- [x] Database / Migrations
- [x] Docs
- [ ] CI/CD

## How has this been tested?
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing (describe below)

**233 passed**, ruff clean, on the branch as it stands.

Two existing tests asserted the *old* mixed `/v1/network/stats` behaviour — seeded database rows counting as ready/busy while nothing was connected — and were updated to the consistent semantics rather than worked around.

**Migration 017 was applied to production before opening this PR**, and verified: the `auth_challenges` table exists, an insert/read/delete round-trip succeeds, and the `created_at` default fires. That ordering is deliberate — merging this branch before the table existed would have broken wallet login outright, the exact failure the auth commit fixes.

Merge into current `main` verified conflict-free, and the two branches turn out to share **no touched files at all**.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines (ruff passes)
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published

## Breaking changes

None for callers. `/v1/models` gains an additive `available` field and `/v1/network/stats` gains `chat_available` / `image_available`; nothing is removed or renamed.

`AuthService` no longer holds state, so `create_challenge` / `verify_signature` now take a db handle like every other service — internal only.

## Additional notes

Migration 017 was applied by hand through the Supabase SQL Editor, so it is **not yet recorded in `schema_migrations`**. Whoever next runs `scripts/migrate.py up` with a `DATABASE_URL` will see it re-run as a no-op purely to record it — the documented bootstrap pattern, not a fault. There is no "mark applied" command.

The capacity wait adds a bounded delay to a request that would previously have failed instantly. `CAPACITY_WAIT_SECONDS` is the lever if that trade turns out wrong under real load; the current GPU is compute-bound, so a saturated node stays saturated for roughly the length of one job.

author: mgrossmann
body:
Fixes #141.

A module invoked outside HTTPD — `CALL 'HTTPD.LINKLIB(HTTPDSL)'` from TSO, or `EXEC PGM=` in a batch job — ended in a bare `__exita()` in `cgistart`: RC 12, no message anywhere. The guard in every module's `main()` that exists to explain exactly this was unreachable, because `cgistart` gave up first over a missing DD.

## What changed

`cgistart` now checks the server context **before** the DDs and routes every failure through one function.

Checking the context first is the part that matters: without it no set of DDs would make the module work, so the message names the real problem instead of whichever DD happened to fail first.

Reporting needs an output channel, which is the very thing that may be missing — so it opens one. `fopen()` on a `'*'`-prefixed name reaches libc370's `__fpstar()`, which allocates the destination via SVC 99 and picks it by environment: the terminal under TSO foreground, a SYSOUT dataset in batch and TSO background. That is the same mechanism libc370's own `__start` uses for every ordinary C program (`@@start.c:67`); `cgistart` requiring `DD:HTTPDOUT` was the anomaly.

**Deliberately no branch on `GRTFLAG1_TSO`.** Probing all three environments showed that flag comes back **clear in every one of them, including TSO foreground**, because it is derived from the shape of the parameter list rather than from the environment — a parameterless `CALL` gives `parmLen == 0`, so the test never fires. Letting `__fpstar()` choose is both correct and less code than branching.

## Verified in all three environments

**TSO foreground** — `CALL 'IBMUSER.HTTPD.V4R0M0D.LINKLIB(HTTPDSL)'` from READY:

```
READY
CALL 'IBMUSER.HTTPD.V4R0M0D.LINKLIB(HTTPDSL)'
 HTTPDSL  is an HTTPD server module and cannot run on its own.
 Start it through the HTTPD server, which passes the server context and
 allocates the files it needs.
 Missing here: the HTTPD server context (GRT)
 READY
```

**Batch** — `EXEC PGM=HTTPDSL` against the staging LINKLIB:

```
IEF142I P141BAT STEP1 - STEP WAS EXECUTED - COND CODE 0012
HTTPDSL  is an HTTPD server module and cannot run on its own.
Start it through the HTTPD server, which passes the server context and
allocates the files it needs.
Missing here: the HTTPD server context (GRT)
```

**TSO background** — covered by the environment probe on #141, which showed `fopen("*SYSPRINT")` succeeds under IKJEFT01 and lands in the job's SYSOUT.

Before this change all three printed nothing at all.

- `make` clean under cc370 `-Wall -Werror`, 6 modules link.
- `make test-host`: 63 assertions pass.

## The server path is untouched

Every check still carries its original `&& !httpc`, so a missing DD **under** HTTPD remains exactly as tolerated as it is today — those `__exita()` calls were only ever reachable outside the server. What modules do in their own `main()` is left alone; the five duplicated guards there are out of scope (and adjacent to #105).

Not yet re-verified on the live server: `/dsl/*` through a restarted STC carrying this build. The changed code is unreachable when `httpc` is set, so the risk is structural rather than empirical, but it is worth one pass once the STC is re-bestückt.

## Not merged with this

The throwaway probe module (`test/mvs/tsttsofg.c`) lives on branch `issue-141-tso-probe`, unmerged — it is what produced the three-environment measurements and the `GRTFLAG1_TSO` finding, and it should be deleted rather than kept.

author: akrambrl
body:
Deux défauts d'affichage signalés en jouant.

## 1. GOAT DUEL affichait deux fois le minuteur

En solo — et en partie rapide, qui tourne sur le même moteur — le chrono global s'égrenait **deux fois** : dans la pastille TEMPS de la barre de score, et juste en dessous dans le gros compte à rebours central du plateau. Deux corps différents, la même valeur.

Le gros compteur central n'a de raison d'être qu'en **multijoueur**, où il porte une autre valeur : les secondes qu'il reste pour répondre à la manche en cours, qu'on ne trouve nulle part ailleurs (la barre de score y affiche la manche, pas le temps). Il ne s'affiche donc plus qu'en multi.

C'est la **barre de score** qui garde le chrono en solo, parce qu'elle est visible à toutes les phases — y compris au décompte d'entrée et au résultat de manche, où le bloc central n'existe pas. L'inverse aurait laissé le joueur sans horloge pendant ces deux temps. Devenue le seul minuteur, la pastille passe du corps 26 au corps 34 et garde son passage au rouge maillot sous les dix dernières secondes. Le plateau y gagne une ligne de hauteur, ce qui compte quand le clavier est ouvert.

## 2. Le terrain se peignait par-dessus le contenu

La barre d'indices jaune de « Trouve le joueur » paraissait translucide : les bandes de tonte et le grain de trame du terrain s'y voyaient. Son aplat était pourtant déjà opaque — c'est le terrain qui passait **au-dessus**.

Le calque du terrain portait `zIndex: 0`. Or un élément **positionné** à `z-index: 0` se peint au-dessus du flux normal, pas en dessous : tout contenu dont le conteneur n'est pas lui-même positionné passait sous le terrain. D'où, au-delà de la barre jaune : les carrés d'indice grenés, et le rond central du terrain qui traversait le champ de saisie et le bouton « Passer » du plateau de duel.

Le calque passe à `zIndex: -1`, où il reste devant le fond de son conteneur et derrière son contenu — sa place exacte. Un seul changement dans la charte plutôt qu'un `zIndex` posé à la main sur chaque écran : il y a seize conteneurs de terrain dans l'app, et le prochain aurait reproduit le défaut.

Ce que suppose un calque négatif : que le conteneur soit un **contexte d'empilement**, sinon le calque remonterait derrière le fond d'un ancêtre et disparaîtrait. Les overlays et feuilles de mode en sont déjà un par leur `zIndex` ; les trois conteneurs qui n'en avaient pas — le shell des écrans de LePont, la racine de GOAT Guess et celle du site desktop — reçoivent `isolation: isolate`, qui en crée un sans rien changer d'autre au rendu.

**Reste voulu** : les panneaux délibérément translucides (le cadre de la grille GOAT GRID et ses cases vides) laissent toujours voir la pelouse. C'est leur fond qui est semi-opaque, pas un problème d'empilement.

## Vérifications

- **Minuteur** — captures des deux modes à moteur solo : solo (`SCORE 0 · TEMPS 83s`) et partie rapide (`Akram 0 · TEMPS 82s · BernabeuKid 0`). Une seule occurrence du chrono dans le texte de la page, contre deux avant. Le chemin multijoueur demande un second client : la condition est une ligne (`!isSolo`), relue, non capturée.
- **Empilement** — captures avant/après sur quatre surfaces : Trouve le joueur (barre jaune franche, carrés d'indice nets), GOAT DUEL en jeu (le rond central ne traverse plus la saisie ni « Passer »), la grille GOAT GRID (inchangée, translucidité voulue), et le site desktop (terrain toujours visible derrière les panneaux, filigrane GOAT FC intact, panneaux propres).
- `npm run build` vert, `npx vitest run` → 53 tests passent.
- `CACHE_NAME` → v415.

## Note sur l'historique

La branche a été repartie de `main` après la fusion de la #449, et poussée en `--force-with-lease` : elle ne portait que de l'historique déjà écrasé dans `main`.

author: osirison
body:
Closes #173.

51 in-scope frames, 51 deterministic datasets, and a browser preview that reads the same ones the fidelity gate does. That pairing is the point: **a frame that passes CI is a frame a human can open and look at**, so "green" stays falsifiable by eye.

```
?frames                 the index — every in-scope frame, linked
?frame=<label>          that frame's dataset, served to every command by api.js's mock
?theme=light|dark       an explicit override, for a light frame on a dark machine
```

### The number that did not move, on purpose

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| frames with a **dataset** | 11 | **51** |
| frames with a **`fids` map** | 11 | **11** |
| assertions | 12,441 | 12,441 |

Those are different claims and the gates are kept apart so neither can inflate the other. `check-fixtures.mjs` proves the first; `assert.mjs` counts the second by looking for `data-fid` in the rendered DOM. Adding forty datasets moved `11/51` by zero frames — which is the honest outcome, since a mapping needs a screen to exist and S1–S10 have not built one yet. Each S-task adds its own.

### Ground truth is the drawn frames, not judgement

Every string, count, filename and progress fraction is read off `frames/*.json`, whose nodes carry the prototype's own `text`. Nothing is paraphrased and nothing is guessed.

### What a fixture may not do

**Invent a Phase-2 API.** Four frames draw content no Phase-1 command returns — G1–G4 — and a plausible-looking field shape for those would settle a design nobody has agreed to from a preview dataset. Each carries only the Phase-1 surface and says so where the field would go. One draft did mint `{ upBytes, downBytes }` for `9a Review` while `plan.js` refused the identical numbers by name on `5a Plan`; the family briefly carried two answers to one question. Removed.

**Compute a displayed string.** One clock rule for all 51 (`clock.js`): a value the app renders *relatively* is pinned as `ago(n)`; a value the frame draws as an *absolute* time is written literally, because an epoch formatted as a clock time depends on the machine's timezone and moves across midnight. `check-fixtures.mjs` fails on a `new Date()` anywhere in the directory.

### Four capability gaps this found — #206, #207, #208, #209

None of them among the ten in `IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §4, none among G1–G4. **P0.2 could not have caught them**: it compared docs against frames, and these are not disagreements — the doc and the frame agree, and no command can produce what they agree on. An absence in a reply shape is invisible until someone tries to fill the reply in.

Two are safety rather than cosmetics:

- **G8 (#208)** — no subtree aggregate for a directory, so `Delete 1,204 photos from this computer?` cannot state the magnitude of the thing you are confirming. The one place in this design where a missing number is a safety problem and not a blank.
- **G6 (#206)** — no size on a planned action, so `9a Review`'s `Needs 38.4 GB free. You have 214 GB.` — and C4's free-space check with it — rests on a number nothing computes.

`DEVIATIONS.md` §60 has all four with their frames.

### What the gates found in this PR's own work

**`check-fixtures.mjs` found a live trap.** `hexFids` handed `hexRect` and `hexNumeral` to states whose marks draw neither — rects are the paused bars alone (`hexagon.js`'s only `svgEl("rect", …)` sits in that branch), and the numeral exists only where there is a count. Inert today because `fid()` never reaches those slots, and a failure the moment a screen did. Fixed at the source.

Its rule is **"alive somewhere", not "alive here"**, and that was measured rather than assumed: the per-frame version flagged 23 of 180 keys, and all 23 were slots that frame legitimately does not draw — `meta` failed on four frames and resolved on `10a Offline`, the only compact drawing a retry line. Clean signal, wrong verdict.

**The adversarial pass found a payload the daemon cannot emit.** `9a Review` carried `total: 471` beside `plan: []` with counters summing to 474. `DryRunReport` is `{summary, plan}` parsed verbatim from the daemon's stdout and `PlanSummary::from_plan` sets `total: plan.len()` — so that reply does not exist, and the screen written against it would have looked right.

The frame is not contradictory, which is the interesting part: it draws `See all 471 actions` **and** `3 files can't be synced`, and `SkipUnsupported` *is* a plan row — so `total` is 474 and the button names `total − skipped`. A derivation, not a conflict (§61). New `fixtures/dryrun.js` makes the whole class unrepresentable, `plan.js` goes through it too, and `test/fixtures.test.js` holds the invariant across every fixture plus `requires_delete_gate` keying on the gated set while `destructive_actions` sums the display set.

**The preview rebuilt itself every poll**, and its own comment claimed it did not. An early return from `render()` does not stop `main()` polling, so a tabbed-to link lost focus every ~2s — the exact failure `dom` exists to prevent, three lines below where `mountFramePanel` guards against it. Latched; verified in a browser (same `<ul>` node and held focus across five seconds).

### Two decisions worth reviewing

**`?theme` is explicit and never inferred from a `12a` label.** Tempting to auto-stamp `data-theme="light"` — and wrong: `tokens.css` publishes the light palette twice, and `assert.mjs` pins the light frames through `emulateMediaFeatures`, which exercises the media-query block. Auto-stamping would make the attribute block answer instead and let the media half rot untested with the gate still green. A gate that supplies its own answer agrees with itself.

**A light frame names its dark twin rather than restating it.** All seven pairs measured identical — same node count, same tree keys, same strings (§62), which is `12-light-theme.md`'s "Everything else is identical" turned from a claim into a number. `sameAs` resolves late against the assembled registry, so it needs no import and closes no cycle. It inherits **data and never `fids`**, which is what stops S1 mapping a dark frame from silently re-mapping its light twin and reintroducing §58b's 142 failures.

### Checks

`npm run check` — 58 tests, 51/51 datasets, 0 failures. `npm run fidelity` — 11/51 mapped, 12,441 assertions, 0 failures; copy gate 224/224.

author: andreadev237
body:
## What this adds

The structural limit phase-6 calibration measured — boundaries invisible inside single-package monoliths, coupling inert (0 across 25 commits on the calibration repo) — is gone.

- **Full-path extraction** — the matchers keep the import as written (`ai_energy_manager.documents`, `plumb_core::manifest`, `react-dom/client`) instead of truncating to the head segment. `node:` builtin specs are skipped like relative ones.
- **Segment resolution** — an import resolves to the module whose path's trailing segments match the import's leading segments for the longest run (`-`/`_` normalised); ties go to the first-declared module. Today's last-segment rule is exactly the run-length-1 case, so every existing resolution is preserved and `## src/pkg/documents` headings simply win by matching deeper.
- **The "only new violations" guarantee, kept honest** — the final review caught that keying suppression by the (now richer) import string let a formatting-only edit to a legacy import resurrect its warnings. Suppression is now keyed by resolved edge `(from_module, to_module)`, stable under any spelling of the same crossing; the accepted trade (one legacy crossing suppresses that edge per file) is documented and pinned.

## Dogfood on the calibration repository

Sub-package modules declared from the repo's *actual* imports (grep-inspected, not guessed). The gate fired on a genuine undeclared cross-sub-package scratch import (exit 2, both modules named). `plumb report --commits 25`, previously coupling-0 everywhere, came alive: 7 of 25 commits non-zero — the big increment merges at +27/+20/+16/+9, and the repo's one code-health/dedup commit at **−1**, the signal correctly distinguishing accreting growth from cleanup. Only that repo's untracked `.plumb/` was touched; no commits there.

Stacked on #7 (calibration fixes). 305 tests, none touching the network.

author: rodrigobrim
body:
Two consecutive runs on the same card:

| | 0016 | 0017 | 0018 |
|---|---|---|---|
| run 1 | copied | `WinError 433` | `WinError 433` |
| run 2 | skipped (known) | copied | `WinError 433` |

Exactly one clip copies per run. `WinError 433` is `ERROR_NO_SUCH_DEVICE` — the camera in mass-storage mode leaves the USB bus during the first sustained read, and every remaining `shutil.copy2` then fails instantly against the dead volume. Ingest had no retry and no re-detection, so it burned through the rest of the card reporting the same error per file.

- `copy_from_card` retries a device-vanished copy (3 attempts, 5 s apart), re-finding the file by name + size across the DCIM volumes first — a re-enumeration can hand the card a different drive letter, which would make the original path permanently stale. A partial copy is deleted before each retry.
- If the card stays gone, the run stops with one line — `camera disconnected mid-ingest (...); N clip(s) not copied, starting at X. Reconnect the camera and run again - copied clips are kept.` — instead of one raw `WinError` per remaining clip.
- A genuine per-file error (I/O, permissions) is explicitly *not* treated as a disconnect: still reported per file, ingest keeps going.

Originals are never touched, and ingest stays idempotent, so re-running after a reconnect picks up exactly the clips that were left behind.

Tests: three new cases (retry across a reappearing volume under a new drive letter; persistent disconnect reporting once and stopping; a real file error still per-file). Full suite passes (360 passed, 1 skipped).

author: bennetwi92
body:
Re-scoped against current main first: #551/#567 replaced the hand-written strategy summary with a generated `research/strategy.md`, which retired claim 4 (CLAUDE.md's red-peak line). The other four stand, and **independent review found each of them a second time** — in the companion spec, or elsewhere in the same file. That doubling is the real finding: the two specs restate each other, so a correction applied to one copy leaves the other authoritative-looking and wrong.

## What was wrong

| Claim | Doc said | Code does |
|---|---|---|
| settings flip | `engine-v2.md`'s header: "the §10 settings flip **never landed**" | `day.py` reads every gate from `Settings` (#302) — and §9 of that same file already said so |
| eps | "1 tick, passed down from settings" (§2.1, §5.1, §11 of `bull-flag.md`; §3, §11 of `engine-v2.md`) | `tokens.py::token_eps` → `tick_size / 2`, **derived**; #196 reversed the value and there has never been a knob |
| phantom knobs | `bull_flag_eps_ticks` and `bull_flag_score_weights` listed as `Settings` fields | neither exists; the second lives at `score.py::DEFAULT_WEIGHTS` |
| gate list | `shape_valid` listed, `peak_green` missing, `loc_in_window` unqualified — in **both** specs | `gates.py::evaluate` has 8 gates + an opt-in 9th |
| red peak | "disqualified entirely, the search continues for a later green peak" | `refine_pole` **keeps** a red/flat peak and the `peak_green` gate rejects it — reject-and-explain, not skip-and-vanish (#196) |

The header one mattered most: `CLAUDE.md` names `engine-v2.md` as the spec for the *how*, so a reader going top-down hit "never landed" in the first 15 lines and concluded `config.py` was fiction.

## Superseded, not overwritten

These files are a historical record — "we locked X on 2026-07-10 and #196 reversed it" is worth reading, and silently rewriting a locked decision to match today's code destroys the reason it changed. So each correction sits next to what it supersedes, with the issue number.

## Guards

Four, all mutation-checked. Written because `test_settings_wiring.py` catches a `Settings` field that isn't wired to the engine and had no way to catch the opposite — a field the *specs* describe that was never added.

- **`bull_flag_*` named in `research/` must be a real field** or carry an exemption saying where the value actually lives. Review caught the first regex requiring the backtick flush against the name, which missed 13 of 44 real mentions — including two rows this PR wrote. `` `≤ bull_flag_foo` `` now fails.
- **The exemption list expires** — if a retired name becomes real, the exemption is exactly what would hide it.
- **Both gate lists match `gates.evaluate`**, read from the AST rather than scanned as text (text-scanning matches the prose in the file's own docstrings — the failure mode this repo's guards keep hitting). `gates.py`'s module docstring points readers at the `bull-flag.md` copy, so guarding only `engine-v2.md` would have left the cited one free to drift. The commentary moved out of that bullet so the list itself stays machine-readable.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| documented gate renamed | ✅ caught |
| `peak_green` row deleted from either spec | ✅ caught |
| new `GateResult` added to `evaluate` | ✅ caught |
| §7 table deleted entirely | ✅ caught (fails, not vacuously passes) |
| phantom knob written as `` `≤ bull_flag_ghost_cap` `` | ✅ caught |

## Deliberately not fixed

`setup.py`'s `eps=getattr(settings, "bull_flag_eps_ticks", 1) * tick` — the dead `getattr` that makes the end-anchored detector run at a full tick. That is **#513**, which asks for a decision this PR shouldn't make on its own. The docs now say so explicitly rather than leaving the reader to discover that the two detectors disagree: #534 settles #513's *documentation* half (option 2 of its checklist), and the exemption entry for `bull_flag_eps_ticks` notes the name is still referenced in live code so nobody fixing #513 is told there's nothing to find.

`make check` green — 925 passed, 93.55%.

Closes #534
Refs #513
Refs #1

author: jay-sahnan
body:
Wave 1 of the hardening plan: the sequence-enrollment state machine (K2, K4, K23 + the cluster's sweep findings).

## The state machine, before

- `createSequence` enrolled **plain sequences as `queued`**, a status no cron path consumes: the entire sequence was dead unless the user manually clicked Send all. **Signal-triggered sequences enrolled as `waiting`**, which the followups sweep sends as soon as a draft is approved: the email went out days or weeks before the trigger signal ever fired.
- The approved-waiting sweep loaded an **unordered `limit(50)`** of waiting enrollments: once more than 50 sat waiting (most parked in review forever), the one the user just approved could miss the window every 15 minutes, permanently.
- **Nothing respected `enrollment.next_send_at`** except the cron's due query: the hero's Send all advanced the enrollment mid-loop and then passed the step-match check for the *next* step, delivering a follow-up seconds after its predecessor.
- Re-running `draftEmailsForSequence` inserted duplicate drafts per (enrollment, step); two approved rows break `sendApprovedDraft`'s `.single()` and the sequence never sends again (K4).
- `discardDraft` on a current step stranded the enrollment on an empty step forever.

## After

- Statuses match their consumers: plain → `waiting` (approval sends), signal → `queued` (only the signal fire sends); the sweep additionally excludes signal-triggered sequences at the query level, protecting legacy rows.
- The sweep is driven from approved drafts (bounded, oldest-first) instead of a page of enrollments; due enrollments process oldest-due-first.
- `sendApprovedDraft` holds the schedule; `ignoreSchedule` exists solely as the single-draft human override. Send all passes `ignoreSchedule:false`, sorts steps ascending, and reports not-due drafts as "will send on schedule".
- Duplicate-draft guard on re-runs (also skips LLM spend for existing steps); `discardDraft` completes the enrollment when it empties the current step and tells the agent so; `draftIsCurrentStep` fails closed on errors; step metadata cached per sequence.

## After deploy

Data repairs 1, 2 (already gated on PR-2), 4, and 6 from the runbook become safe: promote stuck `queued` plain-sequence enrollments, dedupe duplicate drafts, and resolve discard-stranded enrollments.

Tests: 900 passed (7 new across sender schedule, sweep shape, and enroll-status suites); tsc and eslint clean.

author: obiwantoby
body:
### Problem

On Jellyfin 12 (reported on RC4 https://github.com/finamp-app/finamp/issues/1707), opening playlists and browsing the library became several times slower than on 0.9.24. Downgrading Finamp restored the speed.

The cause is in the default item fields Finamp requests. `defaultFields` includes `People` (the cast/credits list), which is applied to every bulk item query. On the server, People live in a separate table from the item, so requesting the field forces a per item relational join across the whole result. Jellyfin 12 handles that join much more slowly than earlier servers, so the previously tolerable cost became the bottleneck. 0.9.24 did not request `People` in these queries, which is why the downgrade "fixes" it.

### Measurements

Same query against a live Jellyfin 12.0.0 server, only difference is whether `People` is requested:

| Request | Without People | With People |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 53 track playlist | 41 ms | 258 ms (~6x) |
| 500 track library page | 179 ms | 2361 ms (~13x) |

The cost scales with track count, so large playlists are the worst affected.

### Fix

Stop requesting `People` in bulk queries, and fetch it on demand only for the currently playing track, through the metadata provider. That single item request measured ~18 ms and still returns the credits, so the additional people chip on the player screen is unchanged. Playlists load at 0.9.24 speeds again.

Only the current track (and the few tracks the player precaches) trigger the extra request, and only when the additional people chip is enabled and the app is online.

### Notes

The server returns an empty `People` list rather than omitting the field, so the item alone can't tell us whether credits were loaded; the provider always fetches when online and the chip is enabled.

There is likely also a server side regression worth reporting upstream (RC4 handling this join notably slower than older servers), but the client should not be over fetching credits for a whole playlist to display them for one track regardless, so this change is worthwhile independent of any server fix.

## Summary
PR #44 merged with the opencode GitHub App action wired directly to a `push` trigger. The action hard-rejects `push` with `Error: Unsupported event type: push`, so every code push to `ares` fails the README job.

This PR bridges it: a `push` to `ares` (excluding README-only pushes) now dispatches a `workflow_dispatch` run of the same workflow, which the action *does* accept. That run reviews the diff and commits the README update back.
