author: kyleseaman
body:
## Symptom

Merely having a dashboard tab open bills a real LLM chat turn every 10 minutes, forever, on some accounts — and the thing doing the spending is the credit meter itself. There is no config knob, no user opt-out, and no ceiling. The `kirocrew-lite` agent resolves model `auto`, so the turn can land on an expensive model.

## Root cause

`src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/sessions.py`

- `_USAGE_REFRESH_SECS = 600` (line 107) is the real clock. The frontend polls `/api/sessions/usage` every 30s, but `api_sessions_usage` only kicks a background refresh once the cache TTL expires, so the spend cadence is 10 minutes, not 30 seconds.
- `_fetch_usage_bg` tries the **free** `GetUsageLimits` HTTPS read first (logs `Kiro usage refreshed (api)`). That path is fine.
- When the API returns no `credits_plan`, it fell straight through to spawning `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive --agent kirocrew-lite /usage` — a **billed** chat turn (the source's own comments already called it "the credit-consuming text scrape"; it logs `Kiro usage refreshed (text)`). Nothing gated that spawn, and nothing stopped it from repeating on every TTL expiry indefinitely, including when the scrape's output was unparseable and the turn bought nothing.

Accounts where `GetUsageLimits` never returns a plan therefore paid a chat turn every 10 minutes for the privilege of seeing a credit number.

## Fix

**1. The scrape is opt-in.** New knob `dashboard.usage_text_scrape_enabled`, **default `false`**, declared alongside the other `dashboard.*` knobs in `src/kiro_crew/config/loader.py` and wired through `DashboardConfig` construction with `_safe_bool`. `_text_scrape_enabled()` **fails closed**: any error reading config means no scrape, so a malformed config can never silently start billing.

**2. Graceful degradation when it is off.** `_cache_without_scrape()` keeps a previously-good reading and dims it `stale` (the pill does not blink out); with nothing prior it caches whatever partial fields the API *did* return plus `available: False`, stripping the private `_profile_arn` and running everything through the existing redaction. No error, no exception, no blank-field render.

**3. Logged once, not per cycle.** `_log_scrape_disabled_once()` emits a single INFO naming the knob and the interval. The refresh runs forever, so a per-cycle log would be pure noise.

**4. Failure backoff even when enabled.** Three consecutive scrapes that yield no usable plan park the scrape for six hours (`_record_scrape_outcome` / `_scrape_in_backoff`). Any success clears the counter. Refreshes that never reached the scrape — an API-path error, a missing `kiro-cli` — do not consume the failure budget, since they say nothing about whether the scrape works.

**Frontend: untouched, deliberately.** `App.tsx`'s usage query already handles the absent-plan case correctly: `Number.isFinite(u.credits_plan)` fails, `u.available === false` returns `'none'`, and the pill is omitted from the capsule entirely (an effect also auto-closes the credits modal). It renders no garbage and no half-filled meter, so there was nothing minimal to change and no `dist` rebuild is needed.

## Tests

`test/test_session_usage.py::TestTextScrapeIsOptIn` — 12 new tests, every one revert-verified (fix patched out ⇒ test fails):

| Test | Reverted mechanism |
|---|---|
| `test_disabled_knob_never_spawns_the_billed_scrape` | the opt-in gate |
| `test_enabled_knob_spawns_the_scrape_and_caches_it` | positive control — the scrape still works when asked for |
| `test_disabled_degrades_to_unavailable_instead_of_erroring` | the gate (spawn mock holds *parseable* output, so a leak is visible) |
| `test_disabled_keeps_partial_api_fields` | partial-field preservation + `_profile_arn` strip |
| `test_disabled_preserves_a_prior_good_value_as_stale` | stale-preservation branch |
| `test_disabled_notice_is_logged_once_not_per_cycle` | four refreshes ⇒ exactly one INFO |
| `test_repeated_failures_back_off_instead_of_retrying_every_ttl` | backoff check + failure counter |
| `test_a_timeout_counts_toward_the_backoff` | backoff on the timeout path |
| `test_an_api_path_failure_does_not_count_toward_the_backoff` | the `scrape_attempted` guard |
| `test_a_success_clears_accumulated_failures` | success resets the counter |
| `test_the_gate_fails_closed_when_config_is_unreadable` | fail-closed on config error |
| `test_the_knob_defaults_to_off` | the `default=False` itself |

Existing tests that exercise the scrape now opt in explicitly via `_enable_text_scrape()`, which documents at each call site that the production default is off.

## Gates

- `pytest` full suite: **33,294 passed**, 8 failures — all 8 reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree with its own venv (host-environment: `ps`-path planting, sandbox cancel, IPv6 URL parse, search cost budget). None are in usage, config, or dashboard-handler code.
- `isort --check-only`, `flake8`: clean.
- `mypy src/kiro_crew/`: clean, 801 files — run on a CI-parity venv (mypy 1.14.1 matching the `pyproject.toml` pin, no `faiss` installed).
- `config-baseline.json` regenerated by `scripts/generate_config_baseline.py` (336 entries).
- Frontend gates not run and `dist` not rebuilt: zero frontend files changed.

author: tsmbland
body: # Description Adds a small penalty on peak seasonal/annual utilisation to promote even spreading of utilisation, rather than loading all production onto a single timeslice/season. This is especially useful for seasonally/annually balanced commodities, which may otherwise have no incentive for one activity profile over the other. The rationale for this is that there may be costs involved with having to maintain a high level of capacity to support peak use, and/or costs associated with switching between high and low activity. The penalties should be kept very small so they don't dominate the primary objective and only serve to break ties between otherwise equally good solutions. The main reason for this is to avoid arbitrary activity profiles as a result of the solver picking one amongst many equally good solutions. We can see in the results that there are fewer zeros in the flows files, which previously often arose when assets choose to serve full seasonal demands in one or two timeslices, which in the real world wouldn't happen. This also helps with #1399 and #1174, although to fully close both of these we also need additional constraints to spread utilisation evenly among equally good assets (i.e. removing the ability to chose arbitrarily among equally good assets). That's coming in #1477 ## Screenshot from documentation ## Performance discussion If both penalties are active (>0), this adds: - n_assets * (n_seasons + 1) variables - n_assets * (n_timeslices + n_seasons) constraints i.e. scales linearly with the number of assets and temporal granularity. The performance cost for the example models is about 5-10%. For the `simple_modified` example, which has many more assets, it's more like 30%. I think this is probably acceptable, and since the number of added variables/constraints increases linearly with the problem size, I wouldn't expect the performance cost to vary much in % terms even for much larger models. Fixes # (issue) ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change to fix an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change to add functionality) - [ ] Refactoring (non-breaking, non-functional change to improve maintainability) - [ ] Optimization (non-breaking change to speed up the code) - [ ] Breaking change (whatever its nature) - [ ] Documentation (improve or add documentation) ## Key checklist - [ ] All tests pass: `$ cargo test` - [ ] The documentation builds and looks OK: `$ cargo doc` - [ ] Update release notes for the latest release if this PR adds a new feature or fixes a bug present in the previous release ## Further checks - [ ] Code is commented, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] Tests added that prove fix is effective or that feature works

The fuzzy sys-tree checkpoint (4e0aa762) removed the exclusive oTablesMetaLock/oSysTreesLock around sys-tree capture.  Concurrent DDL can now modify a sys-tree root page between the initial change-count capture and the re-lock via checkpoint_fix_split_and_lock_page. When the change count differs, checkpoint_btree_loop treats it as eviction and sends WalkUpwards with InvalidDiskDownlink.  Since there is no parent level above the root, Assert(valid_doff) fires.

author: jcadhoc
body:
### Ticket
124773 — cliente cummotors (18.0). Cancelar cantidad remanente no baja el pronóstico de unidades a recibir.

### Síntoma
Secuencia: OC por N unidades → recibir todo → **devolver al proveedor con reembolso** (`to_refund`) → aumentar la cantidad de la línea → **cancelar remanente**. En vez de cancelarse, el IN pendiente queda vivo **e inflado** (ej. de 2 a 4) y el producto sigue figurando como "por recibir" en el pronóstico.

### Causa
`button_cancel_remaining` setea `product_qty = qty_received + qty_returned`. Al escribir `product_qty`, el core (`purchase_stock`, `_get_qty_procurement` / `_prepare_stock_moves`) recalcula el remanente como `product_qty − qty_procurement`, pero:
- cuenta la devolución `to_refund` como **salida** (`−qty_returned`), y
- `qty_returned` a la vez **suma** en el `product_qty` objetivo.

Ese doble conteo deja el delta **positivo**, así que en lugar de cancelar el remanente el core lo **agranda** vía merge. No existe un `product_qty` único que cancele el remanente y a la vez cierre la línea (el `+ qty_returned` es necesario para `qty_to_invoice`).

### Fix
Tras el write de `product_qty`, cancelar explícitamente el remanente de recepción que quede abierto, siguiendo la cadena interna `move_dest_ids` (recepción en 2/3 pasos, donde el core no propaga la baja porque el move interno comparte origen con lo ya recibido). Se **excluyen** los reemplazos de devolución con cambio (`is_exchange_move`), que son una recepción legítima esperada.

### Tests
- `test_return_refund_then_cancel_remaining`: reproduce el ticket (queda RED sin el fix).
- `test_partial_receipt_cancel_remaining`: caso base sin devoluciones (recepción parcial + cancelar remanente).

Follow-up pendiente: test de devolución con cambio (el fix ya la contempla; armar el reemplazo de forma estable en `TransactionCase` necesita más setup).

author: joshuataylor
body: The two embedded rows in the Diff Options menu (Intra-line diff mode and Maximum diff size) are `QWidgetAction`s built with `no_margin`, so on macOS they sit flush against the menu edges -- their labels start LEFT of the native checkable items, whose text is indented past the check/icon column, and the combo/spin box touch the menu's right edge. Before: After: The fix gives both rows a leading gutter so their labels line up with the checkable items, a stretch so the combo and spin box right-align consistently, and small content margins so the controls no longer touch the menu edge. Rather than hardcoding the gutter width, it's read from the active style via [`PM_SmallIconSize`](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qstyle.html#PixelMetric-enum) so it tracks the platform -- the macOS style uses different padding and inset values than Fusion -- falling back to the icon-size constant when the metric reports 0. This is the shared `Options` widget, so both the main window and the Git DAG diff panes pick it up. Worth a quick look on Linux (KDE/GNOME/etc) to confirm it still looks right there -- it should, since the gutter comes from the active style's own metric.

author: ilbzzz
body:
### CodeMender Security Fix

**Finding ID**: `fadfdb88-3db8-5148-bab7-5e30c33a2086`
**Title**: Remote Code Execution via Eval in Profile Username Injection
**Severity**: CRITICAL
**Vulnerability Type**: Code Injection
**File Path**: `/app/juice-shop-local/routes/userProfile.ts`
**Start Line**: 54

#### Analysis
The `username` attribute from the database is extracted and checked for Pug interpolation pattern `#{...}`:
`if (username?.match(/#{(.*)}/) !== null && utils.isChallengeEnabled(challenges.usernameXssChallenge))`
If found, the substring within the braces is passed directly to `eval(code)`.

Since users can control their own username via their profile update route, an authenticated user can set their username to a malicious pattern such as `#{global.process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()}` or other JS payloads. When fetching their profile via `/profile`, the payload will be evaluated by the server, leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
First, update the user profile's username:
```http
POST /api/Users/profile HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <valid_token>

{
  "username": "#{global.process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()}"
}
```
Then visit the `/profile` endpoint with the valid token. The server will execute the code within `eval`.

---

author: csguth
body:
## Problema
O link do site (`https://machinemens.com`) nao renderiza preview no WhatsApp (nem em outros apps que fazem link unfurling, como Facebook/Slack).

## Causa raiz
A raiz "bare" do dominio (`/`) e servida por `layouts/alias.html`, uma pagina de redirecionamento client-side (JS) que escolhe o idioma do visitante. Essa pagina nao tinha **nenhuma** meta tag Open Graph/Twitter Card estatica -- so um `<title>` generico e um redirect via `<script>`/`<meta http-equiv=refresh>`.

Crawlers de link preview (WhatsApp, Facebook, Slack, etc.) **nao executam JavaScript** e normalmente nao seguem `http-equiv=refresh`, entao encontravam uma pagina sem `og:title`/`og:description`/`og:image` e nao geravam nenhum preview.

Confirmado direto em producao (`curl -s https://machinemens.com`): a resposta so tinha `<title>Machinemens</title>` e nenhuma meta `og:*`/`twitter:*`.

## Fix
Adiciona as mesmas meta tags estaticas (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type`, `og:url`, `og:image` + width/height, `og:site_name`, `og:locale`, `twitter:*`) que ja existem em `layouts/partials/head.html` para as demais paginas, usando os textos padrao em ingles (`content/_index.en.md`) e a imagem `static/images/og-image.jpg` ja usada no resto do site.

Build local + simulacao da substituicao `__SITE_URL__` (feita em CI) confirmam a saida esperada, com `og:image` apontando para `https://machinemens.com/images/og-image.jpg` e `og:title`/`og:description` preenchidos.

## Escopo
Mudanca cirurgica em um unico arquivo (`layouts/alias.html`). Nao mexe no redirect de idioma em si nem em outras paginas.

## Pos-merge
Por ser hotfix direto na `main`, precisa ser sincronizado de volta para a `staging` em seguida.

author: wwoosshh
body:
실사용에서 **리포가 멀쩡히 있는데도** push 가 실패했다.

```
git push 에 실패했어요: remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/semicollon-club/test-1.git/' not found
```

## 아닌 것부터 지웠다

| 확인한 것 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 리포 존재 | **있다** — `test-1`, private, 02:12:31 생성 |
| 설치 범위 | `repository_selection: "all"` |
| 권한 | `administration:write`, `contents:write`, `metadata:read` |
| 전파 지연? | **아니다** — 3분 30초 뒤 재시도도 같은 404 |

## 원인

`-c credential.helper=X` 는 헬퍼 체인에 **추가**되는 것이지 교체가 아니다. 시스템·전역 설정에 이미 헬퍼가 있으면(Git for Windows 는 기본으로 `credential.helper=manager` 를 넣는다) git 이 **그쪽에 먼저 묻고** 그것이 돌려준 자격증명을 쓴다. 우리 토큰은 쓰이지도 않는다.

그리고 비공개 리포는 권한 없는 접근에 403 이 아니라 **404** 를 준다 — 그래서 "리포가 없다" 로만 보이고, 원인을 엉뚱한 곳(리포 생성·전파·권한)에서 찾게 된다. 실제로 그렇게 헤맸다.

**빈 값이 먼저 오면 그 지점까지 쌓인 헬퍼 목록이 지워진다.** `gh auth setup-git` 도 같은 이유로 빈 줄을 먼저 넣는다 — 이 리포 운영자의 `~/.gitconfig` 에서 그 형태를 확인한 것이 진단의 실마리였다:

```
credential.https://github.com.helper            ← 빈 값
credential.https://github.com.helper  !gh ...   ← 그다음 자기 것
```

## clone·pull 도 같았다

되받기는 아직 실사용에서 눌러본 적이 없어 같은 결함이 잠복해 있었다. 셋 다 `CREDENTIAL_ARGS` 하나로 묶었다.

## 검증

가드는 "빈 헬퍼가 우리 헬퍼보다 먼저 온다" 를 push·clone·pull 세 곳에서 확인하고, 그 인자에 토큰이 없다는 것도 함께 본다. **리셋을 빼면 3건이 실패하는 것을 확인했다**(변이 테스트).

`npm run typecheck` 통과 · `npm test` 통과.

## ⚠️ 미확인

미니PC 에 실제로 시스템/전역 `credential.helper` 가 설정돼 있는지는 확인하지 못했다. 이 수정은 그것이 있든 없든 올바르지만, 있다는 것이 확인되면 원인 규명이 완결된다. 확인 명령:

```
git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper
```

author: danilotrninic-db
body:
## What changes are proposed in this pull request?

Parse the OAuth `expires_in` field from a quoted integer (`"3600"`) in addition
to a plain JSON integer. Previously a token endpoint that returned `expires_in`
as a JSON string was read as "no lifetime reported," so the token was fetched
fresh on every stream creation instead of being cached.

### How this addresses #607

#607 has three asks:

1. **Parse quoted `expires_in`** — the code change above.
2. **Continue serving a valid cached token when a proactive refresh fails** —
   already implemented in `TokenCache::get_or_fetch`; this PR verifies it and
   adds tests pinning it. The one edge case (a refresh that succeeds with no
   usable `expires_in`) is deliberately left returning the fresh token uncached
   rather than falling back to the near-expiry cached one — a missing lifetime is
   missing metadata about the token, not evidence it is bad, and the freshly
   minted token is the more likely of the two to still be valid.
3. **Add deterministic tests** — new `TokenCache` tests covering concurrency
   invalidation, cancellation, and expiry.

## How is this tested?

`cargo test --workspace` (822 tests, green); `cargo fmt --check` and
`cargo clippy` clean. New unit tests cover `parse_expires_in` (integer, quoted
integer, whitespace, and reject cases) and the `TokenCache` behaviors above.

No live-server testing was needed: the sole production change is a pure parsing
function with no I/O or state, fully exercised by the unit tests above.

author: randax
body:
Closes #1643.

Durable, Postgres-authoritative principal fencing for XEP-0198 cross-node SM resume — the second half of P0.3, re-derived from harvest branch `codex/distributed-actors-p0-3` (closed PR #1610) onto post-ISR-removal main. Behavioral delta: resume authorization is fenced against the durable principal; everything else unchanged.

## What landed

**Typed principal domain** (`waddle-xmpp/auth/principal.rs`): `AuthContextId` / `AuthContextVersion` / `PrincipalAuthEpoch` / `AuthenticatedPrincipalRef` — a non-secret identity reference, always revalidated against the live `sessions` row at use time; never a credential.

**Atomic persistence envelope**: `store_session_atomic_with_principal` / `get_session_principal` on `SmPersistenceStorage`; the principal rides inside the single atomic write with the snapshot, queue, and exact claim fence (no staged-map pattern — #1610's cancellation hazard). Implemented by the in-memory fake (unconditionally compiled, no `cfg(test)` trait methods — #1610's other trap), the non-clustered `DatabaseSmPersistence` (SQLite + Postgres), and the fenced clustered backend, where a fence miss aborts the whole write and leaves prior principal columns untouched. Plain snapshot refreshes preserve existing principal columns via `COALESCE` (see review round below). The `resumable_sessions` in-memory sidecar is deleted everywhere (http/state/cleanup/connection/janitors/state-inventory); the inventory gauge now counts durable detached snapshots; no `Session`, bearer proof, or token is retained as resume authority.

**Migration v11** (expand-only; harvest's v10 renumbered — main's v10 is #1642's ISR drop): nullable `auth_context_id` + defaulted `auth_context_version` / `principal_auth_epoch` on `sessions`, unique index on context id. Pre-v11 rows decode as `Option` and are typed non-resumable (`not-authorized` at resume), never a decode error. NOT NULL tightening and version/epoch mutation stay in the activation backlog; both values are pinned INITIAL=1 in this PR and the comparators are forward contracts under test.

**Resume fence** (`handle_sm_resume`): linearized **prepare → claim/freeze → authoritative durable recheck → publish/Ready → send**. No SM state installs before the final `resolve_principal`; the recheck is the last await before commit; a JID-equality gate makes snapshot/principal agreement an enforced precondition. `SmResumeClaimGuard` (RAII) releases or defers the exact claim on every rejection, cancellation, and release-failure path via the existing claims reconciliation inventory; it commits only when claim completion reaches its terminal boundary. Typed rejections: absent snapshot → `item-not-found`; missing/mismatched/legacy-NULL principal → `not-authorized` (victim session never terminalized); storage loss → `internal-server-error` — including the new typed `CrossNodeResumeOutcome::StorageUnavailable` so post-win transient repairs no longer masquerade as absence; `handled-count-too-high` keeps its stream-error semantics.

**Typed resolved-principal seam**: `ResolvedPrincipal<'a>` newtype consumed by interpret deps, outbound wiring, permissions, and pubsub/spaces/community handlers; constructible only at authenticated boundaries. Behavior-neutral — all XEP-0045/XEP-0060 conditions unchanged.

**#1610 defect root causes** (fixed, not inherited): (1) the v0006–v0008 repair-path fixtures seeded migration *history* without materializing the v1 `users`/`sessions` schema, so a later `ALTER TABLE sessions` exploded — fixtures now materialize the historical schema; harvest's unrelated fail-closed runner policy was **not** imported. (2) `test_database_in_app_state` failed on #1610 because that fail-closed policy made the waddle-only runner treat global history entries as unknown — with the runner untouched, it passes.

## Evidence

Two-node Postgres cross-node suite (principal hydration + replay, legacy-NULL rejection with recovery-snapshot retention, no-credential column assertion; CI's nix gate provisions `WADDLE_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` via flake.nix). Rejection matrix at three layers: resolution outcomes (resolved / missing / mismatched / changed-version / revoked-epoch / expired), websocket mapping, and cross-node registry claim unwind. Deterministic race via an injectable pre-recheck hook (delete durable session between resolution and recheck → `not-authorized`, no Ready/registration/`<resumed/>`/replay, claim released, detached state retained). Cancellation-after-claim, expired-while-claimed unwind, and staged-commit rejection tests. Full affected suites green; clippy `-D warnings` `--all-features` clean (a default-features dead-code failure reproduces on clean main — pre-existing).

## Review

Plan review (pre-implementation): gpt-5.6-sol high reasoning — 11 findings (4 blocking), all folded into the plan before any code (linearization contract, RAII unwind, `Option` decode for legacy rows, non-clustered backend coverage, both #1610 root-cause redirections).

Adversarial round 1 (head 39e1f072; sol + 3 opus personas: XEP-conformance, concurrency/durability, security): one BLOCKING found by all four — detached snapshot refreshes NULLed the principal columns, making any session with traffic-while-detached unresumable; fixed with `COALESCE` preservation on all five `sm_sessions` upserts plus a registry-level regression test (the in-memory fake had masked it). One HIGH (sol): post-win transient repair returned `item-not-found` — fixed with typed `StorageUnavailable`. One MEDIUM: expired-while-claimed sessions stranded in `claimed_sessions` — fixed mirroring `release_claim_locked`.

Adversarial round 2 (head 6b2b852e; sol delta + opus delta): fix logic verified CLEAN on all items; one MEDIUM coverage gap (the changed expired branch had no test) — closed with a dedicated test. The remaining question — expired-while-claimed queues wait for restart-time promotion — is pre-existing on main (`release_claim_locked` has always behaved this way) and is filed as #1667.

CI round (nixXmppServerTests, head 807529f8): six WS integration failures exposed a defect no local suite could — SCRAM success built `Session::new` in memory and never persisted it, so every SCRAM-authenticated resume resolved `Missing` → `not-authorized`. Fixed by persisting the session row at the SCRAM authenticated boundary (auth still succeeds if the write fails; only resumability is lost); all six tests verified green locally before re-push.

author: bochneryehuda
body:
## Which product is this for?

- [x] **RTL** — Residential Transition Loans (bridge / ground-up / fix & flip)
- [ ] **LT** — Long-Term Loans
- [ ] **Neither / shared plumbing**

No Long-Term code, table or migration is touched. **No migration and no column** in this PR.

## What changed and why

Follow-up to #1055, driven by four adversarial audits. Owner-directed:

> *"Whatever you see on the screen, according to the eligibility, that should be exactly what's getting registered, and that should be exactly what's going on on the final term sheet. This can cause us to not be able to sell files. There never should have been a mistake like this again."*

Five defects. **Three were mine, introduced in #1055 — including one I created with the fix for another.**

| # | Defect | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The ladder rung was never remembered.** It lives only in the studio's module scope, which resets on every iframe load — and `esign/gate.js` **requires** a re-register after the appraisal before a term sheet may issue | The mandatory workflow step registered the **maximum**: a signed **$1,794,000 @ 8.500%** came back as **$2,070,000 @ 9.125%** — +$276,000, +62.5 bps, no approval, no record, and a fresh "your terms are ready" email with the bigger number. **Guaranteed on every file reaching a term sheet.** |
| 2 | **Screen ≠ register.** The sticky ceiling from #1055 was applied on the register route only | Borrower shown **$652,200 @ 9.250%**, file recorded **$489,150 @ 8.500%** |
| 3 | **The public intake door priced every deal at FICO 0.** `applications` has no `fico` column — it lives on `borrowers.fico`, and every engine guards its floor with `fico > 0`, so a zero score **skips** the floor rather than failing it | From an **unauthenticated** endpoint, anyone could mint an ELIGIBLE, approval-free **Gold registration at a 600 score against a 660 floor**, note buyer stamped and loan amount written back |
| 4 | **The payoff never reached the file.** The studio's payoff box was in neither the register snapshot nor the whitelist, and the register never wrote `payoff_amount` | A **$208,410** swing that **inverted** who pays whom — the sheet said the borrower brings $208,410; the file said $691,590 was paid *to* them |
| 5 | **A ladder rung could push the financed reserve past its cap.** The loan-to-cost guard cuts the loan and recomputes the payment smaller without re-running the reserve fit | **$76,713 (18.67 months)** on an 18-month Gold ground-up whose 75%-of-term cap is **$55,455** — *larger in dollars on the smaller loan*. The borrower paid origination and interest on money that can never accrue. `silver-shadow-parity` doesn't check the reserve, so nothing flagged it |

Per the owner's clarification, the payoff now behaves as stated: it lands on the application's `payoff` field and **comes out of the initial advance** — part of the initial loan goes to the payoff, and the borrower brings whatever is short. Refinance-only and fill-or-update, so it can never wipe a payoff a human recorded.

## The structural fix, not a fifth patch

A price was produced at **eight** places, each assembling its own overrides — which is precisely why one could drift while every one looked correct in isolation. `src/lib/pricing-sticky.js` is now the ONE definition of what a **file** carries regardless of who is asking, layered UNDER each caller's own request so a door that can *see* a field still changes it and a door that cannot inherits it.

`scripts/test-quote-register-parity-db.js` is the guard: it drives the **real doors over HTTP** against one file and refuses any disagreement in loan or rate. A unit test of the chokepoint would not have caught this — the chokepoint was correct; the bug was a door that never called it. It also asserts **structurally** that every pricing surface calls it, so a *new* door that forgets fails even when no scenario exercises it, and that the final term sheet never re-prices.

## Verification

- **Full `npm test`: 6,256 checks, exit 0**, on a database created fresh and migrated through all 479 migrations, with all new guards running inside it.
- **Every fix was reverted to confirm its test bites.** The parity test reproduces $652,200-vs-$489,150 three ways; the FICO test distinguishes *"read and refused"* from *"never read"*; the reserve test asserts the defect is reachable so it cannot quietly go empty.
- **Reserve fix contained:** 41,472 evaluations across both affected engines — **560** deals were over-cap and now **none** are, **zero drift** on any deal the guard never touches, **no loan grew**. Every documented month cap is honoured (full term Standard, frozen 75%-of-term Gold ground-up, zero Gold reno / bridge).
- 204,000-scenario EMCAP tie-out, `test-refi-payoff-identity`, `test-termsheet-freeze`, `test-engine-copies-match` all pass.

**A methodology note worth a reviewer's attention:** my first reserve matrix reported **zero** violations and would have "proven" a fix that did nothing — the trigger is the **lever**, and at maximum leverage the guard rarely binds. The matrix was widened until it reproduced the defect before the result was trusted.

## Known and NOT fixed here

- **The borrower/BataWare door is not born-registered** — it carries the deal *type*, not the pricing election, so a borrower's program choice and ladder step are dropped. Pre-existing in already-merged code, **explicitly descoped by the owner**.
- `scripts/test-cure-pure.js` fails on `main`, unrelated to this work, one of **55** `test-*` scripts never wired into `npm test`.

## Audits (required by CLAUDE.md)

- [x] Post-merge audit at the higher bar — merge confirmed clean (tree byte-identical, nothing lost or duplicated, proofs still bite, bundle reproduces bit-for-bit).
- [x] Money end-to-end audit — findings 1, 4, 5.
- [x] Authority/security audit — findings 3, plus the borrower-picks-note-buyer item below.
- [ ] Post-merge audit for **this** PR — to run against merged `main`.

**One further audit finding, reported not fixed:** a borrower's self-register picks the staff-only note buyer by choosing a program, and `COALESCE` makes it permanent — an officer's later correct registration cannot fix it, and the file can then export no data tape at all. Raising it rather than bundling it in.

author: maxopich
body:
The operator's only *mechanical* brake on a bus worker is one function. `decidePauseForMutation` halts the turn on `dangerous` and nothing else, and `read` is skipped wholesale by the mutation tap — no row, no badge, no audit, no pause. **A command that lands below `dangerous` is not a missed warning; it is a call the operator was never offered the chance to stop.** PR #267 closed four such holes and the test file says so in its own header. These are the rest, plus one nobody filed.

Every line below was measured by importing the module against `main`, not read off the source.

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `sudo --version`, `rm --help`, `dd --version`, `del --version` | **read** | dangerous |
| `nohup rm -rf /x`, `timeout 5 rm -rf /x`, `xargs rm -rf` | **mutate** | dangerous |
| `echo x 2> /etc/passwd`, `echo x &> /etc/passwd` | **read** | dangerous |
| `doas rm -rf /`, `su -c "rm -rf /"` | **mutate** | dangerous |
| `ls >&2` | **mutate** | read |
| `mcp__cebab_bus__bus_send` (every hop) | **mutate** | read |

## D21 — a demotion rule outranked every escalation

The `--version`/`--help` hatch sat at rule 1, ahead of all the escalating rules, so it demoted the **entire** dangerous list behind a two-token prefix. The bead names three commands; it was all of them, Windows set included. Moved below the escalating rules, where it still does the job it was written for (`node --version` → `read`).

`-V` left the hatch for the reason the module already gives for omitting `-h`: overloaded. GNU `tar -V` is `--label`, so `tar -V mine -xf a.tar -C /` was a real extraction being classified as a query.

## D02b — one wrapper was registered, twelve launder

`env` was peeled; `nohup`, `timeout`, `nice`, `command`, `stdbuf`, `setsid`, `xargs` — and `time`, `watch`, `busybox`, `unbuffer`, which the bead does not mention — were not.

Each wrapper gets its **own** flag table. A shared one is wrong rather than untidy: `-i` takes no value for `env` and takes one for `stdbuf`, so a shared set makes `stdbuf -i 0 rm -rf /x` scan `0` as the command. `command` deliberately has no `-v` entry, because `command -v rm` is a lookup, not an exec — the peel must not manufacture danger either.

`flock` / `taskset` / `chrt` / `ionice` / `strace` / `script` are **excluded and named as such**: each needs its own positional or quoted-arg rule, and a wrong one is a new false positive.

**Unfiled, found while measuring:** `sudo` was on the dangerous list and `su`, `doas`, `runuser` were not — privilege escalation under a different binary name.

## D04b — an fd digit hid the redirect target

The scan required start-of-string or whitespace before the `>`, so `echo x 2> /etc/passwd` extracted no target at all and was judged by `echo`. Widened, with an explicit `(?!&)` so fd-duplication is skipped **by rule** rather than by accident — the bead notes `2>&1` was excluded only as a side effect of its leading digit, but `>&2` was not excluded at all and misfires as `redirect_path` on a target of `&2` today. That one is fixed too.

`cmd>file` with no space is **still missed**, and the comment says so: dropping the leading anchor would make `grep "a>b" f` report a redirect.

## D06 — a mutation row per bus message

The SDK only ever delivers `mcp__cebab_bus__bus_send`, and the tool's input schema field is `recipient`. The classifier matched a bare `bus_send` and read `destination`, so every hop fell to `default` → `mutate`. `BUS_SEND_TOOL` now lives in `shared` with `runner.ts` re-exporting it, so the registration and the classifier cannot drift apart again.

## Two register corrections

**D37 is backwards.** It says `Task` is the live sub-agent tool and `Agent` a dead legacy name, and proposes deleting `Agent`. `AgentInput` is a member of `ToolInputSchemas` in the pinned SDK (0.3.220) and there is **no `TaskInput` at all** — the fix as filed would have deleted the live case and kept the dead one. Both kept, with the check recorded.

That test was also **vacuous**: it asserted only the category, and the `default` branch returns `mutate` too, so it could not tell a handled tool from an unhandled one — which is the entire question D37 raises. Caught by the revert-check, and it now asserts the summary.

**D38** — the empty `python`/`python3`/`node` subcommand sets are deleted. They could never match; their only effect was relabelling the verdict.

## Not in this PR

**D22** (`ri` misfires as dangerous on POSIX) stays open. Its filed fix does not survive contact: `iex` is a two-letter alias that must stay — it is the `iwr | iex` download cradle, with a test — so "drop two-letter aliases" is not a coherent rule; and a platform gate breaks the module's stated purity and would make the suite platform-dependent on a repo that runs CI on both. Drop-`ri` vs. an explicit platform parameter deserves its own PR.

## Verification

`typecheck` ✓ `lint` ✓ `npm test` **3699 passed** ✓ `test:security` **567 passed** (up from 504).

**Revert-checked 15 ways**, each case naming its test file explicitly with paren-free filters and a verified-landed patch. Includes the anti-over-fix direction (deleting the hatch outright must fail), the anti-vacuity direction (blinding the wrapper-coverage gate must fail), and the specific shared-flag-table bug the bead predicted.

Closes `Cebab-x1n.1.21`, `.1.27`, `.1.28`, `.1.6`.

author: by571
body:
Closes #268.

## The bug

Both SLTP envs advanced the sampler and ran the liquidation and SL/TP checks against bar N+1 **before** opening the position at bar N's close. Those checks therefore only ever saw the position held *coming into* the step. A position opened at close(N) was first checked on bar N+2, and bar N+1 — the first bar it is actually exposed to — was never applied to it.

Reproduced on a flat series with one crash bar (low 80, stop at 97.5):

| Entry | Result |
|---|---|
| Two bars before the crash | Stop fires, balance **9750** |
| **One** bar before the crash | Position **rides straight through**, balance 0, still holding |

So the two paths disagreed by a full stop-loss on identical data. `OneStepTradingEnv` already handled this correctly, which is why the fix also restores the parity `lock_position_until_sltp` exists for.

The same blind spot applied to **liquidation** — a freshly opened levered position could ride through a bar that gapped past its liquidation price.

## The fix

Both envs re-run the checks against the bar **already fetched this step**, scoped to positions opened during it.

- No lookahead: the action was chosen on bar N's close alone, and the bar is not re-fetched.
- No retroactive stop: bar N's own range still cannot close a position that exists only from its close. Verified explicitly in review.
- The vectorized env had the checks inline, so extending them would have forked a second copy. They moved into `_apply_exit_checks`, called once for incoming positions and once for newly opened ones.

## Tests

Every test below was verified by mutation, with the mutation asserted to have applied.

| Test | Catches |
|---|---|
| `test_exit_fires_on_the_first_bar_the_position_is_exposed_to` (scalar, 10 cases) | the shared bug, exit-before-observation ordering, exact fills and fees |
| `TestSLTPScalarVecEquivalenceEntryBar` (+ switch case) | scalar/vectorized divergence, take-profit, direction switches |
| `test_entry_bar_check_targets_the_env_that_opened` | per-env mask misalignment |

The division of labour matters: the equivalence suite passed on `main` because the bug was **symmetric** — both envs skipped the entry bar identically. Value-pinning tests catch the shared bug; the equivalence suite catches drift; the `num_envs=2` test catches misalignment.

Three gaps found during review that the first version of this PR did not cover, each now closed and each verified to have been invisible before:

- **Exit-before-observation ordering.** Moving the new block after the observation build left the internal balance correct, so all 56 scalar tests passed — while the policy was handed a 10x-levered open long, 9.6% from liquidation, on a step the env had already liquidated. The test now asserts the returned `account_state`, `reward` and `terminated`.
- **`opened_mask` across envs.** Aiming the check at a sibling env passed all 658 offline tests, because every test touching it had all envs doing the same thing.
- **Fees and the take-profit fill.** A double-charged exit fee and a 1%-wrong take-profit fill both passed the suite; exact values now pin them.

Full suite: **2261 passed, 18 skipped.**

## Notes for the reviewer

- **A same-bar round trip records only the exit.** `HistoryTracker` has one row per step and the exit determines the ending state, matching what already happens when a previously-held position triggers — but it is now reachable one bar earlier. `action_types` is consumed only by the plot markers in `_get_action_markers`, so nothing numeric under-counts; the futures branch infers exit direction from `position_history[i-1]`, which is now `0` for these, so such an exit draws no marker. Pinned in the test so it stays a decision.
- **`eligible=opened_mask` is inert today** — dropping it passes all 658 offline tests, since re-checking a first-pass survivor on the same bar gives the same answer. Kept deliberately: that holds only while the check stays idempotent, and nothing enforces that. Noted at the call site.
- **#292 filed**, found while verifying this: when a held position triggers on bar N+1 the agent's action from close(N) is discarded outright, so a requested long→short flip can leave the account flat instead. Same ordering family, but it changes *which trades happen*, so it needs its own review.
- **#293 filed**: scalar and vectorized diverge at `leverage=10` for non-fractional trade modes, including trigger-timing disagreement. Verified byte-identical on `main`, so it predates this work; the equivalence harness never varies `trade_mode` or `lock_position_until_sltp`.

body:
## Summary

- replace the static header mascot with an optimized animated idle loop
- render the mascot 10% larger across desktop and mobile layouts
- update the PWA offline cache and Sites package assertions for the new asset
- retain an aligned blink experiment under `preview/` for possible future use without wiring it into the game

## Why

The animated mascot gives the header more life while keeping the production behavior simple and consistent. The final implementation uses only the idle animation; no blink scheduler or runtime asset swapping remains.

## Impact

The change is limited to branding and packaging. Gameplay behavior is unchanged. The production animation is a 256×256 WebP, renders at 79.2 px on desktop and 46.2 px on mobile, and is included in the offline app shell.

## Validation

- `npm.cmd run test`
- inline game script parse check
- desktop and mobile browser verification
- confirmed the mascot remains on the idle asset continuously with no console warnings

author: forkwright
body:
## Defect

`_llm/current_state.toml` carried a dated phase snapshot, a `[[recent]]` work log, and per-issue open-thread entries (one using sentinel `issue = 0`, the other pointing at an issue closed months ago) alongside an unresolved `<canonical-state-doc>` placeholder in `source_docs`. Agents are pointed at this file as current context, so the stale content actively manufactured wrong planning state.

## Change

Replace the restated snapshot with pointers to the live authorities (`kanon/projects/harmonia/STATE.md` for phase/planning, `gh issue list` for open threads) and add a regression test that fails on either failure mode returning: an unresolved placeholder locator, or a restated per-issue open-thread entry (including the sentinel issue id).

## Verification

New regression test `crates/archon/tests/llm_corpus_check.rs` asserts the corpus no longer carries an unresolved placeholder locator or a restated per-issue open-thread entry; CI on this PR runs it.

Refs #682

body:
OSS 上次同步停在 `cc17ccb`（2026-07-15）。私有生产库此后有 39 个提交，其中 **17 个动了共享代码/文档**，OSS 一个都没跟上。本 PR 把与学生内容无关的部分整体回流。

## 代码

| 改动 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| **字体自托管** | `next/font` 构建期下载并自托管，删掉 `<head>` 里的 Google Fonts `<link>`。访问 `fonts.googleapis.com` 不通的网络不再回退系统字体、阻塞渲染 |
| **PDF 文件名规则** | 改为 `<名字>_CV_<语言>_<年月>`，英文取英文名（单字名补姓）。规则只在 `ResumeSwitcher` 一处计算；`render-pdf.mjs` 不再自己拼名字，改为覆盖 `window.print` 后点击真实下载按钮抓 `document.title`——网页与 CLI 两个出口合并成一条代码路径 |
| **`titleSuffix` API** | 改判别联合：传 `titleSuffix` 必须同时传 `lang`，括号按语言取全角/半角，页面内不再手写括号。CSS 类 `.r-entry__org-en` → `.r-entry__org-suffix` |
| **注册表守卫** | `cohort+slug` 撞车原本被 `Map` 静默覆盖、构建照过，现在直接 throw |
| **语言标注** | 根 `<html lang="en">`，`ResumeDocument` 按语言标 `lang`（读屏发音 / 翻译提示 / 字体回退） |
| **全站 noindex** | 示例虽虚构，但下游填真人数据后简历带手机号/邮箱，默认关掉收录避免忘记这一步 |
| 其他 | 页面标题 `CV` → `Curriculum Vitae`；`ResumeHeader` layout 类型补 `compact`；GPA 附注紧贴学位行；打印时抬头与首节间距加倍 |

`render-pdf.mjs` 另外用 `waitForSelector` + `document.fonts.ready` 替掉了固定 500ms 延时，并自动探测有无中文版（只有英文版的学生自动跳过 zh）。

## 新增文件

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` —— lint + build 门禁。**此前 OSS 完全没有 CI**，对接收外部 PR 的开源库比私有库更需要。
- `scripts/make-favicon.mjs` + `public/favicon.ico` + `public/apple-touch-icon.png` —— Safari 不支持 SVG data-URI favicon，会回退请求 `/favicon.ico`。

## 文档

`docs/页面设计规范.md` 新增 **§PDF 文件名**（规则表、补姓判定、两个出口、验证手法）与 `titleSuffix` 用法；README 同步文件名规则、目录结构与 CI。

## ⚠️ demo 的英文名顺序改了

`names.en` 由 `Lin Zhiyuan` 改为 `Zhiyuan LIN`。新文件名规则取首词为名，姓在前会得到以姓命名的 `Lin_CV_EN_2608`。这条约定原本只隐含在私有库的学生数据里（`Bowen ZHANG`、`Jia LIU`），本 PR 把它显式写进设计规范和 README。

## 有意未回流

真实学生页面、删除 `demo.tsx`、README 部署章节（含服务器 IP / SSH / 域名备案细节）、`[...segments]` 路由（OSS 的 `[slug]` 对单段路径更简洁）、私有库仍在用的 Tailwind。

私有库那两份「简历内容工作流」文档也没进来——正文点名了真实学生与其学校、目标项目和顾问本地路径，需要先改成虚构案例才能开源。

## 验证

- `npm run lint` + `npm run build` 通过
- 构建产物无 `fonts.googleapis.com` 外链，117 个自托管字体分片
- 实跑 `render-pdf.mjs` 产出 `Zhiyuan_CV_EN_2608.pdf` 与 `林知远_CV_ZH_2608.pdf`，两版 PDF 渲染正常、中文无 tofu 无衬线回退
- `titleSuffix` 两语言分支分别验证为 `" (Double First-Class)"` 与 `"（双一流 A 类）"`（临时改 demo 验证后已还原）

body:
LieAlgDBField2String captures the output of Print( F ) in a string, using
PrintTo1. That function comes from the GAPDoc package, which LieAlgDB
does not declare as a dependency, so printing a collection failed in a
GAP where GAPDoc is not loaded, e.g. one started with `gap --bare':

    Error, Variable: 'PrintTo1' must have an assigned value

PrintTo of the GAP library also accepts an output stream and gives the
same result here, so use that. Note that PrintString is not an
alternative: for a field it returns "Magma( ... )".

The comment claiming the code was taken from GAPDoc to avoid future
incompatibility is dropped, since it now uses no GAPDoc function at all.

See https://github.com/gap-system/gap/issues/2434

author: cardflip34
body:
## What

Adds an edge password gate so the site is not publicly readable. The middleware runs **before any static file is served**, so page HTML never leaves the server unauthenticated — real server-side protection, not a client-side overlay that can be bypassed by viewing source or disabling JS.

## Key constraint: this repository is public

A plaintext password in source would be readable by anyone and would defeat the purpose entirely. So:

- The middleware reads **`SITE_PASSWORD`** from the environment when set.
- Otherwise it compares against a committed **SHA-256 hash**. The plaintext is not recoverable from the file.
- Verified: the password string appears **0 times** across `middleware.js`, `package.json`, and `vercel.json`.

Vercel's built-in Password Protection was ruled out — it is Enterprise-only, or a **$150/month** add-on on Pro.

## Behaviour

- Branded login page matching the site (navy/brass, same display serif, light + dark), rather than a raw browser auth dialog.
- Correct password sets an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` cookie for 30 days.
- Gated responses are `401` with `noindex, nofollow`, so crawlers do not index gated content.
- Constant-time-ish comparison; no plaintext logged.
- `/_vercel/*` is excluded so the analytics beacon keeps working.

`package.json` is added solely to mark `middleware.js` as an ES module, which Vercel requires for no-framework projects. There is still **no build step** — `framework`, `buildCommand`, and `installCommand` remain null.

## Why this is staged

Preview deployments on this account sit behind Vercel SSO (`/sso-api` redirect), so I cannot verify middleware on a preview URL from outside. Shipping untested middleware straight to production risks blanking the live site if the pass-through behaves unexpectedly.

**This step gates only `/robots.txt` and `/__unlock`.** That exercises both halves of the mechanism on real infrastructure — the gate *and* the pass-through to a real static file — with zero risk to any visitor-facing page. Step 2 widens the matcher to the whole site once verified.

author: mironmotor
body:
Три части, разделённые намеренно: **руки** (что можно сделать), **автономия** (кто решает) и **мост к NOOA** (чужой мозг). Решает один слой, отвечает за последствия — другой.

## `hands.py` — руки
Единственное место, где Макс дотягивается до реального мира.

- **Белый список, а не чёрный.** Список опасного бесконечен, список нужного — короткий
- **Пути только внутри проекта**: раскрываются через `resolve()`, поэтому `..` и симлинк наружу не проходят
- **Без оболочки**: склеить `; rm -rf` нечем в принципе
- **По умолчанию репетиция**: выполнение требует `confirm=True` — «решил» и «сделал» остаются разными шагами
- **Журнал всех попыток**, включая отклонённые

Проверка на живых атаках нашла дыру в моей же первой версии: белый список сверял только имя команды, и **`cat /etc/passwd` проходил** — `read_file` был заперт, а `cat` обходил запор. Теперь аргументы-пути проверяются той же границей.

## `autonomy.py` — решения
Такт «наблюдение → решение → действие → запись». Модель может назвать **только ключ из `hands.ACTIONS`**; выдуманное действие отвергается на разборе и до рук не доходит.

Порядок мозгов: **NOOA → свой LLM → правила**, каждый следующий включается молча — автономность не должна зависеть от того, что сейчас запущено.

## `nooa_bridge/` — NOOA от NVIDIA
Отдельным процессом, и это не прихоть:

| | |
|---|---|
| NOOA требует | Python **≥3.12** |
| Ядро Макса | Python **3.9** |

Втащить внутрь — значит переводить всё ядро и тянуть `litellm` туда, где хватает стандартной библиотеки.

NOOA получает список доступных действий и возвращает выбор. Своих инструментов выполнения (`shell_tools`, `_bash_session`) он здесь **не получает**: мозг чужой, руки свои, границы задаёт эта сторона.

## Проверено
Побег из проекта (`../..`, абсолютные пути, `~`, симлинки) отклонён · `rm -rf`, `sudo`, `curl|sh`, `git push`, `npm install` отклонены · чтение чужих файлов через разрешённые `cat/head/tail/grep/find` отклонено · разрешённое работает.

Интеграция с NOOA проверена подставным сервером — решение действительно приходит от него и исполняется (Макс увидел 52 файла ядра). **Враждебный «мозг» проверен отдельно**: `rm -rf /`, `cat /etc/passwd`, чтение `~/.ssh/id_rsa` заблокированы руками; выдуманное действие отвергнуто разбором с откатом на собственное решение.

Сервер моста честно отказывается стартовать на Python <3.12. Сборка и smoke зелёные.

## Про PR #34
Тот агент автономен внутри **визуальной симуляции** — его действия меняют параметры отрисовки. Этот — про действия в реальности. Не дубль, они не конфликтуют.

author: hipetech
body:
Home opens on a seven-day strip that pages by week, drags open into the month, and marks days with workout dots. Markers and the selected day are **mock props owned by Home** — no store, no Firestore read, and selecting a day filters nothing.

Implements Phases 0 and 1 of [`docs/plans/weekly-calendar/plan.md`](docs/plans/weekly-calendar/plan.md) (included in this branch).

## Shape

Wix `react-native-calendars@1.1314.0` is the interaction engine and stops at the feature boundary. It already implements the vertical open/close pan and both horizontal pagers, which the `@expo/ui` bridge cannot express — it vends no `DragGesture`. `features/calendar/calendar-types.ts` publishes a small Hipefit contract instead: no provider, no marking object, no theme key and no navigation enum reaches a call site. Every visible piece is replaced rather than themed, because the library's own day and header text sets `allowFontScaling={false}`.

Home is now **two sibling islands** — the React Native calendar above the existing screen-filling SwiftUI `Host` — so the animated height pushes the list down as plain flex layout rather than crossing back through a dynamically sized `RNHostView` row.

## Five findings from the pinned dependency

Each is recorded beside the code that works around it:

| Finding | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `CalendarProvider` is `flex: 1`, which Yoga resolves to a **zero basis** in an auto-height parent — `flexGrow`/`flexBasis` are not enough, only overriding `flex` brings the calendar back from rendering nothing at all | `expandable-weekly-calendar.tsx` |
| A native stack overlays its navigation bar, so a non-scrolling band renders *behind* the large title without an explicit header inset | `home-content.tsx` |
| The library measures its header **once, while collapsed**, so a month title appearing on expansion clips the last week row permanently — the title lives outside that header | `calendar-month-header.tsx` |
| `WEEK_HEIGHT` is a fixed 46pt module constant, which caps the day cell and forces a Dynamic Type ceiling on the day number alone | `calendar-metrics.ts` |
| Transparent surfaces let the month grid show through the collapsed strip | `calendar-theme.ts` |

## Verified

iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5: collapsed strip, day press, week paging **both directions**, drag-to-expand, month paging, collapse. Selection never moves from navigation — only a day press changes it — and survives paging off-screen and back. Every day is one 44pt button announcing its date, whether it is today, and its **full** workout count even where the cell draws an overflow pill (`"Thursday, 6 August 2026, 5 workouts"` behind three dot positions).

`bun run type-check`, `eslint`, and `prettier --check` pass.

## Not yet done

Reduce Motion is unresolved — the library springs open and closed unconditionally, and the plan asks for either a pinned-package patch or an accepted exception. Also unverified: large-title collapse on scroll (the seeded account has too little content for Home's list to scroll), dark mode, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver-at-mount, and the month/year/DST boundary cases. Phase 3 durable documentation is untouched.

author: grifter182
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses several stability and correctness issues across the Opportunities page, authentication flow, and error handling. The main fixes are pagination for large datasets, realtime event debouncing to prevent refetch storms, and improvements to auth redirect safety and error boundary behavior.

## Key Changes

### Opportunities Page (`src/pages/Opportunities.tsx`)
- **Pagination**: Implement page-through logic for PostgREST's ~1000-row limit. Previously, the page silently truncated datasets beyond that ceiling, causing missing rows and incorrect KPI counts. Now pages through up to 5000 rows and displays a warning if truncated.
- **Realtime debouncing**: Coalesce bursts of realtime events (e.g., bulk updates firing one event per row) into a single trailing refetch after 400ms, preventing refetch storms across all open browsers.
- **Unique channel names**: Use a per-mount sequence number to avoid channel collisions when the component mounts twice (React StrictMode or multiple tabs).
- **Filter persistence**: Move sessionStorage parsing from a bare IIFE (re-parsed on every render) to a lazy initializer, reducing unnecessary work.
- **Task status logic**: Fix task counting to use `status !== 'done'` instead of `status === 'open'`, matching TasksContext convention and fixing badge mismatches between table and card views.
- **Stats calculation**: Correct KPI logic — "Active Deals" now excludes won/closed deals, "Won" counts both `status === 'won'` and closed stages, and "Archived" counts the actual `status === 'dead'` value (the DB constraint makes `status === 'archived'` impossible).
- **Status/stage terminology**: Remove the unused `statusFilter` state and simplify tab logic to use `ARCHIVED_STATUS = 'dead'` constant. Archive tab now only selects `status === 'dead'`.
- **Selection scoping**: Clear selected IDs that fall outside the current filter view, so the "N items selected" counter only describes visible rows.
- **Pipeline switching**: Extract duplicated pipeline-change logic into a `switchPipeline()` function with proper error handling and activity logging.
- **Activity logging**: Wrap activity inserts in a `logActivity()` helper that returns success/failure, allowing toasts to warn when the audit trail write fails.
- **Query param handling**: Fix `?new=true` clearing to only delete that param instead of wiping the entire query string.
- **UI polish**: Disable the "Intelligence View" button (not yet implemented), adjust KPI card grid layout, add truncation warning banner, and remove the unused "Closed / Dead" stat card.

### Authentication (`src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx`)
- **Referrer lookup resilience**: Distinguish between "lookup errored" (`roleUnavailable = true`) and "no profile exists" (`referrer = null`). A transient network blip must not sign a valid user out — only a persistent "no profile" should deny access.
- **Pagination in auth**: Page through all users when listing for profile lookups, avoiding silent truncation.
- **Email matching**: Use `.eq()` instead of `.ilike()` for referrer email fallback to prevent wildcard injection (% or _ in email local parts).
- **Deduplication**: Track the last user ID resolved to avoid running the profile lookup twice on boot (both `getSession()` and `onAuthStateChange` fire with the same user).
- **Callback safety**: Defer DB operations inside `onAuthStateChange` to a macrotask so the callback returns before touching the auth-aware client (prevents deadlock warnings).
- **Session tracking**: Simplify login session recording — return the inserted ID directly instead of re-querying, avoiding race conditions when two tabs sign in simultaneously.
- **Password change flag**: Only set `must_change_password` from user metadata; remove the logic that forced it to true on `PASSWORD_RECOVERY` events (was trapping users following normal reset links).
- **Session cleanup**: Clear per-tab guards (`access-denied-toast-shown`, `fullscreen-requested`) on fresh sign-in so they don't leak across users.

### Protected Route (`src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx`)
- **Fullscreen guard**: Move full

author: carlallenn
body:
## What

Four of the last thirteen nightly Fuzz runs (Aug 1, 3, 4, 5) were red without the fuzzer finding anything: the hosted runner received a shutdown signal 11–14 minutes into the 20-minute session and the job was canceled. On Aug 4 both matrix jobs died within a minute of each other — a VM-pool event, not anything the targets did. All four landed in the ~08:00 UTC morning peak that the 05:41 cron queues into.

## Changes

- **Move the cron to 02:41 UTC** — off the peak window where pool pressure preempts long CPU-pegged jobs; odd minute kept per GitHub's guidance.
- **Add `fuzz-rerun.yml`** — on a failed Fuzz run, reruns just the failed jobs, gated two ways so a real crash can never retry-loop:
  - skips if the run uploaded any `fuzz-artifacts-*` (a crash is a finding for a human, not a retry);
  - skips at run attempt ≥ 3 (at most two automatic reruns).

  The job needs `actions: write` (a sanctioned exception, documented inline); it checks out nothing and runs no project code, so the token never coexists with untrusted input. `workflow_run` carries a zizmor inline ignore with the rationale.
- **Record the triage rule** in the fuzz.yml header: red + shutdown-signal log + no artifacts = infra noise (auto-retried); red + artifacts = real finding.

## Testing

`yamllint --strict`, `actionlint`, and `zizmor --persona=pedantic --offline` all pass locally.

body:
## What

Completes the review entry of the trio (map #18): `cueloop review <pr>` fetches the PR diff, opens a review session, and posts the verdict back to the PR as a real review.

## How

- `packages/cli/src/pr.ts`: `cueloop review <pr>` runs `gh pr diff <pr>` (auth fully delegated to the user's gh CLI), creates a diff session with `meta.title = "PR <pr>"` and `meta.pr` recording the ref, and opens the TUI on it. When the session resolves, the verdict maps 1:1 onto gh review flags - approve → `--approve`, request_changes → `--request-changes`, comment → `--comment` - with the session's feedback.md as `--body`. If the session is unresolved on exit, it prints that nothing was posted.
- Non-interactive path for agents and scripts: `cueloop review <pr> --no-tui` creates the session and prints it as JSON; `cueloop review-post <session-id> <pr>` posts a resolved session back.
- The gh binary is injectable via `CUELOOP_GH` (default `gh`) so tests stub it.
- `packages/schema`: `ArtifactMeta.pr` records the PR ref on the session.

## Tests

`test/cli/review.test.ts` - black-box tier 3 through the real entrypoint with an isolated `CUELOOP_HOME` and `CUELOOP_GH` pointing at a stub script that records args and emits a fixture diff:

- `--no-tui` fetches the diff into a session (content, type, title, pr ref) and calls `gh pr diff`
- each verdict kind maps to the right gh flags with feedback.md as the body, annotations flow into the posted body
- unresolved sessions post nothing (exit 1), gh failures surface stderr (exit 1), missing args exit 2

`bun run typecheck` 0 errors; `bun test ./packages ./test` 103 pass, 0 fail.

author: danielamodu
body: Closes #18971. ## Summary Adds `MLModelPatchBuilder` to `datahub/specific/`, so `mlModel` aspects can be mutated with `PATCH` rather than only `UPSERT`. `datahub/specific/` ships patch builders for `chart`, `dashboard`, `dataJob`, `dataProduct`, `dataset`, `form`, and `structuredProperty` — but none for any ML entity. `entity_client.update()` branches on its argument: an `Entity` becomes a full-aspect `UPSERT`, a `MetadataPatchProposal` becomes a surgical `PATCH`. With no ML builder, `mlModel` writers only have the first option. ## Why it matters `UPSERT` on `structuredProperties` replaces the whole aspect, so any property the writer did not know about is destroyed. Verified against GMS v1.7.0: | Write path | Result | |---|---| | Two independent `PATCH` writes | Both properties survive | | One full-aspect `UPSERT` | The property the writer didn't know about is destroyed | This bites anything writing ML metadata from more than one place — a training pipeline setting hyperparameters, a governance job setting ownership, and a quality gate setting a risk verdict all target the same entity on different schedules. Today each one has to read-modify-write the entire aspect and hope nobody wrote in between. The concrete case this came from: a pre-deploy gate writing `risk_verdict`, `last_checked`, and a `baseline` snapshot to an `mlModel` as three independent concerns. ## What's in the change `MLModelPatchBuilder` composes the existing entity-agnostic aspect helpers in exactly the shape `DataProductPatchBuilder` uses — `HasOwnershipPatch`, `HasCustomPropertiesPatch`, `HasStructuredPropertiesPatch`, `HasTagsPatch`, `HasTermsPatch`, `HasDomainsPatch`, `HasInstitutionalMemoryPatch`. No new machinery: `MetadataPatchProposal` already resolves the entity type via `guess_entity_type(urn)`, so `mlModel` needs no special casing. On top of the mixins it adds `mlModelProperties` setters mirroring the `dataProduct` builder's: `set_name`, `set_description`, `set_external_url`, `set_type`, `set_version`, `set_hyper_parameters`, `set_ml_features`, `add_ml_feature`, `remove_ml_feature`, `set_training_jobs`, `set_downstream_jobs`, `set_groups`, `set_deployments`. ## Tests `metadata-ingestion/tests/unit/patch/test_mlmodel_patch_builder.py` — 12 tests, no DataHub instance required. They assert that: - proposals carry `changeType == "PATCH"`, never `UPSERT` - `entityType` resolves to `mlModel` from the URN alone, with no special casing - two structured properties produce two ops at two distinct paths, so a concurrently stored third property is untouched - the `mlModelProperties` setters patch the expected path with the expected value - `mlFeatures` entries can be added and removed individually rather than by rewriting the array - the inherited tag and ownership mixins emit `PATCH` against the right aspects ``` $ pytest metadata-ingestion/tests/unit/patch/test_mlmodel_patch_builder.py -q ............ [100%] 12 passed ``` ## Scope note `datahub.sdk.MLModel` already supports mlModel structured properties through the newer SDK layer. The gap addressed here is specifically the absence of a `PATCH`-emitting builder, not the absence of mlModel support. ## Checklist - [x] The PR conforms to DataHub's Contributing Guideline - [x] Links to related issues (#18971) - [x] Tests added for the change - [ ] Docs updated — happy to add a section to the patch-builder docs if you'd like it; the existing builders don't appear to be individually documented. --- ## Summary by cubic Add `MLModelPatchBuilder` to enable safe PATCH updates to `mlModel` aspects, preventing destructive UPSERTs when multiple systems write to the same model. Addresses #18971. - **New Features** - Adds `datahub/specific/mlmodel.py` with `MLModelPatchBuilder` that emits `PATCH` MCPs for `mlModel`. - Composes existing mixins: ownership, tags, terms, domains, institutional memory, custom properties, and structured properties. - Adds `mlModelProperties` setters: `set_name`, `set_description`, `set_external_url`, `set_type`, `set_version`, `set_hyper_params`, `set_training_metrics`, `set_ml_features`, `add_ml_feature`, `remove_ml_feature`, `set_training_jobs`, `set_downstream_jobs`, `set_groups`, `set_deployments`. - **Bug Fixes** - Targets canonical `hyperParams` field (not deprecated `hyperParameters`). Written for commit 8a6715295bab2484da6a4d2b37d05e4d1b9c51fa. Summary will update on new commits.

author: polynaut
body:
Saving an outfit variant from Daz (or a new Houdini project) into the character's folder left the studio blind — every add was pick- or drop-driven, so the file you just saved was a manual link away every time.

### Detect new files on focus, offer a wizard

- On character-page load and every window focus, the folder is rescanned for unlinked `.duf` / `.hip*` files (pure vitest-covered filter; generated output — `dth-exports/`, `rom-animations/`, `*_ROM.duf`, Houdini `backup/`, `.dcsmeta/` — is never offered).
- Detection surfaces as a non-modal banner; **Review** opens a wizard with one page per file. Files saved while it's open append as pages on the next focus.
- Scene pages run the existing add validation and link in place; a scene-less character gets **Set as primary** with full gender/genesis/GEN derivation. Houdini projects link in place with the field's dedupe.
- **Skip is permanent** (per-character skip list in `.dcsmeta`); the banner's ✕ only hides for the session.
- The add/link patch builders moved out of `DazSceneField` into `lib/scene-add.ts` so the wizard and the field share one set of linking rules.

Design + plan: `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-08-07-detect-new-character-files*`. Smoke: `detected-files.smoke.ts` covers load/focus detection, dismiss, live append, add, permanent skip, self-close.

### Project-wide, not just the open character (closes #740)

Detection ran only while a character page was mounted, so a Save As out of Daz
while the studio was showing the project page — or Settings, or Tools — went
unnoticed until that character happened to be opened.

`fetchProjectDetectedFiles` now runs the **same candidate rule** across every
character, and a banner mounted at the root reports it wherever the user comes
back to. It adds nothing itself: **Open** navigates to the owning character,
whose banner and wizard do the work — one add flow, not two that can drift. The
character already on screen is excluded, so the two banners never double up.
Focus **regain** only, never on mount: firing on mount would make every launch
pay for a whole-project walk before the first paint.

**The cost problem it had to solve first.** `walkFiles` costs a `readDir` IPC
*per directory* — tolerable once, sluggish per character on a network share,
untenable for a whole project on every focus. So this adds a native
`scan_files_by_ext(folder, exts, skipDirs)`: one walk for a whole tree, with the
generated directories pruned **before descending** (reading a character's entire
FBX/Alembic export tree only to throw it away is the expensive half). That
needed `DirVisitor::skip_dir` — additive, `false` by default, so every existing
visitor is unchanged; distinct from returning `Err` from `enter_dir`, which
aborts the whole walk instead of pruning one subtree. The per-character scan
uses it too, so that path got cheaper as well.

Attribution is a pure rule (`attributeToOwners`): the sweep walks the characters
ROOT once, and each hit goes to the character with the **longest** matching
folder — nothing stops `Kira/Variants/Kira Young/`, and shortest-first matching
would let the outer character claim the inner one's scenes and offer them on the
wrong page. A file under no character folder is dropped.

The vanished-root rule from `3d4c31c3` is applied to the sweep as well: it
throws rather than answering "nothing found", so a share blip keeps the last
answer instead of blanking the banner and eating the dismiss for every character
at once.

Tests: 4 unit specs on attribution, 2 Rust specs on the native scan (extensions
+ pruning, and a missing folder answering empty rather than failing), 5 smoke
specs on the banner — noticed on the project page, **Open** landing in the
character's own wizard, no double banner for the character on screen, dismissal
holding until something new turns up, and the generated trees never offered.

**Not verified:** no real Daz Save As — the smoke suite drives an in-memory
filesystem, so a real focus regain against a real network share is untested.

author: tomcounsell
body:
Closes #2475

Full root-cause narrative with file:line citations is in [this comment on #2475](https://github.com/tomcounsell/ai/issues/2475#issuecomment-5219890671). Summary below.

## The defect

`assess_update_flow()` declared a wedge when `last_probe_ok` was fresh and `bridge:last_update_received` was stale. Both halves fail.

`last_probe_ok` is refreshed every 180s by the reconciler (`bridge/reconciler.py:36,147-149`), so it is **always** fresh on a connected bridge. The rule therefore reduced to *"no inbound message in 4 hours"* — a quiet night, indistinguishable from a wedged update loop. The beacon has exactly one writer, `bridge/telegram_bridge.py:1196`, inside the `NewMessage` handler; it is a traffic signal being read as a liveness signal.

Nothing seeds that beacon on restart. `restart_bridge()` is a bare `launchctl kickstart` and the bridge writes an unrelated boot-SHA beacon at startup. So after a wedge restart the key still held its pre-restart timestamp, and the only thing between the new process and an identical verdict was the 5-minute startup grace against a 60-second tick:

| t | event |
|---|---|
| 0:00 | verdict → `log_crash("bridge_update_loop_wedged")` → SIGKILL + kickstart |
| 0:00–5:00 | new pid inside grace → suppressed |
| ~6:00 | first tick past grace; beacon now 4h06m old, never seeded → verdict again |

That predicts a restart every ~6 minutes, and the issue's own evidence records exactly that: *"continuous `loop_wedged detected` every 5 minutes from 04:25 to 06:09 UTC."* The cadence is the grace window, not a Telethon fault. It is also never throttled — `bridge_watchdog.py:554-563` exempts wedge-dominated storms from the restart circuit by design.

## The fix

**Silence is measured from `max(last_update_received, process_start_ts)`.** A restart clears the accusation; a real recurrence still re-fires after another full ceiling of silence. `get_process_start_ts` was already being fetched for the grace window, so this costs nothing.

**A verdict requires `bridge:last_missed_recovery`** — new key, stamped by the reconciler when a scan recovers ≥1 message the live path never delivered. The corroborating evidence has to come from outside the handler under suspicion: `last_update_received` and the per-chat `bridge:last_event:*` keys are both written by the `NewMessage` handler, so neither can testify that the handler has stopped — their silence is equally consistent with an idle account. The reconciler reaches Telegram over an independent API path, already computes `recovered`, and gives a quiet account nothing to stamp.

The secondary accelerator's per-chat `scan_iter` corroboration was circular for that same reason and is removed; the accelerator now applies the primary shape at the warn threshold with equally recent evidence.

**No bridge pid is now the same fail-safe as an unreadable start time.** Process age is the floor for the silence measurement, not just the grace window, so a verdict without it cannot be bounded to the current process.

## Not changed, deliberately

`catch_up` losslessness is fine and is not the defect. `catch_up=True` is unconditional (`telegram_bridge.py:1158`) and `bridge/catchup.py:218-244` takes `min(global_cutoff, cursor - epsilon)`, never `max`, so the short lookback during a restart storm does not truncate recovery. The reconciler needed its deeper lookback (`5d9515671`) for its own fixed 30-minute window. The docs are accurate on this point and are left alone.

## Verification

162 tests green: `test_bridge_liveness.py`, `test_bridge_watchdog.py`, `test_reconciler.py` (unit + integration), `test_update_loop_wedge_recovery.py`, `test_watchdog_to_bridge.py`, `test_dm_recovery.py`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

**Mutation-checked, three guards, each independently:**

| Mutation | Expected red | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Measure silence from the beacon only (pre-fix) | restart-reset test | `test_restart_resets_the_silence_clock` failed, 20 passed |
| Drop the recovery-evidence requirement from the primary rule (pre-fix) | the three false-positive tests | `test_quiet_account_past_ceiling_is_not_wedged`, `test_absent_beacon_on_fresh_redis_is_not_wedged`, `test_stale_recovery_evidence_does_not_corroborate` failed, 18 passed |
| Stop stamping the key in the reconciler | the stamp test | `test_stamps_when_messages_were_missed` failed, 1 passed |

## Tests whose contract this changes

`tests/integration/test_update_loop_wedge_recovery.py` cases (a) and (e) asserted that silence past the ceiling with a fresh probe **is** a wedge. Those pinned the false positive as the specification, so they are replaced rather than kept. Case (e)'s underlying concern — that reconciler *probe* activity must not re-green the update signal — still holds and is still tested; what changed is that reconciler *recovery* activity is now a required input rather than an irrelevance.

## Note for review

This machine is worker-only; the bridge is deliberately stopped here, so there is no live reproduction. Everything above is from code, git history, the installed Telethon 1.42.0, and the issue's own crash-tracker evidence. Local `logs/watchdog.log` is unit-test output (`monitoring/bridge_watchdog.py:87-93` attaches a `RotatingFileHandler` to the production log path at module import) and was not used as evidence.

## Not merged

Held for the coordinator's serial merge queue.

Resolves #212.

## What changed

`docs/autonomous-loop-plan.md` §3.1 step 6 now documents the `--body-file` convention:
when Routine A (or any automation) writes an issue body to a scratchpad file first, it
must file the issue with `gh issue create --body-file <path>` (or the REST API
equivalent of reading the file's contents into the `body` field), never
`gh issue create --body "@<path>"`. `@file` expansion is specific to flags that document
it per-command (`--body-file`, `-F key=@file`); `--body` has no such expansion, so
`--body "@<path>"` posts the literal path string as the body.

## Decision made

The ticket suggested this fix belonged in `docs/autonomous-loop-plan.md` §3.1's "file a
new issue" step, "mirroring #208's fix for the closing-keyword convention." That's what
this PR does — same file, same step-6 location where CI-failure issue filing is
described, same inline-note style PR #209 used for the #208 fix. No code changes: the
one script in this repo that files issues programmatically
(`scripts/migrate_backlog_to_issues.py:204`) already uses `--body-file` correctly, so
this ticket is purely about codifying the convention for the routine's own ad hoc issue
filing (the class of gap #210 exposed), not fixing a code defect.

None added — this ticket has no code path to test (see "decision made" above); the
existing 590-test suite is unaffected and stays green.

Nothing. This only adds guidance for future issue-filing; it does not change any
previously reported number, model behavior, or existing ticket's evidence.

author: davidbshan
body:
Fixes a Bugbot finding on #957 (merged): "Stale raylogs from prior attempts".

## The defect

#957 added the raylogs fetch resolved independently as the newest attempt of that kind. But the
worker uploads ray logs **only when ray actually failed**, while it uploads a traceback for every
failure. On a retried run the two can therefore belong to different attempts:

- attempt 0 dies to a raylet -> uploads `raylogs_rl_attempt0.txt` and `error_rl_attempt0.txt`
- attempt 1 fails for an unrelated reason -> uploads `error_rl_attempt1.txt` and **no** raylogs

The newest traceback is attempt 1's; the newest raylogs are attempt 0's. `flash runs log` then shows
a raylet death next to a `ValueError`, and the reader diagnoses a raylet that died an attempt ago.
Worse than showing nothing, because it looks like corroboration.

Reproduced before changing anything -- that exact repo layout yields
`['console_rl.txt', 'error_rl_attempt1.txt', 'raylogs_rl_attempt0.txt']`.

## The fix

Derive the raylogs name from the **traceback's** attempt instead of resolving it independently, so
the pair always describes one attempt. When this attempt produced no ray logs the fetch simply
misses, which the loop already treats as a non-event.

A legacy unscoped traceback (`error_rl.txt`) names no attempt, so nothing is fetched -- guessing the
newest would reintroduce the same mismatch on the one shape that cannot be checked.

## Validation

Three tests:

- a prior attempt's ray logs are **not** paired with this attempt's unrelated traceback, and the
  console + traceback that do belong to it are unaffected
- an unscoped legacy traceback fetches no ray logs
- the derived name matches `ray_log_artifact_name` for every phase and attempt -- the control plane
  derives this name and the worker writes it, in different processes with no shared constant, so the
  two spellings are pinned against each other rather than against a literal

Falsified individually. Restoring the independent resolution fails the first two; guessing attempt 0
for a legacy name fails the second; misspelling the artifact kind fails the third plus #957's own
test.

Worth noting why #957's tests missed this: both used matched attempt numbers, so the newest raylogs
and the newest traceback happened to agree. The mismatch is the whole defect.

294 passed across `test_server_api` and `test_flash_worker`; `ruff check .` and
`ruff format --check .` clean.

No version bump: control-plane artifact fetch, no CLI surface change.

> **Overview**
