author: jakechampion
body:
Fixes the read half of #6243 (the issue stays open for the insert half — see below).

## The leak

A string-keyed Map **lookup** leaked 16 bytes per call on arm64, and 32 when the key was a freshly built string. Unbounded in a loop; x86-64 flat.

On the two-word string ABI a string key does not fit the runtime's pointer-wide key slot, so the lowering boxes it into a cell and passes the cell pointer through. `set` keeps that cell; every read method (`get` / `has` / `get_or` / `delete`) does not, and `freeLookupKeyCell` exists to reclaim it — plus `__fern_str_dec` the key's buffer when the key was a fresh owned temporary rather than an alias the caller still holds.

It was gated on `b.ptrW != 4`, its comment asserting a key cell "is only produced when the key was boxed (string K on wasm32)". But boxing is decided by `isStringForBoxing`, i.e. by the **two-word ABI** — which arm64 also runs under via `TwoWordOverride`. So arm64 allocated the cell and freed nothing.

`cellSlot < 0` alone is the correct guard, and always was: all four callers initialise it to `-1` and assign only when they box, so a negative slot *is* "not boxed". x86-64 never boxes, so its lowering is unchanged.

## Measured (arm64-darwin, native Apple Silicon)

`get_or` + `has` + `get_or`-with-a-built-key in a loop, `__heap_bump_bytes()` after:

| n | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 4592 | 1424 |
| 200 | 7792 | 1424 |
| 400 | 14192 | 1424 |
| 800 | 26992 | 1424 |

32 B/iteration, exactly linear, to flat. Split by key shape: a literal key leaked 16 (the cell), a built key 32 (the cell **and** its string buffer) — which is why the regression test exercises both.

## What this does NOT fix

Two things, both recorded on the issue rather than left implicit:

1. **The insert half.** `set` is the one method that keeps the cell, and on an **overwrite** `__map_set_keyed_impl` keeps the key it already had and drops the incoming one on the floor, so the direct `m = m.insert(k, v)` form still leaks 16 B per call (32 with a built key) — measured unchanged. Fixing it needs the type-erased runtime to release a key it did not take, which is a different change from this one.
2. **wasm32 leaks the same 16 B/iter on the read path**, through a Map lowering that never reaches `freeLookupKeyCell` at all (its module is byte-identical before and after this change). A second instance of the same leak behind a different path.

## Tests

`TestMapStringKeyLookupHeapFlatArm64` / `…X86_64`, next to the existing `TestMapCowTempBindingHeapFlat*`. Verified to be a genuine gate: the program returns **2 (leaks)** compiled by stock `main` and **42** after the fix, on arm64-darwin. No wasm leg, since that target still leaks for the separate reason above; the comment says so.

Also corrects the stale note on `TestMapCowTempBindingHeapFlat`, which said the arm64 numbers were "identical before and after this change (#6243)" — now split into which half remains.

## What I ran

`go test ./internal/ir/... ./internal/checker/... ./internal/codegen/...` — green. `go vet ./internal/e2e/` — clean. The Go e2e legs themselves all skip on this host (no qemu), so CI is the gate for the two new legs; the x86-64 one is reasoned rather than measured (it does not box, so its emission is untouched) and CI will confirm.

body: Previously in the sandbox tutorial, we asked the model to write to stdout and evaluated it on that, in addition to restricting the creation of files in its system prompt. This conflicted with the `hello-world` task of writing "Hello, world!" to a file named hello.txt, causing the model to effectively crash out in its chain of thought. This is a stopgap solution while we iterate on the final design for how sandboxes/sandbox pools will look on the Gym, but for now this should help tighten up correctness on this particular tutorial. ---

author: tristanmatthias
body:
The corpus had `defer_lifo.av`, which uses `defer` only at **function top level**. That is the one shape which always worked — it kept passing for the entire period when a `defer` in any nested block was silently dropped. So it was not coverage for the scope path, and nothing else in the corpus was either.

This file pins one distinct emitter per case:

| case | emitter |
|---|---|
| `while` / `for` / `if` body, bare block | `defer_scope_enter` / `defer_scope_exit` |
| `break`, `continue` | `LoopStackFrame.defer_depth` unwinding before the jump |
| block expression | `emit_block_expr`'s scope exit |
| deferred body reads a block-local binding | the walker env threaded into `defer_scope_exit` |
| `return` from a nested block | the whole-stack LIFO walk |
| `if` inside `while` | the two scopes composing, inner first |

The bare-block case earns its place separately: it always *fired*, just at function exit rather than block exit, so a presence check passed on it. The corpus catches it as an **ordering** difference in the emitted calls.

The last row is the finding from #1188's review. Note that `use_it` takes its parameter through to the output deliberately — a helper that ignored the argument would emit the same call regardless of which binding the deferred body resolved to, and the file would not cover the env threading it claims to.

## Why this could not land with the fix

Filed as **t-xwtq** rather than bundled into #1188, because adding it there would have broken that PR's own gate *by construction*: diff-test requires both compilers to agree on every corpus file, OLD dropped nested defers, so this file diverged on purpose. The `intended-ir-change` label does not help either — it switches the oracle to run-equivalence, and the two binaries genuinely print different things.

It becomes an ordinary regression lock only once OLD **is** the fixed compiler, which it now is (#1188 merged, train at v513).

## Verification

- Compiles standalone with a bare `bs2 compile` — the corpus contract, and the thing that gets a file silently skipped if violated.
- Runs with the expected ordering across every shape (per-iteration defers interleaved with body output, inner-before-outer nesting, `use 0` / `use 1` / `use 9` for the block-local case).
- **diff-test: 25 inputs compared, 0 skipped**, selfhost 1,264,185 lines byte-identical.

Docs-and-test-only; no compiler source touched.

Closes t-xwtq.

author: kevinrhaas
body:
Kevin's decision on UX sweep #574 finding 1 (the ⛔ item in the NOW queue): **inside the app the reader's theme wins; `auto` ships as an opt-in, not the default.** Written into the queue as two independently-shippable slices so the loop can execute without guessing.

**N5a ★★ — the Viewer follows the app's theme.** Fixes the actual complaint (dark app frames a light dashboard, reads as broken). Downloads and embeds are *untouched* — an exported dashboard is a deliverable headed for ctic.org and stakeholders' inboxes, and deterministic appearance is worth more there than adaptivity.

Three implementation constraints the spec pins down, because each is a way to get this subtly wrong:
- `buildViewerHtml()` emits both the srcdoc and the download from one call, so the override rides an **explicit opt-in `extraOpts` flag that only the Viewer's call passes** — the download path is provably unchanged (same shape as the existing `{ pdfPageSize… }` options).
- **The Studio builder preview is not the Viewer.** It must keep showing `spec.renderMode`, or an author can't see the appearance they're composing. Read mode only.
- **The byte-identity invariant is amended, not broken:** builder preview ≡ export still holds and stays asserted; the Viewer srcdoc may differ by the theme attribute alone. CLAUDE.md's wording gets updated in the same PR.

**N5b ★ — `auto` as a third Appearance option.** Separate slice, separate PR. Light / Dark / Auto ("match the reader"); **new dashboards stay Light**. When `auto`, the export bakes no `data-theme` and carries a runtime resolver (standalone → `prefers-color-scheme`; framed → host when readable, **never throws** on a cross-origin embed). One byte stream branching at runtime, never a build-time per-context branch. `""` and `"dark"` exports stay byte-for-byte identical to today.

Both slices name their specific new suite checks (viewer-follows-app, download-byte-unchanged, builder-preview-unchanged; auto-has-resolver, `emulateMedia` honors the OS setting, three options with Light default).

Docs-only change here — STATUS.md isn't precached, so no changelog entry or sw bump. Dev gate green locally: validate (206 files), doc-truth, changelog-check.

author: lasnubesenchica-commits
body:
Un usuario tecleó `110` y `135` en modo **%** creyendo que fijaba precios. El cálculo fue correcto (+110% y +135%), pero tres cosas conspiraron para que no se notara hasta ver el total.

## 1. La referencia era el precio de HOY, no el del período

El control mostraba `_lnPrecioCat(cat, HOY)`. Con una promo vigente este mes, eso **no** es lo que se cobró en el período base: decía *"Viernes $90"* mientras el cálculo usaba los **$110 reales de julio**. Dos números distintos para lo mismo en la misma pantalla.

`_proyPrecioRef()` ahora promedia las noches de esa categoría **dentro del período**, que es exactamente lo que usa el cálculo. Sin noches, cae al precio de hoy.

## 2. La anotación no se actualizaba al teclear

`→ $231.00` solo aparecía al usar los botones −/+, porque `_proyOnInput` no re-renderizaba los controles — a propósito, para no perder el foco. Se perdía justo la señal que delata el error.

Ahora se refresca **solo esa línea**, vía `_proyRefHtml` compartido entre el render y el `oninput`.

## 3. No había guard contra confundir el modo

Un +110% no es un ajuste, es un precio mal puesto. Con `|aj| >= 60` en modo %, la fila ahora sugiere:

> ¿Querías **fijar** el precio en $110? Cambia el modo a **Fijo** arriba.

## Verificación (julio 2026)

```
Referencia con julio seleccionado (antes mostraba el precio de HOY):
   Entre semana:  $90        (antes decía $75)
   Viernes:       $110       (antes decía $90)

Modo % con 110 y 135 tecleados:
   Viernes:  $110 → $231.00 (+$121.00)  ¿Querías fijar el precio en $110?…
   Sábado:   $110 → $258.50 (+$148.50)  ¿Querías fijar el precio en $135?…

Modo Fijo con los mismos valores:
   Viernes:  $110            (sin cambio: julio ya cobraba $110)
   Sábado:   $110 → $135.00 (+$25.00)
   → $5920.00 → $6170.00 · Δ $250.00 · equilibrio 4.1%
```

El modo fijo también prellena con el precio del período, y `_proyCatAjustada` compara contra la misma referencia — si no, "fijar viernes en $110" se habría contado como un cambio cuando es exactamente lo que ya cobraba.

**La aritmética anterior era correcta**; lo que fallaba era la información que rodeaba al número.

author: platostwin
body:
## Half 1 — E230's open question, answered in the negative for a structural reason

E230 closed with an explicit fifteen-minute question: does any lower-level XCUITest API expose
`accessibilityElements`-array order directly, rather than through `debugDescription`'s dump?

**No for snapshot-reading APIs, and the reason is not that the right traversal has not been found.**
Four arrangements of screen 01's search field and filter chips, selected at launch by a temporary
`CYPRESS_AXORDER` variable so **one build** produced all four readings, measured against five ways
of reading the automation snapshot: `treeOrder` (`debugDescription`), `allElementsBoundByIndex`,
`allElementsBoundByAccessibilityElement`, a depth-first walk of `try app.snapshot()`'s `children`,
and `.children(matching: .any)` walked one query per level (217 nodes against a 400-node budget —
the walk completed).

**These are five traversals of ONE `XCUIElementSnapshot`, not five independent instruments** — they
share one blind spot by construction, and nothing below should be read as five agreeing witnesses.
(Corrected from the first draft of this body, which invited exactly that reading; the pending
erratum was already explicit about it. The reviewer's own reproduction shows the traversals really
do differ — their level-order walk lands the field at index 16 where the depth-first walks land it
at 188 — of one identical tree.)

All five traversals agreed with each other in all four modes:

| mode | what changed | order reported by all five probes |
|---|---|---|
| `control` | — | field → chips |
| `priority` | field 6 → **2** (below chips' 4) | field → chips — **unchanged** |
| `flat` | priorities **equal**, chips drawn **125 pt above** the field | field → chips — **unchanged** |
| `composition` | chips composed before field, priorities left at 6/4 | **chips → field** |

`treeOrder`'s indices make it smallest: field=164, chips=165 in `control`, `priority` **and** `flat`
— the same two integers, not merely the same relation — against chips=164, field=169 in
`composition`.

**The calibration.** `composition` is the case whose answer was known before the run (E230 measured
it), and every probe distinguished it. A probe that could not would have been a broken probe
reporting a null result. And the geometric inversion really took effect — the dump's own frames say
the field is drawn at y=175 with the chips at y=50, against y=55/y=110 in `control`.

**What that establishes, beyond E230.** E230's second experiment moved a `VStack`'s children, which
changes composition order *and* geometry together. `flat` separates them, and geometry loses — so
the automation snapshot is **raw view-composition order**, not a computed reading order. That is
exactly why the result generalises the way it does: **no traversal of that snapshot can observe a
sort priority**, so a sixth traversal is not worth anyone's time. `composition` also supplies a
second, independent proof: with the shipped priorities intact (field 6 > chips 4), every traversal
reported chips-before-field, the order those priorities say is wrong.

**What is NOT closed, corrected after review.** Snapshot traversal is one class of API. A **focus
engine** is another and does not read this tree; it is **unprobed by either of us**. The reviewer
tried `typeKey(.tab)` plus a `hasFocus` sweep and got no element reporting focus at all on a
simulator without Full Keyboard Access — no counterexample and no working probe. The ROADMAP
sentence previously read "there is no point looking for another one", which generalised from
snapshot traversals to all APIs; it is now scoped to snapshot traversals and names focus traversal
as the untried avenue, with the attempt recorded as inconclusive so the next person starts there
instead of re-deriving it. Same correction in the pending erratum and in this body.

**What replaces the search.** `CypressTests/MapSwipeOrderDeclarationTests` (new, Swift Testing)
reads `MapHomeView.swift` off disk through `AppSourceLiterals` — the helper `DrawnGlyphGuardTests`
(R57) and `BritishSpellingGuardTests` (R56) already use — and pins that the top chrome block's
declared priorities **descend in the same order the block composes its children**. That agreement
is the whole reason a composition-order assertion says anything about reading order.

**What is still not proved, stated rather than implied:** that VoiceOver honors the numbers. That
remains E192's physical-phone debt, unchanged.

## Half 2 — three more screens, chosen because they WRITE

`ReadingOrderAccessibilityTests` goes from three screens to six. The added three are the screens
where a wrong order costs the reader a record, not a second pass:

- **06 report** — two chip vocabularies, one that reaches the city's crew and one that E131
  established goes nowhere. The only thing telling a listener which is which is the section heading
  above it. Asserts each heading precedes its own chips and that no chip crosses the boundary.
- **16 measure** — the one screen that takes a number and writes it. Asserts kind heading → kind
  options → method heading → method options → keypad → `Save measurement`. A reader handed the
  digits before the kind control types a trunk diameter into a height; handed `Save` before the
  keypad, they save the readout's zero.
- **09 care log** — the four toggles ARE the entry. Asserts they precede the optional photo/note
  well (whose `(optional)` label must precede its own field, E185) and both precede `Done`.

**Deliberately left out, measured rather than assumed:** 11 growth history and 13 activity both
resolved to a tree with **no rows at all** on the survey run — their order is only as rich as the
seed's rows for whichever record the deep link lands on. 17 outbox reads a device-local queue. 19
memorial is unreachable from this seed without manufacturing a `removed` override.

## Red-proofs — three rounds, each mutation read for its message

Every new test proven red, and the failure message read to confirm it went red for the expected
reason. Selected messages:

- report: `("8") is not less than ("4")` — "a listener meets a hazard category before being told
  the section sends it to the city" (mutation: `section()` renders content before its label)
- report: `("12") is not less than ("4")` — "a hazard chip … has crossed into the section ERRATA
  E131 established goes nowhere" (mutation: the two pickers swapped)
- measure: `("29") is not less than ("14")` — "a reader reaches the digits before the required
  method" (mutation: keypad composed above `methodSection`)
- measure: `("29") is not less than ("18")` — "saves the readout's zero" (mutation: `ctaBlock`
  above the keypad)
- careLog: `("199") is not less than ("195")` — "files a visit that records nothing" (mutation:
  `Done` above the toggles)
- careLog: `("203") is not less than ("199")` — the `(optional)` label after the field it qualifies
  (E185)
- unit: `declares [6.0, 5.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 7.0] … not strictly descending`, naming all six source
  lines (mutation: the legend's priority raised to 7)

**The provenance test earned its place during the red-proof.** With the block's opener perturbed,

author: ccisnedev
body:
# Delivery

<!-- macss:lang=en · This document becomes the body of the pull request. -->

_What was built, by whoever implemented it. The other half — `verification.md` — is written with you, criterion by criterion, and is not here._

## Metadata

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Issue | [#24](https://github.com/ccisnedev/macss/issues/24) |
| Contract | `specification.md`, frozen at DoR |
| Branch | `feat/language-has-one-source-of-truth` → `main` |
| Version | **0.7.0** — breaking three times |

## What was built

```
$ macss requisition new probe --apply --autoapprove
Error: This project does not declare a language, so there is no way to know which template to write.
Declare it once:
  macss project adopt --lang <en|es> --apply [VALIDATION_FAILED]
```

```
$ macss project adopt --lang en --apply --autoapprove
  created  code/infra/README.md
  created  code/db/README.md
  created  code/api/README.md
  created  code/app/README.md
  created  .gitattributes
  declared .macss/config.yaml (language: en)
  retired  .macss/

Adopted. Run `macss project check` to see what still needs your judgement.
```

```
$ macss requisition new probe --plan
Plan — would open the requisition "probe" at docs/requisitions/20260807-probe:

  create   docs/requisitions/20260807-probe/requisition.md
  create   docs/requisitions/20260807-probe/issue.yaml
  record   docs/requisitions/20260807-probe as the active requisition
  ensure   the MACSS workspace is git-ignored
```

The second command is the whole change. Nobody told the third which language to
write in.

## What changed, and where

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/src/project_config.dart` | **new** — reads and writes `.macss/config.yaml`, and states the one failure the three inheriting commands share |
| `lib/modules/project/commands/create.dart` | `--lang <en\|es>` required; writes the declaration |
| `lib/modules/project/commands/adopt.dart` | the same, and it is the migration path for projects that predate this |
| `lib/modules/requisition/commands/new.dart` | `--lang` gone; derives, or refuses |
| `lib/modules/specification/commands/new.dart` | `--lang` gone; stops inheriting from `issue.yaml` |
| `lib/modules/requisition/commands/export_template.dart` | keeps `--lang`, and now requires it |
| `lib/modules/specification/specification_builder.dart` | `specification export-template` **unregistered** |
| `lib/modules/requisition/issue_metadata.dart` | `lang:` no longer written |
| `lib/modules/specification/workspace.dart` | the active pointer stops carrying a language |
| `lib/modules/requisition/commands/activate.dart` | `_langOf` deleted — nothing left to read |
| `lib/templates/template_resolver.dart` | `lang` becomes required |
| `lib/modules/global/commands/tui.dart` | the quickstart the banner teaches gains `--lang` |
| `assets/skills/macss-specification/SKILL.md` | the agent is told to stop passing `--lang`, and that declaring it is the human's call |
| `test/project_config_test.dart` | **new** — 9 cases |
| eleven other suites | rewritten to declare the language once instead of passing it |

**406 tests green, `dart analyze` clean.**

## Decisions taken during implementation

**One failure message, not three.** `undeclaredLanguageFailure` is stated once
in `project_config.dart` and asked for by every command that inherits, so they
cannot disagree about what "no declared language" means or about which command
resolves it. It is the same shape as `ambiguousRequisitionFailure` from #31.

**The set of commands taking `--lang` is asked of the CLI, not of the source.**
The new catalogue test parses `help --json` and pins the answer to exactly three
routes. A sixth command that gains the flag tomorrow fails the suite without
anybody remembering this rule existed. Reading the source would have tested the
code against itself.

**`TemplateResolver.resolve` lost its `lang = 'en'`.** Falling back to English
when a template is missing for a language is a stated resolution rule and it
carries a notice. A default parameter is the same fallback with the notice
removed, applied to callers who never asked. Every caller now knows its language
with certainty, so no caller needed the silence.

**The document still declares its own language.** `macss:lang=es` comes baked
into the localized template rather than being stamped after the fact: choosing
the template is producing the directive. It matters because the requisition
travels — it is sent as PDF or DOCX to somebody with no repository to consult.

**This repository adopted the canon in a commit of its own** (`7694a42`), which
is the migration this release forces on every existing project. The plan named
every file before anything was written. `.macss/` had to leave the root
`.gitignore` for `config.yaml` to be versionable at all: git does not descend
into an excluded directory, so the workspace's own allowlist was dead letter
while the root excluded it.

## What was not done

- **No comparison of a document's declared language against the project's.**
  Deliberately out of scope in the contract: if every command derives the value,
  the two cannot disagree except by hand-editing, and the gate would be
  answering a question nobody asked.
- **No migration of existing projects.** The CLI stops and names the command.
  Automatic adoption would take, on a user's behalf, exactly the decision this
  requisition exists to stop taking on their behalf.
- **The rest of the CLI's declared defaults are untouched** — `--engine`,
  `--source-root`, `--output`. ADR 0009 obliges each of them to justify itself
  or go, and that is a separate requirement.

## One thing the contract says that the build does not literally satisfy

US-4 AC3 reads: *"of the set of the CLI's commands, the ones that accept
declaring a language are **exactly one**, and it is this one."*

Three routes accept `--lang`: `project create`, `project adopt` and
`requisition export-template`. The reading under which the sentence holds — and
the one the catalogue test encodes — is that the first two **declare the
language for the project**, which is US-2's whole subject, while among the
commands that **write a document**, exactly one takes the flag.

Under the literal reading the criterion fails, and the two stories contradict
each other. This is raised rather than resolved: it is the contract's wording,
and the contract is yours.


---

# Verification

<!-- macss:lang=en · This document becomes the second half of the pull request body. -->

_Every acceptance criterion in `specification.md`, with the evidence that it holds. Written with the human, criterion by criterion, against the built binary rather than the test suite — the suite is evidence that the code does what it was told; this is evidence that what it was told was the agreement._

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Issue | [#24](https://github.com/ccisnedev/macss/issues/24) |
| Method | each criterion run against the compiled **0.7.0** binary in throwaway directories, command and output read together before moving to the next |
| Replicate | `dart compile exe bin/main.dart -o <dir>/macss.exe && cp -r assets <dir>/../assets`, then the commands below in an empty directory |
| Criteria | 17, all judged by the human |

---

## US-1 · The project declares its language once

**US1-AC1** — creating a project declaring its language writes it in a single
configuration file inside the local workspace.

```
$ macss project create --path=hu1 --lang es --apply --autoapprove
  ... 11 other files ...
  created  .macss/config.yaml (language: es)
```

"Single" is not a reading of the code: a sweep over **every file the command
wrote** looking for the language returned exactly one, `.macss/config.yaml`. ✅

**US1-AC2** — that file contains the language and nothing else.

```yaml

# with the repository rather than living on one machine.

```

author: logostona
body:
## 1 · The bar that didn't look scrollable

Health, People and Career have eleven, eighteen and eight tabs. None fits a phone row, so the row scrolled — **with no affordance at all**. It ended mid-word at the right edge, which reads as clipping rather than as an invitation.

One `SubtabBar` now serves all three:
- a **fade** and an **arrow** on the side that has more to reveal, and nothing on the side that doesn't
- the selected chip **scrolls itself into view**, so keyboard navigation never leaves the selection off-screen

Kept as one component rather than three copies deliberately — three bars that started identical would not have stayed identical, and this is exactly the detail that gets fixed in one of them.

## 2 · Career

Eight subtabs: **Job · Ladder · Education · Qualifications · Skills · Money · Side hustle · History**. Every existing card and button is preserved. The old panel was one long scroll that put a child's school report, a mid-career salary negotiation and a transition timeline in the same column.

Two things are new:

- **Qualifications** finally shows `s.edu.cred`, which EDU has recorded since it was built and nothing ever displayed. Labels are **derived from `EDU_STAGES`** rather than hand-written, so they can't drift when a stage is added — with two deliberate overrides, because `bachelor` and `associate` are named after the *institution* in that table and a degree is not the same noun as the place that granted it.
- **History** is new state, captured by **diffing** the job rather than by appending at the seven places that assign or clear `s.career.job`. An eighth write site is covered for free — which is precisely the failure mode the `flags.homeless` / `hreSetTenure` desync was.

```
Sales Associate  retail  age 22–25  120/mo
Shift Lead       retail  age 25–27  180/mo     ← promotion is its own row
Dev              tech    age 28–now 400/mo
years worked: 5.0                              ← the unemployed year excluded
```

## 3 · Keybindings

The game had **no keyboard handling of any kind**. Now: tabs, subtabs, time, Act, popup choices by number, Esc, and Alt/Ctrl combinations throughout — all rebindable from a settings screen reached by `Ctrl+,` or the ⌨ button.

**A binding is data, not a switch statement.** `KB_ACTIONS` rows carry a default chord, and `kbChord` builds the same string from an event that `kbResolve` matches — so what Settings captures is exactly what the handler later fires.

`1`–`9` are **bound twice on purpose**: a tab in game context, an option in popup context. That's safe because a popup is modal, and it's why `kbConflicts` compares *within* a context — comparing globally would report five conflicts on a default install.

Three guards, each for a real failure:
| guard | what it prevents |
|---|---|
| `kbIsTyping` | naming a character would advance time and switch tabs on every keystroke |
| `e.repeat` | holding Space would advance years at the OS key-repeat rate |
| scoped `preventDefault` | `Ctrl+L` and every other browser shortcut keeps working |

Subtab selection moved from inside each panel up into `Game`, because a global handler can't reach state held in a child — and as a side effect, switching tabs and back now returns you to the subtab you were on.

## Also fixed

- The college institution label dereferenced `COLLEGE_TIERS` unguarded, so a save carrying a tier this build doesn't know would take the whole screen down over a label.
- "Open Act" was filed under *Popups & choices* though it's neither, and "Settings" opened a screen that only does keyboard.

## Testing

`test-ui.js` is new: **99 assertions** over chord round-tripping (what `kbChord` produces is what `kbResolve` matches), context resolution, the typing guard, rebinding and reset, career history capture across all four transition kinds, and the credential labels.

`test-render.js` gained 11 more — all eight Career subtabs and the settings modal, against four fixtures (a child, a student, mid-career, retired).

Full suite **2013 assertions**, every suite at or above its previous count, green apart from `test-hre-s09`'s known stale fixture (8 failures, unchanged). Bundle rebuilt, `test-deploy` green, harness import clean, `sw.js` → `a-life-cache-v10`.

author: vinix24
body:
## Problem (measured on main `f58ede91`)

`vnx horizon reconcile` never finished: killed after 5 and 3 minutes with zero bytes of output. Cause, measured by sampling the process: step 2b's dispatch-outcome sweep (`objective_reconcile.py` → `reconcile_all_dispatch_outcomes`) called `_origin_branch_has_commits` per dispatch-id, and each call spawned its own `git ls-remote origin dispatch/<id>` — one network round-trip (~0.53s measured), strictly sequential, `timeout=10` each, no batching, no cache. With **5571 distinct dispatch-ids** in `dispatch_outcomes`, that is 30–50 minutes of network calls in front of the nomination/close pipeline the run exists for — by a sweep explicitly marked best-effort/never-blocking.

## Fix

- **One batched call per run**: `_fetch_remote_dispatch_branches()` runs `git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/dispatch/*'` once (~0.4s measured on this repo — all 64 dispatch branches) and `_origin_branch_has_commits` becomes a set-membership test. 5571 network calls → 1.
- **Run-scoped, not module-global**: the batch is fetched once in `reconcile_all_dispatch_outcomes` and threaded down through `load_evidence` as a parameter. A module-global set would leak between runs and tests, and a long-lived process would miss branches created after process start; a parameter makes the cache lifetime exactly the run.
- **Fail-safe direction kept, made explicit**: a FAILED batch returns `None` (distinct from a successful EMPTY frozenset — two states that would otherwise both look like an empty set), logs a warning, and yields False for every dispatch-id: a salvage check that can't run never claims salvage exists.
- **`--max-gh-calls` honesty**: chose to fix the help text rather than widen the flag. After batching there is exactly one ls-remote per run, so there is nothing left to cap; the flag's counting contract is covered by existing tests (OI-1064) and widening it would change a tested semantic for zero bounding value. Help text (both `vnx_cli/main.py` and `scripts/planning_cli.py`) now states it bounds ONLY live `gh pr view` calls.

author: atqamz
body:
## Summary

This refactors `universe` around explicit ownership, host capabilities, deterministic runtime policy, and observable failure handling.

The goal is not primarily to reorganize files, but to make architectural invariants enforceable in code:

* full and `-minimal` hosts now have genuinely separate composition
* shared modules depend on host capabilities instead of hostname checks
* SFX14 power modes define complete, deterministic states
* automation failures surface through systemd instead of being silently swallowed
* Zen profile sync has a single writer with an observable push path
* runtime health checks are derived from configuration through `doctor`
* editor, browser, and AI tooling ownership is separated from the generic package inventory
* Nix-owned tools no longer leak self-update or compatibility behavior globally
* pavg15 GitHub runners no longer share the host's rootful container socket
* architecture documentation and ADRs now describe durable invariants rather than stale implementation details

## Host composition

Split host configuration into minimal-safe base configuration and full-host additions.

`-minimal` variants now contain only what is required to boot and bootstrap. Full-only services such as the pavg15 GitHub runner and SFX14 power/video policy are no longer pulled into installer-time configurations.

Host-specific behavior is expressed through capabilities and roles rather than using hostnames as hidden feature flags.

## SFX14 power

Moved SFX14 power policy into a dedicated host module.

The three power modes are now intended as canonical states:

* `low` — 15 W
* `normal` — 20 W
* `high` — 25 W

Each mode owns its CPU power, EPP, power-profile, and related state instead of relying on whichever mode happened to run previously.

GPU tuning is separated from CPU power-mode semantics so `high` does not implicitly mean a gaming-specific GPU policy.

## Automation and observability

Tightened the user-timer contract so expected skips remain successful while real self-heal failures propagate as failures.

This includes repo sync, RTK, codedb, GPG preset, access-token refresh, and related maintenance tasks.

Repo sync no longer collapses pull/auth/network failures into success, and vault import only runs after a successful pull.

## Zen profile sync

Reworked Zen profile synchronization around an explicit single-writer model.

On the writer host:

* the close watcher only detects the Zen running → stopped transition
* a dedicated `zen-profile-push.service` performs the snapshot
* systemd owns retry and failure visibility
* failed pushes can trigger the shared failure notification path

Sync semantics also handle deletion of managed profile files rather than only overlaying files that still exist.

## Doctor

Added `nix run .#doctor` as the canonical runtime health check.

Expected timers and persistent services are derived from evaluated configuration instead of duplicated in a manually maintained list.

The doctor checks system access, repositories, generated user units, host-specific services, writable agent-config links, Zen writer requirements, and failed system/user units.

`bootstrap-check` remains available as a compatibility alias.

## Tooling ownership

Split behavior-heavy tooling out of `packages.nix`:

* Zed and its language servers
* browser configuration
* AI tooling

Removed the global Bun-backed `node` / `npx` shims and scoped that compatibility environment to Claude only.

Standardized on `nixd` for Nix language-server support.

Returned OpenCode to Nix-owned update behavior instead of allowing the installed package to self-update independently of the flake.

Moved direnv configuration to the native Home Manager module with `nix-direnv`.

## Agent config

Restored direct writable linking for configuration that tools modify atomically, avoiding a `/nix/store` intermediary for writable runtime config.

This preserves live-editability while keeping ownership explicit.

## pavg15 runner isolation

Reworked the pavg15 self-hosted GitHub runner boundary.

Runner instances now use separate runner users and rootless Podman state instead of sharing the host's rootful Docker-compatible socket.

GitHub App credentials remain separated from runner workloads, while runners consume short-lived registration credentials.

This reduces the authority available to workflow jobs if a runner workload is compromised.

## CI and scripts

* add descriptions for flake apps
* include app derivations in checks so their shell applications are actually built
* declare missing runtime dependencies for shell applications
* check package updates after rebasing onto the latest `main`, so the tested tree is the tree that gets pushed
* make the Termux managed SSH-key block converge instead of only appending keys

## Documentation

Updated `AGENTS.md`, the install runbooks, and ADRs to describe the new invariants:

* minimal/full host boundaries
* host capabilities and roles
* update ownership
* automation failure semantics
* single-writer mutable state
* runtime health checks

Implementation details remain in code where possible so documentation does not become a second source of truth.

## Validation

Run on the refactor branch:

```bash
nix fmt
nix flake check
git diff --check
```

After switching the configuration, runtime validation should include:

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .
nix run .#doctor
systemctl --failed
systemctl --user --failed
```

SFX14 should additionally verify all three power states and the Zen push path.

pavg15 should verify representative self-hosted GitHub Actions workloads against the new rootless runner boundary.

body:
The duplication test asserts the same fact twice: a copy records its source's version **at copy time**, and that record **stays put** when the source later advances. Bray moved to v6 with [#187](https://github.com/michaeljosiah/ArkeStudio/pull/187); the first assertion was updated, the second was not.

Easy to miss — it sits ten lines below its twin, past an intervening `commit()`, and the first one going green made the pair look finished.

Same second-order cost as [#192](https://github.com/michaeljosiah/ArkeStudio/pull/192): the throw lands before `await store.close()`, the WorldStore's handle stays open, and the process cannot exit. With #192 fixed this file was the *sole* remaining reason a full coordinator run never terminated.

before:  12 tests, 11 pass, 1 fail,  duration_ms 150036  (killed at timeout)
after:   12 tests, 12 pass, 0 fail,  duration_ms 10931

author: guangyu-reflexio
body:
Follow-up to #426. The test it added broke enterprise CI (`os-unit-tests`), which surfaced on the enterprise submodule bump.

## What went wrong

`test_reviewer_manifest_regression.py` carried only `pytest.mark.requires_credentials`. That marker **deselects nothing** — the unit jobs filter on:

```
pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e_tests/ -m "not integration"
```

So all 12 cases ran, hit the **global litellm mock**, and got a profile-shaped payload back:

```
schema=PlaybookCandidateReviewOutput
errors=id: missing,decision: missing,reason_code: missing,profiles: extra_forbidden
-> StructuredOutputRepairError: Structured output repair exhausted
```

12 failures that read as a reviewer regression and were not one. My mistake in #426: I verified "deselected by default" against the OSS default `addopts` and never against the job command that actually runs it.

## Fix

Adopts the pattern already used by `tests/server/llm/test_litellm_client.py`:

- adds `pytest.mark.integration` — the marker that actually gates live-provider tests
- adds a `real_provider_key` skipif, rather than `os.getenv`, because the credential floor pins a placeholder key when none is set. `real_provider_key`'s own docstring warns about exactly this: a `requires_credentials` test that would skip cleanly on a bare machine instead runs "against a credential that authenticates with nothing."

## Verification

Reproduced CI's exact command locally rather than the file in isolation:

```
pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e_tests/ -m "not integration"
-> 4252 passed, 3 skipped, 1304 deselected
```

The 12 cases are among the deselected. ruff check + format clean.

author: dk-blackfuel
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint (OpenAI/vLLM backends) reporting `stop_reason: "end_turn"` on tool calls, which blocks all Anthropic-SDK agentic clients (Claude Code, Cowork) from running their tool loop.

- **Infer `tool_use` when the backend omits `finish_reason`.** If a tool-call stream carries no `finish_reason` chunk (observed in production: forced `tool_choice` against vLLM), the closing `message_delta` fell back to a hardcoded `end_turn`. The closing stop reason is now inferred from the emitted content — `tool_use` when `tool_use` blocks were streamed. Applied to both streaming and non-streaming translation. Explicit `finish_reason` keeps precedence (e.g. `length` mid-tool-call still reports `max_tokens`).
- **Implement `stop_sequence` mapping.** `finish_reason: "stop"` + a provably-matched request stop sequence now maps to `stop_reason: "stop_sequence"` with the matched string populated in `stop_sequence`. Detection uses the backend's raw stop signal — vLLM's `stop_reason` vendor field on response choices (new optional schema field, following the `ReasoningContent` precedent) — with a generated-text suffix fallback for backends that leave the matched sequence in the output. Non-matching cases stay `end_turn` with `stop_sequence: null`.
- Both behaviors share one resolver (`resolveAnthropicStopReason`) used by the streaming and non-streaming paths.

Full mapping now matches the Anthropic spec: `tool_calls → tool_use`, `length → max_tokens`, natural `stop → end_turn`, stop-sequence `stop → stop_sequence`, `content_filter → refusal`.

Refs: BLA-3506

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (`go test ./internal/...`) — new regression tests reproduce the issue's streaming trace (tool-call stream with no `finish_reason` chunk → `tool_use`), plus `length → max_tokens` and three `stop_sequence` scenarios (vendor-field match, text-suffix match, negative cases), streaming and non-streaming
- [x] Format/lint/vet clean (`gofmt`, `golangci-lint` 0 issues on changed packages, `go vet ./...`)
- [ ] Post-deploy: issue's curl repro returns `stop_reason: "tool_use"`; Claude Code completes a multi-step tool loop against the endpoint

## The five-step trail

| Step | Artifact | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Spec | IXBRL_SPEC v1, independent hostile sign-off | **4 rounds: REFUSED×3 → GRANTED** (13 blockers — incl. a transform table both real samples contradicted, an order-dependent dedup $38m wrong on real Apple, dimensional leakage, a JS `0 != null` fabricated-URL path) + r5/r6 clarifications |

| 3 · Parser | `lib/edgar/ixbrl.ts` held to the same gospel | **TS ≡ reference on all 4 fixtures**; orchestration pins (restamp, default-sparing, URL/CIK honesty, rejections) |
| 4 · UI | Upload card live on SourceScreen; **no store diff** (screen → parser → existing `loadFromHistoricals`) | display gates green |
| 5 · Conformance | Independent adversarial review: code-vs-spec + diff proof + tier sign-off | **1 BLOCKING found (typed members — both implementations + both adjudication passes had missed it) → fixed both sides + pinned + re-adjudicated → CONFORMANT** |

## Fixtures are REAL documents
- **Apple FY2024 10-K** (trimmed to the mapper read-set + the UnrecognizedTaxBenefits note): pins the real duplicate-key case — **$22,038m (dec −6) beats $22.0bn (dec −8)** under the decimals-aware order-independent dedup.

author: robertnowell
body:
## Why the same layer keeps producing bugs

All three bugs this week were in `Sources/TranquilityApp/`. That isn't coincidence — it's the mechanism:

```swift
.testTarget(name: "TranquilityCoreTests", dependencies: ["TranquilityCore"])
```

The executable target can't be imported by a test. So when the capture states were given stage ownership, there was nowhere to record the invariant, and `AudioInputDevice` shipped last week with no tests at all for the same reason.

`PanelState` and `AudioInputDevice` move to Core. Neither imports AppKit — both were pure logic sitting in the UI target — and Core already hosts exactly this (`ReplyGestureMachine`, `InterruptGate`, `SessionActivity`). Git recorded both as renames, so history survives. **14 tests follow them.**

## A correction, found by writing those tests

The reported Bug 1 was *"an ambient repaint stomps a live announcement,"* evidenced by `speaking -> idle (idle repaint)` in app.log.

**The ambient path cannot reach a card state.** Its caller checks `canSurfaceAmbiently` → `allowsAmbientSurface` → `.hidden`/`.idle` only. It is already guarded, and has been.

What misled the diagnosis is that `showIdle` hardcoded the reason `"idle repaint"` for **all twenty-five callers**, so a deliberate return-to-grid and the five-second tick were indistinguishable in the log. The instrument was the defect.

So `.speaking` is **not** added to the refusing set — that would break return-to-grid, which is the deliberate path through the same function. Instead `showIdleGrid` derives its reason from `#function`/`#line`:

```swift
private func showIdleGrid(note: String? = nil,
                          caller: String = #function, line: Int = #line)
```

All twenty-five callers get real provenance; none has to remember a string. `testAmbientSurfaceIsRefusedByEveryStateThatOwnsTheScreen` pins the guard that actually does the work.

## Bug 2 is real, and fixed

`onWillSpeak` returned `Void`, so a refusal was invisible to `Coordinator.speak` and the announcement spoke anyway — into an open microphone, then advanced the heard cursor because the audio had "completed":

```
23:03:48  arming -> listening
23:03:48  REFUSED listening -> speaking  (audio starting)
   …      21 highlight callbacks over ~10 seconds
23:03:58  queue: cursor e1db64a1 heard=275
```

It returns `Bool` now, and `false` is treated exactly like an interruption: the summary goes back to `prepared`, the cursor doesn't move, the session stays waiting — because it is.

## Found while making that change

`showAnnouncement` assigned `currentTarget` **before** the guard, so a refused announcement still repointed the reply target — the routing that decides which terminal your next dictation is typed into. A refusal that paints nothing but silently moves the reply target is worse than one that paints. Moved below the guard.

## Tests

**213 green, up from 198.** The new ones pin rules someone paid for once: capture states refusing stale repaints, arming only upgrading to listening, replying-during-playback staying legal, card-vs-capture never overlapping, and the preference falling back to built-in when a stored value doesn't parse.

author: mmurakaru
body:
Closes the pi adapter slice of map issue #13.

## What

- `packages/adapters/pi/index.ts` - a pi extension factory (`createCueloopExtension(options)` plus a default export). pi's real ExtensionAPI arrives at the factory; the surface we use is typed structurally in `packages/adapters/pi/pi-types.ts` (registerTool, registerCommand, on("tool_call"), ctx.ui.notify), so pi is an integration target, not a dependency.
- `request_review` tool: creates a cueloop session through `@cueloop/daemon` DaemonClient with autostart, then long-polls `sessionWait` in chunks. Between chunks it re-reads the session and streams the annotation count through `onUpdate`. The abort signal cancels the poll and returns a clean cancelled error result; the session stays collectable. Verdict mapping: approve -> normal tool result with the feedback text; comment/request_changes -> `isError: true` carrying feedback.md.
- `tool_call` gate: while a session opened by this extension is pending, every tool outside a conservative read-only allowlist (read, grep, find, ls) is blocked with `{ block: true, reason: "cueloop review pending ..." }`. The gate releases when the review resolves or the call is cancelled.
- `review` command: reports the current session status (pending + annotation count, or the verdict) via `ctx.ui.notify` when available.
- `tsconfig.json` include widened to `packages/adapters/**/*.ts` so adapter code is typechecked (it lived outside `packages/*/src` and was not covered before).
- `@cueloop/adapters` gains a `./pi` export.

## Tests

`packages/adapters/pi/pi-adapter.test.ts` runs the factory against a fake pi API that captures registrations and drives `execute` against a real daemon in a temp `CUELOOP_HOME` (same pattern as `test/session/e2e.test.tsx`):

- approve -> non-error result containing the feedback document
- request_changes -> `isError: true` with feedback.md including the annotation; `onUpdate` reported the annotation count
- AbortController abort -> cancelled error result, gate released, session still resolvable
- gate blocks edit/write/bash/custom tools while pending, passes read-only tools, releases after resolve
- `/review` notifies pending and resolved status

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` - 0 errors
- `bun test ./packages ./test` - 98 pass, 0 fail

author: malkreide
body:
Ein Portfolio-Durchlauf des Audit-Katalogs am 2026-08-07 las alle 43 Server gegen [`ARCH-014`](https://github.com/malkreide/mcp-audit-skill/blob/main/checks/ARCH-014.md). Dieser Server fiel auf **jedem** Punkt durch, den der Check stellt.

## Was da war

```python
CONNECT_RETRIES = 2
RETRY_STATUS_CODES = frozenset({502, 503, 504})
RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 1.0

async def http_get(url, params=None):
    response = await client.get(url, params=params)
    if response.status_code in RETRY_STATUS_CODES:
        await asyncio.sleep(RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS)
        response = await client.get(url, params=params)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response
```

Dazu der geteilte Client mit `transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=CONNECT_RETRIES)`.

## Was sich ändert

| Eigenschaft | Vorher | Jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| **was** wiederholt wird | nur 502/503/504; ein 500 galt als deterministische Antwort | 5xx, 429, Timeouts, Verbindungsfehler; 4xx ausser 429 bricht sofort ab |
| **wie schnell** | feste 1.0 s, keine Streuung | exponentiell 2/4/8 s, gejittert in `[0.5x, 1.5x]` |
| `Retry-After` | nicht gelesen | gelesen (beide RFC-9110-Formen), schlägt die eigene Kurve |
| Deckel | keiner | `MAX_DELAY_SECONDS`, **nach** dem Jitter angewandt |
| **wie lange** | eine Wiederholung; keinerlei Zeitgrenze | 25 s Wanduhr-Budget an `asyncio.timeout` |
| Ebenen, die wiederholen | **zwei** — diese Schleife *und* der Transport | genau eine |

Drei davon verdienen Worte.

### Die Stapelung war unsichtbar

`AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=2)` unter einer Schleife von 2 sind **3 × 2 Versuche, nicht 3 + 2** — und keine der beiden Zahlen stand irgendwo im Code. Der Docstring nannte die Transport-Retries sogar als Feature («connect failures are retried at the transport layer»), ohne zu bemerken, dass darüber noch eine Schleife läuft.

Der Transport steht jetzt auf `retries=0`, und ein Test hält das fest: Der Wert ist eine Änderung davon entfernt zurückzukommen, und sonst würde es nichts merken.

*(Nebenbei: Mein erster, mechanischer Scan hat diese Stapelung **nicht** gefunden — mein Muster suchte `retries=<Ziffer>`, hier steht eine benannte Konstante. Gefunden hat sie das Lesen von Hand, das `ARCH-014` in Modus 1 ausdrücklich verlangt.)*

### Eine feste Wartezeit von 1,0 s ist ein Retry-Sturm

Jeder Client, der denselben Ausfall trifft, kommt im selben Moment zurück — die Last kehrt als Welle wieder, genau wenn sich die Quelle erholt. Das ist der Ausfall, den der Retry überbrücken sollte, verlängert durch den Retry.

### `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` war nie ein Budget

httpx begrenzt **pro Operation**, und sein Read-Timeout beginnt mit jedem Chunk von vorn: Eine langsam tröpfelnde Antwort überdauert jedes Budget, ohne dass ein einzelner Read abläuft. Die 25 s hängen jetzt an `asyncio.timeout` und liegen **unter** dem 30-s-Default des MCP-SDK — der Server hört auf zu arbeiten, bevor der Aufrufer aufhört zuzuhören.

## Verhaltensänderung, die auffallen wird

**Ein einfacher 500 wird jetzt wiederholt.** Der alte Docstring nannte ihn eine deterministische Antwort; `ARCH-014` behandelt alle 5xx als wiederholbar, und ein 500 von einem Gateway unter Last ist genau der transiente Fall. Zwei Tests in `test_http_client.py`, die «genau eine Wiederholung» festhielten, sind entsprechend ersetzt — sie kodierten die alte Politik.

## Herkunft

Die Politik ist aus der Vorlage `reference/retry_backoff.py` des [`mcp-data-source-probe`](https://github.com/malkreide/mcp-data-source-probe-skill)-Skills übernommen (kopiert, nicht importiert — so will es die Vorlage) und liegt in einem neuen Modul `retry.py`. Sie wirft die ursprüngliche Upstream-Exception **unverpackt**; der einzige Fall ohne Exception zum Weiterwerfen — Budget schon vor dem ersten Request verbraucht — bekommt einen eigenen `UpstreamUnavailableError` statt eines nackten `RuntimeError`.

## Gegenprobe

Nach `OPS-010` geführt, nicht behauptet. Jede Eigenschaft einzeln gebrochen:

| Mutation | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| Jitter entfernt | 2 Tests fallen |
| `Retry-After` nicht mehr gelesen | 1 Test fällt |
| Wanduhr-Deadline entfernt | 1 Test fällt (`DID NOT RAISE TimeoutError`) |
| Deckel vor den Jitter gezogen | 1 Test fällt |
| Transport-Retries zurück auf 2 | 1 Test fällt |
| conftest patcht wieder `retry.asyncio` global | **2** Tests fallen |

Die letzte Zeile ist die interessante. `monkeypatch.setattr(retry.asyncio, "sleep", …)` sieht lokal aus und trifft das stdlib-Modul prozessweit. Die Suite lief unter dieser Mutation **33 Sekunden statt 0,5** und zwei Tests brachen ein — darunter der Wanduhr-Test, der danach nichts mehr misst. Die Fixture patcht deshalb `retry._sleep`, und `test_the_no_backoff_fixture_leaves_the_global_asyncio_sleep_alone` bewacht die Naht.

## Gates

```
ruff check .                    All checks passed
ruff format --check .           42 files already formatted
mypy src/                       Success: no issues found in 23 source files
pytest tests/                   244 passed
coverage                        100.00%  (Gate: --cov-fail-under=100)
```

Die Invarianten aus `CLAUDE.md` — Coverage bleibt bei 100 %, mypy ohne Ausnahmen — sind gehalten. `retry.py` und `http_client.py` stehen beide bei 100 % Zeilenabdeckung; der einzige Zweig, den ich anfangs mit `# pragma: no cover` versteckt hatte, hat jetzt stattdessen einen Test.

## Einordnung

Einer von sechs Servern aus demselben Durchlauf. Die anderen fünf: `amtsblatt-mcp`, `bag-health-mcp`, `openlex-mcp`, `swiss-environment-mcp`, `swiss-statistics-mcp` — je ein eigener PR.

author: andreykizimenko
body:
`withStaticUser` restored a cached session, navigated to `/dashboard`, and treated "URL isn't `/login`" as proof the session was live:

```ts
await page.goto('/dashboard');
if (!/\/login/.test(page.url())) return await fn(page);
```

`goto` resolves before Fleet's client-side auth check runs (`GET /me` → 401 → redirect), so an expired session **still reads as `/dashboard`** at that instant. The helper skipped its own fallback-to-fresh-login path and handed the test a page that signed itself out mid-flow. Every static-user spec then failed on the login screen — **24 premium + 8 free** in a local full-suite run, all with plausible-looking product symptoms. The fallback code was correct; it just never fired.

## Why CI never caught this

- `.auth/` is gitignored and no workflow restores it, so a runner starts with no cache, logs in for real, and only ever reuses sessions minutes old. A stale cache can only exist *across* runs — and CI has none.
- Nightly premium runs were green Aug 4–7, consistent with that.
- The admin storage state doesn't rot either: the setup projects are project dependencies and rewrite it every run. Static-user sessions had no equivalent refresh, no TTL and no timestamp — that asymmetry is the whole bug.

It therefore only bites **local** runs whose cache has outlived Fleet's server-side session, where it presents as ~32 failures that look like a product regression.

## The fix

Liveness is settled by asking the API instead of reading a URL, which also removes the race for valid sessions. Note Fleet **rejects the session cookie on its own (401)** and authenticates the same value as a bearer token, so the token is read out of the cookie and sent as a header — a cookie-only probe fails even for a live session and would silently force a fresh login every time (which would also burn Fleet's shared 10/min `POST /login` budget).

## Verification

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Dead sessions planted in the cache | 7 passed — fell through to fresh login |
| Live sessions in the cache | 7 passed, session files **not rewritten** → cache genuinely reused |
| `GET /me` with cookie only | 401 (why the first attempt was wrong) |
| `GET /me` with cookie value as bearer | 200 |

Full suites with both this and the `pageHealth` change applied: **free 172/172**, premium clean apart from one pre-existing `library.spec.ts` Windows custom-package `waitForURL` flake that reproduces identically on `main` (verified by running the same specs on both branches back to back). Wall-clock timings were *not* used as evidence — a cache-hit run looked no faster than a fresh-login run because cost is dominated by cold SPA loads; the session-file mtime is the reliable signal.

author: kferrone
body:
Two feature files went away, for one reason: **neither described anything a person does.** One described a construct, the other a mechanism. Every scenario in them was really the end state of some behaviour that already had a home, or a behaviour that deserved its own.

Two commits, reviewable separately.

---

## 1. `file-type.feature` — a construct

"Grafana dashboard is a first-class file type" was about a mimetype, a property set and an index. Nobody registers a mimetype; they install an app. Nobody sets metadata; they make a dashboard and the app stamps it.

| it described | whose end state it is | where it went |
|---|---|---|
| the mimetype is registered | **enabling the app** | `lifecycle.feature` |
| a file carries this metadata | **creating** or **syncing** a dashboard | asserted by those, shown when looking |
| the mode property's wire value | what the metadata says | the DAV view outline |
| the metadata cannot be edited | a refusal anyone can provoke | stayed, as a scenario |

What remains is the only part anyone performs: **looking at the thing** — `view-dashboard.feature`.

### Two corrections that fell out

- **The old PROPFIND table asserted values the app never sets.** It listed `grafana_folderUid` and `grafana_apiVersion`. Both are *registered* in `DashboardMetadata` but written by nothing — banked for the subfolder and YAML courses. The table is now the five keys `stampSynced` actually writes.
- **The mode outline had four rows where a mapping only ever produces two.** `unmapped` and `ignored` are what a file *becomes* — moved out, or hand-tagged `grafana:ignore` — so neither is reachable from a mapping form. Their modes are asserted in `move-dashboard.feature` and `reserved-tags.feature`.

### One live assertion added

`lifecycle.feature`'s "Enabling the app" now ends with `And ".grafana.json" files are registered as their own file type`, backed by a real step: it uploads a plain file this app has never touched and checks it comes back typed as the app's own mimetype. That is what registration *means*, and the only part of it a client can observe. Needed a `davContentType()` helper in `WebDavTrait` — this repo had no way to read `getcontenttype`, because the scenarios that would have needed one were all `@todo`.

---

## 2. `reconcile.feature` — a mechanism

Named after the thing that carries a Grafana-side change into Nextcloud. **Nobody reconciles.** The app does, on a timer, and that is an implementation detail. Its six scenarios were four behaviours wearing one coat:

| it said | it meant | where it went |
|---|---|---|
| the button pulls the folder's dashboards in | the FIRST sync | `sync-now.feature` |
| a second sync updates in place | a sync over a folder that already holds mirrors | `sync-now.feature`, renamed |
| …and prunes a file whose dashboard left the folder | a dashboard deleted **in Grafana** | `delete-dashboard.feature` |
| a run that changed nothing rewrote nothing | an mtime, and the reconciler | **deleted** — see below |
| the button pushes a local edit up | **editing** a dashboard file | `edit-dashboard.feature` |
| a root mapping mirrors the whole instance | the first sync of a root mapping | `sync-now.feature` |

Each now reads as pre-state → action → end state, without naming the reconciler.

### The two judgment calls, both reversing decisions this repo had recorded

**The prune moves to `delete-dashboard.feature`.** The old notes argued it should stay: *"this app has no delete-dashboard reconcile path, so a dashboard vanishing from a Grafana folder is only ever noticed BY a sync."* True, and not the point — being the only mechanism that notices a change does not make the mechanism the subject. `delete-dashboard.feature` already had an *"everything above starts in Nextcloud; these start in Grafana"* section waiting for exactly this shape.

**"A run that changed nothing rewrote nothing" is deleted, not moved.** ⚠️ The one live scenario that goes away without a new home. It asserted an mtime — a result — about the reconciler — a mechanism. The old notes argued to keep it as a regression guard, and the defect was real: a pull that rewrote every mirror on every run left the whole folder reading *"Modified a few seconds ago"*, so a file you had actually touched was impossible to spot. All three step definitions stay in `SyncSteps.php` with a docblock recording what they guarded, so re-adding it is one line. **Say the word if you'd rather it kept a home.**

---

## Both retirements are now a written rule

`features/README.md`'s organising rule states it outright — *a mechanism is not a verb, so it never gets a file* — and cites both as the worked examples, so the next file named after a subsystem or a construct gets caught in review.

Same shape n8n took (`view-workflow.feature`, `sync-now.feature`, `edit-workflow.feature`, no `reconcile.feature`, no `file-type.feature`), ported here.

## Checks

- `check-suites.sh` — ok, 25 feature files, each in exactly one suite
- `check-step-definitions.sh` — ok, 148 patterns, no duplicates, every runnable step defined
- Full CI green on the first commit (all three integration legs included), including the new live mimetype assertion
- Swept every stale pointer: README ×3, `features/README.md`, `move-dashboard.feature`, `SetupTrait.php`, `SyncServiceTest.php`, `WebDavTrait.php`, and four in `features/AGENTS.md`

## Testing

No app code changed — spec and test-harness only. Every relocated scenario keeps its steps verbatim, so the same assertions run in their new files. Net live coverage: +1 (the mimetype), −1 (the unchanged-run guard).

author: mehdilaruelle
body:
The bug in your screenshot. Both sites, live.

```
© 2026 • Jane Doe • This work is licensed under a Creative Commons
Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License. • Powered by Hugo …
```

That is a **regression I introduced in #46**. The short copyright lived in the
exampleSite's `[languages]` block, per language. Removing that block left the
root value — the long sentence — as what the footer falls back to.

## And a second one underneath it

`.Site.Copyright` feeds two places with different escaping rules:

| | how it is rendered |
| --- | --- |
| footer | `safeHTML` — markup renders |
| feed `<copyright>` | XML text — markup is escaped |

So the CC link that read correctly in the footer had been arriving in the feed
as escaped markup for as long as it existed. Built from `master` at the commit
before #46:

```xml
<copyright><a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/" …>CC BY-NC 4.0</a></copyright>
```

`plainify` on the feed side settles both: markup is allowed in the setting, the
footer renders it, the feed takes its text.

## After

| | |

body:
## Summary
First slice of P2.5 (inserted into the roadmap after P2's close — real ratings/reviews were never
in the original P0–P8 plan, surfaced by comparing the live site against the project's own AI
Studio design mockup).

- **Prisma**: `Review` (one per user per product via `@@unique([userId, productId])` —
  resubmitting updates rather than duplicates; cascade-deletes with the user). `Product` gains
  denormalized `averageRating`/`reviewCount`, recomputed from a full aggregate (not incremental)
  inside the same transaction as every review write.
- `lib/repositories/reviews.ts` — `upsert`/`delete` (atomic ownership check via
  `deleteMany({ id, userId })`, not read-then-check), `listByProduct`, `getByUserAndProduct`.
- `features/reviews/` — **first real use of `features/` since auth**, for the same reason: a
  genuine session-gated write use-case, unlike P2's read-only browsing. Two Server Actions behind
  a plain `<form>`, no client component, same progressive-enhancement pattern as P2's GET forms.
- `app/(storefront)/products/[slug]` extended with the review list, submission form for logged-in
  visitors, login prompt (not a redirect) for guests.

Closes #39

## Bug found and fixed while validating
Registered a real test account, verified its email directly via the DB (Resend is configured for
real sending, so a fake test address couldn't receive a real verification link), and walked
through submit → update → delete with an actual authenticated session. Found: the rating
`<select>`'s `defaultValue` silently kept showing its *old* value after a Server Action's
`revalidatePath` refresh — React only applies `defaultValue` at mount, and the DOM node wasn't
remounting since nothing keyed it to the review's identity. Fixed by keying the form.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run` — all green (32/32 tests incl. 4 new)
- [x] `npm run build` — `/products/[slug]` confirmed dynamic, not statically optimized
- [x] `npm run preview` with a real authenticated session: submit → aggregate recomputes correctly
      (`averageRating`/`reviewCount` verified against the DB) → resubmit updates in place (same
      row, not a duplicate) → delete removes it and resets the aggregate
- [x] Verified the ownership check directly: deleting with a mismatched `userId` is a no-op
      (count: 0), the review survives
- [x] Verified guest access: `/products/[slug]` shows a login prompt, not the form, when logged out
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated per Gate 4

author: tinglvv
body:
get_package_source_url() routed any package whose name starts with "nvidia-" or "cuda-" to pypi.nvidia.com. A handful of NVIDIA-named packages are not published there -- cuda-bindings, cuda-pathfinder, cuda-python and nvidia-ml-py live on PyPI proper -- so fetching their simple index 404s. The failure is quiet: upload_package_using_simple_index() catches the fetch error and returns, leaving the mirrored index frozen at whatever was last seeded.

The prefix predicate carries two meanings that had to be separated before the exception could be expressed. is_nvidia_package() also gates which packages are initialized for CUDA targets only (get_packages_for_target), so excluding these four inside it would have leaked them into cpu and rocm targets. It keeps the plain prefix heuristic; the new uses_nvidia_index() layers the exception on top and is what the URL builder and the "NVIDIA"/"PyPI" source label now consult, so the printed label always matches the index actually fetched.

Test Plan:

The four listed packages resolve to pypi.org/simple/, nvidia-cublas-cu12 and cuda-runtime-cu13 still resolve to pypi.nvidia.com, numpy to pypi.org and pytorch-triton-rocm to repo.amd.com. is_nvidia_package() returns True for all six NVIDIA names, confirming the CUDA-target gate is unchanged.

cc @atalman

## Summary

Mobile/Android WebView reliability fixes and YouTube-style media player polish, built on top of the earlier YouTube-style player + playlist navigation work.

- **Parent Login mobile fixes**: switched the login screen from `min-h-screen` (100vh) to `min-h-dvh` with safe-area-aware top/bottom padding, so the card no longer sits under a notch/home indicator and resizes correctly when the on-screen keyboard opens.

author: icdev-ai
body:
Follow-up to #1311 (same task, obs-cov-05).

#1311 routed all six writers of `kanban_status_transitions` through
`resolve_transition_reason` — but only under the root `tools/` namespace. Two
writers in `icdev/tools/` were left on the old code, and #1311's own structural
guard could not see them: `_writers_on_disk()` scanned `REPO_ROOT/tools` alone,
so the inventory test passed while naming six of the twelve writers that exist.

That is not cosmetic mirror drift. CLAUDE.md makes `icdev.tools.*` the canonical
import namespace, `tools.X` and `icdev.tools.X` are separate module objects in a
checkout, and a wheel ships only the `icdev/` copy. So every blank row this task
set out to remove was still reachable through the canonical namespace with the
entire root-namespace suite green — the same "fixed the call sites, missed the
boundary" shape as #1183, one namespace over.

## Fixed

- `icdev/tools/genesis/reflexes/kanban.py::_record_status_transition` — passed
  `reason` straight into the INSERT. Now resolves it, with `skip_frames=1` so the
  synthesized text names `_move_task` and its caller rather than the writer.
  Imported inside the function, not at module scope: this mirror is already
  divergent from the root copy and a top-level import would widen that diff.
- `icdev/tools/ci/pr_watcher.py::_set_task_status` — same, and `reason[:200]` on
  the way in would also have raised on `None`.

## The guard that missed them

`_writers_on_disk()` now scans both namespaces and the inventory is 12, so a
seventh writer — or a thirteenth — fails the test in whichever namespace it
lands. Two functional tests exercise the mirror's real INSERT through the storage
layer, because a grep assertion proves an import exists, not that it fires.

## Verification

Mutation-tested against the restored pre-fix files:

- reverting `icdev/.../ci/pr_watcher.py` → 1 failure
- reverting `icdev/.../genesis/reflexes/kanban.py` → 2 failures, and the
  behavioural one fails as `assert (None)` — the mirror was writing a literal
  NULL reason, not a short one.

29 tests in the file (was 27), 355 in `tests/kanban`, fast-tier coherence gate
clean (exit 0; only pre-existing warns).

Live board, `in_progress -> backlog` discards per day — the task's own metric:

| day | discards | blank |
|---|---|---|
| 08-01 | 76 | 53 |
| 08-02 | 146 | 103 |
| 08-03 | 134 | 95 |
| 08-06 | 33 | 0 |
| 08-07 | 133 | 0 |

Two full scheduler days at zero. Blanks remaining on *other* status pairs come
from a scheduler process started 18:15Z, before #1311 merged at 19:09Z, so it
still holds pre-fix code in memory; those clear on its next restart.

body:
## Why every merge is blocked

The merge queue's **Queue Validation → Web Full (Next.js)** re-runs the full vitest suite, which is red on main itself (59 failures in CI, run 31208147239) since the one-location-circles merge (PR #4660). Every queued PR fails validation on main's own breakage — the queue is wedged repo-wide.

## What the diagnosis found

A parallel 7-agent root-cause pass over all 12 failing files: **zero user-facing bugs shipped.** Every component matches its intended, documented contract; the failures are tests that were not updated when intent changed (circles invite screen, KYC preface rewrite, safe-area token switch, CTA renames, throw-propagation, two-step save-place flow).

## Changes

**11 test files** updated to the shipped contracts (no UI component touched), plus **2 shipped-artifact fixes**:
- `connections-service.removeConnection` now parses and returns the removal result that PR #4660's own tests pin (was `Promise<void>` discarding the JSON). Safe: the sole caller (`app/connect/page-client.tsx`) ignores the return; all new fields optional.
- `scripts/testing/signed-in-ui-flows.mjs` walks the five-screen onboarding contract including the invite screen.

## For the one-location authors (non-blocking)

The removal-result contract pins fields (`stillConnected`, `circles[]`) the backend doesn't return yet (`connections_service.py` returns `{removed: N}` only). The frontend normalization satisfies the pinned contract and tolerates the legacy shape — if a backend change was meant to land alongside #4660, it still can, without touching this.

## Proof

- Full suite under Node 24 (CI's runtime): **2990 passed, 0 failed** (main: 59 failed in CI).
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors; eslint clean on all changed files.
- Each cluster independently verified green by its fixing agent before the combined run.

author: douglas-grishen
body:
## Summary

- add team execution ownership continuity with membership-bound authority, durable checkpoint lineage, fence-aware mutations and idempotent takeover
- add outcome-driven team structure adaptation with approved DAG catalogs, decision-bound observations, bounded deterministic learning and fresh-team materialization
- add a transport-neutral collective peer host with durable envelope claims, unambiguous routing, fair bounded scheduling and typed formation/execution/recovery/adaptation commands
- expose all three browser-safe public subpaths and document their architecture, threat models and operational boundaries
- exercise the named APIs from a real packed `@agentplat/collective-runtime` tarball

## Why

Agentplat already exposed the underlying planning, formation, execution and exchange runtimes, but applications still lacked a coherent open-core path for coordinator loss, locally adaptive team topology and production-facing peer composition. These additions close those gaps without introducing a global planner, provider coupling or new effect authority.

## Safety properties

- stale owners are rejected through exact authority, membership and fencing bindings at durable CAS/effect boundaries
- checkpoints bind scope, execution lineage, membership configuration, certification time and successor state
- structure observations must cite the exact stored adaptation decision and terminal execution facts
- unsafe evidence cannot increase preference and quarantines the affected template from the current adaptation high-water
- envelope claims bind the full verified signing document, so same-message equivocation fails closed
- structure-driven formation requires a fresh formation runtime at team epoch 1

## Validation

- `pnpm run audit:public`
- `pnpm run type-check` (48 package projects plus public contracts)
- `pnpm run test:unit` (920 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped, 6 repository TODOs)
- focused self-management tests (25 passed)
- `pnpm run verify:collective-self-management-pack`
- `pnpm run verify:pack` (48 tarballs, 102 public API surfaces)
- Prettier checks for all new and modified feature files
- `git diff --cached --check`

## Stack

This PR targets `codex/distributed-team-execution-exchange-v1` so it remains a focused, reviewable layer on top of the distributed team execution exchange work.

author: ahincho
body:
Segundo y ultimo PR de traduccion. Con este, **los tres ficheros quedan con 0 lineas en espanol**: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/VERSIONING.md` y `docs/GOVERNANCE-STANDARD.md`.

`AGENTS.md` es el documento que leen los agentes antes de cada PR, asi que fui seccion por seccion en vez de reescribirlo de golpe, y va commiteado por bloques para que se pueda revisar por partes.

## Cambios de contenido, no solo de idioma

**§ 5.1 — la regla del idioma se invierte.** Decia "comentarios y documentacion en espanol". Ahora dice ingles, con una nota de que el resto de repos siguen en espanol y migraran despues: la mezcla es una migracion en curso, no una incoherencia que alguien deba "arreglar" traduciendo un repo que nadie pidio.

**§ 6 — CODEOWNERS.** Decia que este repo NO usa catch-all, dando como razon la acumulacion de owners que GitHub no hace. Alineado con la politica del PR #335.

**§ 11 — se retira el inventario.** Decia "21 reusables" con tabla por capa, y hay **27**. La lista de consumidores nombraba ramas que ya no existen. Ninguno de los dos errores rompia nada; los dos enganaban a quien leia la seccion justo para averiguar que hay disponible. Ahora remite al arbol y al README, que desde el #333 tiene guard de fidelidad.

## Avisos nuevos, todos de cosas que mordieron hoy

| Donde | Que se anade |
|---|---|
| § 3 | Las dos reglas de commitlint que mas fallan: scope fuera de la tabla, y subject en mayusculas |
| § 4.4 | Pasar `--subject` **siempre**: el squash usa el titulo del PR como asunto, y el commitlint del PR mira los commits de la rama. Mismo aviso para el cuerpo y `footer-max-line-length` |
| § 5.2 | Un reusable no puede escalar permisos por encima de su caller. Si el caller da menos, GitHub aborta con `startup_failure`: sin logs y sin publicar contexto |
| § 5.3 | Los nombres de job deben ser estaticos, o el ruleset espera un contexto que no llega nunca |
| § 5.6 | Verificar cada guard en las dos direcciones |
| § 7 | El manifiesto es lo que la herramienta **escribe**: declarar de menos borra puertas |
| § 9 | Tres causas de un check requerido que no reporta |
| § 10 | Dos prohibiciones nuevas: silenciar un check en vez de arreglar lo que encontro, y afirmar un recuento en prosa |

## Y una leccion nueva en § 13.2

*Un verde no es evidencia hasta saber que mide.* Con los cuatro casos medidos hoy:

- checkov corria con `--soft-fail`, `|| true` y `continue-on-error`: 262 de 262 en verde sobre veinte PRs, y ese verde significaba "el job termino"
- los filtros de `paths` dejaban 57 de 161 ficheros sin disparar ninguno de los 20 contextos requeridos
- el guard que prohibia el catch-all casaba `^[[:space:]]+\*` y no podia dispararse sobre uno real
- el `minimum_protocol_version` de CloudFront que AWS ignora en silencio: el codigo declaraba TLS 1.2 y la distribucion aceptaba TLSv1

`object` is present in the original payload, but we didn't surface it on the `EventNotification` class. Because ``v2.core.event"` is the only value that will ever be present, It didn't seem worth adding it to the interface.

    (event.try(:object) || event.try(:dig, "object")) == "v2.core.event"
end
```

Because the value is present in the original response, it doesn't make sense to eat it.
