author: e-n-f
body:
Fixes the formatting rules to pin pointer alignment, makes `make indent` a CI requirement in the same manner as `make docs`, and reformats the sources so the new check passes.

## Formatting rules

`PointerAlignment: Right` alone wouldn't have been enough: the Google base style enables `DerivePointerAlignment`, which makes the placement of `*` and `&` depend on whichever way each file already leans, so an explicit setting would still be overridden per file. Both are now set.

The exclusion of `flatgeobuf.cpp` is also gone — it was the one hand-written source the formatter never saw — so the target now covers `$(C) $(H) jsonpull/*.[ch]`.

## CI

New `indent` job in the same shape as `docs`: install clang-format, reformat, fail on any diff with an `::error::` annotation pointing at `make indent`.

clang-format **18.1.8** is pinned, for the same reason go-md2man is pinned in the `docs` job: different versions format the same input differently. This is not theoretical across major versions only — 18.1.3 (the Ubuntu 24.04 system version) and 18.1.8 already disagree on one line in `geometry.cpp`, so an unpinned job would fail spuriously. Staying on 18.x keeps CI close to what contributors on Ubuntu 24.04 get from their system clang-format. The Makefile carries a comment noting that CI pins a version, so a local disagreement gets resolved from the job output rather than by committing whatever the local version prefers.

## Reformatting

The tree wasn't `make indent` clean, so the job would have failed on arrival. Two parts:

- **~14 lines of drift** in `mvt.cpp`, `serial.cpp`, `tile-join.cpp`, `tile.cpp`, `unit.cpp`, and `geometry.cpp`, accumulated while nothing was checking: trailing whitespace, spaces where tabs belong, hand-aligned ternary continuations, and casts missing the space that the existing `SpaceAfterCStyleCast` asks for. Only 2 of these lines come from the pointer-alignment change itself — the codebase was already right-aligned, so that setting pins existing practice rather than changing it.
- **`flatgeobuf.cpp`** (125 lines), which was 4-space-indented and had never been through the formatter. `git diff -w` confirms the only non-whitespace changes are brace placement, expanded single-statement `if` bodies, and `feature_sequence_id ++` → `feature_sequence_id++`.

## Testing

`make && make test` passes clean (10813 assertions in 7 test cases), no new compiler warnings, and `make indent` is idempotent on the result.

author: ql-isha-parihar
body:
The `RangeError: RangeError (end): Invalid value: Not in inclusive range 0..111: 1000` occurs because the `substring` method is being called with an end index (1000) that exceeds the length of the string it is operating on. The stack trace points directly to `package:news_app/widgets/article_card.dart:71` within the `ArticleCard.build` method.

In `lib/widgets/article_card.dart`, line 71 is:
`Text(isSecondTab ? article.title.substring(0, 1000) : article.title, ...)`

When `isSecondTab` is true, the code attempts to truncate the `article.title` using `substring(0, 1000)`. If `article.title` has fewer than 1000 characters, this throws the `RangeError`.

Although the intent is likely to limit the title length, using a fixed large number (1000) is unsafe. Since the `Text` widget already handles truncation using `maxLines: 3` and `overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis`, explicitly calling `substring` is redundant and dangerous if the maximum desired length is small. If the goal is to ensure the string is never excessively long before passing it to the widget, it should be capped at a much smaller, reasonable limit, or better yet, the `Text` widget's built-in capabilities should be relied upon.

**Step-by-step fix:**
1. **Locate the problematic line:** In `lib/widgets/article_card.dart`, find the line where the title is displayed (around line 71).
2. **Modify the title logic:** Replace the unsafe `substring(0, 1000)` call with a safe truncation mechanism. Since the `Text` widget handles truncation for display, the safest and simplest fix is to just use `article.title` and let the `Text` widget manage the display limit, or if a hard limit is strictly required, use `article.title.substring(0, 100)` (or whatever the desired maximum length is).
3. **Apply the fix (Recommended):** Change the line to simply use `article.title`, as the `Text` widget already has `maxLines: 3` and `overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis` set, which handles truncation gracefully.
4. **Apply the fix (If hard limit is needed):** Change the line to `article.title.substring(0, 150)` (or a suitable limit, as 1000 is excessive for a card title), ensuring the limit is much smaller than the potential string length.

**Implementation (Using the recommended approach - relying on Text widget):**
Change line 71 from:
`Text(isSecondTab ? article.title.substring(0, 1000) : article.title,`
To:
`Text(article.title,`

If `isSecondTab` is only meant to trigger a specific truncation (e.g., for a list view vs. a detailed view), and the truncation is necessary before the `Text` widget, a safe limit (e.g., 150 characters) should be used instead of 1000.

author: wking53214
body:
## Summary

Root-caused and fixed the concurrency bug three tests in `test_governance_harness_stress.py` had been marked `xfail` for, under a shared, vague reason string ("tuple concurrently updated in role-management logic under simultaneous bind_cassette_version calls").

**Root cause, confirmed live**: 10 threads each constructing a `PostgreSQLLedger` concurrently → 9 of 10 failed with exactly that error. Points precisely at `_provision_runtime_password`'s `ALTER ROLE` statement — **not** `bind_cassette_version`, which the xfail reason blamed. Every single ledger construction runs an unlocked `ALTER ROLE ... WITH PASSWORD` against Postgres's shared `pg_authid` catalog; concurrent `ALTER ROLE` on the same role from different sessions can raise Postgres's own "tuple concurrently updated" error. **This affects real production concurrency too**, not just this test — multiple `sentinel_worker.py` processes booting simultaneously would hit the identical race.

**Fix**: wrap the `ALTER ROLE` in the same `pg_advisory_xact_lock` pattern `bind_cassette_version` already uses in this file, keyed per `runtime_user`. Transaction-scoped, so it only serializes the brief provisioning window. Re-ran the standalone 10-thread reproduction after the fix: 0 errors out of 10.

## Two more bugs found once the masking race was gone

- `test_concurrent_ledger_writes_from_multiple_harnesses_at_volume` had a **second, unrelated** bug: asserted `len(rows) == 200` but called `get_decisions()` without overriding its `limit=100` default — always failed regardless of whether the concurrent writes themselves were correct. Fixed with `limit=200`.
- `test_repeated_construct_shutdown_does_not_leak_connections` never exercised the concurrency bug at all — its 50 cycles are sequential, not threaded. The xfail marker was copy-pasted onto it by mistake.

All three verified passing **5x in a row** (the two genuinely-concurrent ones) before removing their xfail markers. Updated the module docstring's stale "no live Postgres in this sandbox" claim and documented the real root cause for the record.

## Test plan
- [x] Standalone reproduction: 10 concurrent `PostgreSQLLedger` constructions, 9/10 failed before the fix, 0/10 after.
- [x] All three previously-xfail tests: 5 consecutive clean runs each.
- [x] `Tests/test_governance_harness.py` + `test_governance_harness_stress.py`: 32/32 passed.
- [x] Full suite (excluding `test_twin_live.py`): **986 passed/1 failed/2 xfailed/1 xpassed → 990 passed/0 failed/0 xfailed/0 xpassed, 22 skipped**. (The 1 prior failure, `test_L11_frozen_redis_health_stays_alive`, was unrelated environmental contamination — a stale orphaned redis-server from earlier testing squatting on its port — cleared separately, not part of this diff.)
- [x] The 22 remaining skips are BISG research-mode gating (16, a deliberate legal/IP-review hold — not touched or overridden) and BISG live tests requiring a real `CENSUS_API_KEY` (6, an external credential not available here).
- [x] `ruff check` / `bandit -ll` clean on both touched files.

author: msalvatti
body:
Repairs the CodeQL conversion already merged here. The pull request that made it described the change as carrying triggers over unchanged and as a pure definition move. Neither was true for this repository.

## What was lost

- **`queries: security-extended`** — a **superset** of the default suite. The conversion did not carry it, so this repository has been analysing strictly less than before the move. In the workflow whose entire purpose is coverage.
- **`workflow_dispatch`** and/or the **concurrency group**, depending on what this repository declared. Without the group, repeated pushes to a branch can leave several analyses of the same ref running at once.

## How this was determined

By reading this repository's own pre-conversion file, not a template. The original premise — that the ten copies were byte-identical — was wrong: six ran `security-extended`, five declared `workflow_dispatch`, six had a concurrency group, and the pinned action revision differed across three versions. Centralising on what one of them happened to contain is what caused the regression.

The reusable workflow gained a `queries` input and moved to `v4.37.4` — the newest revision already in use — in [`bymaxone/.github#23`](https://github.com/bymaxone/.github/pull/23).

author: ravenwater
body:
## Summary
Completes **#417**. `lu_factor`/`qr_factor`/`cholesky_factor` dispatched to `getrf`/`geqrf`/`potrf` only for **column-major** dense2D, because those pass the raw `A.data()` buffer to Fortran and a row-major buffer is the *transpose* of what LAPACK reads. This enables the default (row-major) type by factoring through a column-major scratch: copy A in via the `(i,j)` accessor, run LAPACK in place, copy the factor back via `(i,j)`. The accessor-based solves (`lu_solve`, `qr_solve`/`qr_extract_Q`, `cholesky_solve`) then read the factor exactly as on the column-major path; pivots/tau come out identically.

This is Category B of #417 — the harder half A (#418) left, since these dispatches can't just drop the guard.

## Changes
- `lu.hpp` / `qr.hpp` / `cholesky.hpp` — row-major copy-in → LAPACK → copy-out.
- `cholesky_h_factor` **delegates to `cholesky_factor`** for real BLAS types (`A = L*L^H` is `A = L*L^T` there). This keeps the two entry points **bit-identical** — the invariant `test_cholesky.cpp` pins with `==`, which independent factoring would break once `cholesky_factor` uses `potrf` — and extends the dispatch. Complex Hermitian stays generic.
- **Zero-dimension guard** on all three: LAPACK rejects `lda == 0` (XERBLA), so an empty matrix skips the call and falls through to the generic no-op. (Surfaced by the degenerate-sizes test via the cholesky delegation.)

## ⚠️ Behavior change caught by #297 — and how it's resolved
`test_factorization_mt` (#297) asserts the threaded factorization is **bit-identical to a serial *generic* reference** — a property of MTL5's `parallel_for` kernels, not of LAPACK. Since the default `double` path now dispatches to LAPACK (a *different* algorithm), that assertion no longer holds for `double`.

Per the chosen resolution, the determinism tests switch to a **non-BLAS element type** (`det_t = long double`, never `is_blas_scalar`), so `dense2D<det_t>` always takes the generic `parallel_for` kernel and the race-freedom check holds in **both** LAPACK and non-LAPACK builds. The `apply_householder_*` tests stay `double` — those kernels never dispatch. Correctness/residual checks still pass on `double` via the LAPACK path (the existing lu/qr/cholesky suites).

## Proof it isn't vacuous
```
this branch:     U dgetrf_  U dgeqrf_  U dpotrf_   (row-major factorization TU)
parent commit:   (none)
```

## Test Results
| Config | full suite / affected |
|---|---|
| gcc 13 + LAPACK | **163/163** (full ctest) |
| clang 18 + LAPACK | lu/qr/cholesky/factorization_mt/dispatch PASS |
| clang 18, no LAPACK | PASS (generic path; det_t compiles) |

## Test plan
- [ ] Fast CI + LAPACK CI job (exercises the row-major factorization dispatch)
- [ ] Tier-2 regression (dense solvers consume these factorizations)
- [ ] Promote when satisfied

Resolves #417

body:
## Summary
Improves detection of distant/small football players in the Panorama without replacing the current PR #39 workspace or Digital Twin pipeline.

## Changes
- Keeps the existing full-panorama COCO-SSD pass for large/near players
- Adds 3 overlapping panorama tiles and upscales each tile before inference
- Lowers tile detection threshold to 0.20 and full-frame threshold to 0.24
- Maps tile detections back into the original panorama coordinate system
- Applies IoU-based NMS to remove duplicate detections across full-frame and overlapping tiles
- Transparently feeds the merged detections into the existing persistent-ID association, homography and Pitch Digital Twin logic
- Keeps the current Panorama UI and camera pipeline unchanged

## Why
A very wide football panorama makes distant players occupy too few pixels for a single full-frame COCO-SSD inference. Tiled inference increases their effective pixel size while preserving the existing browser-only MVP architecture.

## Test
1. Connect 1–3 cameras and open Panorama
2. Start Person Tracking
3. Compare far-side/small player detections with the current main build
4. Confirm duplicate boxes around tile seams are suppressed
5. Confirm persistent IDs continue to appear in the Pitch Digital Twin

Note: this is an MVP improvement. A football-specific YOLO + ByteTrack pipeline remains the recommended production direction.

Consequência prática: o #5407 — que altera **3 strings** de texto na tela — está bloqueado. E qualquer PR futuro que toque esse arquivo estaria também.

Expande o núcleo visual de **12 → 13** telas. Mesmo movimento do #5326 (as 5 telas da Governança, 05/08). Liberação da tela informada por **[M]** em 2026-08-07; **o merge continua sendo ato do [W]**.

## O que entra

| arquivo | o quê |
|---|---|
| `tests/Browser/visreg-screens.json` | +8 linhas — a entrada da tela |
| `...PixelBaselineTest/it_Produto_Unificado_....snap` | a foto de referência (novo) |

Campos **medidos na fonte**, não inventados:

| campo | valor | de onde |
|---|---|---|
| `screen` / `source` | `Produto/Unificado` | saída do próprio `ui-impact` no [run 31207886621](https://github.com/wagnerra23/oimpresso.com/actions/runs/31207886621) |
| `component` | `Produto/Unificado/Index` | `ProdutoUnificadoController.php:52` |
| `route` | `/products/unificado` | `routes/web.php:450` |
| `anchor` | `Catálogo` | o `<h1>` da tela — é um `assertSee` (`PixelBaselineTest:161`). Escolhi o título e **não** os KPIs do topo, que são zerados/condicionais |
| `baseline` | `it_Produto_Unificado_bate_com_a_baseline_de_pixel__núcleo_6_.snap` | padrão das 12 entradas |

## ⚠️ Proveniência da foto — e um problema de infra que o [W] precisa ver

A baseline **não foi gerada localmente**. Saiu do **modo update** ([run 31210326708](https://github.com/wagnerra23/oimpresso.com/actions/runs/31210326708)), no mesmo runner canônico das outras 12. O runner gerou e commitou — mas o step de publicar **falhou**:

```
remote: Permission to wagnerra23/oimpresso.com.git denied to github-actions[bot]
fatal: ... The requested URL returned error: 403
```

O `COWORK_BOT_PAT` **passou** no teste `permissions.push` do próprio workflow e mesmo assim teve o push recusado — ou seja, o token não tem escrita efetiva. Recuperei pelo caminho que o próprio workflow documenta (artifact `pixel-snapshots`). **O PAT precisa ser corrigido antes do próximo dispatch**, senão todo modo update vai exigir essa recuperação manual.

PNG conferido: 1 linha base64, magic `PNG`, `1728x1117`, 100.420 bytes.

## Decisão deliberada: só a foto NOVA entra

O run reescreveu **mais 20 baselines** (Financeiro, Clientes, Oficina, Compras) em nível de **byte**. Deixei todas de fora, de propósito:

1. **Byte ≠ pixel.** O gate compara pixel com limiar (τ_baixo 0,1% auto-aprova). Regeneração de PNG não é byte-determinística — churn de byte não prova mudança visual nenhuma.
2. Commitar as 20 seria **fotografar a dívida**: se alguma daquelas telas regrediu de verdade no main, sobrescrever a baseline esconde a regressão dentro de um PR que fala de Produto.
3. Se alguma regrediu mesmo, **o gate deste PR mostra** — e mostrar é o comportamento desejado.

## Como este PR se prova

Medido: tocar `visreg-screens.json` classifica o diff como `scope: global` (`reason: contrato-visual`). O gate refotografa as **13** telas e compara com as baselines commitadas — prova que a baseline nova bate (anti-#3297) e, de quebra, dá o retrato honesto das outras 12.

Lints L2 rodados localmente, os mesmos do workflow:

```
visreg-states-lint · 6 screen(s) no manifesto · 0 problema(s)
visreg-flows-lint · 0 problema(s)
visreg-sells-lint · 0 problema(s)
```

## ⚠️ O que o [W] deve pesar antes de aprovar

1. **Muda o que o gate cobre no projeto inteiro** — 13ª tela no núcleo visual.
2. **A baseline congela a tela como ela está HOJE**, com `Populares`, `Margem média` e `Sem giro` zerados (`0` literal em `ProdutoUnificadoController:85-88` — gap **G-03 / CU-PROD-12**). Quando a agregação for implementada, a baseline terá de ser regerada pelo mesmo modo update. Não é impeditivo — é a foto do que existe —, mas não deve virar surpresa.

## Depois deste PR

O #5407 (conserto do `null` no estoque + nome de outra empresa no cabeçalho) fica verde e pode seguir.

Refs: #5407 · #5326 · CU-PROD-12 · `memory/requisitos/Produto/SDD-tela-cadastro-produto-v1.0.md` §5.3 F4

## 🔄 Reestruturado em 2026-08-07 — este PR absorveu o #5407

**Por que.** A 1ª versão deste PR contratou a tela e tirou a baseline **antes** de consertar os textos. Isso congelaria como referência oficial uma tela mostrando `null` no estoque e o nome de **outra empresa** no cabeçalho — e faria o #5407 (o conserto) nascer **vermelho por construção**, já que a tela corrigida não bate com a foto do estado defeituoso. Erro de sequenciamento meu. A ordem certa é **conserta → fotografa**.

O #5407 foi **fechado** apontando pra cá. Sei que isso mistura dois objetivos num PR só, contra a regra da casa — mas eles **não são separáveis na prática**: a baseline tem que ser da tela corrigida, senão um dos dois PRs fica obrigatoriamente vermelho.

### O que este PR contém agora

| commit | o quê |
|---|---|
| manifesto | a tela entra no contrato visual (12 → 13 telas) |
| `Index.tsx` | os 3 consertos de texto (nome de outra empresa · `null` no estoque · plural) |
| `Index.tsx` | **fix do fix**: o nome da empresa vinha vazio — ver abaixo |
| `documentation-loop.mjs` | o mesmo fix do #5417 (ver "Sobreposição") |
| `.snap` | baseline da tela **já corrigida** |

### 🔍 O meio-fix que só a foto pegou

A baseline do 1º dispatch saiu com o cabeçalho **`Catálogo · 1 PRODUTO`** e **nenhum nome de empresa** — enquanto a sidebar, na mesma imagem, mostrava `Tenant Visual Regression`. Ou seja: o commit original tirou o `ROTA LIVRE` errado e **não pôs o certo no lugar**.

Causa: duas fontes para o nome, uma frágil. `business.name` (shared prop) sai da **sessão**, e o bridge do visreg dá `session()->forget(['business'])` → vazio. `shell.cockpit.businessNome` sai de **query em `App\Business`** (`HandleInertiaRequests:302`) — é a que o `AppShellV2:273` usa na sidebar e funciona. Passei a preferir a do shell, com a da sessão como fallback e **sem default inventado**.

**Nenhum teste teria pego isso** — não há teste desta tela e o CI ficaria verde com o cabeçalho vazio. Apareceu porque decodifiquei o PNG e olhei.

Baseline atual, verificada por inspeção:

```
cabeçalho: "Catálogo · 1 PRODUTO · TENANT VISUAL REGRESSION"
sidebar:   "Tenant Visual Regression"          ← batem
plural:    "1 PRODUTO" (singular)
sub-telas: Produtos · Categorias · Insumos·BOM · Tabelas de preço · Histórico
```

### ⚠️ O que a baseline NÃO prova

O tenant de teste tem **1 produto** e ele é `sob demanda` — a coluna Estoque nunca entra no ramo `stockQty === null`. O conserto do `null UNID` → `—` está no código e é verificável por leitura, mas **esta foto não é testemunha dele**. Declarado de propósito: baseline que não exercita um caminho não vira álibi dele.

### ⚠️ Infra: `COWORK_BOT_PAT` quebrado (2 dispatches, 2 falhas)

O modo update gerou as baselines certinho nas duas vezes e **falhou ao publicar** nas duas, sempre no mesmo ponto:

```
remote: Permission to wagnerra23/oimpresso.com.git denied to github-actions[bot]
fatal: ... The requested URL returned error: 403
```

O token passa no teste `permissions.push` do próprio workflow e mesmo assim tem o push recusado. **Não é intermitência** — todo dispatch futuro vai exigir a recuperação manual pelo artifact `pixel-snapshots`, que foi o que fiz aqui. Conserto é com o [W].

Dedup-ack: **sobreposição consciente com o #5417.** Este PR carrega o mesmo commit de `documentation-loop.mjs` porque, sem ele, o gate `Módulo novo — contrato + projeções derivadas` recusa esta branch (a baseline tem `núcleo` no nome — é exatamente o bug que o #5417 conserta). O **#5417 segue sendo a revisão canônica** daquele fix. Ordem de merge indiferente: se o #5417 entrar primeiro, este rebaseia e o commit duplicado some; se este entrar primeiro

author: orlandomenke
body:
## First, the part that needed no change

The proposal was *"build main after every merge, keep branch building optional"* — and **that is already the configuration**, since PR #5:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]     # merges only; no other branch builds on push
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:     # the optional manual branch build
```

All three workflows agree (`publish-wiki.yml` is `push: branches: [main]` with path filters, `cleanup-artifacts.yml` is manual-only). The file's own comment records the measurement behind it: unfiltered `push` *plus* `pull_request` ran the entire suite **twice** per push, and the concurrency group can't dedupe them because a push gives `build-refs/heads/<branch>` while a PR gives `build-<branch>` — two groups, neither cancels the other.

## What was actually costing the minutes

`pull_request` fires on **every push to an open PR**. PR #64 took **six runs** for one review: the original, a ledger sighting, two merges of main, and two index rebuilds. That's the waste, and it was mostly my push cadence.

So: **drafts build nothing.** Open the PR as a draft while merging and re-indexing, mark it ready when it's worth checking. Marking it ready is itself a trigger.

## Two ways to half-implement this, both silent, so both are tested

- **A job without the gate** builds on drafts while its neighbours don't — so the saving quietly stops applying the next time a job is added. `EveryJobIsSwitchedOffForADraftPullRequest` walks the YAML's job list rather than naming jobs, so a fifth one is caught.
- **`ready_for_review` is not a default event type.** The defaults are `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened` — none fire when a draft is marked ready. Without it, a PR drafted and later readied would **never build at all** and would be mergeable carrying a green tick it never earned. `MarkingADraftReadyTriggersABuild` holds that.

And a third mistake, guarded by `AMergeToMainStillBuilds`: the condition is `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false`, and the **first half is load-bearing** — `draft` only exists on a `pull_request` event, so testing it alone compares an empty string to `false` and would switch off the very merge build this change exists to protect.

## Verified the guards bite

Not assumed: I removed the `docs` gate and `ready_for_review`, and **3 of 3 failed** with messages naming the fix. Restored — 6 pass.

`CiRuntimeTests` still passes too, which mattered: it slices `build.yml` between `  test:` and `\n  changes:`, so job order had to stay put. I checked that before editing rather than discovering it.

## One cost, named in the file rather than left to be found

`docs` is the cheapest job here (~10s: `manual.py check`, `bugs.py check`, `roadmap.py check`) and it is the one that catches **duplicate bug ids on a merge** — which happened on main earlier today. It goes quiet on drafts along with everything else.

That's deliberate: the rule is "a draft builds nothing", and a rule with one exception is a rule nobody remembers. But the comment says plainly that if duplicate ids start reaching main again, this is why, and letting `docs` alone run on drafts is the fix. Say the word if you'd rather carve that exception now.

## Testing

`dotnet test`: **1703 App + 792 Core + 459 Raster + 98 Ai = 3052 passing**, 0 failures. `bugs.py check`, `manual.py check`, `roadmap.py check` pass. `README.md` updated where it documents which pushes produce a bundle.

author: hoaxpoet
body:
Docs-only. Closes BUG-078 on its last outstanding criterion — the manual one.

## The validation

Matt ran local-file playback end-to-end on session `2026-08-07T19-10-25Z` (5 files): start, pause/resume, natural track end, single Next, two rapid-Next bursts, quit. Clean — `CHAIN_HEALTH: verdict=clean reasons=[]`, drawable lifecycle 4815/4815, no hang, no crash.

The run left an artifact rather than an impression:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `provider.start INSTANCE` | 19 |
| `provider.teardown ENTER` | 18 |
| sequence | `I(EXI)*` — strict |

Every adopted instance was torn down before the next was adopted. **Zero orphans in production**, through bursts of 3 and 5 starts inside a single second. The unpaired 19th is the instance still playing at log end — `deinit` tears down with `diagnostic: nil` and emits no breadcrumb.

## What the live run does NOT prove

Every teardown is ordered `ENTER → EXIT → INSTANCE` — the pre-lock `stop()` path. The BUG078.1 stale-teardown branch prints `INSTANCE → ENTER` and never fired, because the app drives `start()` from the MainActor and serialises it. The session establishes no-regression plus the orphan invariant on the shipped path; the concurrent-start race stays covered by `LocalFilePlaybackStartRaceTests`. That the app cannot easily reach the race is also why the trap has only ever been seen in the test process.

Both statements are in KNOWN_ISSUES; neither alone closes the bug.

## Doc-gate note

Moving the entry into §Resolved (recent) pushed that section over its 50 KB DOC.6 budget, and `rotate_docs.sh` was a no-op (nothing there is older than 14 days). Rather than widen the budget, BUG-078's four per-sighting paragraphs are collapsed into one summary line — they existed to narrow an unknown cause, which is no longer unknown. Their durable content is kept: the exit-code-without-failure signature and the ~2-in-6 trip rate.

`DocIntegrityTests` 12/12 green.

body:
Restores the LangGraph OIDC **mandatory-audience** default now that the issuer defines a resource-server `aud` contract (partner#952). Closes the SDK side of #63. **Held/draft — do not merge until dev is live-tested** against the deployed per-env `OIDC_PROTECTED_RESOURCES`.

## What it does (Python `langgraph` auth only)
- **Fail closed (401) when no `audience` is configured.** Set it per env (dev/integration/staging/production → `https://accounts-<env>.internal-nuggets.life/agent`, prod `https://accounts.nuggets.life/agent`); scope `agent.invoke`.
- **`allow_any_audience=True`** — deliberate, documented-**insecure** escape hatch that bypasses **only** the `aud` match; signature, `iss`, `exp`, `typ`, and the RS256 pin still apply. Logs a warning. Not a production setting.
- **`typ == at+jwt` enforced** (RFC 9068) — blocks ID-token/access-token confusion.
- **15s clock-skew leeway** on `exp`/`iat`, matching the issuer's `clockTolerance`.
- **JWT-only:** removed the unaudienced `/me` userinfo opaque fallback so it can't bypass the audience check. Authenticated introspection stays a documented follow-up.
- Retained from prior hardening: RS256 pin (never the header `alg`) + JWKS `kty`/`use`/`alg` filtering.
- Scope stays app-side via `require_scopes`; the verifier does identity/`aud`/`typ`/`exp`/signature only.

## Release
- Bumps both packages to **1.2.0** (JS is a no-functional-change lockstep bump — the work is Python-only). CHANGELOG carries a ⚠️ Migration note for the breaking audience default.

## Verification (TDD, RED→GREEN)
New/updated tests: fail-closed-without-audience, blank-audience rejected, `typ` wrong/missing rejected, clock-skew within/beyond leeway, opaque rejected, and an `allow_any_audience` class proving it bypasses **only** `aud` (still rejects wrong `iss`/expired/bad `typ`). Python `207 passed`, ruff + changed-file mypy clean; JS `105 passed` + typecheck + build.

## Gate
The `aud` values are **provisional until dev is deployed** with the env var (infra handover) and we run a live end-to-end token verification against dev. Then: mark ready → merge → tags `js-v1.2.0`/`python-v1.2.0` → deploy-gate approval.

author: platostwin
body:
## #252 — the FAB's flaky guard was reporting a real occlusion badly

**This PR is prose only: one unnumbered entry in `docs/errata-pending/`. No code.** That is the
finding, not a shortfall of one — read "What I did not land" below before merging.

CI note: a prose-only diff deliberately skips `unit` and `ui` since #216, so the green check on this
PR is evidence about the diff and not about the code. There is no code here for it to be evidence
about.

### What I proved

**The standing hypothesis in my brief is wrong, in both halves.** It said this is *not* an app
layout defect — "the FAB's frame is stable and correct; the assertion is not reliably observing it"
— and that the cause is the hundreds of `MKAnnotationView`s the FAB overlays (the E202/E216
family). The frame is stable. It is not correct, and no annotation is involved.

At AX5 with location denied, on an iPhone 16 Pro at `origin/main`, screen 01's **species legend is
drawn on top of the identify FAB**:

| element | frame |
|---|---|
| species legend | `(16, 230, 344.33, 262.67)` → bottom **492.67** |
| identify FAB | `(22, 371, 364.33, 83)` |
| recenter control | `(342.33, 315, 44, 44)` |

The legend's rectangle contains the recenter control entirely and all but the bottom 14 pt of the
FAB, and `MapHomeView.chrome` applies the bottom block first *so the top block draws over it* — a
deliberate ordering with its own note. A screenshot of the running app shows `What tree is this?`
behind an opaque `Southern Magnolia` legend chip with only a `?` visible past its right edge. **The
same overlap is on the 430 pt iPhone 16 Plus.** It is not width-specific.

**Why the guard was intermittent instead of red.** XCUITest resolves `isHittable` by hit-testing the
activation point and then points sampled inside the frame, so a control covered everywhere except a
14 pt band reports reachable exactly when the sampling finds the band. The four green runs were the
luck, not the two red ones — a three-in-four chance of missing a defect that was on the screen the
whole time.

Proved in one run rather than argued: with the candidate fix disabled by one line and everything
else identical, the two geometric assertions go red naming the legend and
`testTheFABIsReachableAtAX5WithLocationDenied` — the hittability one — **passes, in 4.6 s**. Same
launch, same device: the occlusion is there, the rectangles see it, the hittability check does not.

**The cause.** `MapLayout.topChromeReservedAX5` stops at the filter chip row. Below the chip row the
same `VStack` also stacks the search status, the `Needs care` toast, and the legend, which wraps to
as many lines as the palette's names need — 262.67 pt at AX5. The reservation predicts 216; the
block ends at 492.67. It is #250's defect one child further down the same stack.

### What I did not land, and why

**The layout fix.** I built it (measure the top block's real bottom edge; `min` with the constant
path). It removes the standing occlusion — measured, screenshotted, and green on **two full
`CypressUITests` runs on 430 pt** (96 tests, 0 failures, twice) and one on 402 pt. The next 402 pt
run was red: top chrome at 492.67, bottom chrome at 437.0, which is where it belongs for a
*three*-row legend against a legend that had four. `FABLagDiagTests`, sampling both edges every
250 ms for 26 s across repeated launches, turned that into a number — **roughly one launch in four
freezes**, from the first sample to the last, never converging, while a hand launch of the same
build converges within ten seconds. Four wirings were tried (`onChange` in a `.background`;
`PreferenceKey` read on the ancestor, with and without a `@MainActor` hop; read on the producing
block). All four flake; which launch freezes moves with the wiring, which is a race rather than a
missing invalidation.

A layout fix that is right three launches in four would close this ticket and come back as somebody
else's flaky test, so it is not here. The entry names the two candidates that have no feedback loop
to resolve — an `AX5ReflowTests`-guarded constant gated on `isAccessibilitySize`, or collapsing the
two overlays into one `VStack` — and is honest that the second is a product call, because it changes
R25/#143's deliberate draw-over for the suggestion list.

**The guard.** `IdentifyFABReachabilityTests` is written and red-proved four ways (offset off-screen
→ the reachability message; the fix disabled → both geometric messages; `locateToFabGap: -10` → the
recenter message). It is at `89f5001`/`5a2112f` on this branch's history and should be resurrected
the moment screen 01 passes it. It cannot land now because screen 01 fails it, correctly.

**One repair worth stealing from that history** (`5a2112f`): `settledFrame` gains
`requireHittable:`, default `true` so all eleven existing callers are untouched. The guard's first
version measured *through* a hittability gate and a full-suite run caught it — 30 s spent waiting
for a hittability that never came, reporting the symptom, where the two rectangles it was about to
compare were readable throughout. Hittability is what an occlusion removes, so a guard against
occlusion must not depend on it. Not in this PR because its only caller is not.

### Also found, not fixed

`MapTreeCard` shares the bottom slot and is **not** given `noticeMaxHeight` — only the four
`MapLocationNotice` arms are. Same shape, different arm of the same `switch`, unguarded.

### Hypothesis, still

Why the measurement freezes is *not* established — only that it does, at what rate, and that it is
not a lag. I did not find the SwiftUI mechanism.

### PR #51

**Close as superseded.** Its tests were intermittently detecting this defect rather than flaking,
which is the finding; its chip-row assertion is dominated by the legend and cannot be red-proved for
its own reason; and its file's central comment ("this is not an app layout defect") is false.
Nothing in it should be rebased forward — the replacement is in this branch's history, cited above.

### Runs

All via `Tools/run_tests.sh` + `Tools/verify_test_log.sh`, logs in the shared scratchpad.

| log | device | result |
|---|---|---|
| `fab2-final-16plus-1.log` | 16 Plus `24D1629F`, 430 pt | `VERIFY-OK: Executed 96 tests, with 0 failures in 1417.298s` |
| `fab2-final-16plus-2.log` | 16 Plus `24D1629F`, 430 pt | `VERIFY-OK: Executed 96 tests, with 0 failures in 1407.559s` |
| `fab2-full-16pro-1.log` | 16 Pro `EA0AD796`, 402 pt | `VERIFY-OK: Executed 96 tests, with 0 failures in 1550.078s` |
| `fab2-full-16pro-2.log` | 16 Pro `EA0AD796`, 402 pt | `VERIFY-FAIL` — the hittability-gated read (fixed in `5a2112f`) |
| `fab2-final-16pro-1.log` | 16 Pro `EA0AD796`, 402 pt | `VERIFY-FAIL` — `492.67 > 437.0`, the stale measurement |
| `fab2-unit.log` | 16 Pro `EA0AD796` | `VERIFY-OK: Test run with 1277 tests in 126 suites passed` |

Every log carries its `CYPRESS-RUN` header; all report `active-city=none`, `camera-auto-healed no`,
`XCTest skipped=0`. **Those greens certify a tree that is not this one** — they are the evidence for
the fix I am not landing, and they are listed so the next attempt knows the fix is close rather than
wrong in principle.

author: grantlella87-design
body:
One commit on top of `6b954c4` (the merge of #68).

## Nothing in the left pane can be pushed off the bottom

A section could still end up below the bottom edge, and the cause was in the arithmetic that shares the pane out between the open sections: it was estimating what everything else took, and it estimated the **mode buttons above them at nothing** — most of a section's worth of height. Everything is measured now: the buttons, the headers of the closed sections, and the bars between the open ones, all read from what is on screen.

The share is also worked out in two passes. An even share is the wrong answer when a section has less content than its share — it keeps its own height and gives the rest back, and what is given back is shared out again among the ones that were capped. Otherwise a short section was handed a third of the pane it could not fill while a long one was cut off at the bottom.

**On the snap-to-bottom alternative:** I have fixed the cause rather than added the fallback, because with the pane measured properly nothing should be unviewable in the first place. If a section still ends up off the bottom after this, say so and I will add the explicit pin — but a fallback that hides a bad measurement is worse than the measurement being right.

## Placed features can be moved and removed

The tool panel now lists what has been placed and not yet sent, under the palette, with **Move** and **Remove** on each row. The section is only there when there is something in it.

- **Move** waits for the next click on the map and puts the feature there, snapping onto a proposed main and turning to lie along it exactly as a new placement does.
- **Remove** takes it off the map and out of the list.

Only one of the things a click on the map can mean is ever armed at once: arming a symbol calls off a move, and arming a move calls off a symbol. Drawing still beats both.

The list is emptied once the features have gone to GIS. They are GIS's then, and a Remove button beside something already sent would be offering to undo what it cannot.

author: nbudin
body:
Fixes #11892

## Summary

Follow-up to #11870/#11891, which handled bucket key/id correlation only for editing an existing registration policy. This converts the remaining internal identity uses of `RegistrationPolicyBucket#key` — in `SignupBucketFinder`, `RegistrationPolicyBucket`'s occupancy checks, and `EventChangeRegistrationPolicyService`'s simulation/removed-bucket logic — to use `id` for persisted buckets, or object identity for not-yet-persisted candidate buckets during registration policy simulation (a bucket being added in the same edit has no real id until the edit is persisted, so key is the only identity that predates the object entirely disappearing — object identity replaces it everywhere it's actually needed).

- `RegistrationPolicyBucket#occupies_bucket_as_signup?`/`#signup_definitely_occupies_slot_in_bucket?`: single id-or-object-identity comparison, key-based fallback removed.
- `SignupBucketFinder`/`FakeSignup`: track bucket **objects** (`bucket`/`requested_bucket`) instead of key strings.
- `EventChangeRegistrationPolicyService`: `bucket_key_mappings` resolves to id (`bucket_id_mappings`) up front instead of round-tripping through a removed bucket's key at every use site; the simulation bridges a real signup's persisted bucket to its detached candidate counterpart via one clearly-commented key lookup (structurally required — see comments), instead of using key everywhere.
- Removed `RegistrationPolicy#bucket_with_key` and the `bucket_key`/`requested_bucket_key` readers on `Signup`/`SignupRequest`/`SignupRankedChoice`, since `SignupBucketFinder` was meant to be their only caller. Turned out there were a handful of other legitimate callers (deprecated GraphQL `bucketKey`/`requestedBucketKey` mutation arguments, and `import_convention_data_service.rb`) — those got an inlined equivalent lookup rather than resurrecting the shared method.
- `sync_buckets_from_hash!`'s key-based fallback (from #11870) is untouched, as planned — dropping the `key` column is tracked separately.

## No GraphQL/frontend changes

`update_event`'s `bucket_key_mappings` argument, `BucketKeyMappingInputType`, and the frontend bucket remapping UI are unchanged. The registration policy editor never has real bucket ids for candidate buckets (confirmed via `RegistrationPolicy#as_json`/`RegistrationPolicyBucket#as_json`, which deliberately omit `id`), so `to_key` must stay key-based — it can name a bucket being created in the very same edit.

## Test plan

- [x] `bin/rubocop` clean on all changed files
- [x] Full affected model/service/graphql test suites pass (274 tests, 0 failures)
- [x] Reviewed diff manually for the trickier identity-comparison edge cases (detached candidate buckets, FakeSignup wiring, `RegistrationPolicyBucketTest#signup_definitely_occupies_slot_in_bucket?`)

author: soney
body:
## NSF

It's the one mark the white knockout can't carry. The seal is **209 shapes across four fills** (`#005699`, `#99add2`, `#d3b34e`, `#fff`) **plus a radial gradient**, and its design lives entirely in the tonal differences between them — `brightness(0)` collapses all of that to a single white, so every internal boundary disappears and it renders as a featureless blob.

The other five survive because they're wordmarks or monochrome, where boundaries are shape edges rather than colour changes: Adobe 9 shapes, Google 6, UMSI 22, and misc has 127 but only one fill.

So NSF alone is exempted and given back the white surface it was drawn for. `box-sizing: content-box` keeps the mark at its full 100px inside the plate rather than shrinking it to 84.

That does mean one plated mark among five knockouts. I think it reads as deliberate rather than accidental — it's an emblem sitting among wordmarks — but it's a judgment call, and the alternative is putting all six back on plates and losing the white look you asked for.

## Captions

The logos no longer have a name above them.

**`alt` is now load-bearing.** With the visible caption gone, the img `alt` is the only thing giving each link an accessible name for a screen reader — so dropping it would turn six links into unlabelled ones. The include now says so explicitly.

Applied to the sponsor row as well as the affiliations row; leaving one captioned and the other not would look accidental. Say the word if you meant affiliations only.

author: rsafargalin
body:
Closes #3.

For a directory that is not a repository, the fallback read only bare directory names from `.gitignore` — every line containing `/` or `*` was dropped. So `Generated/**`, `[Dd]ebug/` and `Sources/*/Legacy` did nothing, and those files landed in `map`, `api`, `search` and `lint`.

## Why not a better matcher

Getting from "bare names" to correct means negation, bracket classes, nested `.gitignore` files, "last matching pattern wins" and the anchoring rules. A partial implementation fails **silently** — #8 dropped an entire `Sources` tree and broke `!` re-includes — and a subset nobody can predict the edges of is worse than no gitignore at all.

## Borrowing instead

The project is handed to git as a work tree whose git dir lives in the cache:

```sh
git --git-dir=~/Library/Caches/sextant/gitdir/<hash>.git --work-tree=<root> \
    -C <root> ls-files --others --exclude-standard
```

Every rule then behaves exactly as git defines it, because it *is* git. Nothing is written inside the project — answering a read-only question must not turn someone`s directory into a repository.

## How it was verified

A directory outside any repository, carrying precisely the rules the old reader threw away:

```
.gitignore: Sources/**/Generated/*.swift · [Dd]ebug/ · Sources/Legacy/
5 .swift files on disk → map shows 1: Sources/App/Main.swift
no .git inside the project
```

Also checked against git`s own verdict with `git check-ignore -v`, so the expectation is git`s semantics rather than mine.

author: octalide
body:
Closes #2714.

```toml
[project]
id      = "std"
version = "0.26.0"
mach    = "4.14.0"
```

## The demonstration, with its control

This exists because a comptime gate **cannot** report a syntax requirement — parsing precedes comptime evaluation, so a file using a spelling the running compiler cannot tokenize fails at the grammar rule and the `$error` never runs.

A dependency with deliberately unparseable source, imported by a consumer. **Control, no requirement stated:**

```
error: expected ';' after 'ret'
 --> ./dep/futurelib/src/lib.mach:1:37
```

A grammar rule, pointed into a dependency's source, saying nothing about the compiler being too old. **With `mach = "99.0.0"` in that dependency's manifest:**

```
error: dependency 'futurelib' requires mach 99.0.0 or newer; running 4.14.0
```

I ran the control **after** the positive case and it changed the test: my first probe never imported the dependency, so its source was never parsed and the control passed for the wrong reason. The gate looked like it was beating a parse error that would not have happened. Importing it made the demonstration real.

## Decisions

**It cascades from a dependency, and that is the case that matters.** A consumer builds mach-std, not the file inside it that fails, so the message names the dependency that demands the version rather than the project the user invoked.

**One comparison serves both paths.** The dep resolver reads a dependency's manifest as raw toml rather than through `parse`, so `check_toolchain_str` is factored out. Two implementations would be two chances for the root and dependency paths to disagree about what satisfies a requirement.

**Semver ordering, not string compare.** A string compare calls `"4.9.0"` newer than `"4.14.0"` because `'9' > '1'`. That case is asserted directly. Uses `std.types.semver` rather than a hand-rolled compare.

**An absent key means no requirement**, so every existing manifest is unchanged. A present but unparseable one is an **error**, not an ignored key — a typo'd requirement that silently permits everything is worse than stating none.

**An unparseable *running* version reads as satisfied.** Not the project's fault, and treating it as a shortfall would refuse a development build from every manifest that states a requirement.

## Tests, mutation-checked

Both new tests were mutated and both bit:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| gate always satisfied | FAIL |
| attribution dropped, dependency reported as root | FAIL |

Root behaviour verified end to end by running the compiler: requirement above the running version refused; equal and below accepted; malformed refused; absent accepted.

## Verification

`mach test .` 1267 passed, 0 failed. Full linux `int` suite passes.

author: jonyoder
body:
The last finding from rstudio/package-manager#19466 — and **most of it does not hold.**

## What F15 claims, and what's actually true

Filed as *"normalized-versus-raw version display is inconsistent between subcommands."* Traced against the code:

**No subcommand can print a raw version key for a resolved version.** That information is destroyed in `index/rsfindex.go`, which sets `Version: ver` — the version the *caller asked for* — and discards `bestKey`, the key it actually matched. So the display is already consistent: everything shows normalized. The raw-vs-normalized framing describes something that cannot happen.

What survived triage:

| Sub-issue | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `versions` prints raw keys on its unparseable-keys path | **Left alone, judged correct.** Those keys don't parse, so they can't be normalized, and the message already says exactly that. |
| `deps` echoes the normalization of your *input*, not of the record it resolved | **Real but narrow.** Read from the code; frequency not measured. Noted, not fixed. |
| `walk` printed no version at all | **The actual defect.** Fixed here. |

## The real fix

`walk` takes **one** version of each package and its shape depends on which — yet `walkResult` had no version field. The version chosen was used for the `Metadata` lookup and thrown away. A reader couldn't tell which version produced any edge, and two walks over different snapshots printed identically while describing different graphs.

Adds `SelectedVersions`: text output shows the version beside each name, `--json` gains `selected_versions`.

A **map** rather than turning `packages` into objects, because `packages` is published JSON as of v0.1.0 and changing its element type would break consumers. Built only from names that made it into `Packages`, so the map cannot disagree with the list beside it.

## ⚠️ Selection moved ahead of the depth cutoff

At the cutoff we already hold the version list, so selecting costs nothing — and with the cutoff first, `--depth 1` reported a version for the root and nothing else. Verified by putting the check back: `SelectedVersions = map[flask:3.0.1]`, alone.

One behavior change follows: a package **at** the cutoff whose selection fails is now classified as having no usable version, where before the cutoff returned first and it was reported as plainly reachable. Having no selectable version is a fact about the package, not about how deep the walk happened to go.

## Partial by design

Absent and uncaptured packages get **no entry**, because no version was chosen for them. A missing entry is not "version unknown" — the category lists already say why — so text output prints the bare name rather than inventing a placeholder. Names under `unusable_metadata` **do** get an entry: a version was selected and its metadata then failed to parse. All three cases are pinned by tests.

## Verification

Production snapshot, not just fixtures:

```
$ pyresolve walk flask --depth 2
...
werkzeug 3.1.8
zipp 4.1.0

33 package(s) reachable
```

All 33 labelled, and `--depth 1` labels the ones at the cutoff.

- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` pass; `gofmt -l .` empty.
- Feature verified to fail without itself, and the cutoff reorder verified load-bearing independently.

## Status of #19466

With this, **every finding is closed or explicitly judged invalid.** F1–F8 fixed previously; F9, F10, F11, F13, F14 in the last two PRs; F12 relocated to rstudio/package-manager#18646; F5's residue deliberately open pending R-data measurement.

author: theodorstorm
body:
Closes #356. Closes #352.

## What a user gets

**One ordinary action no longer erases their configuration.** Two readers treated "the JSON parsed" as "the JSON is usable". A `catch` handles malformed input but cannot fire on input that parses into the wrong shape — `{}`, `[]`, `null`, `{"projects":[]}` are all valid JSON. Those fell through to an empty fallback, and the next write persisted that emptiness over the real file.

The user-visible consequence was total: one CLI choice, or one Codex launch, erased every stored project preference and wake target. The next session asked which CLI to use in every project they had already answered for. The second instance, in the lifecycle log guard, discarded suppression state and produced duplicate arrival signals.

**Declining the server install now says what it did.** Previously a user selected their agent CLIs, approved the exact list of files that would change, declined the server install, and got *"Installation was declined. No server package or server state was changed."* with exit status 0 — while **zero** files were written. Nothing said the agent configuration they had just approved was also skipped, and they would not find out until an agent failed to see Borg.

## How

The fix is the property, not the two call sites: readers return a third state — present-but-unreadable, distinct from absent — and writers refuse rather than overwrite when they see it. The refusal names the file so the user can act on it. Both input classes, malformed and valid-wrong-shape, reach that state in both readers.

The decline message is scoped on `options.initializeServer`. `borg setup` gets the agent-configuration sentence and setup recovery; `borg assimilate` and `borg server cube init`, which never offer to configure agents, get server-only recovery. The all-or-nothing transaction is deliberate and is unchanged — this changes what the command *says*, not what it does.

## Verification

Every claim below was executed, and each control demonstrated red before green.

- **Data preservation, 6 of 6 combinations** against the shipped `dist`: malformed and valid-wrong-shape input × `lifecycle-log-state.json`, `launch.json`, `codex-wake-targets.json`. Every one refuses, names its path, leaks no parser text, and preserves the file byte-for-byte.
- **Flow discrimination** proven by mutation, not by reading: restoring the unconditional message reddens the assimilate-path assertions; each punctuation mutant reddens only its own path's guards, so the two are independent checks rather than one covering both.
- **Message bytes** compared against the objects they had to match — the assimilate line is byte-identical to what `main` shipped, not merely well-formed.
- Full unit suite 145/145 files, 2088/2088 tests; `npm run check`; `npm run test:release` 41/41; build; committed `dist` byte-identical to a rebuild.

## Review

Three gates, three rounds. Code Review and Security approved; Release Quality blocked the first candidate on a defect both had passed — the new decline sentence was emitted on the `borg assimilate` path, which never offered to configure agents, telling that user to re-run setup when their blocker was a server. The guarding tests were unconditional and would have passed a wrong-flow message, which is the same class of defect as the bug itself. Both were corrected.

A second round caught a punctuation regression against `main` in the same shipped sentence and was folded rather than deferred.

## Not exercised

The accept path was never executed in any round, because accepting installs `borgmcp-server` globally. It is bounded by the diff rather than by assumption: every changed line in `first-run-server.ts` is inside `if (decision !== 'yes')`, so the accept branch is byte-unchanged from `main`. No server was started and no operator state was touched — all execution ran under an isolated `HOME` against read-only clones of the committed objects.

## Overview

Adds configurable AWS Pod Identity Webhook annotation prefixes to the control-plane and dataplane charts.

The standard webhook annotation is `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`, but clusters can install the webhook with a custom `--annotation-prefix`. This PR adds `global.AWS_POD_IDENTITY_ANNOTATION_PREFIX`, defaulting to `eks.amazonaws.com`, and derives the relevant service-account annotation keys from it.

Changes include:

- Configure the prefix for control-plane Flyte and artifacts service accounts.
- Configure the prefix for dataplane system and workflow service accounts.
- Evaluate control-plane service-account annotations with Helm `tpl` so templated keys render correctly.
- Update the standalone EKS Auto Mode example to use and define the shared prefix.
- Add focused control-plane and dataplane fixtures for a custom `customer.example.com` prefix.
- Update AWS fixtures to layer the canonical `values.aws.yaml` overlay.
- Document custom-prefix configuration.
- Replace stale control-plane links to deleted local AWS and GCP deployment guides.

## Compatibility

The default remains `eks.amazonaws.com`, so standard EKS deployments require no values changes.

Clusters using a custom webhook prefix can set:

```yaml
global:
  AWS_POD_IDENTITY_ANNOTATION_PREFIX: customer.example.com
```

The value should be configured in both control-plane and dataplane values when both charts use AWS IAM roles.

# Plan: Index extracted Finance reports in Brain

## Goal

Successful Finance report extraction writes extracted text into the linked
FINANCE-domain `Document` and `BrainSource`, but currently emits only the
interpretation event. Emit the existing public-safe `document.updated` event
from the same successful transaction so the established
`knowledge.sync.document` pipeline automatically indexes the document while
preserving its `FINANCE` access domain.

## Risk tier

- `high`

This is a narrow domain change, but it activates an existing asynchronous
workflow and shared knowledge-indexing behavior. The change remains bounded to
four files and far below the high-risk size cap.

## Out of scope

- Customer rollout, production release execution, or feature-flag changes.
- Private or customer data in code, tests, logs, proof, or PR metadata.
- Schema changes, migrations, direct database writes, or `prisma db push`.
- Backfilling Finance imports extracted before this fix.
- UI changes or new demo fixtures.
- Changes to workflow derivation, knowledge handlers, retrieval policy,
  authorization, caches, Azure Search, or agent tools. The existing document
  context-graph handler is changed only to refuse non-`WORKSPACE` documents so
  protected Finance text cannot enter the currently unscoped context graph.

## Files to touch

- `packages/domain/src/finance-import-extraction.ts`
- `packages/domain/src/finance-import-extraction.test.ts`
- `packages/workflows/src/handlers/context-graph-sync.ts`
- `packages/workflows/src/handlers/context-graph-sync.test.ts`

## Demo exposure

No new UI or seeded product state is introduced. The behavior is a backend
correctness repair for the existing customer-neutral Finance upload workflow;
safe synthetic post-deploy proof will use an internal validation workspace and
will not be published as customer proof.

## UX spine decisions

No workspace UI paths change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The non-skipped success path of `completeFinanceReportImportExtraction`
  emits exactly one `document.updated` event in the same transaction as the
  document/content update and existing `finance-report-import.extracted`
  event.
- [x] The new event uses `aggregateType: "Document"`, the linked Finance-owned
  document id as both `aggregateId` and `payload.documentId`, and includes no
  filename, source text, file hash, extracted evidence, or customer facts.
- [x] Skipped, stale, failed, or rejected extraction paths do not emit the new
  event.
- [x] Same-package domain coverage asserts both success events, exact public-
  safe payloads, no private/source-content leakage, and no additional event on
  the already-completed no-op path.
- [x] Existing unmodified workflow tests prove `document.updated` derives one
  deduplicated `knowledge.sync.document` job and the document handler passes
  the persisted `FINANCE` access domain to chunk indexing.
- [x] The diff stays within the four-file allowlist, changes no schema or
  migration, and remains within the high-risk 400 non-doc LOC/15-file cap.
- [x] Focused tests, `npm run check`, and the database-independent
  `npm run build` all pass.
- [x] The context-graph document handler returns without an upsert for a
  `FINANCE` document, while retaining the existing behavior for a `WORKSPACE`
  document, with focused handler coverage for both paths.

## Post-merge gate

- [ ] After merge and deployment, a real synthetic import on the exact release
  proves the document-update event, successful document-index job,
  FINANCE-domain PostgreSQL/Azure index state, positive Finance-authorized
  list/search/Ask-citation/download/agent retrieval, and safe non-Finance
  exclusion across those same paths, with no Finance report context-graph
  object or content, without publishing source content.

## Test plan

```sh
npx vitest run packages/domain/src/finance-import-extraction.test.ts
npx vitest run packages/workflows/src/outbox.test.ts
npx vitest run packages/workflows/src/handlers/knowledge-sync.test.ts
npx vitest run packages/workflows/src/handlers/context-graph-sync.test.ts
npm run check
npm run build
```

## Rollback

Pure application code with no schema or migration. Revert the commit to stop
emitting the additional event. Existing Finance extraction and interpretation
continue unchanged. Already-created events, workflow jobs, and correctly
FINANCE-scoped knowledge chunks remain valid audit/index state and must not be
deleted. Reverting the context-graph guard must not occur unless that graph
first gains and enforces equivalent access-domain authorization.

## Labels this PR needs

None.

## Summary

Implements R10-B1 as a write-time evidence/storage remediation. A refresh now
persists the existing user-base `AccountSnapshot` plus an atomic
account-currency companion when the currencies differ. Public portfolio,
dashboard, history, OpenAPI, generated TypeScript, and frontend presentation
remain unchanged; R10-B2 owns that cutover.

## Git identity

- Exact base: `003b9430651e690067eea4ebd39682c18dde2285`
- Exact final HEAD: `fd4f8fde19e062797dac18e04a12f5f8923818fd`
- Branch: `remediation/0.1-r10b1-account-currency-evidence`

## Changed files

- `backend/python/app/modules/market_data/requirements.py`
- `backend/python/app/modules/market_data/service.py`
- `backend/python/app/modules/snapshots/account_projection.py`

- `backend/python/tests/test_market_backed_snapshot_refresh_integration.py`
- `backend/python/tests/test_market_data_requirements.py`
- `backend/python/tests/test_r10b1_account_currency_evidence.py`
- `backend/python/tests/test_r10b_account_currency_representability.py`
- `backend/python/tests/test_r10b_account_currency_representability_integration.py`
- `backend/python/tests/test_snapshot_refresh_executor_integration.py`
- `backend/python/tests/test_version_0_1_acceptance.py`
- `src/app/version-0-1-final-audit.test.ts`
- `ChatGPT/audits/0.1-r10b1-account-currency-evidence.md`
- `ChatGPT/steps/0.1-remediation.md`
- `!docs/01-architecture/02-modules.md`
- `!docs/02-domain-model.md`

## R10-B blocker mapping

R10-B correctly ended NOT READY because native `*ByCurrency` breakdowns could
not represent a mixed-native account total in `Account.currency`, and the
physical snapshot had no account-currency liability scalar. R10-B1 removes
both blockers at snapshot write time. The historical R10-B audit remains
unchanged.

## Companion snapshot design and authority

- Same currency: one physical snapshot; it is both aggregate and
  account-presentation evidence.
- Different currencies: one primary snapshot in `User.baseCurrency` and one
  companion snapshot in `Account.currency`.
- Both identities share account, timestamp, granularity, source, calculation
  version, and canonical evidence, with distinct deterministic IDs.
- Primary remains the sole NetWorth, aggregate portfolio, global dashboard,
  and history input.
- Companion is the future R10-B2 account-presentation authority.
- No calculation-version bump; primary values/items remain unchanged for the
  same evidence.

## Valuation behavior

- Mixed EUR/USD: a CZK primary and EUR companion persist exact investment
  value and cost basis.
- Liability: the CZK primary persists converted liability while the EUR
  companion persists the exact native EUR liability in `liabilitiesValue`.
- Items: companion `value` and `costBasis` are in `Account.currency`; native
  value/cost fields retain their original currencies.
- Historical net deposits, realized P/L, fees, and taxes consume source and
  target legs at the event-date as-of boundary, never snapshot-time FX.

## Exact CZK-pivot contract

- The ?NB provider remains `foreign -> CZK` only.
- Same currency consumes no FX evidence.
- Foreign -> CZK consumes one direct persisted observation.
- CZK -> foreign consumes the target foreign -> CZK observation.
- Foreign -> foreign consumes source -> CZK and target -> CZK observations.
- Pivoted account-currency valuation rejects non-?NB legs.
- Exact arithmetic uses one high-precision `Decimal` expression:
  `amount * source_to_czk / target_to_czk`.
- There is no float, intermediate rounding, repair, inverse/cross provider
  lookup, or live read.
- A non-representable final MONEY value fails closed.
- Internal audit version 2 records exact direct rate IDs and
  `pivot_source`/`pivot_target` roles; direct-only version 1 remains stable.
- PostgreSQL proof confirms no synthetic `USD -> EUR source=cnb` row exists.

## Atomicity, ordering, replay, and concurrency

- Currency identities are advisory-locked in sorted canonical order.
- Canonical and market evidence is locked once.
- Both complete evidence graphs and projections are validated before either
  insert.
- Primary, companion, and both item sets share one writer transaction.
- Missing, stale, future, wrong-provider, wrong-timestamp, wrong-pair,
  ambiguous, conflicting, corrupt, or non-representable evidence creates no
  partial pair.
- Exact replay leaves row counts and IDs unchanged.
- Concurrent identical refreshes converge to one primary and one companion,
  with one created/replayed pair and no deadlock.

## NetWorth and public isolation

- Three active accounts with two companions produce five physical
  `AccountSnapshot` rows but exactly three NetWorth-selected primary IDs.
- Companions never increase the required account count or global total.
- Portfolio aggregate, selected-account browser behavior, dashboard, and
  history remain unchanged in B1.
- No public endpoint or response field was added.
- OpenAPI and `src/generated/python-api.ts` are unchanged.
- No schema, Prisma, Alembic migration, database revision, or financial scalar
  column changed.
- R10-C is not started.

## Verification

- Focused backend: **888 passed**, 0 failed.
- Dedicated PostgreSQL: **PostgreSQL 16.10**, **70 passed**, 0 failed,
  0 skipped, 0 xfailed.
- Full backend: Ruff, format, mypy, and checks passed; **3,174 passed**,
  630 environment-gated skips, 65 existing deprecation warnings.
- Coverage: **89.03%** (required gate 70%).
- Frontend: **551 passed**, 5 existing skips; ESLint and TypeScript passed.
- Prisma generation and validation: passed.
- Python API drift: passed; OpenAPI/generated TypeScript unchanged.
- Scoped Prettier and `git diff --check`: passed.
- npm audit baseline (informational): 11 findings ? 1 low, 1 moderate,
  8 high, 1 critical; no automatic remediation.
- Remote CI on exact final HEAD: Backend Python PASS; Database Schema PASS; Frontend PASS.

## Status

- R10-B remains historically `completed ? NOT READY`.
- R10-B1 persisted account-currency valuation evidence: implemented.
- Next: `0.1-R10-B2 ? account-currency read/API/frontend presentation`.
- R10-C not started.
- Version 0.1 remains in progress.
- Working tree: clean after publication.
- PR state: draft, open, unmerged.

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
coachtui
body:
A 1:30 voice note reported "Couldn't save your note" and wrote nothing. Two independent defects combined to make recording length the trigger.

## Why length is the trigger

The transcript parser emits one full object per idea (raw/cleaned text, title, why-it-matters, entities, tags, hints) as non-streamed JSON, so generation time scales with how much was said. A 20s note is a couple of objects; 1:30 is closer to ten and several thousand output tokens — which is where gpt-4o crossed the 60s budget.

## Defect 1 — the nested budgets were identical

| Layer | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| ml-service → OpenAI (`parser.py`) | 60s | 90s |
| api → ml-service (`mlService.ts`) | 60s | 105s |
| mobile → api (`api.ts` saveTranscript) | 90s | 180s |

The API gave the ML service exactly the 60s the ML service gave OpenAI, and the API's clock starts first — so a parse that would have returned at 58s was always read as a failure. Nested timeouts have to decrease going inward or the inner layer can never report anything.

Nothing waits on the client budget (RecordScreen navigates to Home immediately; the notification fires whenever the save resolves), so a long tail costs the user nothing while a premature abort costs them a note.

## Defect 2 — a failed parse threw the note away

`save-transcript` already had a fallback that saves the transcript as a single unparsed object, but it was gated on `checkMLServiceHealth()` rather than on whether the parse succeeded. A timeout isn't unhealthy: health returns true, the parse throws, and the code took the rethrow branch — 500, zero objects written, session marked `failed`. The safety net existed and could never fire for the one failure it was there for.

Parse failure now degrades to that same fallback. A write failure still surfaces as a 500, since at that point there's no degraded path left.

## Also

- `transcribeAudio` 60s → 120s. Its body is base64 raw PCM (~1.3MB per 30s) and it fails *silently* into the lower-accuracy Deepgram text, so the tight budget was quietly degrading exactly the long notes that most need the accuracy.
- `test-setup` loads the untracked root `.env.local` and falls back to a placeholder `OPENAI_API_KEY`. `transcriptionService` builds its OpenAI client at module scope, so any suite importing it died at import time.

## Verification

- New `saveTranscriptRoute.test.ts`, 6 cases. The key one was confirmed to **fail against the unfixed route and pass against the fixed one**.
- Full API suite: **48 suites, 280 tests, all passing**. `voiceSessionService.test.ts` was failing on `main` before this (missing key at import) and now passes.
- API typechecks clean. Mobile's 3 typecheck errors are pre-existing and untouched (verified by stashing).
- ml-service tests were **not** run — no venv locally and `httpx`/`pytest` aren't installed. `parser.py` compiles; the change is a named constant plus two substitutions.

body:
[impl agent, gpt-5.6-sol]

## Summary

- fail closed when vDSO discovery, required-symbol resolution, protection changes, writes, or post-write verification are incomplete
- bind the required patch set to the Tool's syscall subscriptions and add the existing `getrandom` syscall path to the x86-64 and aarch64 vDSO patch tables
- restore RX protection even after a write failure, then read back every final patch byte before returning a typed `VdsoPatchReceipt`
- bracket the mechanism with missing-symbol and corrupted-byte mutations, plus a real ptrace tracee positive case

Fixes rrnewton/reverie#408. Related: rrnewton/hermit#1931.

## Determinism

The patch does not change Detcore clock resolution, virtual-time progression, scheduling, or random-byte generation. It closes bypasses around those existing deterministic implementations: every subscribed vDSO wrapper must be resolved, rewritten to its syscall thunk, restored to RX, and read back byte-for-byte before the guest continues. A missing or mismatched patch now stops initialization instead of allowing host vDSO behavior to escape the Tool. `getrandom` remains handled by the existing subscribed syscall path; the new thunk only ensures the vDSO fast path reaches it.

- Repository: `rrnewton/reverie`.

author: fthiess
body:
Two live-test findings on OFC-391, one commit each.

---

## 1. Unlisted brothers were being copied (N164)

Ticking an unlisted brother as an administrator put his address on the clipboard with the rest.

**D167 got this wrong explicitly, not by omission.** Its "deliberately not done" list said unlisted brothers stay in, reasoning that *D124 hides a record from peers, not from staff, and the staffer has deliberately selected him*. Every clause is true and it still reaches the wrong answer — because it answers **"may staff see this record?"** when the question this feature turns on is **"may this address be republished to other brothers?"** That is the exact distinction D167's own fork 2 had already drawn for `shareEmail`, and then failed to carry across. A brother who hides his **whole record** from his peers has made a *stronger* privacy statement than one who merely turned off `shareEmail`; honouring the weaker signal while ignoring the stronger was incoherent.

⚠ **The rule now recorded: on this feature, "should X be skipped?" is settled by the republication test, never by the visibility table.**

**Audited rather than patched**, since one gap implies others: `PrivacyFlags` has five members and only `shareEmail` governs an email address; `unlisted` and the `deceased`/`debrothered` pair are the only other record-level signals; `allowNewsletterEmail` is settled out of scope by N162; `allowShareWithMITAA` governs a third-party data share. **`unlisted` was the only gap.**

Folded into the existing `skippedPrivate` bucket — to the user, "he asked us not to" is one answer, and the toast already pairs deceased with de-brothered on the same logic. A brother who is both counts **once**; a test pins that, since a double count would stop the total reconciling.

---

## 2. The notice never went away (N165)

Forrest: *"the toasts don't disappear — you have to manually close them. Is there a UX reason for this?"* There was one, and it was too cautious.

N163 kept it permanent because a self-clearing message imposes a time limit on reading (SC 2.2.1). But a **status message** is governed by **SC 4.1.3**, which the `<output>` live region already satisfies completely — a screen reader is handed the whole text the instant it appears, however briefly it shows. The only reader genuinely at risk is a **sighted slow one**, and the mitigation for that is **pausing the countdown on hover and focus**, not permanence. Standing forever protected nobody and cost everybody a click.

**An error notice is exempt** and still waits to be acknowledged — it reports that the copy did *not* happen, and letting it time out re-creates exactly the failure it was built to prevent.

Two details worth keeping: the dismiss callback is `useCallback`-stable, or a fresh closure lands in the effect deps and restarts the countdown on every re-render, so the notice never clears — a bug that looks just like the feature not working. And the pause covers **focus** as well as hover, or a keyboard user tabbing toward the button has it vanish under their hands.

---

## Verified

Both changes' tests were watched **failing against the pre-change code and passing after**. `verify:fast` green (1217 tests); e2e green (80).

The auto-dismiss tests use **Playwright's fake clock** rather than real waits, so the spec still runs in ~6 s instead of growing by a minute: the notice survives 9 s and is gone by 11 s (proving the disappearance is the timer's doing), hovering holds it through 30 s, and the error notice survives 60 s.

Touches the privacy surface, so it waits for Forrest's merge per Gate 4.

author: runway-github[bot]
body:
- fix(ci): restore exec bit on hermesc and shell scripts in node_modules (#34004)

## **Description**

The EAS/OTA pipelines transport `node_modules` as a plain zip artifact,
which strips Unix executable bits, so consumers call
`restore-node-modules-permissions` to put them back. Its globs required
an exact `bin` path segment (`*/bin/*`), which never matched the
platform-suffixed directories `hermes-compiler` uses: `linux64-bin`,
`osx-bin`, `win64-bin`.

Metro spawns `hermesc` directly during bundling, so OTA pushes fail
with:

```
Error: spawn .../node_modules/hermes-compiler/hermesc/linux64-bin/hermesc EACCES
```

This became reachable when React Native `0.83.6` (#32281) moved
`hermesc` out of the `react-native` package. Previously it lived at
`react-native/sdks/hermesc/<os>-bin/hermesc`, which the existing
`*/sdks/*` glob covered incidentally. `hermes-compiler`'s flat layout
matches none of the four existing patterns.

This also covers `*.sh` scripts, which are spawned directly (Xcode build
phases, packager helpers) and carry the same exposure. They aren't
failing today only because native builds use the tarball/cache path,
which preserves permissions.

Failing run:
https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/actions/runs/30454324689/job/90593099632

### Why this surfaced now

`release/8.3.1-ota` had identical inputs (RN `0.83.6`, `hermes-compiler`
`0.14.1`, byte-identical CI files) but its OTA run failed earlier at
**Fingerprint Mismatch Guard**, which skipped the bundling jobs
entirely, so it never executed this path. `release/8.4.1-ota` is the
first release to get past that guard since the upgrade.

### Scope reviewed

Only the zip-artifact path is affected. Reviewed all `node_modules`
transport modes:

| Transport | Used by | Preserves exec bit | Affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/cache` | `build.yml` on `release/*` | Yes | No |
| zstd tarball via `tar` | `build.yml` other branches | Yes | No |
| plain zip artifact | EAS/OTA workflows | No | Yes |

Affected call sites are the three consumers of this action:
`push-eas-update.yml` (PR deps and base-branch deps) and
`eas-update-platform.yml`. All three pass `working-directory` correctly.
`build.yml` is unaffected and correctly does not call this action.

I also enumerated every executable file in `node_modules` (2,343) to
find remaining gaps. Excluding noise (packages shipping
`.md`/`.json`/`.ts` as 755), the only spawnable ones still uncovered are
