author: raphaelvigee
body:
Adds `test_race` / `xtest_race`: the same targets as `test` / `xtest`, built with `-race`.

```
heph run //mypkg:test_race@v=dev
heph run 'label(test-race)'
```

## Shape

Race instrumentation is a whole-program property — every archive in the link, stdlib included, has to agree — so this is a new build **factor** rather than a flag on one target. It rides the address as `race=1` and threads down the entire graph, so first-party, thirdparty and stdlib all resolve to race-instrumented archives kept separate from the ordinary ones.

`test_race` is a separate *name* rather than an addr arg on `test` because race is opt-in: it is several times slower to build and to run. For the same reason it is labelled `test-race` / `go-test-race` and deliberately does **not** carry `test`, so `heph run 'label(test)'` keeps meaning the ordinary suite. Both together is `label(test) || label(test-race)`.

The pipeline is `go list -race` (the file set *and* the import graph differ), `go tool compile -race` per package, `go install -race std` into its own `pkg/<goos>_<goarch>_race` dir, and `go tool link -race`. `runtime/race` is seeded into the link explicitly — it carries the prebuilt TSan runtime but **nothing imports it**, because `go build -race` injects it into the link itself; without the seed the link fails on undefined `__tsan_*` symbols.

## Two per-platform differences, both forced by Go

Neither changes what `test_race` means — it behaves identically on all three supported targets.

**cgo.** Go's `runtime/race` is a cgo package everywhere except darwin, which ships `race_darwin_<arch>.go` with syso-derived symbol info instead. So a darwin race build stays as hermetic as an ordinary one (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, no C toolchain at all), while linux enables cgo for the std install and stages a compiler — a new `cc` provider option defaulting to the hostbin `//@heph/bin:cc`. Only the std install needs it: the per-package compiles are pure Go, and the link resolves the TSan runtime internally. Both were verified with an empty `PATH` and no compiler present.

**buildmode.** `go build` refuses `-buildmode=pie` with `-race` on linux. `go tool link` — which is what this plugin calls — does *not* enforce that: it accepts the combination and produces a binary that dies at startup with `ThreadSanitizer failed to allocate`. So linux race links `-buildmode=exe`, and `-shared` drops with it to match the archives `go install -race` produced.

## No cache invalidation

The `race` addr arg is omitted when unset, and the golist/compile def hashes contribute nothing when it is false, so every ordinary target's address and cache key are byte-identical to what they were before this landed. Both hashes are pinned by tests that fail if that stops being true.

A `race` value other than `1` is rejected rather than ignored — silently building without instrumentation and reporting a clean run is the one failure mode of this feature a user cannot spot.

## Testing

Unit tests cover the factor threading, flag emission, the `runtime/race` seeding, the platform rules, the labels, and the two cache-key properties.

`crates/plugingo-e2e/tests/race.rs` covers what no spec assertion can — that the binary is *actually* instrumented:

- a package with a real data race **fails** under `test_race`, with the detector's report;
- the same package **passes** under plain `test` (the control — pins the failure on the instrumentation, not a broken fixture);
- a clean package **passes** under `test_race`.

Verified end to end on darwin/arm64 locally and on linux/arm64 in a container. These build std with `-race`, so they are slower than the rest of the suite.

body:
## Problema
No app **Dias sem Doença**, ao registrar/corrigir os dias doentes e atualizar a página, o valor voltava ao anterior.

## Causa
O service worker (`sw.js`) usava estratégia *cache-first* para **todos** os GET e acabava cacheando também as requisições de sincronização com o Firebase (`state.json` / `_at.json`). Fluxo:
1. A primeira leitura da nuvem era guardada no cache do SW.
2. As gravações (`PUT`) iam certo para a nuvem — o SW ignora não-GET.
3. Ao atualizar, a leitura retornava a **cópia velha do cache** (o `cache: "no-store"` do `fetch` não ignora o service worker), sobrescrevendo o localStorage. → os dados "voltavam".

## Correção
- `sw.js`: o fetch handler agora só cacheia requisições de **mesma origem** (o app em si). Requisições de outra origem (Firebase) vão sempre direto à rede.
- Cache `v5` → `v6`, para que o `activate` purgue as respostas velhas presas no cache dos aparelhos.

Nenhuma mudança em `app.js`/`index.html`/`styles.css`, então não foi preciso regenerar o standalone.

## Teste
- `node --check sw.js` e `node --check app.js` OK.

author: kno
body:
Part of #361

PR **2 of 5** for `17c-profile-body-metrics`. Follows #384 (profile scalars, merged). Adds the bodyweight time series. Nothing consumes it yet — generation reads it in PR 3, volume in PR 4.

## Why a table and not a column

Weight is the one body metric that must be a series rather than a scalar. A column would answer "what do you weigh" and permanently discard "what did you weigh in March" — and progress over time is the dimension users care about most in this category. `user_weight_entries` is 1:many with the user, so there is deliberately **no unique index on `user_id`**, unlike `user_profiles` and `user_preferences`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "user_weight_entries" (
  "id"          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "user_id"     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "weight_kg"   numeric(5, 2) NOT NULL,
  "recorded_at" timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "created_at"  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Indexed on `(user_id, recorded_at)` — a plain index, which is what the PR 4 resolution rule ("nearest reading at or before the session") will query against. The cascade follows the universal convention for user-scoped child tables and inherits the deletion story established in #354.

## The CI list — the point of this PR

`user-weight-entry.integration.test.ts` is added to the real-Postgres job's hardcoded file list (`.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`) **in this same PR**, and the edit was verified by re-reading the file afterwards.

This matters because nine `apps/api` integration suites sit outside that list and **never execute anywhere** — they pass by skipping (#382, approved). Change `17b` shipped four unproven guarantees exactly that way: the assertions existed, read as coverage, and had never run once. A test outside that list is not a weaker test, it is not a test.

## Contracts

`WeightEntryDTO` and `CreateWeightEntryResponse`. The response carries `wasFirstEntry` — the signal PR 4 needs to announce the volume shift at the right moment. **The notice UI itself is not in this PR**; only the field that makes it possible.

## Privacy boundary — unchanged, still not exercised

Nothing here renders a weight into a prompt, so nothing reaches Langfuse yet. PR 3 carries the redaction module that makes the model input and the trace input diverge, plus its fail-closed backstop.

Two constraints that hold regardless: these values never enter an output schema (`WorkoutExerciseSchema`, `WorkoutSessionSchema`, `WorkoutProgramSchema` feed `.withStructuredOutput`, and #357 is the cautionary tale), and they never enter an observability event — `ObservabilityMetadata` blocks nested objects structurally, **but a scalar `weightKg` would compile fine**, so that one is review discipline rather than a type guarantee.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm type-check` — exit 0, all 7 workspaces
- [x] `pnpm -r --if-present test:coverage` — exit 0; api 176 files (+3), web 158 (+2); thresholds held (api ≥85%, web ≥90%)
- [x] `pnpm build` — exit 0
- [x] Migration `0028` present, journal `idx: 28`; the directory-driven guard test from `17b` covers it automatically
- [x] Integration suite present **and on the CI list**, verified by re-reading the workflow

## Review size

680 non-test lines, 875 test. Within the 800-line non-test budget, so no exception is needed — but it is well above the ~180–250 forecast, and reported as measured rather than trimmed. Unlike the `17b` overruns, this one is implementation rather than test mass.

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a full bodyweight time-series feature spanning API, web, and contracts, including persistence, routes, client/server wiring, and UI on the profile page.

New Features:
- Add a user_weight_entries table and repository to store per-user bodyweight readings as a time series, including transactional computation of whether an entry is the user’s first.
- Expose authenticated GET/POST /weight-entries API routes with validation, returning typed responses including a wasFirstEntry flag.
- Introduce WeightEntryDTO and CreateWeightEntryResponse contracts and wire them into the shared contracts package.
- Add a bodyweight entry form and read-only list to the profile page, backed by server actions and an API client that operate via the existing session cookie.

Enhancements:
- Extend the profile page server component to fetch bodyweight entries alongside the profile and degrade gracefully to an empty series on fetch failure.
- Add i18n messages and tests for the new weight-entry form, list, and validation errors in both English and Spanish.

CI:
- Add the user-weight-entry Postgres integration test suite to the real-Postgres CI job’s hardcoded test list to ensure it actually runs.

Tests:
- Add unit, integration, and route tests for the user-weight-entry repository (including real Postgres coverage of cascade, concurrency, and ordering), routes, web API client, profile page wiring, and WeightEntryForm behavior.
- Extend migration-journal tests to pin the new 0028_user_weight_entries migration and confirm its index in the Drizzle journal.
- Extend contracts tests to assert the new bodyweight types without changing the runtime export surface.

Chores:
- Mark the relevant 17c-profile-body-metrics checklist items as completed in the open-spec task file.

body:
## Summary

- add `TypeSpec(name, fields, sample, ...)` for symbolic regression over custom Julia value types
- compile each TypeSpec into one deterministic private Julia module per process, with exact-source reuse, replacement warnings, and conflicting checkpoint-restore protection
- make fitting transactional so failed searches and rejected warm starts leave the previously fitted Julia state intact
- preserve and replay operators, objectives, complexity mappings, early-stop conditions, templates, and worker definitions across serialization and multiprocessing
- support discrete constants through `mutate` and continuous constant optimization through `scalar_constants` and `with_scalar_constants`
- support typed `OperatorEnum` evaluation, full objectives, `ExpressionSpec`, explicit-keyword `TemplateExpressionSpec`, and custom expression specs that declare TypeSpec support
- remove the legacy positional `TemplateExpressionSpec` constructor and its obsolete compatibility machinery
- pin SymbolicRegression.jl `v2.0.0-beta.5` for custom-value mutation support

## Example

```python
type_spec = TypeSpec(
    name="Vec2",
    fields={"data": "Vector{Float64}"},
    sample="rng -> Vec2(randn(rng, 2))",
    scalar_constants="value -> value.data",
    with_scalar_constants="(value, constants) -> Vec2(constants)",
)

model = PySRRegressor(
    type_spec=type_spec,
    operators={
        1: ["rotate90(x::Vec2) = Vec2([-x.data[2], x.data[1]])"],
        2: ["add_vectors(x::Vec2, y::Vec2) = Vec2(x.data + y.data)"],
    },
    elementwise_loss=(
        "vector_loss(x::Vec2, y::Vec2)::Float64 = "
        "sum(abs2, x.data - y.data)"
    ),
)
```

The documentation includes custom full objectives plus vector-valued, string-valued, heterogeneous tensor, variable-length constant, template, multiprocessing, and checkpoint examples.

body:
Closes #38

## Problem

`SwarmSim.Render --help` advertised `--preset peaceful` and named `peaceful, warbands` as preset
examples, but the runtime registry (`Program.Presets`) accepts only `balanced`,
`strong-separation`, `tight-flocking`, `fast-loose`, `slow-cohesive`. Reproduced on the base commit:

```
$ dotnet run --project SwarmSim.Render -c Release --no-build -- --preset peaceful
Unknown preset 'peaceful'. Use --list-presets to view options.
```

`configs/peaceful.json` / `configs/warbands.json` are real, but they are `--config` inputs, not
preset IDs. Root cause: nothing connected the help text to the registry — `Presets`,
`TryGetPreset` and `PrintPresetList` were all `private`, so `GetHelpText()` hardcoded names and no
check could catch the drift.

## Fix — build the seam, don't just retype the strings

`SwarmSim.Render.csproj` already declares `InternalsVisibleTo Include="SwarmSim.Tests"`, so the
registry can be asserted directly rather than mirrored.

- `Program.PresetIds` — `internal static readonly IReadOnlyList<string>` derived from `Presets`,
  declared textually **after** the array (static field initializers run in declaration order; an
  earlier declaration would read a null `Presets`).
- `Program.IsRegisteredPreset(string?)` — delegates to the same `TryGetPreset` that `Main` uses, so
  tests assert the real matching rules instead of reimplementing them.
- `Program.FormatPresetList()` — holds the text `PrintPresetList()` prints; `PrintPresetList()` is
  now `Console.Write(FormatPresetList())`, byte-identical output.
- `CommandLineOptions.GetHelpText()` — the `--preset` parenthetical and the usage example are
  derived from `PresetIds`; the JSON names moved to the `--config` line. Column alignment of the
  help block is unchanged. The `--config configs/warbands.json -n 5000` example is left as-is —
  that use of `warbands` was already correct.
- `README.md` — verbatim transcript resynced; the now-fixed first bullet of the
  "Known executable-help defects" note removed. The F12-vs-O canonical overlay bullet is
  **kept** (that is #39, out of scope here).
- `SwarmSim.Tests.csproj` — copies `README.md` to the test output so a test can read it from
  `AppContext.BaseDirectory`.

`SwarmSim.Render/Program.cs` lines 1–220 are untouched (first diff hunk starts at 221), so the
`Presets` array keeps the line range that `docs/QUICKSTART.md` and `docs/RENDERER_GUIDE.md` cite.
`FormatPresetList` uses a fully qualified `System.Text.StringBuilder` for the same reason — adding
a `using` would have renumbered that region.

## Tests (5 new, `SwarmSim.Tests/CommandLineOptionsTests.cs`)

- `HelpText_EveryAdvertisedPresetResolvesThroughRegistry` — every `--preset <token>` in the help
  text (minus the literal `NAME` placeholder) resolves through `Program.IsRegisteredPreset`.
- `HelpText_PresetOptionParenthetical_ResolvesThroughRegistry` — every entry in the `(e.g., …)`
  list on the `--preset` line resolves.
- `HelpText_JsonConfigNamesAreNotAdvertisedAsPresets` — help contains neither `--preset peaceful`
  nor `--preset warbands`, and does mention `configs/peaceful.json`.
- `HelpText_MatchesReadmeTranscript` — reads README from `AppContext.BaseDirectory`, extracts the
  fenced block starting `Usage: SwarmSim.Render`, and compares it against
  `GetHelpText() + NewLine + FormatPresetList()` (exactly what `Main` prints for `--help`).
- `PresetIds_AreUniqueAndResolveThroughLookup` — non-empty, no blanks, no case-insensitive
  duplicates, all resolve.

**The drift guard was mutation-tested, not assumed.** Changing one character in the README block
(`default: 400` → `default: 999`) and re-running produced:

```
Failed SwarmSim.Tests.CommandLineOptionsTests.HelpText_MatchesReadmeTranscript [14 ms]
Expected: ···"ent count (default: 400)\n  -b, --benchmar"···
Actual:   ···"ent count (default: 999)\n  -b, --benchmar"···
```

author: iderex
body:
Closes #151

This does not close #107, and the reason is what this change measured. That
issue stays open and carries the finding.

## What failure this prevents

#107 asks for a stored baseline, a stated margin, and a red check when a case
falls below it, with the margin justified by measured run-to-run variance rather
than chosen. Nobody had measured that variance. Building the gate first and
measuring afterwards would have produced a number that looked derived and was
not, in the one place this project cannot afford one.

Measured, on `ubuntu-latest`, with the harness at 200 samples. Inside one job
two runs of one tree never moved more than 0.1 percent over seven jobs. Across
jobs on one commit they came back 13.9 and 17.4 percent apart, because the fleet
handed out two processors. Across two commits that touched nothing either case
measures, one processor was unmoved and the other moved 28.7 percent,
reproducibly on both sides.

So no margin separates a regression from what this fleet does on its own. A
margin above 28.7 percent refuses nothing anybody would ship; one below it
reddens on a change that touched nothing, which is the check people learn to
wave through. This lands the measurement, the route that keeps producing it, and
the document that records what it leaves undecided.

## The means, and why it fits

Rust in `tools/bench`, inside the harness that already produces every number in
this tree, and a workflow that runs it. The alternative for the judgement was a
shell step comparing two files, and it fails this project's first question: a
comparison written in a workflow file has no suite to hold it, so a rule about a
duration would live where no near-miss can reach it. `docs/benchmarks.md` is
Markdown beside the harness it describes, which is where every number this
project quotes already lives.

## What was run, and what came back

    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets
    cargo test --locked --workspace

came back clean, with 45 tests in `bench`.

    cargo run --locked -q -p docs-lint -- --tracked /tmp/tracked.txt --declarations docs/lint-declarations.txt
    examined=25 document(s) tracked=89 path(s) programs=8 declared / 8 used references=11 declared / 11 used

Every check on this pull request came back green, read from the head commit
rather than from the tab.

The judgement in `tools/bench/src/gate.rs` was proven to bite end to end on a
developer machine, against a baseline that machine recorded and then a copy of
it with one median edited to a number the tree cannot reach:

    placeholder-digest-a-megabyte                  60.000 us      116.500 us  REGRESSED +94.1 percent
    refused: placeholder-digest-a-megabyte is +94.1 percent against target/bench/doctored.txt, which is 60.000 us to 116.500 us and is past the 2.0 percent margin
    exit=1

Every branch of that judgement carries a near-miss in the suite, including the
one-character `>=` mistake at the margin, judging the slower pass instead of the
quicker one, and a second baseline claiming one machine's conditions.

## What was not done

No gate. Nothing refuses a number after this change, which is the whole of what
#107 asked for and is not delivered here. The workflow is named for what it does
so that no reader takes a green tick from it as a statement about the
performance bar.

No target from `docs/decisions/0009-performance-bar.md` was measured. Every one
of them is about code this tree does not contain, and the only cases the harness
has are its own placeholders, which measure nothing this project does.

Why the AMD EPYC 9V74 moved 28.7 percent and the AMD EPYC 7763 did not was not
measured. Code layout is the ordinary explanation for a tight loop moving that
far on one microarchitecture and not another, and neither the document nor this
body asserts it, because nothing here took the measurement that would show it.

The two earlier commits on this branch reach a conclusion the third one
corrects, and their messages are left as they were written. The correction says
what was wrong and how it was found, which is the shape this repository asks
for; rewriting them would remove the evidence that the measurement changed the
answer.

This branch has no second reader tonight. The evidence above stands in place of
one.

author: owenpkent
body:
## Summary

- Adds Hypothesis and two property-based test suites: one for the two hostile-input import paths (Data Backup archives, vocabulary packs), one for the prediction-engine invariants the rest of the code is allowed to assume.
- Sweeps the docs for drift, including one doc that was actively wrong about swipe typing.
- **No production code changes.** `git diff --stat` on `src/` and `qml/` is empty for both commits.

Stacked on `feat/compact-view` (#13) so the diff here is just these two commits. It will retarget to `main` automatically when #13 merges.

## Related issue

No issue. Follow-up to a "how are our fuzzing tests" review, which found the suite had no property-based or generated-input coverage at all.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [x] Docs only (second commit)
- [x] Build / CI / tooling (first commit: tests + one new dev dependency)
- [ ] Other (describe)

## What the tests actually assert

**Import hardening** (`tests/test_property_import_hardening.py`, 19 tests). The central property is the one the hardening exists for, stated directly:

> nothing outside the destination directory is ever created, modified or removed, whatever the archive or folder is called

Asserted end-to-end for both `data_export.import_user_data` and `PackManager.import_pack`, against a sandbox holding a canary tree that is snapshotted before and compared byte-for-byte after. Also asserted at the allow-list level: any name the allow-list admits must resolve *inside* the config dir.

Supporting properties: size caps trip on zip metadata rather than extracted bytes (the `ZipInfo` in that test has no backing bytes at all, so it could not pass if the check needed to read the member); arbitrary bytes named `.zip` always come back as the typed `DataExportError` the bridge knows how to display; symlinks are never dereferenced; re-import converges; and a valid archive still round-trips byte-for-byte.

**Engine invariants** (`tests/test_property_prediction_invariants.py`, 20 tests). `_user_total == sum(user_vocab.values())` is checked after *every individual* operation across generated sequences of all twelve mutation paths, so a failure names the operation rather than the sequence that contained it. Plus save/load round-trip, the spatial model's normalisation and monotonicity under a widening radius, fuzzy candidate capping and ranking, and the `_context_buffer` / `_current_word` accounting including the rehydrate path.

## Test plan

- [x] `python check.py` passes locally (ruff, mypy, full pytest)
- [x] Added or updated tests — 39 new, 1 skipped (the symlink case needs privileges Windows does not grant by default)
- [ ] Tested in `python run.py` — n/a, no runtime code changed
- [x] Verified on Windows
- [ ] Verified on Linux — n/a, but CI covers it
- [ ] Verified on macOS — n/a

Suite is 840 tests total after this.

## Accessibility check

n/a — no behaviour, timing, or visual change. The docs commit corrects a claim *about* an existing accessibility gap (see below) but does not alter it.

## Notes for reviewers

**1. The docs commit documents a real, unfixed bug.** `SWIPE_TYPING.md` claimed "tap fall-through is what lets a single key still work normally even when swipe mode is on". That is only true for character keys. The overlay's MouseArea fills the whole keyboard block with `preventStealing: true` and dispatches taps solely through `charKeyRegistry`, which `Main.qml`'s `registerCharKey` populates only for single-character `char` keys. So **while swipe typing is on, Backspace, Tab, Enter, Del and the arrows are dead taps.** Swipe is off by default, which is why it has gone unreported. This PR only corrects the documentation; the fix is separate, and the doc spells out what it should look like and warns against the tempting wrong fix (admitting specials into `charKeyRegistry`, which would put phantom key centres into every swipe shape match).

**2. New dev dependency.** `hypothesis>=6.100.0` in `requirements-dev.txt`. Worth a glance because the OSV gate scans that lockfile. Not a runtime dependency and not in any shipped bundle.

**3. Determinism was a design constraint, not an afterthought.** A property test that only fails on the machine with the right cached corpus is worse than no property test: unreproducible, and it reads as flake. The `alpha-osk` profile in `tests/conftest.py` sets `database=None` and `derandomize=True`, so these cannot pass locally and fail on CI from a stale `.hypothesis` directory. An `alpha-osk-fast` profile (25 examples) exists for iterating.

**4. Two things in these tests are deliberate and look wrong at a glance:**

- The buffer tests assert a per-keystroke **delta**, not a mirror of the screen. Pressing space with no word in progress deliberately commits nothing, so `_context_buffer + _current_word` does not track the document character-for-character after a double space. A strict-equality model flags that as a defect; it isn't one.
- `test_privacy_mode_...` goes through `setPrivacyMode()` rather than setting `_privacy_mode`. My first version poked the flag and failed intermittently: every keystroke calls `_check_password_field_sync()` to close the 200 ms polling race, and that overwrites a hand-set flag on the first press. Only `_privacy_mode_manual` makes it stand down.

**5. Deliberate non-changes in the docs sweep.** `research/SECURITY_AUDIT.md` still says "266+ tests" — it is a dated point-in-time record (*Last audited: April 2026*) where that was correct, so updating it would falsify the record rather than fix drift. Same for `ROADMAP.md`'s historical per-phase counts. A path checker also flagged 17 cited paths that do not exist; 16 are legitimate (proposed files in deferred design docs, runtime config-dir paths, worked examples, references to a sibling repo) and only the `CPP_WINDOWS.md` link was a genuine break — it pointed relatively at a file that exists only on `cpp-rewrite`, so it resolved to nothing on `main`.

Verified 0 broken relative links across all 57 markdown files.

author: pathofleastresistor
body:
Stacked on #11 — review that first; the base retargets to `main` automatically once it merges.

Two unrelated bugs, both surfaced while chasing #11.

## Timestamps broke hydration on every page

Every timestamp was formatted with `toLocale*()` during SSR and again in the browser. The container runs in one fixed zone and the visitor is in another, so the two renders disagreed on the text — and React answers a text mismatch by discarding the server's markup for that subtree and logging error #418. The values were also simply wrong before the client corrected them: what the server emitted was the *server's* local time.

- `useHydrated` — false through SSR and the hydrating render, true immediately after. Built on `useSyncExternalStore`, so the transition is a legal re-render rather than a mismatch of its own.
- `LocalTime` — UTC under a pinned locale on the server pass, the visitor's own zone and locale once hydrated, and a `dateTime` attribute identical across both so anything reading the markup (an agent included) gets an unambiguous instant.
- The dashboard greeting had the same defect in another shape — "Good evening" chosen from the container's clock — and settles the same way.
- `formatVolume` is fixed differently: nothing about a thousands separator needs the visitor's locale, so it is pinned to `en-US` and agrees outright, with no second pass.

## Unknown URLs returned a plain-text server error

No route matched, so middleware never ran and the CSP nonce was never set. `entry.server` read it unconditionally and `RouterContextProvider.get` throws on a context with no value and no default — inside the render of the 404 itself. The route error was handled correctly and then the page built to display it died.

`nonceContext` now carries an empty default, normalised to `undefined` in `entry.server`. Nothing is loosened: the same missing middleware means no CSP header on that response, so there is no policy for a nonce to satisfy. On every path that does render one, `requestContextMiddleware` precedes `securityMiddleware` in the same chain.

## Verification

Driven against the running deployment from `Asia/Tokyo` with a `de-DE` locale — about as far from the container's `America/Los_Angeles` as the pair get:

| Page | Error boundary | Hydration errors | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| home, signed out | no | 0 | 1 |
| dashboard | no | 0 | 7 |
| workout page | no | 0 | 14 |

History dates render in German (`Fr., 7. Aug.`), the greeting correctly reads "Good morning" against a container that thinks it is late afternoon, and `/no-such-page` returns **404** with the styled "Page not found" boundary.

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, 79 tests pass.

## Trois connecteurs communaux nouveaux

- **SDES — parc automobile** (`sdes-parc-auto-communal`) : voitures particulières au 1er janvier (2011-2026) et part électrique + hybride rechargeable, calculée sans secret statistique. Témoin figé : Bordeaux 2023 = 111 924 VP (millésime définitif). Paris y est l'inverse de la Dares, et c'est mesuré : 75056 est un résidu (6 521 voitures), pas la somme des arrondissements (596 643) ; repli par `commune_mere`, résidu compris. Codes fictifs de la source (dép + 000, 97x00) écartés nommément. ~1,12 M d'observations.
- **Cerema — consommation d'espaces** (`cerema-conso-espaces-communal`) : flux annuel d'espaces naturels, agricoles et forestiers consommés et part habitat, en m², 2011-2024, 34 856 communes exactement au COG. Identités internes exactes (écart 0 sur le fichier national), témoin Gironde 2023 = 3 117 494 m², somme nationale retombant sur les 15 119 ha publiés par le portail. La fiche dit que la dernière année est provisoire, et que consommation d'espaces ≠ artificialisation au sens strict. Unité `m2` nouvelle, affichée en hectares dès 10 000 m².
- **Justice/DGAP — population carcérale** (`justice-detenus-etablissements`) : détenus et densité carcérale (détenus / places opérationnelles, calculée par niveau à partir des sommes) par établissement, rattachés à leur commune d'implantation via un crosswalk versionné de 186 lignes (16 corrections manuelles documentées). Témoins : France 89 446 détenus / 63 289 places au 01/07/2026, Gradignan à 205,6 %. Les délais de justice par tribunal n'existent pas en open data : refus documenté.

## Audit qualité appliqué (doublons, bullshit, évolutions)

- **Bug réparé : l'inflation ne s'affichait jamais.** La fiche recevait l'indice des prix mais l'appel interne omettait le douzième argument : la phrase « en euros constants » était morte depuis sa naissance. Réparée et raccourcie.
- **Les variations sont partout** : chaque marche et chaque composante du pont porte son évolution vs l'exercice précédent (calculée sur la grandeur comptable brute : une épargne qui remonte de −2 à −1 M€ s'améliore) ; les six rapports disent leur mouvement dans leur unité (+2,0 pt, pas +20 %).
- **Doublons fondus** : chambres/hôtels, votants/participation, montant/nombre d'établissements subventionnés, budget voté replié dans l'exécuté avec l'écart d'exécution chiffré, lignes-identités (population active, IPC, consommation effective) derrière le pli, allocations RSA/APA/PCH de la ventilation fonctionnelle dépubliées (doublons des indicateurs OFGL branchés au pont).
- **Nomenclature traduite partout** (CVAE, TSCA, DMTO, TICPE, GAD, « hors remb ») via un module partagé ; libellés publiés purgés des tirets cadratins et de « nombre de infractions » ; nouveau module `plateforme.redeclarer` pour rejouer les `declarer()` sans réingérer.
- **Purge du bruit** : ligne « Maire : non renseigné » supprimée, note de mandature en une ligne, panneaux morts et `tendance()` supprimés, contradiction budget principal/annexes de la page Données résolue.

## Vérification

- Pipeline : 1529 tests passent (dont 36 nouveaux pour les trois connecteurs), ruff propre.
- Site : 312 tests passent, tsc propre.
- Fixtures réelles, octets conservés ; témoins relevés à la main sur les sources, dates notées.

author: hotragn
body: Fixes #820. A heartbeat fire that lands on a busy session is currently consumed and lost, and the beats that do land carry no way to notice the gap. ## The fire is consumed before the busy check `claimDueInState` advances `job.nextRunAt` at claim time, before `runCronJob` ever asks `shouldDeferHeartbeatCronJob`. When the session turns out to be busy, `recordDispatchResult`'s skip branch advances `nextRunAt` a *second* time, from `now`. Three consequences: - The missed beat is never re-armed. - An interval schedule loses its phase on every skip: `every 5m` skipped 90s late becomes `every 5m` measured from the skip, so the cadence drifts by the length of every busy check. - A busy window spanning several beats is indistinguishable from one skipped beat. `lastSkippedAt` is a single overwritten timestamp. `rescheduleAfterSkip` now advances from the dispatch record's `scheduledFor` — the beat that was actually skipped — and steps the schedule forward until the next fire is strictly after `now`. So: - `every 5m` due at 12:05 and declined at 12:06:30 re-arms at **12:10**, not 12:11:30. - The same job declined at 12:27 re-arms at 12:30 and reports **5** swallowed fires (12:05, 12:10, 12:15, 12:20, 12:25). - Because the result is always strictly after `now`, a busy session cannot make the scheduler spin on an already-due job. Dispatch attempts stay at one per interval, exactly as today. - The step loop is bounded (`MAX_COALESCED_SKIPS`); a pathologically short schedule against a very long busy window falls back to the plain advance while keeping the count it accumulated. Those fires land in a new `AgentCronJob.missedRunCount`, which accumulates across skips and is cleared when a beat is delivered. All three skip paths feed it: the `recordDispatchResult` skip branch, `recordSkipResult`, and `claimDueInState`'s already-claimed branch (a fire arriving while the previous dispatch is still outstanding is swallowed the same way). I deliberately did not make a declined beat re-fire immediately. Re-arming at the original `scheduledFor` would leave the job due while the session is still busy, and `runCronJob` declines cheaply, so it would busy-loop for the length of the busy window. Coalescing forward preserves both the user's cadence and the scheduler's load profile. ## The delivered prompt could not report any of this `createHeartbeatPromptMessage` put `runCount`/`lastRunAt`/`nextRunAt` in `HeartbeatPromptDetails`, which `convertToLlm` drops, and set `content: job.prompt`. Every delivery was byte-identical, so a heartbeat-driven agent could not tell "beat 3 of 3" from "beat 3 of 40". The heartbeat message content is what `convertToLlm` turns into the provider's user message, so `formatHeartbeatPromptContent` now prefixes the instruction with a compact block: ```text beat 7 schedule every 5m previous delivery 2026-01-01T12:05:00.000Z 2 scheduled fires skipped while this session was busy (most recent 2026-01-01T12:15:00.000Z) Check the deployment and report meaningful changes ``` The instruction stays last so it remains the final thing the model reads, and the skipped-fires line appears only when there is a backlog. Queue previews and `clearQueue()` are unaffected — they read the prompt text passed to `_promptInjectedMessage`, which is still the bare instruction, so `Heartbeat prompt: ` renders exactly as before. ## Human-visible surfaces `/heartbeat status` gained `Missed: since last run, most recent `; previously it showed nothing about skips at all. `formatAgentCronJob` gained `missed=` alongside the existing `skipped=`. ## Daemon protocol `DaemonCronJob` is an alias of `AgentCronJob`, so `missedRunCount` is published on cron/heartbeat job rows. That is an additive change on an existing response shape — a new daemon's extra field is ignored by an old client, and a new client renders nothing when an old daemon omits it — matching revisions 9/10/12, which also published new fields. `DAEMON_SCHEMA_REVISION` moves to 16 with a matching comment and `DAEMON_SCHEMA_ID` (14 was taken by the telemetry opt-out in #521 and 15 by the queued-message mutation command in #838, both of which landed while this was open; rebased onto each in turn). The schema digest is unchanged from `main` because it hashes the `daemon-protocol.ts` wire-type source, which this PR does not touch. The schema digest hashes the `daemon-protocol.ts` wire-type source only, so it is unchanged; `test/daemon-protocol.test.ts` verifies the identity stays synchronized. ## Tests New: `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/820-heartbeat-missed-beats.test.ts` (6 cases) — phase preservation on a declined beat, coalescing five fires across a 22-minute busy window with the re-armed fire proven to be in the future, accumulation across two skips followed by a delivery that clears the backlog, `missed=` in the daemon listing, the composed prompt text in first-delivery/backlog/singular forms, and an end-to-end case asserting the model actually receives the backlog notice. Updated (intentional behavior changes, not relaxations): - `test/cron-jobs.test.ts` — two tests asserted the drifting reschedule. One is renamed from "reschedules a skipped dispatch from the skip time" to "...on the original cadence"; both now also assert `missedRunCount`. - `test/suite/regressions/4482-heartbeat-injected-prompt.test.ts` — four assertions compared the delivered text to the bare instruction; they now compare against `formatHeartbeatPromptContent`. The queue-preview and `clearQueue` assertions were left untouched and still pass, which is the check that previews stayed clean. Verified: `npm run check` clean; `cron-jobs`, `daemon-protocol`, `daemon-client`, `agent-connection-daemon`, `messages`, `4482`, and the new suite pass (180 + 6). `daemon-mode.test.ts` has 5 failures on this Windows machine (unix-socket bind and symlink cases) that reproduce identically on a clean `main` worktree. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix heartbeat cron jobs to preserve schedule cadence and track missed fires on busy session declines > - When a heartbeat fire is declined (session busy), the scheduler now re-arms from the original scheduled beat rather than the skip time, preserving the schedule phase. > - Missed fires during a busy window are coalesced into a `missedRunCount` on the job, reset to zero on the next successful delivery. > - Delivered heartbeat prompts include a `` block with beat number, schedule expression, previous delivery time, and a missed-fire summary when backlog exists. > - `missed=` appears in daemon job listings and the interactive `/heartbeat status` view when there is a backlog. > - Behavioral Change: `recordSkipResult` and `recordDispatchResult` in [`cron-jobs.ts`](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent/pull/890/files#diff-fb783dad61580c3b11d0731df2a325b6e3dd852fc430a309a5f3ae7ebcc826dd) now advance `nextRunAt` along the original cadence instead of from the skip time; daemon schema bumped to revision 17. > > > > Macroscope summarized d101619. > >

author: joseph-cursio
body:
## The gap

`DocCitationTests` reads two populations: `docs/…` paths in **Swift comments**, and markdown **link** syntax between docs. The backtick-in-prose form — which is how these docs cite each other nearly everywhere — was read by neither.

That is not a corner case. The reorganisation that moved 64 docs left **130 unresolvable occurrences over 60 distinct paths**, with both existing checks green throughout. 72 were plain directory moves (fixed in #162).

`DocProseCitationTests` closes it: 62 live docs + `CLAUDE.md`, ~117 citations.

## The exclusions are the design, not the leftovers

`docs/archive/`, `CHANGELOG.md` and root `README.md` are **history**. They record what was true when written, so a citation to a since-pruned doc is *correct* there and repointing it would be the actual error. Excluding whole files costs coverage of anything newly added to them — taken knowingly, because the alternative is a ~330-entry allowlist nobody would read.

Three exemptions inside the live set:
1. `git show <sha>:docs/…` — the existing convention, asserted in the opposite direction by the existing `historicalCitationsNameRemovedDocs`.
2. **A bare mention carrying its recovery pointer on the same line.** Keeps *"recorded in `docs/x.md` (pruned in `abc123`; recover with `git show abc123^:docs/x.md`)"* writable. Same-line so the pairing is mechanical, not a judgment about paragraph reach.
3. **Sibling-repo paths.** This changed three citations' spelling: `SwiftProjectLint/docs/rules/…` rather than a bare `docs/…` with the repo named in the surrounding English — each of which read as pointing at a file in *this* repo.

What survives is a four-entry allowlist, and every entry is one idiom: a sentence whose **subject** is a broken path (*"this row said `docs/glossary.md`, which does not exist"*). No spelling both reads correctly and resolves.

## Three guards guard the guard

- The allowlist fails if an entry stops matching — a stale exemption protects nothing while reading as though it does.
- The history exclusions fail if one names a path that isn't there.
- `scanIsNotEmpty` **asserts the denominator**. Every exemption narrows the population; one bad prefix would empty it, and the green run would then mean "found nothing wrong" and "looked at nothing" indistinguishably. This repo's *confident zero*.

## Also in this PR

- **Scanner extraction.** The helpers moved to `DocCitationScanner` — two suites need them, and the addition pushed `DocCitationTests.swift` to 402 lines against SwiftLint's 400 cap.
- **Three extraction bugs**, each surfaced by the new population. The notable one: **`git show <sha>^:docs/…` did not read as a history citation** — `suffix(while: isHexDigit)` ran straight off the `:`, so `^` ended the run at zero digits. That is the form that matters, since a doc pruned *by* commit X is only readable at `X^`, and three such annotations exist in the PRDs. Also globs (`docs/**/*.md` is a set, not a file — ten false positives on the first run) and sibling-rooted detection.
- **The replay-idempotence sketch moved to `docs/archive/`** (shipped M1–M13). Its inline summary said "M1–M5" while its own build order ran to M13 — the stale-summary shape CLAUDE.md tracks twice already.

## What a reviewer should scrutinise

1. **Is excluding `CHANGELOG.md` / `README.md` / `docs/archive/` wholesale right?** It is the load-bearing judgment here, and it trades real coverage for a readable allowlist.
2. **The same-line pairing rule.** It is a convention this repo now has to follow; a wrap between the name and its pointer reads as a dangling citation. It caught my own `docs/README.md` prose while writing this.
3. **The four allowlist entries** — each should be a sentence that cannot be fixed, not one that is merely inconvenient.

## Testing

11 doc-guard tests green; `make test-fast` green at **5,037 tests**; `swiftlint --strict` clean on all touched files. Negative controls run by hand: a planted dangling citation fires with `file:line`, a planted sibling-form citation stays correctly silent.

THE LIVE BLOCKER ON 100 TASKS/DAY. Measured 2026-08-07: POST /api/conduct/sessions answers

    500 {"detail": "Exceeded allowed rows written in Durable Objects free tier."}

`_register_relay_session` is on EVERY relay write path, so this single wall blocks the
#2014 canonical-heal rung, dispatch receipts, and board publication at once. The keeper is
the only sanctioned board writer, so while its writes are refused the board cannot advance
at all: twelve needs-human `ASK-quicken-*` atoms stay regressed on
origin/tabularius/board-projection and the throughput governor stays at `dispatched: 0`,
bootstrap cap 25. The last successful keeper write was 2026-08-07T12:55:47-04:00 —
immediately after #2016's own merge, so unblocking the write path is what spent the day's
remaining allowance.

Resolving it is a recurring SPEND, which is a human-gated lever, not agent work. What the
fleet owes is that the condition be legible and HOMED rather than recited at the operator:

  · `BrokerQuotaExhausted(ConductError)` — its own type, because this is neither a bug nor a
    transient fault: no retry, no backoff, and no correct client code makes the next write
    land. A subclass, so every existing `except ConductError` keeps working unchanged.
  · `heal-board.py --canonical` catches it and reports ONE legible line naming its registry
    owner, exiting 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL). Deliberately non-zero: a tidy exit 0 here would restore
    exactly the "everything looks healthy" blindness that let this sit unseen, and the beat's
    rung ledger needs a real failure to record.
  · lever `L-CLOUDFLARE-DO-QUOTA` in his-hand-levers.json (issue #2054) — the durable home,
    with both answers spelled out: raise the plan, or decide explicitly not to and accept a
    board that advances once per daily reset. Either is legitimate; being the default nobody
    noticed is not.

ONE DELIBERATE RULE EXEMPTION, stated because it contradicts a rule this repo enforces:
`ConductError`'s own docstring says callers classify on `status`, never on rejection prose,
because three keepers word the same condition differently. A Cloudflare storage refusal
arrives as an undifferentiated 500 with no machine-readable field, so prose is the ONLY
available signal. The match is kept narrow (three explicit substrings, and a marker is
REQUIRED — status alone never suffices) precisely so real 500s stay real bugs; that negative
direction is the more load-bearing half of the tests. The durable fix is for the keeper to
answer a structured code, which is recorded on the lever as fleet-owned follow-on — it needs
a wrangler deploy, which does NOT happen on merge, so it is not smuggled in here.

Verified at runtime by A/B against a loopback keeper returning the exact 500 body, with the
baseline extracted from origin/main and asserted NOT to contain the fix's markers first:

  BEFORE  62 lines, an uncaught traceback whose final line is `}`            exit 1
  AFTER    6 lines naming the condition, the lever, all 12 blocked atoms     exit 75

Gates: ruff 0 · verify-scoped.sh 0 (5519 cli + 48 api) · no-tasks-on-me registry rung green
(80 levers, all owned + traceable, no PII shapes).

author: viraj-vekariya
body:
## Summary
Root cause of "predictions are UNSAFE far more than expected": the Arduino firmware has always had a working MQ-135 calibration curve (`readAmmoniaPpm()`, using the datasheet's Rs/R0 log-log relationship), but `sendReadings()` never called it — it sent the raw uncalibrated 0-1023 analog average instead, under a `mq_raw` field. When the model was migrated to XGBoost, the frontend slider was silently widened from its original **0-50ppm** range to **0-1023** to match, and a hard "biological override" failsafe was added at `mq_raw >= 600` with no relationship to any real threshold. The model was then retrained entirely on this made-up 0-1023 scale, disconnected from both the sensor's actual physics and the project's own Phase 1 literature research (TVB-N/pH/ammonia spoilage bounds, Arrhenius kinetics) that the **original** pre-XGBoost Random Forest model was trained on. Every fix this session preserved that broken scale faithfully instead of questioning it.

Found by tracing back through git history to the original `sensopack_colab.py` training script and `PHASE1_LITERATURE.md`.

## Changes
- **`PJSketch.ino`** — `sendReadings()` now calls the existing (previously dead) `readAmmoniaPpm()` and sends `ammonia_ppm` instead of raw `mq_raw` counts.
- **`arduino_bridge.py`** — relays `ammonia_ppm` to Firebase instead of `mq_raw`.
- **`train_rf.py`** — replaced the ad-hoc synthetic data generator with the literature-grounded Arrhenius-kinetics + TVB-N methodology from the original `sensopack_colab.py` (Ea=118kJ/mol, chill/moderate/abuse temp bands -2 to 30C, TVB-N-derived 3-class labels), producing `ammonia_ppm` (~0-20ppm) instead of the fabricated `mq_raw` scale. Accuracy is 79% (down from a misleadingly clean 97%+ on the old artificially-separable synthetic data) because this generator targets realistic ~0.75-0.90 sensor correlation by design, per the literature doc, instead of near-perfect separability.
- **`api/index.py`** — `PredictRequest` field renamed `mq_raw` → `ammonia_ppm`; Firebase read key updated; biological override thresholds recalibrated to the literature's actual "Spoiled" bounds (ammonia ≥15ppm, pH ≥7.5, temp ≥32°C — just above the training data's abuse-band ceiling) instead of the arbitrary `mq_raw≥600`/`ph≥8.0`/`temp≥35` values that had no grounding once the sensor scale changed.
- **`webapp/app.js` + `index.html`** — payload key, `sensor_data_used` key, and ammonia slider (back to 0-50ppm, default 4.8ppm, matching the original pre-XGBoost UI) all updated to match.

## Test plan
- [x] `/api/health` returns healthy
- [x] Clearly-fresh scenario (low ppm, cold chain) → SAFE
- [x] Caution-zone scenario (mid ppm/pH, moderate time) → CAUTION with sensible confidence spread
- [x] Clearly-spoiled scenario → UNSAFE
- [x] Failsafe fires exactly at the literature threshold (`ammonia_ppm=16` triggers, `14` doesn't) instead of an arbitrary raw-sensor value
- [x] Malformed input still returns 422, not 500

body:
# KL-000: cross-implementation conformance, with its limits measured

This is the draft PR body for the KL-000 program: five repository runs
(RUN-20260807-1..5), three independent runs (IND-20260807-1..3), four
protocol versions. Nothing in this PR promotes any claim into the canonical
records; promotion is a separate owner-reviewed commit.

## What is established, by object and at its actual strength

Two independently written implementations — the Python reference, and a
zero-dependency Rust implementation with hand-written JSON/SHA-256/PRNG
whose author reports never having located or read the reference — agree on:

- **The evaluator and the complete conclusion function, across the full
  enumeration.** Identical partitioning of all 176,120 exhaustive worlds
  (110,840 receipts / 65,280 fail-closed, one cause) and an identical
  conclusion distribution over all 110,840 receipt-producing worlds:
  absent 160, not_established 49,480, present 41,820, supported 19,380.
  Zero violations of every registered hard invariant, in every run of both
  implementations.
- **The canonical form and digests — for the two pinned receipts only, not
  for all 110,840.** Fixtures C11 and C12 reproduce byte-for-byte across
  implementations: canonical unsigned forms identical (703 and 691 bytes),
  digests equal (`sha256:84e63c21…33eafe`, `sha256:61000a9b…aa3b6e`). This
  became possible only when v1.2.0 registered the receipt object — before
  that, 279 of the 703 hashed bytes were specified nowhere, and the digest
  provably could not be computed from the documents.
- **That four versions of specification repair changed nothing the evaluator
  does.** Every repair was published with a registered exact-equality
  prediction and tested by full re-execution: no count, no conclusion, and
  no pinned digest ever moved.

The randomized phase (1,000,000 seeded worlds, zero violations on both
sides) is a **replication, not a reproduction**, permanently: the frozen
seed fixes no cross-implementation world stream.

## The qualification that travels with the claim (LEAK-101)

The v1.1.0 commission package leaked the expected counts — including the
conclusion distribution — to the independent implementer, through the
registered protocol's own prediction table, shipped verbatim; the redaction
was correctly applied to the preregistration and defeated by the file beside
it. The conclusion-agreement line was therefore not blind. Two mitigations
are verified in the record: the line is derivable from the implementer's
*previously published* output plus the registered rule, and both later
independent runs recompute it from the worlds. **The digest result is
unaffected** — a count gives no path to a hash, and the receipt object the
digests cover was registered after the leaked package. The qualification
stays in the claim regardless.

## The decisions are now enforced (I12)

Until v1.3.0, the program's two owner decisions — the R1 tie rule and
R5.2's absolute margin — were enforced by **zero invariants**: an evaluator
with either decision inverted passed all eleven invariants over the complete
enumeration, caught only by the two pinned fixtures (R5.2's entire detection
surface was one world). v1.3.0 registered **I12**
(`conclusion == conclusionFunction(world)`;
`margin == abs(|supporting| − |opposing|)`, both world-referential) and
demonstrated its power at the exact previously measured surfaces:

| Ablation | Caught by I12 on | Other invariants | Fixture involved |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 inverted — ties conclude `supported` | exactly **22,440** worlds | 0 | none |
| R5.2 inverted — margin signed | exactly **38,760** worlds | 0 | none |

The reference records zero I12 violations, and the enforcement change moved
nothing — every count, conclusion, baseline total, and both pinned digests
are unchanged. (The independent implementation conformed through v1.2.0; its
checker is its own and it has not run against v1.3.0.)

## What remains open, deliberately

- **A1** — does absence require supporting evidence, or coverage alone?
  **4 worlds.** The registered text says coverage alone; never brought to an
  explicit decision.
- **A2** — does presence require complete coverage? **19,152 worlds, 17.3%
  of receipts** — the largest undecided surface in the kernel. Recorded as
  an owner decision the program did not reach, with both readings and their
  consequences preserved. Neither is decided in this PR.

Also on the open ledger: the receipt-internal forms of I2/I5 (a registered
must-fail baseline does not fail literal I2 — measured in both
implementations), the margin-collision observation (unopposed support and
outnumbered-two-to-one produce identical `margin` scalars), the permanently
replication-only randomized phase, and the packaging rule that any future
commission must withhold the conclusion distribution.

## What this is not

KL-000's state is `adversarial-passed` — not "verified", not
`verified-independent`; that is an owner promotion decision not taken here.
**The first-transaction gate is NOT REACHED.** KL-000 was the precondition
for attempting KL-011; **eleven kernels (KL-001..KL-011) remain seeded**
with exact next gates, none executed. No knowledge transaction, no
cross-system result, no Candidate First Transmission, and no First
Transmission exists or is claimed.

## In the diff

Four preserved protocol registrations with commit-bound sidecars; the

author: readerwei
body:
Small follow-up to #5, found by running the merged `master` from a fresh clone rather than trusting my own working tree.

## The bug was in my reasoning, not the runtime

In the #5 review I told @TradingBot that the crypto smoke test could safely require data because *"silence there is always suspicious."* That was wrong, and a clean clone of `master` proved it by reporting **FAILED on a perfectly working stream**.

Measured on the live feed:

```
connected      0.13s
authenticated  0.16s
subscribed     0.20s      <- handshake is fine
first data     none within 20s
```

The handshake is fast and correct. **The data is bursty.** Alpaca sends a snapshot on subscribe and then publishes only on change:

| sample | result |
|---|---|
| 75s window | 6 events in the first second, **nothing for the next 74** |
| 40s window | nothing at all until **24.2s** |

That also retires a loose end from #5: quote counts of 32, 8, 5, 2 and 0 across earlier runs looked like a stream in varying health. They were a fixed window sampling a feed whose cadence is longer than the window.

## Fix

Same shape as the `smoke_stream.py` fix @TradingBot asked for: handshake and data flow are **separate results**. The handshake is asserted, because a failure there is unambiguous. Absent data is reported and explicitly **not** treated as conclusive.

```
handshake     : OK
data flow     : none in 10s (this feed is bursty; not conclusive)   -> exit 0
```

Also: a missing `CRYPTO_SYMBOLS` raised `IndexError` from a tuple subscript. It now names the variable to set.

## Worth stating plainly

Two of the last three findings were the same defect in mirror image:

- **#5 review** — accepting evidence a *broken* system can produce (a silent socket passing as OK)
- **this one** — requiring evidence a *correct* system cannot always produce (a bursty feed failing)

Both make a check report something other than what it measured. The first hides a real bug; the second manufactures a fake one and erodes trust in every green run after it.

`68 passed`. No runtime code changed — `scripts/smoke_crypto.py` only.

author: telfardo
body:
## What changed

The footer credit was a flat line of small text. It now uses two type registers, echoing the move the brand mark already makes ("Ed White" in serif, "· Tuition" dropped back in faint sans):

- `SITE BY` — 0.58rem Inter, uppercase, 0.14em tracking, `--ink-faint`
- `Telfardo` — 0.82rem Source Serif, tight tracking, `--ink-soft`
- a 4px `--accent` diamond at half opacity

**Hover** stages four changes at slightly different speeds rather than a single colour swap: an accent underline sweeps out from the left under the name (400ms), the name warms to accent, the label steps up a shade, and the diamond rotates 90° to full opacity.

The underline is drawn as a `linear-gradient` background with an animated `background-size`, because `text-decoration` width cannot be transitioned.

## Notes

- Dropped the blanket `opacity: 0.75`. Two explicit ink colours carry the hierarchy, and the hover state reads cleaner without a translucency layer over it.
- Wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` so it snaps rather than animates for anyone who has asked their OS for less motion.
- The diamond is `align-self: center` — an empty flex item has no baseline to sit on and hangs low under `align-items: baseline`.
- Net size still sits under Ed's 0.9rem footer text, so it stays subordinate despite the serif carrying more visual weight than the 0.65rem it replaced.

Not visually verified — the Browser pane is not displaying in this environment, so screenshots time out. The hover state in particular is worth an eyeball.

author: felipedaros
body:
## Summary
- The crossbow's weapon definition (`weaponDefinitionId` 1414) has 3 fire groups, one per projectile type: Wooden Arrow, Flaming Arrow, Explosive Arrow.
- Pressing the switch-fire-mode keybind (default V) sends `Weapon.SwitchFireModeRequest`, but the handler only rebroadcast a cosmetic packet to other players and never changed which ammo the weapon actually consumed/reloaded with.
- Added a `firegroupIndex` to the `Weapon` class, and use it in `getWeaponAmmoId` / `getWeaponReloadTime` (previously hardcoded to fire group 0). `Weapon.SwitchFireModeRequest` now cycles through the weapon's fire groups for weapons that expose more than one (crossbow), resets the loaded ammo count (so the player has to reload with the newly selected arrow type), and syncs the change to the shooter and to other players.
- Weapons with a single fire group keep the previous behavior untouched, including the existing ADS-sound workaround.
